(He says) in the afternoon 'To the bounteous one, to him to be attended'; that is the symbol of night, (for they say) 'They sit round in the evening this fire which is to be attended as it were.' Both these symbols are recognized;
therefore day by day in alternation should he repeat (hoping) ‘Let both symbols, both desires be attained.’ He should repeat without taking breath, for the continuity of the breaths; for continuous as it were are these breaths. Thrice each one should he repeat; these worlds are three; verily thus he obtains these worlds. They repeated together make up nine; the seasons are six; these worlds are three; verily thus they make up that. He should not say this Nigada in the kindling verses; the Nigadas are omitted; it would be repetition if one were to say this Nigada. ‘He should not invite at all,’ some say; ‘But how without inviting can he say the offering verse for a deity?’ (For this reason). After the Ṛc he should invite with (the invitatory verses), ‘Bring Agni, bring Soma, bring Viṣṇu.’ For these three gods he says the offering verses; these worlds are three; verily thus he makes these worlds full of light.

sanskrit_iast: te devāḥ pariśriteṣv eṣu lokeṣv etam pañcadaśam vajram apaśyan |
meaning: ते देवाः परिश्रितेष्व् एषु लोकेष्व् एतम् पञ्चदशम् वज्रम् अपश्यन् |

sanskrit_iast: etena vai devāḥ pañcadaśena vajreṇa ebhyo lokebhyo asurān anudanta |
meaning: एतेन वै देवाः पञ्चदशेन वज्रेण एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो असुरान् अनुदन्त |

sanskrit_iast: tatho eva etad yajamāna etena eva pañcadaśena vajreṇa ebhyo lokebhyo dviṣato bhrātṛvyān nudate |
meaning: तथो एव एतद् यजमान एतेन एव पञ्चदशेन वज्रेण एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो द्विषतो भ्रातृव्यान् नुदते |

sanskrit_iast: upasadyāya mīḍhuṣe ity etam tṛcam pūrva ahṇe anubrūyāt |
meaning: उपसद्याय मीढुषे इत्य् एतम् तृचम् पूर्व अह्णे अनुब्रूयात् |

sanskrit_iast: tad vai karma samṛddham yat prathamena abhivyāhriyate |
meaning: तद् वै कर्म समृद्धम् यत् प्रथमेन अभिव्याह्रियते |

sanskrit_iast: upasadyam iva vā etad ahar amunā ādityena bhavati iti |
meaning: उपसद्यम् इव वा एतद् अहर् अमुना आदित्येन भवति इति |

sanskrit_iast: imām me agne samidham ity apara ahṇe tad rātre rūpam |
meaning: इमाम् मे अग्ने समिधम् इत्य् अपर अह्णे तद् रात्रे रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: samiddham iva vā imam agnim sāyam paryāsata iti |
meaning: समिद्धम् इव वा इमम् अग्निम् सायम् पर्यासत इति |

sanskrit_iast: imām me agne samidham iti pūrva ahṇe tad ahno rūpam |
meaning: इमाम् मे अग्ने समिधम् इति पूर्व अह्णे तद् अह्नो रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: samiddham iva vā etad ahar amunā ādityena bhavati iti |
meaning: समिद्धम् इव वा एतद् अहर् अमुना आदित्येन भवति इति |

sanskrit_iast: upasadyāya mīḍhuṣa ity apara ahṇe tad rātre rūpam |
meaning: उपसद्याय मीढुष इत्य् अपर अह्णे तद् रात्रे रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: upasadyam iva vā imam agnim sāyam paryāsata iti |
meaning: उपसद्यम् इव वा इमम् अग्निम् सायम् पर्यासत इति |

sanskrit_iast: te vā ubhe eva rūpe yaj jñāyete |
meaning: ते वा उभे एव रूपे यज् ज्ञायेते |

sanskrit_iast: ubhe rūpe kāmā upāptāv asatām iti |
meaning: उभे रूपे कामा उपाप्ताव् असताम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: ṣaḍ vā ṛtavas traya ime lokāḥ |
meaning: षड् वा ऋतवस् त्रय इमे लोकाः |

sanskrit_iast: na etam nigadam brūyād ya eṣa sāmidhenīṣu |
meaning: न एतम् निगदम् ब्रूयाद् य एष सामिधेनीषु |

sanskrit_iast: jāmi ha syād ya etam nigadam brūyāt |
meaning: जामि ह स्याद् य एतम् निगदम् ब्रूयात् |

sanskrit_iast: na āvāhayec cana iti ha eka āhuḥ |
meaning: न आवाहयेच् चन इति ह एक आहुः |

sanskrit_iast: kim u devatām anvāvāhya jayed iti |
meaning: किम् उ देवताम् अन्वावाह्य जयेद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: agnim āvaha somam āvaha viṣṇum āvaha iti |
meaning: अग्निम् आवह सोमम् आवह विष्णुम् आवह इति |

sanskrit_iast: imān eva tal lokān jyotiṣmataḥ karoti |
meaning: इमान् एव तल् लोकान् ज्योतिष्मतः करोति |

text:
The two verses for Agni are Gāyatrī verses; this world is connected with the Gāyatrī; thus he obtains this world. Those for Soma are Triṣṭubh verses; the world of the atmosphere is connected with the Triṣṭubh; thus he obtains the world of the atmosphere. Those for Viṣṇu are Jagatī verses; yonder world is connected with the Jagatī; thus he obtains yonder world. These he inverts; those which in the forenoon were invitatory verses he makes offering verses in the afternoon; those which were offering verses he makes invitatory verses, to avoid exhaustion, (thinking) ‘The Ṛc becomes exhausted through the vaṣaṭ call; let me perform the vaṣaṭ call with (verses) unexhausted on the same day’. In that he inverts also, (it is) for the strength of the neck; therefore the joints of the neck are as it were intertwined. The gods have butter as their oblation, the sacrificer has milk as his fast food; that is in accord. He should treat them as broader above; on the first day (he should milk) three teats, then two, then one; verily thus he makes the worlds mutually broader. He should not take out; they advance to the world of heaven who undertake the Upasads; the world of heaven is twelve journeys away; he who takes out once, it is with him as if one should follow after those with one object sent on a single
night before. If he takes out twice, it is as if the time were two nights; through a third (taking) he loses the world of heaven, he cannot attain it. ‘He may however follow,’ used to say Paiṅgya. ‘But he should not take out; wherever he wishes, there first should he go in the world of heaven and stop: such a completion is better,’ used Kauṣītaki to say. In the case of (need of) eating his compeers may bring curds for him, but not in the time of the fast food; curds is Soma; his food becomes unobstructed; he obtains it. If they purchase (the Soma) together, the others should proceed for two days with the middle Upasad, for it is an insertion, being in position the world of the atmosphere: so without conflict he proceeds.

sanskrit_iast: yāḥ pūrva ahṇe puronuvākyās tā apara ahṇe yājyāḥ karoti |
meaning: याः पूर्व अह्णे पुरोनुवाक्यास् ता अपर अह्णे याज्याः करोति |

sanskrit_iast: vaṣaṭ kāreṇa ha vā ṛg yāta yāmā bhavati samāne ahan |
meaning: वषट् कारेण ह वा ऋग् यात यामा भवति समाने अहन् |

sanskrit_iast: ayāta yāmābhir me vaṣaṭkṛtam asad iti |
meaning: अयात यामाभिर् मे वषट्कृतम् असद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: yad v eva viparyasyati grīvāṇām sthemne |
meaning: यद् व् एव विपर्यस्यति ग्रीवाणाम् स्थेम्ने |

sanskrit_iast: tasmādd ha āsām grīvāṇām vyatiṣaktāni iva parvāṇi bhavanti |
meaning: तस्माद्द् ह आसाम् ग्रीवाणाम् व्यतिषक्तानि इव पर्वाणि भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tāḥ parovarīyasīr abhyupeyāt trīn agre stanān atha dvāv atha ekam |
meaning: ताः परोवरीयसीर् अभ्युपेयात् त्रीन् अग्रे स्तनान् अथ द्वाव् अथ एकम् |

sanskrit_iast: paraspara eva tal lokān varīyasaḥ kurute |
meaning: परस्पर एव तल् लोकान् वरीयसः कुरुते |

sanskrit_iast: svargam ha vā ete lokam abhiprayanti ya upasada upayanti |
meaning: स्वर्गम् ह वा एते लोकम् अभिप्रयन्ति य उपसद उपयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: dvādaśo ha vā antar uṣyāt svargo lokaḥ |
meaning: द्वादशो ह वा अन्तर् उष्यात् स्वर्गो लोकः |

sanskrit_iast: yathā eka rātram sārthān proṣitān anupreyād evam tat |
meaning: यथा एक रात्रम् सार्थान् प्रोषितान् अनुप्रेयाद् एवम् तत् |

sanskrit_iast: apy anugacched iti ha sma āha paiṅgyaḥ |
meaning: अप्य् अनुगच्छेद् इति ह स्म आह पैङ्ग्यः |

sanskrit_iast: tat pūrvo gatvā svargasya eva lokasya avasyed iti |
meaning: तत् पूर्वो गत्वा स्वर्गस्य एव लोकस्य अवस्येद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: samāptiḥ śreyasī iti ha sma āha kaṣītakiḥ |
meaning: समाप्तिः श्रेयसी इति ह स्म आह कषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: saṃrājo bhakṣo asmai dadhy ānayeyur na vrate |
meaning: संराजो भक्षो अस्मै दध्य् आनयेयुर् न व्रते |

sanskrit_iast: anantarhitau ha asya bhakṣo bhavati samāpnoti |
meaning: अनन्तर्हितौ ह अस्य भक्षो भवति समाप्नोति |

sanskrit_iast: atha asamaram abhyudaity atha asamaram abhyudaiti |
meaning: अथ असमरम् अभ्युदैत्य् अथ असमरम् अभ्युदैति |

text: Agni is the holy power; in that on the fast day they bring forward the fire, with the holy power do they strike away the evil of the sacrificer, in front with the Āhavanīya, behind with the Gārhapatya, on the north with the Āgnīdhrīya, on the south with the Mārjālīya, in the middle with those within the Sadas. Therefore on the fast day they lead forward the fire to the east, they take out the fires of the priests; verily (they serve) to smite away the evil of the sacrificer. The gods being about to consecrate themselves had recourse to speech, ‘Thou hast much and varied experience; but we wish to be compact of truth, compact of restraint.’ She desired a portion in the consecration, but the gods would not give her a share therein. She (desired a share) in the introductory sacrifice, and they would not (give) her (a share) therein; in the sale, and they would not (give) her (a share) therein; in the guest reception, and they would not (give) her (a share) therein. She did not at all approach the Upasads being as it were vexed; therefore there should they proceed inaudibly so that they can just hear one another. She came when the fire was being brought forward on the fast day; the gods gave her a share therein; therefore there first should he recite aloud, so that they may know that she has arrived and has been given a share in the sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: brahmaṇā eva tad yajamānasya pāpmānam apaghnanti |
meaning: ब्रह्मणा एव तद् यजमानस्य पाप्मानम् अपघ्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: sā prāyaṇīye tām u tatra no bhava |
meaning: सा प्रायणीये ताम् उ तत्र नो भव |

sanskrit_iast: sā kraye tām u tatra no bhava |
meaning: सा क्रये ताम् उ तत्र नो भव |

sanskrit_iast: sā ātithye tām u tara no bhava |
meaning: सा आतिथ्ये ताम् उ तर नो भव |

sanskrit_iast: so vā etad upasado nācana āgacchan nirvidya eva |
meaning: सो वा एतद् उपसदो नाचन आगच्छन् निर्विद्य एव |

sanskrit_iast: so vā etad upavasathe agnau praṇīyamāna āgacchat |
meaning: सो वा एतद् उपवसथे अग्नौ प्रणीयमान आगच्छत् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād u tatra prathamata eva uccair anubrūyāt |
meaning: तस्माद् उ तत्र प्रथमत एव उच्चैर् अनुब्रूयात् |

sanskrit_iast: yathā enām āgatām anubudhyeran na abhaktām yajñe |
meaning: यथा एनाम् आगताम् अनुबुध्येरन् न अभक्ताम् यज्ञे |

sanskrit_iast: pra devam devyā dhiyā iti pravantam tṛcam prahriyamāṇāya anvāha |
meaning: प्र देवम् देव्या धिया इति प्रवन्तम् तृचम् प्रह्रियमाणाय अन्वाह |
text: He recites for him as he is taken forth the three verses containing ‘forth’, ‘Forth the god with the thought divine.’ ‘Thee in the footstep of the sacrificial food’, he says; the sacrificial food is this (earth), for in it he praises (īṭṭe) all. He praises him when deposited with the half verse containing (the word) ‘deposit’, ‘O All-knower, we deposit thee.’ He praises him when he has sat down with (the verses ) containing (the word) ‘sit’, ‘O Agni, of fair face, with all the gods’; ‘Sit, O Hotṛ, in thine own place, discerning’, and ‘The Hotṛ in the Hotṛ’s seat, well knowing.’ He concludes with (a verse ) containing the word ‘herald’, ‘Thou art a herald; thou also our protector from afar.’ He recites appropriate verses; what in the sacrifice is appropriate, that is perfect; verily (it serves) for the perfection of the sacrifice. Eight he recites; the Gāyatrī has eight syllables; Agni is connected with the Gāyatrī, and has the Gāyatrī as his metre; verily thus with his own metre they bring Agni forward. (He recites) the first thrice, the third thrice; they make up twelve; the year has twelve months; verily (they serve) to obtain the year. They repeated together make up eighteen Gāyatrī verses; verily by the metre it is connected with Agni. Of whatever even metre there are six, they make up a Gāyatrī; of whatever there are seven, an Uṣṇih, of whatever there are eight an Anuṣṭubh, of whatever there are nine a Bṛhatī, of whatever there are ten a Paṅkti, of whatever there are eleven a Triṣṭubh, of whatever there are twelve (syllables) a Jagatī.

sanskrit_iast: jātavedo nidhīmahi iti nihitavatā ardharcena nidhīyamānam anustauti |
meaning: जातवेदो निधीमहि इति निहितवता अर्धर्चेन निधीयमानम् अनुस्तौति |

sanskrit_iast: agne viśvebhiḥ svanīka devaiḥ sīda hotaḥ sva u loke cikitvān nihotā hotṛ ṣadane vidāna iti sannavatībhiḥ sannam anustauti |
meaning: अग्ने विश्वेभिः स्वनीक देवैः सीद होतः स्व उ लोके चिकित्वान् निहोता होतृ षदने विदान इति सन्नवतीभिः सन्नम् अनुस्तौति |

sanskrit_iast: tvam dūtas tvam u naḥ paraspā iti dūtavatyā paridadhāti |
meaning: त्वम् दूतस् त्वम् उ नः परस्पा इति दूतवत्या परिदधाति |

sanskrit_iast: yad yajñe abhirūpam tat samṛddham yajñasya eva samṛddhyai |
meaning: यद् यज्ञे अभिरूपम् तत् समृद्धम् यज्ञस्य एव समृद्ध्यै |

sanskrit_iast: etābhir vai devāḥ sarvā aṣṭīr āśnuvata |
meaning: एताभिर् वै देवाः सर्वा अष्टीर् आश्नुवत |

sanskrit_iast: tatho eva etad yajamāna etābhir eva sarvā aṣṭīr aśnute |
meaning: तथो एव एतद् यजमान एताभिर् एव सर्वा अष्टीर् अश्नुते |

sanskrit_iast: triḥ prathamayā trir uttamayā dvādaśa sampadyante |
meaning: त्रिः प्रथमया त्रिर् उत्तमया द्वादश सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: yasya ha kasya ca ṣaṭ samānasya chandasas tā gāyatrīm abhisampadyante |
meaning: यस्य ह कस्य च षट् समानस्य छन्दसस् ता गायत्रीम् अभिसम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: vāk ca vai manaś ca havir dhāne |
meaning: वाक् च वै मनश् च हविर् धाने |
text:
The two oblation holders are speech and mind; in speech and in mind is all this (universe) placed. In that they move forward the two oblation holders, verily (it serves) to obtain all desires. The oblation holders are two, the cover as the third they deposit; with them he obtains all that which is threefold regarding the gods or the self. He recites for them as they are moved forward (a verse ) containing (the word) ‘forward’, ‘Let the two come forward with weal for the sacrifice’, ‘May sky and earth for us this’, and ‘Rich in ghee is their milk’ he says; the first (verse) contains a benediction; the second mentions two deities: the libation which
the Adhvaryu offers in the track of the two oblation holders he accompanies with the first (verse); in that they move forward the two oblation holders, that he accompanies with the latter. He praises the two oblation holders with the appropriate (verse ), ‘What time ye came like twins striving.’ ‘Let men in service to the gods’ (he says ), for many drag the two. ‘In the two hast thou placed the word of praise’ and ‘All forms the sage doth assume’, (he says); in that they put on the cover third, that he accompanies with the first, in that they enclose the two oblation holders, that with the latter.

sanskrit_iast: vāci ca vai manasi ca idam sarvam hitam |
meaning: वाचि च वै मनसि च इदम् सर्वम् हितम् |

sanskrit_iast: tair yat kiṃca trividham adhidaivatam adhyātmam tat sarvam āpnoti |
meaning: तैर् यत् किंच त्रिविधम् अधिदैवतम् अध्यात्मम् तत् सर्वम् आप्नोति |

sanskrit_iast: pretām yajñasya śambhuvā iti pravatīm pravartyamānābhyām anvāha |
meaning: प्रेताम् यज्ञस्य शम्भुवा इति प्रवतीम् प्रवर्त्यमानाभ्याम् अन्वाह |

sanskrit_iast: dyāvā naḥ pṛthivī imam tayor id ghṛtavat paya iti |
meaning: द्यावा नः पृथिवी इमम् तयोर् इद् घृतवत् पय इति |

sanskrit_iast: yām adhvaryur vartmany āhutim juhoti tām pūrvayā anuvadati |
meaning: याम् अध्वर्युर् वर्त्मन्य् आहुतिम् जुहोति ताम् पूर्वया अनुवदति |

sanskrit_iast: yame iva yatamāne yadā etam ity abhirūpayā havir dhāne anustauti |
meaning: यमे इव यतमाने यदा एतम् इत्य् अभिरूपया हविर् धाने अनुस्तौति |

sanskrit_iast: pra vām bharan mānuṣā devayanta iti |
meaning: प्र वाम् भरन् मानुषा देवयन्त इति |

sanskrit_iast: adhi dvayor adadhā ukthyam vaco viśvā rūpāṇi prati muñcate kavir iti |
meaning: अधि द्वयोर् अदधा उक्थ्यम् वचो विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुञ्चते कविर् इति |

sanskrit_iast: yac chardis tṛtīyam abhinidadhati tat pūrvayā anuvadati |
meaning: यच् छर्दिस् तृतीयम् अभिनिदधति तत् पूर्वया अनुवदति |

sanskrit_iast: yadd havir dhāne pariśrayante tad uttarayā |
meaning: यद्द् हविर् धाने परिश्रयन्ते तद् उत्तरया |

text:
Moreover (he accompanies) with the latter the offering on the front. When he thinks of the two, ‘They will not move them there’, when they make them standing in the middle, then (should he say ) ‘To your lap, O ye that deceive not’; when there is rest, then a lap is made. He concludes with (a verse ) containing (the word) ‘around’, ‘Around thee, O singer, the songs.’ He recites appropriate (verses); what in the sacrifice is appropriate, that is perfect; verily (they serve) for the perfection of the sacrifice. They make up eight; with them the gods attained all attainments; verily thus also with these the sacrificer attains all attainments. (He recites) the first thrice, the last thrice; they make up twelve; the year has twelve months; verily (they serve) to obtain the year. Further, in that (he recites) the first thrice and the last thrice, verily thus he ties the two ends of the sacrifice, for firmness and to avoid slipping. Then they say to the Hotṛ ‘Do thou, O Hotṛ, act so that there may be freedom from fear.’ Thus exhorted, before pronouncing the Ṛc, he pushes a clod westwards with the fore part of his right foot (saying ),
‘From hence the fear from men and from others than men, O Vṛtra slayer.
Away the wheels have rolled’;
Hence is there risk from the wheels; thus for this region there is freedom from fear. He should resort to the left track of the right
oblation holder, which is facing east, (thinking) ‘The right oblation holder is this world; this world is a support; let me be unmoved in going on this support.’ He should not move to right or left from the place where he stands as he says the final verse. If he should move from it to right or left, and if some one were to say of him, ‘He shall fall away’, so would it be. After concluding, having wheeled round on his right arm, keeping silence, have gone as he came, having stood where standing he has uttered the first (verse), both in the rite and in the taking forth of the fires, he should go to his place.

sanskrit_iast: te yadā manyeta atra na iṅgayiṣyanti iti |
meaning: ते यदा मन्येत अत्र न इङ्गयिष्यन्ति इति |

sanskrit_iast: pari tvā girvaṇo gira iti parivatyā paridadhāti |
meaning: परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिर इति परिवत्या परिदधाति |

sanskrit_iast: etābhir vai devāḥ sarvā aṣṭīr āśnuvata |
meaning: एताभिर् वै देवाः सर्वा अष्टीर् आश्नुवत |

sanskrit_iast: tatho eva etad yajamāna etābhir eva sarvā aṣṭīr aśnute |
meaning: तथो एव एतद् यजमान एताभिर् एव सर्वा अष्टीर् अश्नुते |

sanskrit_iast: triḥ prathamayā trir uttamayā dvādaśa sampadyante |
meaning: त्रिः प्रथमया त्रिर् उत्तमया द्वादश सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: yad v eva triḥ prathamām trir uttamām |
meaning: यद् व् एव त्रिः प्रथमाम् त्रिर् उत्तमाम् |

sanskrit_iast: yajñasya eva tad barsau nahyati sthemne avisraṃsāya |
meaning: यज्ञस्य एव तद् बर्सौ नह्यति स्थेम्ने अविस्रंसाय |

sanskrit_iast: tad u hotāram abhibhāṣante yathā hotar abhayam asat tathā kurv iti |
meaning: तद् उ होतारम् अभिभाषन्ते यथा होतर् अभयम् असत् तथा कुर्व् इति |

sanskrit_iast: sampreṣitaḥ purarcaḥ pratipadanād dakṣiṇasya pādasya prapadena pratyañcaṃl lokam apāsyati |
meaning: सम्प्रेषितः पुरर्चः प्रतिपदनाद् दक्षिणस्य पादस्य प्रपदेन प्रत्यञ्चंल् लोकम् अपास्यति |

sanskrit_iast: apeto janyam bhayam anya janyam ca vṛtrahan |
meaning: अपेतो जन्यम् भयम् अन्य जन्यम् च वृत्रहन् |

sanskrit_iast: tata u ha tasmā ardhāya abhayam bhavati |
meaning: तत उ ह तस्मा अर्धाय अभयम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: sa prān yan dakṣiṇasya havir dhānasya uttaram vartma upaniśrayīta |
meaning: स प्रान् यन् दक्षिणस्य हविर् धानस्य उत्तरम् वर्त्म उपनिश्रयीत |

sanskrit_iast: ayam vai loko dakṣiṇam havir dhānam |
meaning: अयम् वै लोको दक्षिणम् हविर् धानम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmāt paridhāya dakṣiṇam bāhum anvāvṛtya vācam yamo yathetam pratyetya |
meaning: तस्मात् परिधाय दक्षिणम् बाहुम् अन्वावृत्य वाचम् यमो यथेतम् प्रत्येत्य |

sanskrit_iast: tat sthitvā atra ca agni praharaṇe ca |
meaning: तत् स्थित्वा अत्र च अग्नि प्रहरणे च |

text: Agni is the holy power; Soma the lordly power; in that on the fast day they lead forward Agni and Soma, verily thus by the holy power and by the lordly power, they smite away the evil of the sacrificer. They say ‘Sitting the Hotṛ should recite this first (verse); all beings move forward with the leading forward of Soma, the king; in that sitting the Hotṛ recites this Ṛc, verily thus he restrains all beings in their due place.’ ‘Do thou pour forth, O god, for the first the father’, this verse for Savitṛ he first recites, to secure instigation by Savitṛ; to one instigated by Savitṛ no possible injury happens; (verily it serves) to secure freedom from injury. (With the verse), ‘Rise up, O Brahmaṇaspati’, he causes (the fire) to be removed; (with the verse), ‘Let Brahmaṇaspati move forward’ he leads (it) forward. He recites two appropriate (verses) for Brahmaṇaspati; Brahmaṇaspati is the holy power; verily thus by the holy power he makes the sacrifice successful. ‘The Hotṛ, the god, the immortal’ and ‘To thee, O Agni, day and day’, these sets of three verses for Agni alone he recites, for Agni they take first. These contain (the word) ‘go’, for he praises Agni as he is taken. When he comes to (the words), ‘The embryo of beings I take up’, then he should think of an embryo for one who desires an embryo; she obtains an embryo. In the Agnīdh's altar they put down the fire. When the Adhvaryu offers the libation, then should he repeat this (verse), ‘O Agni, rejoice; be glad in this prayer.’ This is the offering verse for this (libation), being appropriate as containing the words ‘rejoice’ and ‘be glad’.

sanskrit_iast: brahma kṣatrābhyām eva tad yajamānasya pāpmānam apaghnanti |
meaning: ब्रह्म क्षत्राभ्याम् एव तद् यजमानस्य पाप्मानम् अपघ्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tad u vā āhur āsīna eva hotā etām prathamām anubrūyāt |
meaning: तद् उ वा आहुर् आसीन एव होता एताम् प्रथमाम् अनुब्रूयात् |

sanskrit_iast: sarvāṇi ha vai bhūtāni somam rājānam praṇīyamānam anu pracyavante |
meaning: सर्वाणि ह वै भूतानि सोमम् राजानम् प्रणीयमानम् अनु प्रच्यवन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: tad yad āsīno hotā etām ṛcam anvāha |
meaning: तद् यद् आसीनो होता एताम् ऋचम् अन्वाह |

sanskrit_iast: tad eva sarvāṇi bhūtāni yathā āyatanam niyacchati iti |
meaning: तद् एव सर्वाणि भूतानि यथा आयतनम् नियच्छति इति |

sanskrit_iast: sāvīr hi deva prathamāya pitra iti sāvitrīm prathamām anvāha |
meaning: सावीर् हि देव प्रथमाय पित्र इति सावित्रीम् प्रथमाम् अन्वाह |

sanskrit_iast: savitṛ prasūtasya ha vai na kācana riṣṭir bhavaty ariṣṭyai |
meaning: सवितृ प्रसूतस्य ह वै न काचन रिष्टिर् भवत्य् अरिष्ट्यै |

sanskrit_iast: uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspata ity utthāpayati praitu brahmaṇaspatir iti praṇayati brāhmaṇaspatye abhirūpe anvāha |
meaning: उत्तिष्ठ ब्रह्मणस्पत इत्य् उत्थापयति प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिर् इति प्रणयति ब्राह्मणस्पत्ये अभिरूपे अन्वाह |

sanskrit_iast: hotā devo amartya upa tvā agne dive diva iti kevala āgneyau tṛcāv anvāha |
meaning: होता देवो अमर्त्य उप त्वा अग्ने दिवे दिव इति केवल आग्नेयौ तृचाव् अन्वाह |

sanskrit_iast: sa yatra upādhigacched bhūtānām garbham ādadha iti |
meaning: स यत्र उपाधिगच्छेद् भूतानाम् गर्भम् आदध इति |

sanskrit_iast: tām sampraty etām anubrūyād agne juṣasva pati harya tad vaca iti |
meaning: ताम् सम्प्रत्य् एताम् अनुब्रूयाद् अग्ने जुषस्व पति हर्य तद् वच इति |

sanskrit_iast: tasyā eva eṣā yājyā juṣasva prati haryā ity abhirūpā |
meaning: तस्या एव एषा याज्या जुषस्व प्रति हर्या इत्य् अभिरूपा |

text: Then they lead Soma alone eastwards; therefore he recites verses for Soma alone, 'Soma goeth, who knoweth the way.' Reciting the three verses, which contain a reference to 'going', he follows on. There the Adhvaryu offers again a libation in the Āhavanīya; then he should recite this (verse ), 'To the dear one, the strengthener.' This is the offering verse for this (libation), being appropriate as containing (the word) 'increasing the libation'. Then they cause the king to enter by the eastern door; as he is made to enter, he recites for him made to enter (the verse ), 'This of him King Varuṇa, this the Aśvins,' which is appropriate in having (the words), 'This stall doth Viṣṇu, with his companions, reveal.' For him when he has arrived he recites (the verse ) 'Within hast thou come forward; thou shalt be Aditi', which contains (the word) 'forward'. He praises him when seated with the verses containing (the word) 'sit', 'Like an eagle his nest, the seat wrought with devotion', 'Thee, lord of hosts, we invoke', and 'He hath established the sky, the Asura, all-knower.' He concludes with (a verse ) containing a benediction, 'Do thou welcome Varuṇa the great.' He recites appropriate verses; what in the sacrifice is appropriate, that is perfect; verily (they serve) for the perfection of the sacrifice. He recites twenty verses; they make up the Virāj; Soma is connected with the Virāj; the Virāj is food; Soma is food; thus by food he causes proper food to abound. (He recites) the first thrice and the last thrice; they make up twenty-four; the half months of the year are twenty-four; verily (they serve) to obtain the year. If they cause the king to enter by the eastern door thus is it; but if they (cause him to enter) by the western (door) the Hotṛ should follow after (thinking) 'The Hotṛ is the body of the sacrificer; Soma is the breath; let me not sever the body from the breath.' He concludes standing facing south to the north (of the oblation holder); Soma the king is glory; proper food from thence onwards he confers and glory upon himself.

sanskrit_iast: somo jigāti gātuvid iti itavat tṛcam anubruvann anusameti |
meaning: सोमो जिगाति गातुविद् इति इतवत् तृचम् अनुब्रुवन्न् अनुसमेति |

sanskrit_iast: atha adhvaryur āhavanīye punar āhutim juhoti |
meaning: अथ अध्वर्युर् आहवनीये पुनर् आहुतिम् जुहोति |

sanskrit_iast: tām sampraty etām anubrūyād upa priyam panipnatam iti |
meaning: ताम् सम्प्रत्य् एताम् अनुब्रूयाद् उप प्रियम् पनिप्नतम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tasyā eva eṣā yājyā āhutī vṛdham ity abhirūpā |
meaning: तस्या एव एषा याज्या आहुती वृधम् इत्य् अभिरूपा |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin prapādyamāne tam asya rājā varuṇas tam aśvinā iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् प्रपाद्यमाने तम् अस्य राजा वरुणस् तम् अश्विना इति |

sanskrit_iast: vrajam ca viṣṇuḥ sakhivām aporṇuta ity abhirūpām prapādyamānāya anvāha |
meaning: व्रजम् च विष्णुः सखिवाम् अपोर्णुत इत्य् अभिरूपाम् प्रपाद्यमानाय अन्वाह |

sanskrit_iast: antaś ca prāgā aditir bhavāsi iti prapannavatīm prapannāya |
meaning: अन्तश् च प्रागा अदितिर् भवासि इति प्रपन्नवतीम् प्रपन्नाय |

sanskrit_iast: śyeno na yonim sadanam dhiyā kṛtam gaṇānām tvā gaṇa patim havāmahe astabhnād dyām asuro viśva devā iti sannavatībhiḥ sannam anustauti |
meaning: श्येनो न योनिम् सदनम् धिया कृतम् गणानाम् त्वा गण पतिम् हवामहे अस्तभ्नाद् द्याम् असुरो विश्व देवा इति सन्नवतीभिः सन्नम् अनुस्तौति |

sanskrit_iast: evā vandasva varuṇam bṛhantam ity āśīrvatyā paridadhāti |
meaning: एवा वन्दस्व वरुणम् बृहन्तम् इत्य् आशीर्वत्या परिदधाति |

sanskrit_iast: yad yajñe abhirūpam tat samṛddham yajñasya eva samṛddhyai |
meaning: यद् यज्ञे अभिरूपम् तत् समृद्धम् यज्ञस्य एव समृद्ध्यै |

sanskrit_iast: triḥ prathamayā triru uttamayā caturviṃśatiḥ sampadyante |
meaning: त्रिः प्रथमया त्रिरु उत्तमया चतुर्विंशतिः सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: evam nu yadi pūrvayā dvārā rājānam prapādayeyuḥ |
meaning: एवम् नु यदि पूर्वया द्वारा राजानम् प्रपादयेयुः |

sanskrit_iast: na it prāṇād ātmānam apādadhāni iti |
meaning: न इत् प्राणाद् आत्मानम् अपादधानि इति |

sanskrit_iast: yaśo vai somo rājā anna adyam |
meaning: यशो वै सोमो राजा अन्न अद्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: amuta eva tad arvāg ātman yaśo dhatte yaśo dhatte |
meaning: अमुत एव तद् अर्वाग् आत्मन् यशो धत्ते यशो धत्ते |

text: The sacrificial post is a thunderbolt. In that they erect the post on the fast day, verily thus with a thunderbolt they smite away the evil of the sacrificer. It should not be bent, as it were, for to be bent in the stomach is the symbol of one hungry. Again it should be turned towards the Āhavanīya; that is the symbol of one well fed; his wives are not like to be hungry, who makes a post so formed. One of Palāśa wood he should make who desires splendour, of Bilva wood he who desires proper food, and of Khadira he who desires heaven. It should be three cubits with the symbol of these worlds, four cubits with the symbol of cattle, five cubits with the symbol of the Paṅkti, six cubits with the symbol of the seasons, seven cubits with the symbol of the metres, eight cubits with the symbol of the Gāyatrī, nine cubits with the symbol of the Bṛhatī, ten cubits with the symbol of the Virāj, eleven cubits with the symbol of the Triṣṭubh, twelve cubits with the symbol of the Jagatī. These measures are suitable forms for the post. One suitable form should he produce and make the post. They say, however, ‘One should not measure the post; let it be unmeasured; the measured by the measured one wins; the unmeasured by the unmeasured; (therefore it serves) to win the incommensurable.’ ‘Both for the post and the altar (he should choose) the size which he considers in his mind suitable’, (Kauṣītaki) used to say. Mind is Prajāpati; Prajāpati is the sacrifice; the sacrifice itself rejoices in the sacrifice when mind in mind. The post in the Vājapeya alone is determined as of seventeen cubits. It is placed in with eight corners, for the attainment of all desires. Then they wash it; thus what of it has here been harshly treated as it were with the axe and hewn as it were, that of it verily he makes whole, that he heals. Then they anoint it; thus the waters which are in man, these they place in it; well anointed himself should the sacrificer make it; so does the sacrificer become not rough as it were.

sanskrit_iast: vajreṇa eva tad yajamānasya pāpmānam apaghnanti |
meaning: वज्रेण एव तद् यजमानस्य पाप्मानम् अपघ्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: anaśanāyukā ha asya bhāryā bhavanti ya evam rūpam yūpam kurute |
meaning: अनशनायुका ह अस्य भार्या भवन्ति य एवम् रूपम् यूपम् कुरुते |

sanskrit_iast: tāsām ekām sampadam abhisampādya yūpam kurvīta |
meaning: तासाम् एकाम् सम्पदम् अभिसम्पाद्य यूपम् कुर्वीत |

sanskrit_iast: tad u vā āhur na mined yūpam |
meaning: तद् उ वा आहुर् न मिनेद् यूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: yatra eva manasā velām manyate tat kurvīta |
meaning: यत्र एव मनसा वेलाम् मन्यते तत् कुर्वीत |

sanskrit_iast: tad yūpasya ca vedeś ca iti ha sma āha |
meaning: तद् यूपस्य च वेदेश् च इति ह स्म आह |

sanskrit_iast: svayam vai tad yajño yajñasya juṣate |
meaning: स्वयम् वै तद् यज्ञो यज्ञस्य जुषते |

sanskrit_iast: vājapeya yūpa eva avadhṛtaḥ saptadaśa aratniḥ |
meaning: वाजपेय यूप एव अवधृतः सप्तदश अरत्निः |

sanskrit_iast: tad yad eva idam paraśunā krūrī kṛta iva taṣṭa iva bhavati |
meaning: तद् यद् एव इदम् परशुना क्रूरी कृत इव तष्ट इव भवति |

sanskrit_iast: tad eva asya etad āpyāyayati tad bhiṣajyati |
meaning: तद् एव अस्य एतद् आप्याययति तद् भिषज्यति |

sanskrit_iast: tad yā eva imāḥ puruṣaḥ āpaḥ |
meaning: तद् या एव इमाः पुरुषः आपः |

sanskrit_iast: tathā ha yajamāno arūkṣa iva bhavati |
meaning: तथा ह यजमानो अरूक्ष इव भवति |

sanskrit_iast: añjanti tvām adhvare devayanta ity aktavatīm abhirūpām ajyamānāya anvāha |
meaning: अञ्जन्ति त्वाम् अध्वरे देवयन्त इत्य् अक्तवतीम् अभिरूपाम् अज्यमानाय अन्वाह |
text:
For it when being anointed he recites the appropriate (verse) containing the word ‘anoint’, ‘They anoint thee at the sacrifice, pious men’. For it when being placed erect he recites (verses) containing the words ‘erect’ and ‘up’, ‘Rise erect, O lord of the forest’, ‘Rising before the kindled’, ‘Born he is born in the fairness of the days’, ‘Aloft to our aid’, and ‘Aloft do thou guard us from tribulation with thy ray’. He concludes with (a verse) containing the word ‘covered round’, ‘The youth, well clad, covered round, hath come.’ He recites appropriate verses; what in the sacrifice is appropriate, that is perfect; verily (it serves) for the perfection of the sacrifice. He recites seven (verses); the metres are seven; verily (they serve) to obtain all the metres. (He recites) the first thrice and the last thrice; they make up eleven; the Triṣṭubh has eleven syllables; cattle are connected with the Triṣṭubh; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. So is (the ceremony) in the case of one victim and one post. If at one post they should deal with eleven victims, then in the case of each victim the Adhvaryu gives directions, in the case of each victim there is the same concluding (verse), ‘The youth, well clad, covered round, hath come’; it is (recited) for it as it is being covered round. ‘So in the case of one post, but how in the case of eleven posts?’ (they ask). The same seven verses he should recite for them up to ten; in the case of the last post they set up he should apply the remainder of the hymn, before the Pragātha, ‘Then like horns of the horned they appeared.’ Verily all he accompanies; there is the same concluding verse, ‘The youth, well clad, covered round, hath come’; it is (recited) for it as it is being covered round. ‘It’, they say, ‘he should throw along; the post is the sacrificer; the Āhavanīya is the world of heaven; verily thus he makes him go to the world of heaven; that is heavenly’. But they say ‘Let it stand; in that this is the place of the splinter of the post, the Asuras and the Rakṣases could drink after if this were not so; therefore this (post) should stand erect as a thunderbolt on the place of sacrifice, smiting away the Asuras and the Rakṣases, and repressing them, and also guarding the sacrifice and the sacrificer.’ One is suited for the post, one is rich in wood, one is fitted for a hole. That which has its rind downwards, that is fitted for a hole; such a one he should not wish; that which has its rind pointing up, and is rich in wood,
is that connected with man; he may use it if he desires; the tree, whose rind grows from left to right in accord with the course of the sun, is that suited for the post and is heavenly. (The tree), which stands alone, unrivalled, or is covered up to the root with shoots, is not bare; it is connected with cattle; it one desiring cattle should use.

sanskrit_iast: ucchrayasva vanaspate samiddhasya śrayamāṇaḥ purastāj jāto jāyate sudinatve ahnām ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaya ūrdhvo naḥ pāhy aṃhaso ketunā ity ucchritavatīś ca udvatīś ca ucchrīyamāṇāya anvāha |
meaning: उच्छ्रयस्व वनस्पते समिद्धस्य श्रयमाणः पुरस्ताज् जातो जायते सुदिनत्वे अह्नाम् ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु ण ऊतय ऊर्ध्वो नः पाह्य् अंहसो केतुना इत्य् उच्छ्रितवतीश् च उद्वतीश् च उच्छ्रीयमाणाय अन्वाह |

sanskrit_iast: yuvā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgād iti parivītavatyā paridadhāti |
meaning: युवा सुवासाः परिवीत आगाद् इति परिवीतवत्या परिदधाति |

sanskrit_iast: yad yajñe abhirūpam tat samṛddham yajñasya eva samṛddhyai |
meaning: यद् यज्ञे अभिरूपम् तत् समृद्धम् यज्ञस्य एव समृद्ध्यै |

sanskrit_iast: triḥ prathamayā trir uttamayā ekādaśa sampadyante |
meaning: त्रिः प्रथमया त्रिर् उत्तमया एकादश सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: iti nv eka yūpa eka paśau ca |
meaning: इति न्व् एक यूप एक पशौ च |

sanskrit_iast: atha yady eka yūpa ekādaśinīm ālabheran |
meaning: अथ यद्य् एक यूप एकादशिनीम् आलभेरन् |

sanskrit_iast: paśau paśāv eva yuvā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgād iti sā eva paridhānīyā sā parivīyamāṇāya |
meaning: पशौ पशाव् एव युवा सुवासाः परिवीत आगाद् इति सा एव परिधानीया सा परिवीयमाणाय |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin yat sūktasya pariśiṣyeta tad anuvartayet |
meaning: तस्मिन् यत् सूक्तस्य परिशिष्येत तद् अनुवर्तयेत् |

sanskrit_iast: śṛṅgāṇi iva it śṛṅgiṇām sam dadṛśra iti sarvān eva abhivadati |
meaning: शृङ्गाणि इव इत् शृङ्गिणाम् सम् ददृश्र इति सर्वान् एव अभिवदति |

sanskrit_iast: yuvā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgād iti sā eva paridhānīyā sā parivīyamāṇāya |
meaning: युवा सुवासाः परिवीत आगाद् इति सा एव परिधानीया सा परिवीयमाणाय |

sanskrit_iast: tad eva enam svargaṃl lokam gamayati |
meaning: तद् एव एनम् स्वर्गंल् लोकम् गमयति |

sanskrit_iast: tad u vā āhus tiṣṭhed eva |
meaning: तद् उ वा आहुस् तिष्ठेद् एव |

sanskrit_iast: yad idam āsthānam svarostata īśvarā yadi na asura rakṣasāny anvavapātoḥ |
meaning: यद् इदम् आस्थानम् स्वरोस्तत ईश्वरा यदि न असुर रक्षसान्य् अन्ववपातोः |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād eṣa vajra udyato yajña vāstau tiṣṭhed eva asura rakṣasāny apaghnann apabādhamāno yajñam caiva yajamānam ca abhigopāyann iti |
meaning: तस्माद् एष वज्र उद्यतो यज्ञ वास्तौ तिष्ठेद् एव असुर रक्षसान्य् अपघ्नन्न् अपबाधमानो यज्ञम् चैव यजमानम् च अभिगोपायन्न् इति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yūpya keo dravya eko gatya ekaḥ |
meaning: अथ यूप्य केओ द्रव्य एको गत्य एकः |

sanskrit_iast: atha ya ūrdhva vakalo dravyaḥ sa mānuṣaḥ |
meaning: अथ य ऊर्ध्व वकलो द्रव्यः स मानुषः |

sanskrit_iast: atha yasya prasavy ādityasya āvṛtam anvāvṛttā vakalāḥ |
meaning: अथ यस्य प्रसव्य् आदित्यस्य आवृतम् अन्वावृत्ता वकलाः |

sanskrit_iast: sa yūpyaḥ sa svargyam ekastho bhrātṛvyaḥ |
meaning: स यूप्यः स स्वर्ग्यम् एकस्थो भ्रातृव्यः |

sanskrit_iast: yo vā anuvṛtaḥ palāśair āmūlāt syāt |
meaning: यो वा अनुवृतः पलाशैर् आमूलात् स्यात् |

sanskrit_iast: agnīṣomayor vā eṣa āsyam āpadyate yo dīkṣate |
meaning: अग्नीषोमयोर् वा एष आस्यम् आपद्यते यो दीक्षते |
text:
He who is consecrated enters the jaws of Agni and Soma; in that on the fast day he offers a victim to Agni and Soma, this is a buying off of himself; with this buying off of himself he becomes free from debt and then sacrifices. So he should not eat of it, for it is man in counterfeit. But they say 'Every oblation is a buying off of oneself; he would not eat of any oblation, if he were not willing to eat because it is a buying off of oneself. Therefore at will should one eat.' Agni and Soma are day and night; in that by day they proceed with (the offering of) the omentum, thereby is day pleased. In that the offering to Agni is carried out during the night, thereby is the night as connected with Soma pleased. 'That is the final setting free of day and night' (they say); by the sacrifice are day and night set free; they do not obtain him, who knowing thus offers this victim. They say 'It should be two coloured; white and black with the symbols of day and night; or white and red with the symbols of Agni and Soma.' There are eleven fore-offerings and eleven after-offerings, and eleven supplementary offerings; these are thirty-three; all the gods are thirty-three; verily (they serve) to delight all the gods. The fore-offerings are expirations, the after-offerings inspirations; therefore are they alike, for the expirations and the inspirations are similar. They say 'Why does he sacrifice with a Ṛc in the fore-offerings and with the opening words only in the after-offerings?' 'The fore-offerings are seed to be poured, the after-offerings are seed to be deposited; therefore with a Ṛc he sacrifices in the fore-offerings, and with the opening words in the after-offerings.' In that he says the last whole, verily thus he places the sacrificer in the world of heaven. He invokes with the Āprī verses; with the whole self, with the whole mind, he gathers together the sacrifice, who sacrifices. The self of him becomes empty as it were; he fills it up for him with these (verses). In that he fills it up, therefore are they
called Āprīs (fillers). He surrounds the animal with fire, to smite away the Rakṣases; Agni is the smiter away of the Rakṣases; he carries the fire round thrice from left to right; that is as if Agni were to put three forts. Therefore, ‘Go round again’ he should say to the Agnīdh, if he desire of a man, ‘May he not fall away.’

sanskrit_iast: tad yad upavasathe agnīṣomīyam paśum ālabhate |
meaning: तद् यद् उपवसथे अग्नीषोमीयम् पशुम् आलभते |

sanskrit_iast: ātma niṣkriyaṇo ha eva asya eṣa tena ātmānam niṣkrīṇīya anṛṇo bhūtvā atha yajate |
meaning: आत्म निष्क्रियणो ह एव अस्य एष तेन आत्मानम् निष्क्रीणीय अनृणो भूत्वा अथ यजते |

sanskrit_iast: tad u vā āhur havir havir vā ātma niṣkrayaṇam |
meaning: तद् उ वा आहुर् हविर् हविर् वा आत्म निष्क्रयणम् |

sanskrit_iast: haviṣo haviṣi eva sa tarhi na aśnīyāt |
meaning: हविषो हविषि एव स तर्हि न अश्नीयात् |

sanskrit_iast: ya ātma niṣkrayaṇam iti na aśnīyāt |
meaning: य आत्म निष्क्रयणम् इति न अश्नीयात् |

sanskrit_iast: ya evam vidvān etam paśum ālbhate |
meaning: य एवम् विद्वान् एतम् पशुम् आल्भते |

sanskrit_iast: tam āhur dvirūpaḥ syāt śuklam ca kṛṣṇam ca aho rātrayo rūpeṇa iti |
meaning: तम् आहुर् द्विरूपः स्यात् शुक्लम् च कृष्णम् च अहो रात्रयो रूपेण इति |

sanskrit_iast: śuklam vā ca lohitam c agnīṣomayo rūpeṇa iti |
meaning: शुक्लम् वा च लोहितम् च् अग्नीषोमयो रूपेण इति |

sanskrit_iast: tasya ekādaśa prayājā ekādaśa anuyājā ekādaśa upayajaḥ |
meaning: तस्य एकादश प्रयाजा एकादश अनुयाजा एकादश उपयजः |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhuḥ kasmād ṛcā prayājeṣu yajati pratīkair anuyājeṣv iti |
meaning: तद् आहुः कस्माद् ऋचा प्रयाजेषु यजति प्रतीकैर् अनुयाजेष्व् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād ṛcā prayājeṣu yajati pratīkair anuyājeṣv iti |
meaning: तस्माद् ऋचा प्रयाजेषु यजति प्रतीकैर् अनुयाजेष्व् इति |

sanskrit_iast: svarga eva tal loke yajamānam dadhāti |
meaning: स्वर्ग एव तल् लोके यजमानम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: sarveṇa ha vā eṣa ātmanā sarveṇa manasā yajñam sambharate yo yajate |
meaning: सर्वेण ह वा एष आत्मना सर्वेण मनसा यज्ञम् सम्भरते यो यजते |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā tisro agni puraḥ kuryād evam tat |
meaning: तद् यथा तिस्रो अग्नि पुरः कुर्याद् एवम् तत् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmāt punaḥ parīhi ity agnidham brūyāt |
meaning: तस्मात् पुनः परीहि इत्य् अग्निधम् ब्रूयात् |

sanskrit_iast: daivyāḥ śamitāra uta ca manuṣyā ārabhadhvam upanayata medhyā dura āśāsānā medhapatibhyām medham iti |
meaning: दैव्याः शमितार उत च मनुष्या आरभध्वम् उपनयत मेध्या दुर आशासाना मेधपतिभ्याम् मेधम् इति |
text: ‘O ye divine slayers and ye human make ready; bring (the victim) to the doors of the sacrifice, ordaining the sacrifice for the two lords of the sacrifice’; regarding this some say, ‘The lord of the sacrifice is the sacrificer.’ ‘What man (is the lord)?’ he should say, ‘the lord of the sacrifice is the deity only.’ ‘Its bends are twenty-six’, (he says); the bends are the ribs. On both sides of the blood he breathes down, (thinking) ‘The Rakṣases have the blood as their share; let me not set away the share of the gods with the share of the Rakṣases.’ It is the Adhrigu (formula). The instruction is ‘Do not mutilate the limbs.’ What is unspoilt is the oblation of the gods; they do not eat the oblation which is spoilt. Nine times does he breathe down in the Adhrigu; the breaths are nine; verily thus he places breaths in the sacrificer, to secure full life in this world and immortality in yonder world. Thrice he utters the concluding verse, to avoid non-recurrence. He says one before; the fathers are one as it were; the victim has as it were the fathers for its deity when it is being offered. In that he says three after, and among the gods (things are) thrice, verily thus he makes it have the gods as its deities, and renews it. Having concluded he mutters inaudibly, ‘Both and he that is not evil’; the slayer of the gods is not evil; to him verily does he hand it over, for he knows the gods.

sanskrit_iast: asṛg bhājanāni ha vai rakṣāṃsi bhavanti |
meaning: असृग् भाजनानि ह वै रक्षांसि भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: na id rakṣasām bhāgena daivam bhāgam prasajāni iti |
meaning: न इद् रक्षसाम् भागेन दैवम् भागम् प्रसजानि इति |

sanskrit_iast: yadd ha vā aduṣṭam tad devānām haviḥ |
meaning: यद्द् ह वा अदुष्टम् तद् देवानाम् हविः |

sanskrit_iast: na vai te duṣṭam havir adanti |
meaning: न वै ते दुष्टम् हविर् अदन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: pitṛ devatya iva vai paśur ālabhyamāno bhavati |
meaning: पितृ देवत्य इव वै पशुर् आलभ्यमानो भवति |

sanskrit_iast: deva devatyam eva enam tad ayāta yāmānam karoti |
meaning: देव देवत्यम् एव एनम् तद् अयात यामानम् करोति |

sanskrit_iast: paridhāya upāṃśu japaty ubhāv apāpaś ca iti |
meaning: परिधाय उपांशु जपत्य् उभाव् अपापश् च इति |

text:
Then he recites (the verses) accompanying the drops; verily with them he makes the drops suitable for Agni. These are the invitatory verses for them, these the offering verses. Therefore they are appropriate. Having proceeded with the (offering to the) calls of Hail! they proceed with the (offering of the) omentum; verily thus they make the fore-offerings sharers in the victim. He should not utter speech between the (offering to the) calls of Hail! and the (offering of the) omentum,
(thinking) ‘The calls of Hail! are the breaths; the omentum is the body; let me not separate the breaths and the body by anything.’ In that the invitatory verses of the victim for Agni and Soma are Anuṣṭubh verses, (it is because) the Anuṣṭubh is the Gāyatrī and the metre of Agni is the Gāyatrī; in that the offering verses are Triṣṭubh verses, it is because the Triṣṭubh is the metre of the lordly power, and Soma is the lordly power. Thus according to the metre he delights the two deities. During the offering of the victim a cake is offered; the cake is the sap of animals; verily thus he makes (the victim) full of sap and fit for sacrifice. Where a cake in connection with the victim is offered, the Sviṣṭakṛt of the cake (offering) is permanent; the Sviṣṭakṛt is Agni (the unmoved); therefore it becomes permanent. Having recited (a verse) of Viśvāmitra, as the invitatory verse for the cake Sviṣṭakṛt, he recites (a verse) of Viśvāmitra as the offering verse; the cake is the continuity of the sacrifice; Viśvāmitra is speech; by speech the sacrifice is continued.

sanskrit_iast: etā ha vā u teṣām puronuvākyā etā yājyāḥ |
meaning: एता ह वा उ तेषाम् पुरोनुवाक्या एता याज्याः |

sanskrit_iast: prayājān eva tat paśu bhājaḥ kurvanti |
meaning: प्रयाजान् एव तत् पशु भाजः कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: na svāhā kṛtīś ca vapām ca antareṇa vācam visṛjeta |
meaning: न स्वाहा कृतीश् च वपाम् च अन्तरेण वाचम् विसृजेत |

sanskrit_iast: na it prāṇāṃś ca ātmānam ca anyena antar dadhāti iti |
meaning: न इत् प्राणांश् च आत्मानम् च अन्येन अन्तर् दधाति इति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yad anuṣṭubho agnīṣomīyasya paśoḥ puronuvākyā bhavanti |
meaning: अथ यद् अनुष्टुभो अग्नीषोमीयस्य पशोः पुरोनुवाक्या भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atha vai paśum ālabhyamānam puroḍāśo anunirupyate |
meaning: अथ वै पशुम् आलभ्यमानम् पुरोडाशो अनुनिरुप्यते |

text:
Then he recites the Manotā. All the deities gather towards the victim as it is offered, (thinking) ‘He will utter my name; he will utter my name.’ The minds of all these are woven in the victim; these he delights herein; so it is not in vain that all these have assembled together. They say ‘Since the victims are offered to diverse deities, then why does he accompany that for Agni alone?’ ‘Three are the Manotās of the gods; Agni is the Manotā of the gods, for in him the minds of the gods are woven. Moreover, speech is the Manotā of the gods, for in it are their minds woven. Moreover, the cow is the Manotā of the gods, for in her are their minds woven. All the Manotās are Agni; in Agni the Manotās unite; therefore he accompanies that for Agni only’ (is the answer). They make up thirteen; thirteen are the cuttings of the victim; these he accompanies. (He recites) the first thrice and the last thrice; they make up seventeen; Prajāpati is seventeenfold; that rite is beneficial which is commensurate with Prajāpati. He recites seventeen kindling verses; Prajāpati is seventeenfold; that rite is beneficial which is
commensurate with Prajāpati. When the victim is offered, then the lord of the forest is unmoved; the lord of the forest is Agni, he bestows the oblation on the gods; therefore he becomes unmoved; he also has milk as his portion; so Agni becomes a sharer in all the oblations. They say ‘Since the gods possess the solid, then why does the lord of the forest possess the liquid as his share?’ ‘The gods shared the solid of the sacrifice, the fathers the liquid; the victim has, as it were, the fathers as its deities; the milk has the fathers as its deities; therefore is it’, he should reply. They say ‘Why in the Soma sacrifice do they offer two libations for the choosing (of priests), and not in the Haviryajña?’ ‘The Haviryajña is an incomplete sacrifice; the Soma sacrifice is a complete sacrifice; therefore at the Soma sacrifice alone do they offer the two libations for the choosing and not at the Haviryajña’ (is the answer). He offers in the first case with the call of Hail! ‘Acceptable to speech may I become, acceptable to the lord of speech; O divine speech, what of thy speech is sweetest, in that us may he to-day place; hail to Sarasvatī.’ Thus he releases speech; therefore hence onwards speech being released supports the sacrifice; with the mind (he accompanies) the second (libation); for by mind is mind delighted.

sanskrit_iast: sarvā ha vai devatāḥ paśum ālabhyamānam upasaṃgacchante mama nāma grahīṣyati mama nāma grahīṣyati iti |
meaning: सर्वा ह वै देवताः पशुम् आलभ्यमानम् उपसंगच्छन्ते मम नाम ग्रहीष्यति मम नाम ग्रहीष्यति इति |

sanskrit_iast: tāsām sarvāsām paśāv eva manāṃsy otāni bhavanti |
meaning: तासाम् सर्वासाम् पशाव् एव मनांस्य् ओतानि भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tathā ha āsām sarvāsām amoghāya eva upasametam bhavati |
meaning: तथा ह आसाम् सर्वासाम् अमोघाय एव उपसमेतम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yan nānā devatāḥ paśava ālabhyante atha kasmād āgneyam eva anvāha iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यन् नाना देवताः पशव आलभ्यन्ते अथ कस्माद् आग्नेयम् एव अन्वाह इति |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin hy eṣām manāṃsy otāni bhavanti |
meaning: तस्मिन् ह्य् एषाम् मनांस्य् ओतानि भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tasyām hy eṣām manāṃsy otāni bhavanti |
meaning: तस्याम् ह्य् एषाम् मनांस्य् ओतानि भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tasyām hy eṣām manāṃsy otāni bhavanti |
meaning: तस्याम् ह्य् एषाम् मनांस्य् ओतानि भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: triḥ prathamayā trir uttamayā saptadaśa sampadyante |
meaning: त्रिः प्रथमया त्रिर् उत्तमया सप्तदश सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā ārdhnukam karma yat prajāpati sammitam |
meaning: एतद् वा आर्ध्नुकम् कर्म यत् प्रजापति सम्मितम् |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā ārdhnukam karma yat prajāpati sammitam |
meaning: एतद् वा आर्ध्नुकम् कर्म यत् प्रजापति सम्मितम् |

sanskrit_iast: atra agniḥ sarveṣu havihṣu bhāgī bhavati |
meaning: अत्र अग्निः सर्वेषु हविह्षु भागी भवति |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad dhāma bhājo devā atha kasmāt pātho bhāg vanaspatir iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् धाम भाजो देवा अथ कस्मात् पाथो भाग् वनस्पतिर् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhuḥ kasmāt saumya eva adhvare pravṛta āhutī juhvati na havir yajña iti |
meaning: तद् आहुः कस्मात् सौम्य एव अध्वरे प्रवृत आहुती जुह्वति न हविर् यज्ञ इति |

sanskrit_iast: akṛtsnā eva vā eṣā deva yajyā yadd havir yajñaḥ |
meaning: अकृत्स्ना एव वा एषा देव यज्या यद्द् हविर् यज्ञः |

sanskrit_iast: atha eṣā eva kṛtsnā deva yajñā yat saumyo adhvaraḥ |
meaning: अथ एषा एव कृत्स्ना देव यज्ञा यत् सौम्यो अध्वरः |

sanskrit_iast: tasmāt saumya eva adhvare pravṛta āhutī juhvati na havir yajña iti |
meaning: तस्मात् सौम्य एव अध्वरे प्रवृत आहुती जुह्वति न हविर् यज्ञ इति |

sanskrit_iast: juṣṭo vāco bhūyāsam juṣṭo vācaspater devi vāk |
meaning: जुष्टो वाचो भूयासम् जुष्टो वाचस्पतेर् देवि वाक् |

sanskrit_iast: yat te vāco madhumattamam tasmin no adya dhāḥ svāhā sarasvatyā iti purastāt svāhā kāreṇa juhoti |
meaning: यत् ते वाचो मधुमत्तमम् तस्मिन् नो अद्य धाः स्वाहा सरस्वत्या इति पुरस्तात् स्वाहा कारेण जुहोति |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād vāg ata ūrdhva utsṛṣṭā yajñam vahati |
meaning: तस्माद् वाग् अत ऊर्ध्व उत्सृष्टा यज्ञम् वहति |

sanskrit_iast: manahā hi manaḥ prītam manaḥ prītam |
meaning: मनहा हि मनः प्रीतम् मनः प्रीतम् |

text:
Next comes the morning litany. In that he recites it in the morning, that is why the morning litany has its name. In that he mutters the formulae of recourse, in that he offers the libations, verily thus he produces a benediction. After uttering the sound hiṅ he recites the morning litany; the sound hiṅ is a thunderbolt; verily thus with a thunderbolt he smites the evil of the sacrificer. He should recite aloud in a clear tone. The clear is the one part of speech which is not infested by evil; therefore in a clear tone should he recite, to smite away the evil of the sacrificer. By half verses should he recite; these worlds are com-
mensurate with the Ṛc; the first half verse is this world, the second yonder world; what is between the two half verses is the atmosphere here. In that he recites by half verses, verily thus he makes the sacrificer to prosper with these worlds; verily thus he places the sacrificer in these worlds.

sanskrit_iast: atha yat prapado japati yad āhutīr juhoti |
meaning: अथ यत् प्रपदो जपति यद् आहुतीर् जुहोति |

sanskrit_iast: vajreṇa eva tad yajamānasya pāpmānam hanti |
meaning: वज्रेण एव तद् यजमानस्य पाप्मानम् हन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: etadd ha vā ekam vāco ananvavasitam pāpmanā yan niruktam |
meaning: एतद्द् ह वा एकम् वाचो अनन्ववसितम् पाप्मना यन् निरुक्तम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha yad ardharcāv antareṇa tad idam antarikṣam |
meaning: अथ यद् अर्धर्चाव् अन्तरेण तद् इदम् अन्तरिक्षम् |

sanskrit_iast: ebhir eva tal lokair yajamānam samardhayati |
meaning: एभिर् एव तल् लोकैर् यजमानम् समर्धयति |

sanskrit_iast: eṣv eva tal lokeṣu yajamānam dadhāti |
meaning: एष्व् एव तल् लोकेषु यजमानम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: atha vai paṅkteḥ pañca padāni katham sārdharcaśo anuktā bhavati iti |
meaning: अथ वै पङ्क्तेः पञ्च पदानि कथम् सार्धर्चशो अनुक्ता भवति इति |
text: ‘Now the Paṅkti has five feet; how is it recited by half verses?’ (they ask). The syllable om is the third with the last two; so is it recited by half verses. He recites the service to Agni; thus he obtains this world; he recites that to Uṣas; verily thus he obtains the world of the atmosphere; he recites that to the Aśvins; verily thus he obtains yonder world. He recites a Gāyatrī; the Gāyatrī is the mouth; he recites an Anuṣṭubh; the Anuṣṭubh is speech; thus he places speech in the mouth; by the mouth he utters speech. He recites a Triṣṭubh; the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus he places might and strength in the sacrificer. He recites a Bṛhatī; the Bṛhatī is cows and horses; he recites a Uṣṇih; the Uṣṇih is sheep and goats; he recites a Jagatī; the Jagatī is might and strength; the Triṣṭubh is might and strength in the front; the Jagatī is might and strength behind;

sanskrit_iast: madhye bārhatāś ca auṣṇuhāś ca paśavaḥ |
meaning: मध्ये बार्हताश् च औष्णुहाश् च पशवः |
text: in the middle are cattle connected with the Bṛhatī and the Uṣṇih; verily thus with might and strength he encircles the cattle on both sides and confers them upon the sacrificer. So from the sacrificer cattle are not likely to depart. Just as in this world men eat cattle, just as they enjoy them, so in yonder world cattle eat men, so they enjoy them. He wins them here with the morning litany; won here they eat him not in yonder world, they enjoy him not in requital. Just as he eats them in this world, just as he enjoys them, so in yonder world he eats them, so he enjoys them. He recites a Paṅkti verse; the Paṅkti is a support; verily thus in all creatures he makes the sacrificer find support.

sanskrit_iast: balena eva tad vīryeṇa ubhayataḥ paśūn parigṛhya yajamāne dadhāti |
meaning: बलेन एव तद् वीर्येण उभयतः पशून् परिगृह्य यजमाने दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā ha vā asmiṃl loke manuṣyāḥ paśūn aśnanti |
meaning: तद् यथा ह वा अस्मिंल् लोके मनुष्याः पशून् अश्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: evam eva amuṣmiṃl loke paśavo manuṣyān aśnanti |
meaning: एवम् एव अमुष्मिंल् लोके पशवो मनुष्यान् अश्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: sa ya enān iha prātar anuvākena avarundhe |
meaning: स य एनान् इह प्रातर् अनुवाकेन अवरुन्धे |

sanskrit_iast: tam iha avaruddhā amuṣmiṃl loke na aśnanti |
meaning: तम् इह अवरुद्धा अमुष्मिंल् लोके न अश्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: yathā eva enān asmiṃl loke aśnāti |
meaning: यथा एव एनान् अस्मिंल् लोके अश्नाति |

sanskrit_iast: evam eva enān amuṣmiṃl loke aśnāti |
meaning: एवम् एव एनान् अमुष्मिंल् लोके अश्नाति |

sanskrit_iast: yathā eva enān asmiṃl loke aśnāti |
meaning: यथा एव एनान् अस्मिंल् लोके अश्नाति |

sanskrit_iast: evam eva enān amuṣmiṃl loke aśnāti |
meaning: एवम् एव एनान् अमुष्मिंल् लोके अश्नाति |

sanskrit_iast: sarveṣv eva tad bhūteṣu yajamānam pratiṣṭhāpayati |
meaning: सर्वेष्व् एव तद् भूतेषु यजमानम् प्रतिष्ठापयति |

sanskrit_iast: atha sarvā ha vai devatā hotāram prātar anuvākam anuvakṣyantam āśaṃsamānāḥ pratyupatiṣṭhante mayā pratipatsyate mayā pratipatsyata iti |
meaning: अथ सर्वा ह वै देवता होतारम् प्रातर् अनुवाकम् अनुवक्ष्यन्तम् आशंसमानाः प्रत्युपतिष्ठन्ते मया प्रतिपत्स्यते मया प्रतिपत्स्यत इति |
text:
Now all the gods resort to the Hotṛ as he is about to recite the morning litany, expecting ‘With me will he commence, with me will he commence.’ If he were to commence indicating one deity, he would fall a victim to the other deities. He commences with (a verse) not addressed (to one deity); thereby he does not fall a victim to any deity. (With the verse), ‘O waters, the rich ones’ he commences; all the deities are the waters; verily thus with all the deities he commences. ‘Advancing
forward up to the sacrifice’, (with this) he continues. ‘Up’ is the symbol of this world, ‘advancing’ is that of yonder (world); ‘up’ is the symbol of Agni, ‘advancing’ is that of yonder sun; so in all the formulae of recourse, in all the services to Agni, to Uṣas, and to the Aśvins the first utterance is the symbol of Agni, the second that of yonder sun. There are varied metres and between them pits as it were; these two are the strongest, the uninjured, the untroubled, deities; with these two he commences. With the one hymn should he mount; that is the symbol of mounting without falling into a pit and is heavenly. When there occurs in the one hymn a difference of authorship, then without taking breath should he step over. Breath is immortality; thus by immortality he passes by death; just as one steps over a pit by means of a beam or a roller, so with the Praṇava he steps over; the Praṇava is holy power; verily thus with the holy power he continues the holy power.

sanskrit_iast: sa ya ekām devatām ādiśya pratipadyeta |
meaning: स य एकाम् देवताम् आदिश्य प्रतिपद्येत |

sanskrit_iast: tena u na kasyai cana devatāyā āvṛścyate |
meaning: तेन उ न कस्यै चन देवताया आवृश्च्यते |

sanskrit_iast: āpo revatīḥ kṣayathā hi vasva iti pratipadyate |
meaning: आपो रेवतीः क्षयथा हि वस्व इति प्रतिपद्यते |

sanskrit_iast: upa iti tad asya lokasya rūpam |
meaning: उप इति तद् अस्य लोकस्य रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: evam eva sarvāsu pratipatsu sarveṣu ṛtuṣu |
meaning: एवम् एव सर्वासु प्रतिपत्सु सर्वेषु ऋतुषु |

sanskrit_iast: āgneya uṣasya āśvine pūrvā pūrvā eva vyāhṛtir agne rūpam |
meaning: आग्नेय उषस्य आश्विने पूर्वा पूर्वा एव व्याहृतिर् अग्ने रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha etad dve nānā chandāṃsy antareṇa kartā iva |
meaning: अथ एतद् द्वे नाना छन्दांस्य् अन्तरेण कर्ता इव |

sanskrit_iast: atha ete baliṣṭhe ariṣṭe anārte devate |
meaning: अथ एते बलिष्ठे अरिष्टे अनार्ते देवते |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā vaṃśena vā matyena vā kartam saṃkrāmed evam tat |
meaning: तद् यथा वंशेन वा मत्येन वा कर्तम् संक्रामेद् एवम् तत् |

text: The Praṇava should be uttered pure for those who desire offspring, with m at the end for those who desire support. ‘The Praṇava should have m at the end’, some say, but the rule is that it should be used pure. The Praṇava is investigated as to the fact that ‘Here it is pure, here it is in full form’. ‘The Praṇava should be pure in the middle of Śastras and of recitations’, Kauṣītaki used to say. This is continuity. It should have m at the end for the sake of a pause; the pause is a support; verily (it serves) for a support. Verily (the two serve) to obtain both desires. These are the carryings of the metres; they carry the subsequent over the preceding metre. No harm befalls him, who by the metre is carried over the metre. ‘When he is passing over, he should pierce with his mind as it were him whom he hates; in the fractures of the metre he either goes to ruin or is crushed,’ so he used to say. The Paṅktis at the end of the offerings he recites with the same endings; the end is sap, the metres are cattle; verily thus the metres end in sap; cattle ending as it were rejoice in the good grass. This is a Virāj with one syllable short; with one twice repeated it is exactly a Virāj; with one thrice repeated there is one over the Virāj.

sanskrit_iast: makāra antaḥ praṇavaḥ syād iti ha eka āhuḥ |
meaning: मकार अन्तः प्रणवः स्याद् इति ह एक आहुः |

sanskrit_iast: atha ata iha śuddha iha pūrṇa iti |
meaning: अथ अत इह शुद्ध इह पूर्ण इति |

sanskrit_iast: śuddha eva praṇavaḥ syāt śastra anuvacanayor madhya iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: शुद्ध एव प्रणवः स्यात् शस्त्र अनुवचनयोर् मध्य इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: eta u ha vai chandaḥ pravāhā avaram chandaḥ param chando atipravahanti |
meaning: एत उ ह वै छन्दः प्रवाहा अवरम् छन्दः परम् छन्दो अतिप्रवहन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tasya ārtir na asti chandasā chando atiproḍhasya |
meaning: तस्य आर्तिर् न अस्ति छन्दसा छन्दो अतिप्रोढस्य |

sanskrit_iast: tam manasā pra iva vidhyet chandasām kṛntatreṣu |
meaning: तम् मनसा प्र इव विध्येत् छन्दसाम् कृन्तत्रेषु |

sanskrit_iast: dravati vā sam vā śīryata iti ha sma āha |
meaning: द्रवति वा सम् वा शीर्यत इति ह स्म आह |

text: Three desires are there in the sacrifice, that in its completion, that in its deficiency, that in its superabundance. The complete part of the sacrifice is heavenly, the defective food, the superabundant serves for generation. Verily thus here the sacrificer obtains all desires. He concludes with (a verse) containing a benediction, 'Uṣas with her ruddy kine hath appeared'; verily thus he utters a benediction for cattle. So cattle are not likely to stray from the sacrificer. At this verse he lets out his voice; thus he announces him to the gods, 'He has been born,' for in it is he born. He repeats (the verse ) of two Padas, 'With this let us win the prize set by the gods'; the metres increasing by four (syllables) are cattle; (the verses) with two Padas are the sacrificer's metre; verily thus he places the sacrificer in command of cattle; man stands over cattle, as it were. He recites the thrice seven metres of the services; that makes up twenty-one; the fourfold Stoma, the highest of the Stomas, is the twenty-onefold; thus he obtains the highest of the Stomas. In that there are twenty-one, the months are twelve, the seasons five, these worlds three, and the sun yonder the twenty-first, verily thus he fixes the sacrificer in unity of world with him.

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ sampanne yo nyūne yo atirikte |
meaning: यः सम्पन्ने यो न्यूने यो अतिरिक्ते |

sanskrit_iast: yad vai yajñasya sampannam tat svargyam |
meaning: यद् वै यज्ञस्य सम्पन्नम् तत् स्वर्ग्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad atra eva yajamānaḥ sarvān kāmān āpnoti |
meaning: तद् अत्र एव यजमानः सर्वान् कामान् आप्नोति |

sanskrit_iast: abhūd eṣā ruśat paśur ity āśīrvatyā paridadhāti |
meaning: अभूद् एषा रुशत् पशुर् इत्य् आशीर्वत्या परिदधाति |

sanskrit_iast: tathā ha yajamānāt paśavo anutkrāmukā bhavanti |
meaning: तथा ह यजमानात् पशवो अनुत्क्रामुका भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: ayā vājam deva hitam sanema iti dvipadām abhyasyati |
meaning: अया वाजम् देव हितम् सनेम इति द्विपदाम् अभ्यस्यति |

sanskrit_iast: paśavo vā etāni catur uttarāṇi chandāṃsi |
meaning: पशवो वा एतानि चतुर् उत्तराणि छन्दांसि |

sanskrit_iast: adhiṣṭhāyām eva tat paśūnām yajamānam dadhāti |
meaning: अधिष्ठायाम् एव तत् पशूनाम् यजमानम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: adhi iva vai paśūn puruṣas tiṣṭhati |
meaning: अधि इव वै पशून् पुरुषस् तिष्ठति |

sanskrit_iast: dvādaśa māsāḥ pañca ṛtavas traya ime lokāḥ |
meaning: द्वादश मासाः पञ्च ऋतवस् त्रय इमे लोकाः |

sanskrit_iast: tena eva tas salokatāyām yajamānam adhyūhati |
meaning: तेन एव तस् सलोकतायाम् यजमानम् अध्यूहति |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad imā havir yajñasya vā paśor vā sāmidhenyo atha kāḥ saumyasya adhvarasya iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् इमा हविर् यज्ञस्य वा पशोर् वा सामिधेन्यो अथ काः सौम्यस्य अध्वरस्य इति |
text: They say 'Seeing that there are these kindling verses of the Haviryajña or the animal sacrifice, then what are those of the Soma sacrifice?' 'The morning litany', he should reply, for by the syllables of the others he seeks to obtain the year, by the Ṛcs here. A hundred only should he recite; man has a hundred (years of) life; verily thus he confers life upon him. He should recite a hundred and twenty; the days of a season are one hundred and twenty; thus he obtains the season; by the season the year, and the desires that are in the year. He should recite three hundred and sixty; the days of the year are three hundred and sixty; verily (they serve) to obtain the year. He should recite seven hundred and twenty; seven hundred and twenty are there of the days and nights of the year; thus he obtains the days and nights of the year. A thousand should he recite; a thousand is all, the morning litany is all; thus all he obtains with all, who knows thus. But Kauṣītaki used to say 'The morning litany is Prajāpati; Prajāpati is incommensurable; who ought to measure it?' This is the rule.

sanskrit_iast: akṣarair ha vā itarāsām saṃvatsaram upepsati |
meaning: अक्षरैर् ह वा इतरासाम् संवत्सरम् उपेप्सति |

sanskrit_iast: trīṇi vai ṣaṣṭi śatāni saṃvatsarasya ahnām |
meaning: त्रीणि वै षष्टि शतानि संवत्सरस्य अह्नाम् |

sanskrit_iast: sapta vai viśaṃti śatāni saṃvatsarasya aho rātrāṇām |
meaning: सप्त वै विशंति शतानि संवत्सरस्य अहो रात्राणाम् |

sanskrit_iast: tat sarveṇa sarvam āpnoti ya evam veda |
meaning: तत् सर्वेण सर्वम् आप्नोति य एवम् वेद |

sanskrit_iast: tad u ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: तद् उ ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yat sadasy ukthāni śasyante atha kasmādd havir dhānayoḥ prātar anuvākam anvāha iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यत् सदस्य् उक्थानि शस्यन्ते अथ कस्माद्द् हविर् धानयोः प्रातर् अनुवाकम् अन्वाह इति |
text:
They say 'Since the hymns are recited in the Sadas, then why does he recite the morning litany at the two oblation holders?' The two
oblation holders are the head of the sacrifice; the metres are the breaths; thus he places breath in the head. In the Sadas the hymns are recited; the Sadas is the stomach; the hymns are food; proper food is suited for the stomach. As is a cart, so is the sacrifice in counterfeit; as the corn, so the morning litany; as the vessels, so the hymns. If a man recites a little just as vessels come together (in a cart) with a little corn only, so his hymns come together, and on account of the coming together of the hymns tottering is liable to befall the sacrificer; therefore should he repeat many; thus he makes strong the hymns. (He says) 'Let the benediction of the sacrifice as successful be obtained for me'; the benediction of the sacrifice as successful is the sacrificer's. Three are these sets of a thousand in the sacrifice, the morning litany, the Aśvins' litany, and the great litany. He should begin when night is far advanced, before the emission of speech, before the time when cattle, men, and birds take up speech; speech these creatures make to swell, in that they lie silent (thinking) 'Let us first prosper on speech, swollen, not dissipated.' Between the morning litany and the Upāñśu and Antaryāma cups he should not set free his speech (thinking) 'The Upāñśu and Antaryāma cups are expiration and inspiration; the morning litany is speech; let me not separate expiration and inspiration and speech by any other thing.' Some begin with 'O waters, ye wealthy ones', after muttering (thinking) 'This is a yoking of the metres'; but the rule is 'He should not insert anything before the words 'O waters, ye wealthy ones', to prevent him being laid low.

sanskrit_iast: śiro vai yajñasya yadd havir dhāne |
meaning: शिरो वै यज्ञस्य यद्द् हविर् धाने |

sanskrit_iast: udara saceyam u vā anna adyam |
meaning: उदर सचेयम् उ वा अन्न अद्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā ha vā ana evam yajñaḥ pratimayā |
meaning: तद् यथा ह वा अन एवम् यज्ञः प्रतिमया |

sanskrit_iast: ukhānām anu samaram īśvaro yajamānam bhreṣonvetoḥ |
meaning: उखानाम् अनु समरम् ईश्वरो यजमानम् भ्रेषोन्वेतोः |

sanskrit_iast: tad u vā āhur bahum eva anubrūyāt |
meaning: तद् उ वा आहुर् बहुम् एव अनुब्रूयात् |

sanskrit_iast: yā yajñasya samṛddhasya āśīḥ sā me samṛdhyatām iti |
meaning: या यज्ञस्य समृद्धस्य आशीः सा मे समृध्यताम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: yā vai yajñasya samṛddhasya āśīḥ sā yajamānasya |
meaning: या वै यज्ञस्य समृद्धस्य आशीः सा यजमानस्य |

sanskrit_iast: atho trīṇi vā etāni sāhasrāṇy adhiyajñam |
meaning: अथो त्रीणि वा एतानि साहस्राण्य् अधियज्ञम् |

sanskrit_iast: prātar anuvāka āśvinam mahā vratam iti |
meaning: प्रातर् अनुवाक आश्विनम् महा व्रतम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: etad uktham mahā rātra upākuryāt purā vāco visargāt |
meaning: एतद् उक्थम् महा रात्र उपाकुर्यात् पुरा वाचो विसर्गात् |

sanskrit_iast: yatra etat paśavo manuṣyā vayāṃsi iti vācam vyālabhante purā tataḥ |
meaning: यत्र एतत् पशवो मनुष्या वयांसि इति वाचम् व्यालभन्ते पुरा ततः |

sanskrit_iast: āpīnām vācam avyāsiktām prathamata ṛdhnavāni iti |
meaning: आपीनाम् वाचम् अव्यासिक्ताम् प्रथमत ऋध्नवानि इति |

sanskrit_iast: na prātar anuvākam ca upāṃśv antaryāmau ca antareṇa vācam visṛjate |
meaning: न प्रातर् अनुवाकम् च उपांश्व् अन्तर्यामौ च अन्तरेण वाचम् विसृजते |

sanskrit_iast: na it prāṇa apānau ca vācam ca anyena antar dadhāti iti |
meaning: न इत् प्राण अपानौ च वाचम् च अन्येन अन्तर् दधाति इति |

sanskrit_iast: tadd ha eke kaś chandasām yogam āveda dhīra iti japitvā atha āpo revatīḥ kṣayathā hi vasva iti pratipadyante |
meaning: तद्द् ह एके कश् छन्दसाम् योगम् आवेद धीर इति जपित्वा अथ आपो रेवतीः क्षयथा हि वस्व इति प्रतिपद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: na āpo revatyai purastāt kiṃcana parihared iti |
meaning: न आपो रेवत्यै पुरस्तात् किंचन परिहरेद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad iha sthitam anāvraskāya tad iha sthitam anāvraskāya |
meaning: तद् इह स्थितम् अनाव्रस्काय तद् इह स्थितम् अनाव्रस्काय |

text:
The waters are the sacrifice; in that they come to the waters, verily thus they come to the sacrifice. Moreover the waters are strength and sap. Verily thus they unite the sacrifice with strength and sap.
Moreover, the waters are immortality; verily thus he confers immortality upon himself. Now aforetime the Rakṣases, confounders of the sacrifice, used to watch the waters at the fords; then whosoever came to the waters they killed them all; then Kavaṣa saw this hymn of fifteen verses, 'Forth among the gods let there be speeding for the Brahman'; he recited it; thereby he smote away the confounders of the sacrifice, the Rakṣases, from the fords; thence since then they return in safety and uninjured from the sacrifice. Yonder in the waters the Adhvaryu offers a libation; then should he accompany this (with the verse), 'Send forth our sacrifice with divine offering.' This is the offering verse for this (libation), being appropriate by containing (the word) 'offering'. (He recites) 'Winding hitherward, those of two streams,' when (the waters) are being brought; 'What time the waters are seen coming forward,' when they are discerned; 'Some come together; others come up,' as they come up; some waters come, others come up; 'Like the waters divine, they come up to the vessel of the offering', as they are poured down into the Hotṛ's bowl; 'May the cows with milk eager for the end', the cows are the waters, for the waters impel all this (universe). The Adhvaryu stands turned towards the Hotṛ; the Hotṛ asks him, 'O Adhvaryu, hast thou found the waters?' 'Hast thou found the sacrifice?' verily thus he says to him. 'They have indeed condescended' he replies; 'We have found what we have sought in these waters; for this they have condescended,' verily thus he says to him. Being answered the Hotṛ begins the Nigada; the Nigada is strength and sap; verily strength and sap he places in the oblation by means of the Nigada.

sanskrit_iast: aurjena eva tad rasena haviḥ saṃsṛjanti |
meaning: और्जेन एव तद् रसेन हविः संसृजन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tadd ha sma vai purā yajña muho rakṣāṃsi tīrtheṣv apo gopāyanti |
meaning: तद्द् ह स्म वै पुरा यज्ञ मुहो रक्षांसि तीर्थेष्व् अपो गोपायन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tad ye ke ca āpo accha jagmuḥ |
meaning: तद् ये के च आपो अच्छ जग्मुः |

sanskrit_iast: tat etat kavaṣaḥ sūktam apaśyat pañcadaśarcam pra devatrā brahmaṇe gātur etv iti |
meaning: तत् एतत् कवषः सूक्तम् अपश्यत् पञ्चदशर्चम् प्र देवत्रा ब्रह्मणे गातुर् एत्व् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tena yajña muho rakṣāṃsi tīrthebyo apāhan |
meaning: तेन यज्ञ मुहो रक्षांसि तीर्थेब्यो अपाहन् |

sanskrit_iast: tata u ha etad arvāk svasty ariṣṭyāḥ punaḥ pratyāyanti |
meaning: तत उ ह एतद् अर्वाक् स्वस्त्य् अरिष्ट्याः पुनः प्रत्यायन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atha ado amutra apsv adhvaryur āhutim juhoti |
meaning: अथ अदो अमुत्र अप्स्व् अध्वर्युर् आहुतिम् जुहोति |

sanskrit_iast: hinotā no adhvaram deva yajyā iti |
meaning: हिनोता नो अध्वरम् देव यज्या इति |

sanskrit_iast: tasyā eva eṣā yājyā deva yajyā ity abhirūpā |
meaning: तस्या एव एषा याज्या देव यज्या इत्य् अभिरूपा |

sanskrit_iast: āvarvṛtatīr adha nu dvidhārā ity āvṛttāsu |
meaning: आवर्वृततीर् अध नु द्विधारा इत्य् आवृत्तासु |

sanskrit_iast: prati yad āpo adṛśramāyatīr iti pratikhyātāsu |
meaning: प्रति यद् आपो अदृश्रमायतीर् इति प्रतिख्यातासु |

sanskrit_iast: samanyā yanty upa yanty anyā iti samāyatīṣu |
meaning: समन्या यन्त्य् उप यन्त्य् अन्या इति समायतीषु |

sanskrit_iast: āpo na devīr upa yanti hotriyam iti hotṛ camase avanīyamānāsu |
meaning: आपो न देवीर् उप यन्ति होत्रियम् इति होतृ चमसे अवनीयमानासु |

sanskrit_iast: tam hotā pṛcchaty adhvaryav aiṣīr apa iti |
meaning: तम् होता पृच्छत्य् अध्वर्यव् ऐषीर् अप इति |

sanskrit_iast: aiṣīr yajñam ity eva enam tad āha |
meaning: ऐषीर् यज्ञम् इत्य् एव एनम् तद् आह |

sanskrit_iast: avidāma tad yad āsya aiṣīṣma anaṃsata tasmā ity eva enam tad āha |
meaning: अविदाम तद् यद् आस्य ऐषीष्म अनंसत तस्मा इत्य् एव एनम् तद् आह |

sanskrit_iast: aurjam eva tad rasam nigadena haviṣi dadhāti |
meaning: और्जम् एव तद् रसम् निगदेन हविषि दधाति |

text:
'The mothers go with the paths' (he recites); the mothers are the waters, for he praises the waters as they go. 'They have come, rich, with living gifts' (he recites) when they have come up. He concludes with
(a verse ) containing the word 'across', 'The waters have arrived, eager, to this strew.' He recites appropriate (verses); what in the sacrifice is appropriate, that is perfect; verily (they serve) for the perfection of the sacrifice. The morning litany had been recited, the hymns had not been obtained; at this conjunction the Asuras went against them; the gods, perceiving in fear, saw this thriceforged thunderbolt; 'The waters' is the first form of the thunderbolt; 'Sarasvatī' is the second form of the thunderbolt; this is a hymn of fifteen verses, that is the third form of the thunderbolt. The gods with the thriceforged thunderbolt pushed away the Asuras from these worlds; verily thus also the sacrificer pushes away with this thriceforged thunderbolt the rivals who hate him from these worlds.

sanskrit_iast: emā agman revatīr jīva dhanyā ity āgatāsu |
meaning: एमा अग्मन् रेवतीर् जीव धन्या इत्य् आगतासु |

sanskrit_iast: āgmann āpa uśatīr barhir edam ity āgatavatyā paridadhāti |
meaning: आग्मन्न् आप उशतीर् बर्हिर् एदम् इत्य् आगतवत्या परिदधाति |

sanskrit_iast: yad yajñe abhirūpam tat samṛddham yajñasya eva samṛddhyai |
meaning: यद् यज्ञे अभिरूपम् तत् समृद्धम् यज्ञस्य एव समृद्ध्यै |

sanskrit_iast: te devāḥ pratibudhya bibhyata etam trihsamṛddham vajram apaśyan |
meaning: ते देवाः प्रतिबुध्य बिभ्यत एतम् त्रिह्समृद्धम् वज्रम् अपश्यन् |

sanskrit_iast: āpa iti tat prathamam vajra rūpam |
meaning: आप इति तत् प्रथमम् वज्र रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: sarasvatī iti tad dvitīyam vajra rūpam |
meaning: सरस्वती इति तद् द्वितीयम् वज्र रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: etena vai devās triḥ samṛddhena vajreṇa ebhyo lokebhyo asurān anudanta |
meaning: एतेन वै देवास् त्रिः समृद्धेन वज्रेण एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो असुरान् अनुदन्त |

sanskrit_iast: tatho eva etad yajamāna etena eva triḥ samṛddhena vajreṇa ebhyo lokebhyo dviṣato bhrātṛvyān nudate |
meaning: तथो एव एतद् यजमान एतेन एव त्रिः समृद्धेन वज्रेण एभ्यो लोकेभ्यो द्विषतो भ्रातृव्यान् नुदते |

text: The Mādhyamas performed a session on the Sarasvatī. Then Kavaṣa sat down in the midst, they said to him, 'Thou art the son of a female slave; we will not eat with you.' He rushing on in anger praised the Sarasvatī with this hymn; she followed after him; thereupon they felt themselves free from passion; they went after him and said 'O seer, homage be to thee; harm us not; thou art of us the best, seeing that she follows after thee.' Thus they informed him; they removed his anger. This is the greatness of Kavaṣa and the founder of the hymn (is he). In that they go with their wives, (it is because) the Gandharvas as commissioners in the waters guard the Soma of Indra. They love women, and they turn their minds towards them; so it is as if one might take the sacrifice of careless persons. The sacrifice condescends to him who knows thus. He recites twenty (verses); they make up the Virāj; the waters are connected with the Virāj, the Virāj is food, the waters are food; thus by food he causes proper food to abound. (He recites) the first thrice, and the last thrice; they make up twenty-four; the Gāyatrī has twenty-four syllables; the Gāyatrī supports the morning pressing; thus the waters contain the symbol of the morning pressing. So much for the Aponaptriya.

sanskrit_iast: tadd ha api kavaṣo madhye niṣasāda |
meaning: तद्द् ह अपि कवषो मध्ये निषसाद |

sanskrit_iast: dāsyā vai tvam putro asi na vayam tvayā saha bhakṣayiṣyāma iti |
meaning: दास्या वै त्वम् पुत्रो असि न वयम् त्वया सह भक्षयिष्याम इति |

sanskrit_iast: sa ha kruddhaḥ pradravant sarasvatīm etena sūktena tuṣṭāva |
meaning: स ह क्रुद्धः प्रद्रवन्त् सरस्वतीम् एतेन सूक्तेन तुष्टाव |

sanskrit_iast: tata u ha ime nirāgā iva menire |
meaning: तत उ ह इमे निरागा इव मेनिरे |

sanskrit_iast: ṛce namas te astu mā no hāsīḥ |
meaning: ऋचे नमस् ते अस्तु मा नो हासीः |

sanskrit_iast: sa eṣa kavaṣasya eva mahimā sūktasya ca anuveditā |
meaning: स एष कवषस्य एव महिमा सूक्तस्य च अनुवेदिता |

sanskrit_iast: gandharvā ha vā indrasya somam apsu pratyāhitā gopāyanti |
meaning: गन्धर्वा ह वा इन्द्रस्य सोमम् अप्सु प्रत्याहिता गोपायन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā pramattānām yajñam āhared evam tat |
meaning: तद् यथा प्रमत्तानाम् यज्ञम् आहरेद् एवम् तत् |

sanskrit_iast: upanāmuka u eva enam yajño bhavati |
meaning: उपनामुक उ एव एनम् यज्ञो भवति |

sanskrit_iast: triḥ prathamayā trir uttamayā caturviṃśatiḥ sampadyante |
meaning: त्रिः प्रथमया त्रिर् उत्तमया चतुर्विंशतिः सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: tad u ha prātaḥ savana rūpān na apaiti |
meaning: तद् उ ह प्रातः सवन रूपान् न अपैति |

text: The Upāṅśu (cup) is expiration; as it is offered he should breathe forth along it (saying) ‘Protect my expiration, quicken my expiration; hail! Thee of fair birth to the sun!’ This is its call of vaṣaṭ and its call of Hail! These libations go not to the gods over which the vaṣaṭ call or the call of Hail! is not pronounced. Inspiration is the Antaryāma (cup); as it is offered he should breathe down along it (saying) ‘Protect my inspiration, quicken my inspiration; hail! Thee of fair birth to the sun!’ This is its call of vaṣaṭ, and its call of Hail! These libations go not to the gods over which the vaṣaṭ call or the call of Hail! is not pronounced. The Upāṅśu and Antaryāma are expiration and inspiration; one of these they offer when the sun has risen, the other before the sun has risen; verily thus they separate expiration and inspiration; therefore expiration and inspiration, though being together, are separate as it were. ‘In that they offer one when the sun has risen and the other before the sun has risen, verily thus from day and night they obstruct the Asuras, for on both sides of yonder sun are day and night, and the sacrificer (obstructs) evil,’ so he used to say. He for whom they offer both (cups) after the sun has risen or before the sun has risen is a sacrificer with water, not a sacrificer with Soma; he for whom these two are offered in their order is a real sacrificer with Soma. So for the Upāṅśu and Antaryāma (cups).

sanskrit_iast: tam hūyamānam anuprāṇyāt prāṇam me pāhi prāṇam me jinva svāhā tvā subhava sūryāya iti |

sanskrit_iast: tam hūyamānam anvavānyād apānam me pāhy apānam me jinva svāhā itvā subhava sūryāya iti |

sanskrit_iast: sa eva tasya vaṣaṭ kāraḥ sa svāhā kāraḥ |
meaning: स एव तस्य वषट् कारः स स्वाहा कारः |

sanskrit_iast: na ha vai tā āhutayo devān gacchanti yā avaṣaṭ kṛtā vā asvāhā kṛtā vā bhavanti |

sanskrit_iast: tau vā etau prāṇa apānāv eva yad upāṃśv antaryāmau |

sanskrit_iast: tayor vā udite anyam anudite anyam juhvati |

sanskrit_iast: imāv eva tat prāṇa apānau vitārayati |
