sanskrit_iast: viśve devāḥ śṛṇuta imam havam ma ity uktham śastvā yajati vaiśvadevyā |
meaning: विश्वे देवाः शृणुत इमम् हवम् म इत्य् उक्थम् शस्त्वा यजति वैश्वदेव्या |

sanskrit_iast: balam eva tad vīryam yajamāne dadhāti |
meaning: बलम् एव तद् वीर्यम् यजमाने दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: yo ayam aniruktaḥ prāṇaḥ sa surūpa kṛtnuḥ |
meaning: यो अयम् अनिरुक्तः प्राणः स सुरूप कृत्नुः |

sanskrit_iast: prāṇo apāno vyāna iti tisra eka pātinyaḥ |
meaning: प्राणो अपानो व्यान इति तिस्र एक पातिन्यः |

sanskrit_iast: ātmā sūktam yad antar ātmaṃs tan nivit |
meaning: आत्मा सूक्तम् यद् अन्तर् आत्मंस् तन् निवित् |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhuḥ kasmād brahma kṣatre eva pracyāvuke viḍ acyuta iti |
meaning: तद् आहुः कस्माद् ब्रह्म क्षत्रे एव प्रच्यावुके विड् अच्युत इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad yad yathā upapādam eva prātaḥ savana madhyaṃdinayoḥ paridadhati |
meaning: तद् यद् यथा उपपादम् एव प्रातः सवन मध्यंदिनयोः परिदधति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yat tṛtīyasya savanasya paridhānīyā acyutā |
meaning: अथ यत् तृतीयस्य सवनस्य परिधानीया अच्युता |

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtasya yaja saumyasya yaja ity āha |
meaning: घृतस्य यज सौम्यस्य यज इत्य् आह |
text:
‘Say the offering verse for the ghee’ and ‘Say the offering verse for the Soma drink’, he says; by ghee and by Soma is the sacrifice carried on; these here he delights (thinking) ‘They delighted shall support the sacrifice.’ Inaudibly he says the offering verse for the ghee; ghee is a pouring of seed; inaudibly is seed poured. In that he says the offering verse aloud for the Soma drink, (it is because) Soma is the moon, and the moon is distinct. ‘After it he should not perform any additional offering,’ they say, ‘So do they yonder from yonder look back on this (world)’. But the rule is, ‘Let him perform’. The butter is the world of the gods, the Soma the world of the fathers; verily thus they arise from the world
of the fathers to the world of the gods. 'Moreover thus they delight the fathers only in that they proceed with the Soma drink; moreover thus the Upasads are left over,' they say. In the Upasads he sacrifices to Agni, Soma, and Viṣṇu and to match this here also to Agni, Soma, and Viṣṇu. They take the Soma drink to the Sadas; the Hotṛ takes it and deposits it; then he looks at himself in the melted butter in it and with two fingers touches the melted butter; (with the words) 'Thou art the guardian of the eye, guard mine eye,' he should rub his eyes; verily thus he guards his eyes. It he hands over to the Udgātṛs.

sanskrit_iast: etābhyām vai yajñas tāyate yad ghṛtena ca somena ca |
meaning: एताभ्याम् वै यज्ञस् तायते यद् घृतेन च सोमेन च |

sanskrit_iast: tasya na parastāt pariyajed ity āhuḥ |
meaning: तस्य न परस्तात् परियजेद् इत्य् आहुः |

sanskrit_iast: tathā amī amuta idam arvāñcaḥ paśyanti iti |
meaning: तथा अमी अमुत इदम् अर्वाञ्चः पश्यन्ति इति |

sanskrit_iast: deva lokam eva tat pitṛ lokād abhyutkrāmanti |
meaning: देव लोकम् एव तत् पितृ लोकाद् अभ्युत्क्रामन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atho pitṝn eva tat prīṇanti yat saumyena caranti |
meaning: अथो पितॄन् एव तत् प्रीणन्ति यत् सौम्येन चरन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atho etad upasada utsṛjyanta ity āhuḥ |
meaning: अथो एतद् उपसद उत्सृज्यन्त इत्य् आहुः |

sanskrit_iast: agnim somam viṣṇum iti vā upasatsu pratiyajati |
meaning: अग्निम् सोमम् विष्णुम् इति वा उपसत्सु प्रतियजति |

sanskrit_iast: atha asya sarpiṣy ātmānam paryavekṣya aṅgulibhyām sarpir upaspṛśati |
meaning: अथ अस्य सर्पिष्य् आत्मानम् पर्यवेक्ष्य अङ्गुलिभ्याम् सर्पिर् उपस्पृशति |

sanskrit_iast: cakṣuṣpā asi cakṣur me pāhi iti cakṣuṣī vimṛjīta |
meaning: चक्षुष्पा असि चक्षुर् मे पाहि इति चक्षुषी विमृजीत |

text: Then they proceed with the Pātnīvata cup; verily thus they make the wives of the gods sharers in the Āhavanīya. He does not say for it the second vaṣaṭ, for it is mixed with butter, and butter has no share in the second vaṣaṭ call. Inaudibly he says the offering verse; the Pātnīvata cup is a pouring of seed; inaudibly is seed poured. He does not say the second vaṣaṭ (thinking) 'The Pātnīvata cup is a pouring of seed; the second vaṣaṭ is completion; let me not before the due time complete the pouring of seed.' The offering verse contains (the words) 'be drunk', for the third pressing is connected with 'be drunk'. They say 'Since this is the offering verse of the Neṣṭṛ, then why does the Āgnīdhra say it as an offering verse?' 'This offering verse is connected with Agni; the Āgnīdhra is connected with Agni; therefore the Āgnīdhra uses it as an offering verse; moreover, thus the vaṣaṭ calls of these unuttered become the same' (is the reply).

sanskrit_iast: patnīr eva tad āhavanīya bhājaḥ kurvanti |
meaning: पत्नीर् एव तद् आहवनीय भाजः कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: retaḥ siktir vai patnīvata graha upāṃśu vai retaḥ sicyate |
meaning: रेतः सिक्तिर् वै पत्नीवत ग्रह उपांशु वै रेतः सिच्यते |

sanskrit_iast: retaḥ siktir vai patnīvata grahaḥ saṃsthā anvaṣaṭ kāraḥ |
meaning: रेतः सिक्तिर् वै पत्नीवत ग्रहः संस्था अन्वषट् कारः |

sanskrit_iast: na id retaḥ siktam purā kālāt saṃsthā apayāni iti |
meaning: न इद् रेतः सिक्तम् पुरा कालात् संस्था अपयानि इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad eṣā neṣṭur yājyā atha kasmād enayā agnīdhro yajati iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् एषा नेष्टुर् याज्या अथ कस्माद् एनया अग्नीध्रो यजति इति |

sanskrit_iast: atho evam samā anukthānām vaṣaṭ kārā bhavanti iti |
meaning: अथो एवम् समा अनुक्थानाम् वषट् कारा भवन्ति इति |

text:
He recites the Āgnimāruta with twenty-one calls; the four-verse Stoma, the highest of Stomas on which support is to be found, is twenty-onefold; verily (it serves) for a support. The (Śastra) is twenty-fourfold; there are twenty joinings; these make forty-four; the Triṣṭubh has forty-four syllables; the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus he places might and strength in the sacrificer. He recites (a hymn ) to Vaiśvānara, for a cup for Vaiśvānara has been drawn; verily therewith he accompanies
it. He recites (a verse ) to Rudra; Rudra is dread; verily thus he makes medicine; moveover his share is at the end; therefore in the end Śastra he recites it. He recites (a hymn ) to the Maruts; Rudra has them as his horde; verily thus he makes him prosper with his own horde. Then come the strophe and antistrophe of the Yajñāyajñīya; these two he recites in the middle to frighten, for in the middle of the body is the womb placed to frighten. He recites (a hymn ) to Jātavedas; thereby is it called the Āgnimāruta (Śastra). Therefore should he recite it quickly, just as one escaping a forest fire. He recites (verses ) with the waters as deities; the waters are healing and medicine; verily thus at the end in the sacrifice are healing and medicine produced. Therefore should he recite them slowly, just as one spraying himself in the waters. He recites 'the Dragon of the Deep'; the dragon of the deep is Agni; him with it he makes to glow; moreover, with it he accompanies the altars. He recites 'the wives of the gods' and 'Rākā'; verily with these he accompanies the Pātnīvata cup; moreover, the wives have their portion at the end; therefore in the end Śastra he recites these verses.

sanskrit_iast: ekaviṃśo vai stomaḥ stomānām paramaḥ pratiṣṭhānīyaḥ |
meaning: एकविंशो वै स्तोमः स्तोमानाम् परमः प्रतिष्ठानीयः |

sanskrit_iast: balam eva tad vīryam yajamāne dadhāti |
meaning: बलम् एव तद् वीर्यम् यजमाने दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: atho anta bhāg vā vā eṣaḥ |
meaning: अथो अन्त भाग् वा वा एषः |

sanskrit_iast: śāntir eva eṣā bheṣajam antato yajñe kriyate |
meaning: शान्तिर् एव एषा भेषजम् अन्ततो यज्ञे क्रियते |

sanskrit_iast: devānām ca patnī rākām ca śaṃsati |
meaning: देवानाम् च पत्नी राकाम् च शंसति |

text:
He recites the Akṣarapaṅktis; the Akṣarapaṅktis are cattle; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle; moreover, the Akṣarapaṅktis are expiration and inspiration; thereby then he places expiration and inspiration in himself; moreover (they serve) to secure the presence of Indra in the Śastra. He recites (verses) to the fathers and to Yama; verily thus he accompanies the Nārāśaṅsa cups; moreover the fathers have their portion at the end; therefore he recites these (verses) in the end Śastra. He recites (the verses ) 'Sweet indeed is he'; verily with them he makes sweet the Soma for Indra; moreover, Indra is the world of the gods, Yama the world of the fathers; verily thus he arises from the world of the fathers to the world of the gods. To them the Adhvaryu responds with (a formula containing the word) 'mad', for the third pressing is connected with 'be drunk'. He recites (a verse) to Viṣṇu and Varuṇa; the sacrifice is
connected with Viṣṇu and Varuṇa; whatever mistake or error there is in the sacrifice, that with this he remedies; verily this is medicine. He recites (a verse) to Viṣṇu and (a verse) to Agni; of the gods Agni and Viṣṇu are those whose portions are at the end; therefore these he recites in the end Śastra. He concludes with (a verse) to Indra, for he is Indra's; verily him Indra at the end establishes.

sanskrit_iast: atho prāṇa apānau vā akṣara paṅktayaḥ |
meaning: अथो प्राण अपानौ वा अक्षर पङ्क्तयः |

sanskrit_iast: prāṇa apānāv eva tad ātman dhatte |
meaning: प्राण अपानाव् एव तद् आत्मन् धत्ते |

sanskrit_iast: deva lokam eva tat pitṛ lokād abhyutkrāmanti |
meaning: देव लोकम् एव तत् पितृ लोकाद् अभ्युत्क्रामन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: yad vai yajñasya skhalitam vā ulbaṇam vā bhavati |
meaning: यद् वै यज्ञस्य स्खलितम् वा उल्बणम् वा भवति |

sanskrit_iast: kim devatyaḥ soma iti madhuko gauśravam papraccha |
meaning: किम् देवत्यः सोम इति मधुको गौश्रवम् पप्रच्छ |
text: ‘What is the deity of the Soma?’ Madhuka asked Gauśra. He, after running over (the words) ‘Soma becometh pure’, replied ‘There may be different ones.’ ‘As with the Bahvṛcas, it should be connected with Indra’ was the rule of Paiṅgya. ‘It should be connected with Indra and Agni’ is Kauṣītaki's view. ‘By Agni it begins in that (it begins) with the Ājya; with Indra it ends (in) this concluding verse; therefore it should be connected with Indra and Agni.’ ‘This is the Agniṣṭoma; this is taken for every desire. He who offers with any other sacrifice without having sacrificed with this prepares for himself a pitfall, he comes to ruin’, he used to say. This Agniṣṭoma begins with the Ājya (Śastra) and ends with the Āgnimāruta. What has to be recited makes up three hundred and sixty Ṛc verses; three hundred and sixty are the days of the year; verily (it serves) to obtain the year. After reciting the litany he uses as offering verse, ‘O Agni, with the Maruts, resplendent, loud singing’, addressed to Agni and the Maruts, for this litany is addressed to Agni and the Maruts; in Jagatī metre, for the third pressing is connected with the Jagatī; containing (the words) ‘be drunk’, for the third pressing is connected with ‘be drunk’. He says the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations.

sanskrit_iast: sa ha somaḥ pavata ity anudrutya |
meaning: स ह सोमः पवत इत्य् अनुद्रुत्य |

sanskrit_iast: etasya vā anye syur iti prtyuvāca |
meaning: एतस्य वा अन्ये स्युर् इति प्र्त्युवाच |

sanskrit_iast: aindra iti tv eva paiṅgyasya sthitir āsa |
meaning: ऐन्द्र इति त्व् एव पैङ्ग्यस्य स्थितिर् आस |

sanskrit_iast: eṣa vā u kāmāya kāmāya āhriyate |
meaning: एष वा उ कामाय कामाय आह्रियते |

sanskrit_iast: yo ha vā etena aniṣṭvā atha anyena yajate |
meaning: यो ह वा एतेन अनिष्ट्वा अथ अन्येन यजते |

sanskrit_iast: kartapatyam eva taj jīyate pra vā mīyata iti ha sma āha |
meaning: कर्तपत्यम् एव तज् जीयते प्र वा मीयत इति ह स्म आह |

sanskrit_iast: sa vā eṣo agniṣṭoma ājya prabhṛtyā agni māruta antaḥ |
meaning: स वा एषो अग्निष्टोम आज्य प्रभृत्या अग्नि मारुत अन्तः |

sanskrit_iast: yat śasyaṃs trīṇi ṣaṣṭi śatāny ṛcām sampadyante |
meaning: यत् शस्यंस् त्रीणि षष्टि शतान्य् ऋचाम् सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: trīṇi vai ṣaṣṭi śatāni saṃvatsarasya ahnām |
meaning: त्रीणि वै षष्टि शतानि संवत्सरस्य अह्नाम् |

sanskrit_iast: agne marudbhiḥ śubhayadbhir ṛkvabhir ity uktham śastvā yajaty āgnimārutyā |
meaning: अग्ने मरुद्भिः शुभयद्भिर् ऋक्वभिर् इत्य् उक्थम् शस्त्वा यजत्य् आग्निमारुत्या |

text:
The litanies of the Ukthya are addressed to Indra and Agni; all the gods are Indra and Agni; the third pressing is connected with the All-gods; verily (they serve) to delight all the gods. In (verses) to Agni they give the lead for the Maitrāvaruṇa, in (verses) to Indra in the other two cases; thereby these are addressed to Indra and Agni. They recite four hymns each; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fourfold; moreover,
cattle are four-footed; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. They make up twelve; the year has twelve months; verily (they serve) to obtain the year. The Śastras contain four calls; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fourfold; moreover cattle are four-footed; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. The offering verses of the litanies are addressed to two deities; the sacrificer has two feet; (therefore they serve) for support. They make up four; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fourfold; moreover, cattle are four-footed; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. That of the Maitrāvaruṇa is addressed to Indra and Varuṇa, for his litany is addressed to Indra and Varuṇa; that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin to Indra and Bṛhaspati, for his litany is addressed to Indra and Bṛhaspati; that of the Achāvāka to Indra and Viṣṇu, for his litany is connected with Indra and Viṣṇu. The first and last contain (the words) 'be drunk', for the third pressing is connected with 'be drunk'. They make up three; these worlds are three; verily thus they obtain these worlds. They are Triṣṭubh verses; the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus they place might and strength in the sacrificer. They say the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations.

sanskrit_iast: balam eva tad vīryam yajamāne dadhati |
meaning: बलम् एव तद् वीर्यम् यजमाने दधति |

sanskrit_iast: ānuṣṭubho vā eṣa vajro yat ṣoḍaśī |
meaning: आनुष्टुभो वा एष वज्रो यत् षोडशी |
text:
The Ṣoḍaśin is a thunderbolt composed of the Anuṣṭubh; in that they undertake the Ṣoḍaśin, they smite away the evil of the sacrificer with the thunderbolt composed of the Anuṣṭubh. It refers to the 'bay steeds'; the bay is breath, for it draws; therefore it refers to the 'bay steeds'. The Ṣoḍaśin is he yonder that gives heat; verily thus they delight him. There is a sixteenth Stotra, a sixteenth Śastra; therefore is it called the Ṣoḍaśin. In that they undertake the Ṣoḍaśin, and all this (universe) is of sixteen parts, verily (it serves) to obtain all this. Moreover, the Ṣoḍaśin is Indra; therefore it refers to the 'bay steeds', for Indra's bay steeds are praised. 'O Indra rejoice, bring forward, come hither, O hero,
of the bay steeds’ these (verses) have twenty-five syllables and one by one have nine syllables added. The self is twenty-fivefold, what is added is offspring and cattle; verily thus he adds to himself in offspring, cattle, servants, and proper food. These make up thirty-four; whatever is of thirty-four syllables, that metre is the Svarāj; verily thereby he obtains self rule. Repeated together they make up five Anuṣṭubh verses and a ten-syllable quarter verse is left over, two syllables for each verse. ‘Of such a one as thou, O thou of much light’, this Gāyatrī verse he recites next, for the completion of these syllables; moreover along with it they make up a strophe of six Anuṣṭubh verses; therefore he recites it, for completion. To match it some make an antistrophe; but as to this they say ‘The Ṣoḍaśin is he yonder that gives heat; there is none other to be a counterpart of him; if he were to make a counterpart and one were to say of him, “The rival who is hateful will reject him”, so would it be. Therefore he should not trouble about a counterpart.’

sanskrit_iast: ānuṣṭubhena eva tad vajreṇa yajamānasya pāpmānam apaghnanti |
meaning: आनुष्टुभेन एव तद् वज्रेण यजमानस्य पाप्मानम् अपघ्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tad asau vai ṣoḍaśī yo asau tapati |
meaning: तद् असौ वै षोडशी यो असौ तपति |

sanskrit_iast: atho ṣoḍaśam vā etat stotram ṣoḍaśam śastram |
meaning: अथो षोडशम् वा एतत् स्तोत्रम् षोडशम् शस्त्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: indra juṣasva pra vahā yāhi śūra harī iha iti |
meaning: इन्द्र जुषस्व प्र वहा याहि शूर हरी इह इति |

sanskrit_iast: eka ekā navabhir nabavhir akṣarair upasṛṣṭāḥ |
meaning: एक एका नवभिर् नबव्हिर् अक्षरैर् उपसृष्टाः |

sanskrit_iast: prajayā eva tat paśubhiḥ preṣyair anna adyena ity ātmānam upasṛjate |
meaning: प्रजया एव तत् पशुभिः प्रेष्यैर् अन्न अद्येन इत्य् आत्मानम् उपसृजते |

sanskrit_iast: yat kiṃca catustriṃśad akṣaram svārājyam anena āpnoti |
meaning: यत् किंच चतुस्त्रिंशद् अक्षरम् स्वाराज्यम् अनेन आप्नोति |

sanskrit_iast: atho etayā saha stotriyaḥ ṣaḍ anuṣṭubhaḥ sampadyante |
meaning: अथो एतया सह स्तोत्रियः षड् अनुष्टुभः सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: etat pratirūpam u ha eke anurūpam kurvanti |
meaning: एतत् प्रतिरूपम् उ ह एके अनुरूपम् कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tad u vā āhur asau vai ṣoḍaśī yo asau tapati |
meaning: तद् उ वा आहुर् असौ वै षोडशी यो असौ तपति |

sanskrit_iast: na vā etasya anyo anurūpo asti |
meaning: न वा एतस्य अन्यो अनुरूपो अस्ति |

sanskrit_iast: sa yo atra anurūpam kurvantam brūyāt |
meaning: स यो अत्र अनुरूपम् कुर्वन्तम् ब्रूयात् |

text:
Thereafter he transposes the metres which follow; the metres are the breaths; verily thus in the body he interweaves the breaths, to prevent separation; therefore these breaths, though breathing in different directions, do not blow out. Moreover the Ṣoḍaśin is connected with the Anuṣṭubh; verily thus he brings all the metres into relation with the Anuṣṭubh. He transposes Gāyatrī and Paṅkti verses; the Paṅkti is the metre of the sacrificer; the Gāyatrī is brilliance and splendour; verily thus he places brilliance and splendour in the sacrificer. He transposes Uṣṇih and Bṛhatī verses; the Uṣṇih is the metre of the sacrificer; the Bṛhatī is cattle; verily thus he confers cattle as connected with the Bṛhatī upon the sacrificer. He transposes a verse of two Padas containing twenty syllables and a Triṣṭubh; the verse of two Padas
is the metre of the sacrificer; the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus he confers might and strength upon the sacrificer. He transposes verses of two Padas containing sixteen syllables and Jagatī verses; verses of two Padas are the metre of the sacrificer; the Jagatī is cattle; verily thus he confers cattle as connected with the Jagatī on the sacrificer. He recites Gāyatrī verses; Gāyatrī verses are breath; verily thus he places breath in himself. He recites a verse of seven Padas; the metres are seven; verily (it serves) to obtain all the metres; moreover, with it the Gāyatrī verses make up four Anuṣṭubh verses; therefore he recites it, for completion.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇān eva tad ātman vyatiṣajaty avivarhāya |
meaning: प्राणान् एव तद् आत्मन् व्यतिषजत्य् अविवर्हाय |

sanskrit_iast: tasmādd hi ime prāṇā viṣvañco vā anto na nirvānti |
meaning: तस्माद्द् हि इमे प्राणा विष्वञ्चो वा अन्तो न निर्वान्ति |

sanskrit_iast: sarvāṇy eva etat chandāṃsy anuṣṭubham abhiṣampādayati |
meaning: सर्वाण्य् एव एतत् छन्दांस्य् अनुष्टुभम् अभिषम्पादयति |

sanskrit_iast: teja eva tad brahma varcasam yajamāne dadhāti |
meaning: तेज एव तद् ब्रह्म वर्चसम् यजमाने दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: bārhatān eva tat paśūn yajamāne dadhāti |
meaning: बार्हतान् एव तत् पशून् यजमाने दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: dvipadām ca viṃśaty akṣarām triṣṭubham ca viharati |
meaning: द्विपदाम् च विंशत्य् अक्षराम् त्रिष्टुभम् च विहरति |

sanskrit_iast: balam eva tad vīryam yajamāne dadhāti |
meaning: बलम् एव तद् वीर्यम् यजमाने दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: dvipadāś ca ṣoḍaśa akṣarā jagatīś ca viharati |
meaning: द्विपदाश् च षोडश अक्षरा जगतीश् च विहरति |

sanskrit_iast: jāgatān eva tat paśūn yajamāne dadhāti |
meaning: जागतान् एव तत् पशून् यजमाने दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: atho etayā saha gāyatryaś catasro anuṣṭubhaḥ sampadyante |
meaning: अथो एतया सह गायत्र्यश् चतस्रो अनुष्टुभः सम्पद्यन्ते |

text: Then he recites Anuṣṭubhs of normal type; the Ṣoḍaśin is connected with the Anuṣṭubh; thus he causes it to prosper by its own symbol. They make up eight; by these (verses) the gods attained all attainments; verily thus also with these the sacrificer attains all attainments. With the last verse thrice repeated they make up ten; the Virāj consists of tens; the Virāj is prosperity and proper food; (they serve) to obtain the Virāj as prosperity and proper food. He concludes with ‘When up to the place of the bright one’; yonder is the place of the bright one where he yonder gives heat; verily thus he places the sacrificer there. Three times he utters the call for the Ṣoḍaśin, in the strophe, for the Nivid, for the concluding verse; the Ṣoḍaśin is threefold; verily thus with a threefold thunderbolt he smites the evil of the sacrificer. These are the fame, the sounds, the strengths of the litanies. Famous, resounding, strong, renowned does he become who knows thus the strengths of the litanies. They recited together make up forty Anuṣṭubhs; the Paṅkti has forty syllables; the Paṅkti is a support; verily thus in all creatures he establishes the sacrificer.

sanskrit_iast: etābhir vai devāḥ sarvā aṣṭīr āśnuvata |
meaning: एताभिर् वै देवाः सर्वा अष्टीर् आश्नुवत |

sanskrit_iast: tatho eva etad yajamāna etābhir eva sarvā aṣṭīr aśnute |
meaning: तथो एव एतद् यजमान एताभिर् एव सर्वा अष्टीर् अश्नुते |

sanskrit_iast: ado vai bradhnasya viṣṭapam yatra asau tapati |
meaning: अदो वै ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपम् यत्र असौ तपति |

sanskrit_iast: trivṛtā eva tad vajreṇa yajamānasya pāpmānam hanti |
meaning: त्रिवृता एव तद् वज्रेण यजमानस्य पाप्मानम् हन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: ta ete ślokā ghoṣā vīryāṇi ity ukthānām |
meaning: त एते श्लोका घोषा वीर्याणि इत्य् उक्थानाम् |

sanskrit_iast: ślokī ghoṣī vīryavān kīrtimān bhavati ya evam veda ukthānām vīryāṇi |
meaning: श्लोकी घोषी वीर्यवान् कीर्तिमान् भवति य एवम् वेद उक्थानाम् वीर्याणि |

sanskrit_iast: sarveṣv eva tad bhūteṣu yajamānam pratiṣṭhāpayati |
meaning: सर्वेष्व् एव तद् भूतेषु यजमानम् प्रतिष्ठापयति |

sanskrit_iast: vihṛtayā triṣṭubhā yajed iti ha eka āhuḥ |
meaning: विहृतया त्रिष्टुभा यजेद् इति ह एक आहुः |
text:
Some say ‘He should use an interpolated Triṣṭubh as offering verse’. ‘For indeed the courser.—Thou hast drunk of the ancient draughts, O lord of the bays.—For the courser is a courser.—Now let this pressing be thine only.—The courser is a bearer.—Drink the Soma rich in honey, O Indra.—For the courser is active.—Do thou ever, O strong one, pour into thy belly.’ But the rule is not to interpolate. The offering verses are duly prepared dishes for the gods; verily thus with a duly
prepared dish for the gods he tenders the oblation to the gods. He should not undertake it at night; the Ṣoḍaśin is Indra; there is nothing above Indra; much is accomplished at night, the rounds as it were, and the Āśvina (Śastra); therefore he should undertake it on the fourth day; that is the abode of the Ṣoḍaśin; that day concludes with the Ṣoḍaśin as its end. But they say 'Let him undertake it'; the Ṣoḍaśin is the day and night complete; in that they undertake the Ṣoḍaśin it is to make day and night complete.

sanskrit_iast: evā hi vājyapāḥ pūrveṣām harivaḥ sutānām vājo hi vājy atho idam savanam kevalam te |
meaning: एवा हि वाज्यपाः पूर्वेषाम् हरिवः सुतानाम् वाजो हि वाज्य् अथो इदम् सवनम् केवलम् ते |

sanskrit_iast: voḍhā hi vājī mamadd hi somam madhumantam indra jiṣṇur hi vājī satrā vṛṣan jaṭhara āvṛṣasva iti |
meaning: वोढा हि वाजी ममद्द् हि सोमम् मधुमन्तम् इन्द्र जिष्णुर् हि वाजी सत्रा वृषन् जठर आवृषस्व इति |

sanskrit_iast: saṃsiddhāni vā etāni deva pātrāṇi yad yājyāḥ |
meaning: संसिद्धानि वा एतानि देव पात्राणि यद् याज्याः |

sanskrit_iast: saṃsiddhena eva tad deva pātreṇa devebhyo haviḥ prayacchati |
meaning: संसिद्धेन एव तद् देव पात्रेण देवेभ्यो हविः प्रयच्छति |

sanskrit_iast: na vā indrād anyad uttaram asti |
meaning: न वा इन्द्राद् अन्यद् उत्तरम् अस्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tata eva enam caturthe ahany upeyāt |
meaning: तत एव एनम् चतुर्थे अहन्य् उपेयात् |

sanskrit_iast: tad vai tad ahaḥ ṣoḍaśy antam saṃtiṣṭhate |
meaning: तद् वै तद् अहः षोडश्य् अन्तम् संतिष्ठते |

sanskrit_iast: tad u vā āhur upeyād eva etat |
meaning: तद् उ वा आहुर् उपेयाद् एव एतत् |

text: In that they undertake the Atirātra, (it is because) the year is as great as day and night; in that they undertake the Atirātra, (it serves) to obtain the year. Moreover, all this (universe) is twofold, unguent and brilliance; both of these are obtained by day and night. In that they undertake the Atirātra, (it is) for the obtaining of unguent and brilliance.

sanskrit_iast: atho dvayam vā idam sarvam snehaś caiva tejaś ca |
meaning: अथो द्वयम् वा इदम् सर्वम् स्नेहश् चैव तेजश् च |

text: They recite strophes and antistrophes in Gāyatrī; the Gāyatrī is light; night is the evil, the darkness; thus thereby they smite away the evil, the darkness. They recite with repetitions, for so do the Sāman chanters sing; (they say) 'According as it is sung, is it recited.' Then they say 'Why after the final Pratihāra do they call and link the Śastra with the Sāman?'

sanskrit_iast: tena taj jyotiṣā tamaḥ pāpmānam taranti |
meaning: तेन तज् ज्योतिषा तमः पाप्मानम् तरन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: yathā stutam v anuśastam bhavati iti |
meaning: यथा स्तुतम् व् अनुशस्तम् भवति इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur ataḥ kasmād uttamāt pratīhārād ūrdhvam āhūya sāmnā śastram upasaṃtanvanti iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् अतः कस्माद् उत्तमात् प्रतीहाराद् ऊर्ध्वम् आहूय साम्ना शस्त्रम् उपसंतन्वन्ति इति |

text:
The sacrifice is a man; of him the oblation holders are the head, the Āhavanīya the face, the Sadas the stomach, the litanies the food, the Mārjālīya and the Āgnīdhriya the arms, the altars within the Sadas the internal divinities; the Gārhapatya and (the fire) for cooking the fast milk the support. Again, of him the Brahman priest is the mind, the Udgātṛ the expiration, the Prastotṛ the inspiration, the Pratihartṛ the cross-breathing, the Hotṛ the speech, the Adhvaryu the eye, the Sadasya
generation, the sacrificer the body, the Hotrāśaṅsins the limbs. In that the Adhvaryu starts the Stotra, verily thus he unites the eye with the breaths; moreover, verily thus he connects inspiration with the mind. In that the Prastotṛ addresses the Brahman with ‘O Brahman, shall we begin the praise, O Praśāstṛ?’ (it is because they think), ‘Mind is the leader of these breaths; impelled by mind let us sing the Stoma’; moreover, verily thus he connects inspiration with the mind. In that the Brahman approves the Stotra, verily thus he unites the mind with the breaths; moreover, verily thus he connects inspiration with the mind. In that the Prastotṛ begins the praise, verily thus he places inspiration in expiration. In that the Udgātṛ sings, verily thus he places expiration in cross-breathing. In that the Pratihartṛ utters his part, verily thus he places cross-breathing in expiration. So all these deities find support in expiration. In that the Hotṛ connects the Śastra with the Sāman, and the Hotṛ is speech, verily thus he unites speech with the breaths; moreover, verily thus he connects inspiration with mind. In that the Hotrāśaṅsins make a continuity with the Sāman, verily thus they connect the limbs with the breaths. In that the sacrificer sings in accompaniment to the Stotra, and the singers are the breaths, verily thus he places the breaths in himself. Therefore the sun should not set on him outside the altar place, nor should it rise on him, nor should he make preparations, nor utter the invitation, nor say the vaṣaṭ, nor should (the sun) heat (him) when in what is not an altar, (thinking) ‘Let me not sever the body from the breaths.’

sanskrit_iast: tasya śira eva havir dhāne mukham āhavanīya udaram sado annam ukthāni |
meaning: तस्य शिर एव हविर् धाने मुखम् आहवनीय उदरम् सदो अन्नम् उक्थानि |

sanskrit_iast: yā imā antar devatās te antaḥ sadanam dhiṣṇyāḥ |
meaning: या इमा अन्तर् देवतास् ते अन्तः सदनम् धिष्ण्याः |

sanskrit_iast: tasya mana eva brahmā prāṇa udgātā apānaḥ prastotā vyānaḥ pratihartā vāg ghotā cakṣur adhvaryuḥ prajātiḥ sadasya ātmā yajamānaḥ |
meaning: तस्य मन एव ब्रह्मा प्राण उद्गाता अपानः प्रस्तोता व्यानः प्रतिहर्ता वाग् घोता चक्षुर् अध्वर्युः प्रजातिः सदस्य आत्मा यजमानः |

sanskrit_iast: atha yat prastotā brāhmaṇam āmantrayate brahmant stoṣyāma iti |
meaning: अथ यत् प्रस्तोता ब्राह्मणम् आमन्त्रयते ब्रह्मन्त् स्तोष्याम इति |

sanskrit_iast: mano vā agraṇīr bhavaty eṣām prāṇānām |
meaning: मनो वा अग्रणीर् भवत्य् एषाम् प्राणानाम् |

sanskrit_iast: manasā eva prasūtāḥ stomena stuyāma iti |
meaning: मनसा एव प्रसूताः स्तोमेन स्तुयाम इति |

sanskrit_iast: atho apānam eva tan manasā saṃtanoti |
meaning: अथो अपानम् एव तन् मनसा संतनोति |

sanskrit_iast: tā vā etāḥ sarvā devatāḥ prāṇa eva pratiṣṭhitāḥ |
meaning: ता वा एताः सर्वा देवताः प्राण एव प्रतिष्ठिताः |

sanskrit_iast: atha yadd hotā sāmnā śastram upasaṃtanoti |
meaning: अथ यद्द् होता साम्ना शस्त्रम् उपसंतनोति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yadd hotrāśaṃsinaḥ sāma saṃtatim kurvanti |
meaning: अथ यद्द् होत्राशंसिनः साम संततिम् कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tasmān na enam bahir vedyabhyas tam iyāt |
meaning: तस्मान् न एनम् बहिर् वेद्यभ्यस् तम् इयात् |

sanskrit_iast: na it prāṇebhya ātmānam apādadhāni iti |
meaning: न इत् प्राणेभ्य आत्मानम् अपादधानि इति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yat prathameṣu paryāyeṣu prathameṣu padeṣu ninartayanti |
meaning: अथ यत् प्रथमेषु पर्यायेषु प्रथमेषु पदेषु निनर्तयन्ति |
text: In that in the first rounds they repeat in the first Padas, verily thus from the first night they smite away the Asuras; in that in the middle rounds they repeat in the middle Padas, verily thus from the middle night they smite away the Asuras; in that in the last rounds they repeat in the last Padas, verily thus from the last night they smite away the Asuras. Just as one can by separate repetition and by repeating severally smite away evil again and again, so with these strophes and antistrophes from day and night they smite away the Asuras.

sanskrit_iast: prathama rātrād eva tad asurān nirghnanti |
meaning: प्रथम रात्राद् एव तद् असुरान् निर्घ्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yan madhyameṣu paryāyeṣu madhyameṣu padeṣu ninartayanti |
meaning: अथ यन् मध्यमेषु पर्यायेषु मध्यमेषु पदेषु निनर्तयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: madhya rātrād eva tad asurān nirghnanti |
meaning: मध्य रात्राद् एव तद् असुरान् निर्घ्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yad uttameṣu paryāyeṣu uttameṣu padeṣu ninartayanti |
meaning: अथ यद् उत्तमेषु पर्यायेषु उत्तमेषु पदेषु निनर्तयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: uttama rātrād eva tad asurān nirghnanti |
meaning: उत्तम रात्राद् एव तद् असुरान् निर्घ्नन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā abhyāgāram abhininartam punaḥ punaḥ pāpmanam nirhaṇyāt |
meaning: तद् यथा अभ्यागारम् अभिनिनर्तम् पुनः पुनः पाप्मनम् निर्हण्यात् |

sanskrit_iast: evam eva etat stotriya anurūpair ahorātrābhyām asurān nirghnanti |
meaning: एवम् एव एतत् स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपैर् अहोरात्राभ्याम् असुरान् निर्घ्नन्ति |

text:
They recite the beginnings of the litanies in Gāyatrī verses; the Gāyatrī is brilliance and splendour; verily thereby they place brilliance
and splendour in the sacrificer. Having recited Gāyatrī verses, they recite Jagatī verses; between the Gāyatrī and Jagatī verses they insert the calls; verily thus they make the metres of varied strength. Having recited Jagatī verses, they conclude with Triṣṭubh verses. The Triṣṭubh is might and strength, the Jagatī cattle; verily thus in might and strength at the end and in cattle they find support. The offering verses are in Triṣṭubh, and contain (the words) 'Soma juice', 'be drunk', and 'drink' as their characteristics and are perfect; that is the symbol of night. They should keep awake through the night; keeping awake is the light; the night is the dark, the evil; thereby by the light they cross the dark, the evil. So long as there is no singing or reciting, so long are the Rakṣases able to drink after; therefore 'Do ye lighten up the kindled Āhavanīya, the Āgnīdhriya, the Gārhapatya and the altars' they should say aloud; they should lighten up, it should be light as it were, they should lie snoring; them the evil does not attack (perceiving) 'They are in motion'; they smite away the evil.

sanskrit_iast: teja eva tad brahma varcasam yajamāne dadhati |
meaning: तेज एव तद् ब्रह्म वर्चसम् यजमाने दधति |

sanskrit_iast: vyāhvayante gāyatrīś ca jagatīś ca antare a |
meaning: व्याह्वयन्ते गायत्रीश् च जगतीश् च अन्तरे अ |

sanskrit_iast: chandāṃsy eva etan nānā vīryāṇi kurvanti |
meaning: छन्दांस्य् एव एतन् नाना वीर्याणि कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: bala eva tad vīrye antataḥ paśuṣu ca pratitiṣṭhanti |
meaning: बल एव तद् वीर्ये अन्ततः पशुषु च प्रतितिष्ठन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: andhasvatyo madvatyaḥ pītavatyas triṣṭubho yājyāḥ samṛddhas trilakṣaṇāḥ |
meaning: अन्धस्वत्यो मद्वत्यः पीतवत्यस् त्रिष्टुभो याज्याः समृद्धस् त्रिलक्षणाः |

sanskrit_iast: tena taj jyotiṣā tamaḥ pāpmānam taranti |
meaning: तेन तज् ज्योतिषा तमः पाप्मानम् तरन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: yāvad u ha vai na vā stūyate na vā śasyate |
meaning: यावद् उ ह वै न वा स्तूयते न वा शस्यते |

sanskrit_iast: tāvad īśvarā yadi na asura rakṣasāny anvavapātoḥ |
meaning: तावद् ईश्वरा यदि न असुर रक्षसान्य् अन्ववपातोः |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād āhavanīyam samīddhvam āgnīdhriyam gārhapatyam dhiṣṇyānt samujjvalayata iti bhāṣeran |
meaning: तस्माद् आहवनीयम् समीद्ध्वम् आग्नीध्रियम् गार्हपत्यम् धिष्ण्यान्त् समुज्ज्वलयत इति भाषेरन् |

sanskrit_iast: tān ha tac ceṣṭanti nv ā iti |
meaning: तान् ह तच् चेष्टन्ति न्व् आ इति |

sanskrit_iast: te pāpmānam apaghnate te pāpmānam apaghnate |
meaning: ते पाप्मानम् अपघ्नते ते पाप्मानम् अपघ्नते |

sanskrit_iast: atirikta somo va eṣa yad āśvinam |
meaning: अतिरिक्त सोमो व एष यद् आश्विनम् |
text:
The Āśvina (Śastra) is (a sacrifice) wherein there is a redundancy of Soma; wherein in the sacrifice there is a redundancy, thereby the rival of the sacrificer is energetic against him. In that afterwards he sacrifices to the Aśvins, and the Aśvins are the physicians of the gods, verily thus he makes medicine. Now when Savitṛ gave Sūryā to Soma, the king, he made over to his daughter whether she was Prajāpati's (or his own) on
marriage this thousand (of verses) that was in the possession of these deities; they said ‘Let us run a race for this thousand’; they ran the race; then the Aśvins were victorious by means of the ass. Therefore are many gods celebrated, and yet it is called the Āśvina. Hence, moreover, the ass does not run with his full speed, considering himself worn out (because) ‘I have done my running.’ A thousand should he recite, for a thousand they too won.

sanskrit_iast: atha yatra ha tat savitā sūryām prāyacchat somāya rājñe |
meaning: अथ यत्र ह तत् सविता सूर्याम् प्रायच्छत् सोमाय राज्ञे |

sanskrit_iast: tā abruvann ājim āyāma asmint sahasra iti |
meaning: ता अब्रुवन्न् आजिम् आयाम अस्मिन्त् सहस्र इति |

sanskrit_iast: tata u ha etad uta rāsabho na sarvam iva javam dhāvati |
meaning: तत उ ह एतद् उत रासभो न सर्वम् इव जवम् धावति |

sanskrit_iast: sutam mayā iti hatam manyamānaḥ sahasram śaṃset |
meaning: सुतम् मया इति हतम् मन्यमानः सहस्रम् शंसेत् |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad bṛhatyā āyatanāni pṛṣṭhāni bhavanty atha kasmāt triṣṭubhā pratipadyata iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् बृहत्या आयतनानि पृष्ठानि भवन्त्य् अथ कस्मात् त्रिष्टुभा प्रतिपद्यत इति |
text: They say ‘Seeing that the Pṛṣṭhas depend on the Bṛhatī, then why does he begin with a Triṣṭubh?’ Thrice repeated it makes three Bṛhatī verses and one Gāyatrī. The three Bṛhatī verses are the symbol of union, the Gāyatrī the symbol of the first. In that he produces the Bṛhatī, (it is because) it is with regard to the Bṛhatī that the vow is produced. In that of the strophes in Bṛhatī he recites the first Pragātha, repeating it and making it into Kakubh form, (it is because) the Sāman chanters sing with repetitions; verily thus the symbol of this is produced. He recites the service for Agni; thus he obtains this world. He recites that for Uṣas; thus he obtains the world of the atmosphere. He recites that for the Aśvins; thus he obtains yonder world. He recites the service for Sūrya; there is a fourth world of the gods, the waters; verily thereby he obtains it. He recites a Pragātha; the Pragātha is cattle; verily (it serves) to obtain cattle. Moreover the Pragātha in Bṛhatī is expiration and inspiration; verily thus he places expiration and inspiration in himself; also (it serves) to secure the presence of Indra in the Śastra. He recites (a hymn) to sky and earth; sky and earth are supports; verily (it serves) for support. He recites (a verse) of two Padas; (the verse) of two Padas is a metre in which to find support; verily (it serves) for support. He concludes with (a verse) to Bṛhaspati; Bṛhaspati is the holy power; verily thus in the holy power at the end he finds support. Now this is the completion.

sanskrit_iast: triḥ śastā eṣā tisraś ca bṛhatyaḥ sampadyanta ekā ca gāyatrī |
meaning: त्रिः शस्ता एषा तिस्रश् च बृहत्यः सम्पद्यन्त एका च गायत्री |

sanskrit_iast: idam u ha saṃdhe rūpam yat tisro bṛhatyaḥ |
meaning: इदम् उ ह संधे रूपम् यत् तिस्रो बृहत्यः |

sanskrit_iast: atha yad bārhatīnām pratipadām prathamam prathamam pragātham punar ādāyam kakup kāram śaṃsati |
meaning: अथ यद् बार्हतीनाम् प्रतिपदाम् प्रथमम् प्रथमम् प्रगाथम् पुनर् आदायम् ककुप् कारम् शंसति |

sanskrit_iast: asti vai caturtho deva loka āpaḥ |
meaning: अस्ति वै चतुर्थो देव लोक आपः |

sanskrit_iast: atho prāṇa apānau vai bārhataḥ pragāthaḥ |
meaning: अथो प्राण अपानौ वै बार्हतः प्रगाथः |

sanskrit_iast: pratiṣṭhe vai dyāvā pṛthivī pratiṣṭhityā eva |
meaning: प्रतिष्ठे वै द्यावा पृथिवी प्रतिष्ठित्या एव |

sanskrit_iast: pratiṣṭhānīyam vai chando dvipadā pratiṣhityā eva |
meaning: प्रतिष्ठानीयम् वै छन्दो द्विपदा प्रतिष्हित्या एव |

sanskrit_iast: trīṇi gāyatrī śatāni te dve bṛhatī śate |
meaning: त्रीणि गायत्री शतानि ते द्वे बृहती शते |
text:
Three hundred Gāyatrī verses are two hundred Bṛhatī verses;
seventy Anuṣṭubh and seventy Paṅkti verses are one hundred and forty Bṛhatī verses; deducting a hundred Gāyatrī from three hundred Triṣṭubh verses there are three hundred Bṛhatī verses; the hundred Gāyatrī verses and a hundred Jagatī verses are two hundred Bṛhatī verses; fifty Triṣṭubh and fifty Uṣṇih verses make up a hundred Bṛhatī verses; then there are fifty-seven Bṛhatī verses actually found; the fifty-first and fifty-second Triṣṭubh verses and (the verse) of two Padas are three Bṛhatī verses; thus a thousand Bṛhatīs are made up from a thousand of varied metres. ‘He should not recite over a thousand, nor less than a thousand’ is the rule; the expansion of the Āśvina is however conspicuous. This is a service for Agni; verily he should not fall away from the service for Agni; if he should pass over the service for Agni before the due time, he should apply there whatever in the Āśvina is addressed to two gods in the Ṛcs; in the service for Sūrya (he should use) (the verses) for Soma, the purifying, according to metre, Gāyatrī in Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh in Triṣṭubh, Jagatī in Jagatī; all that is connected with Sūrya in the place of (the service) for Sūrya; all Pragāthas to Indra in the place of the Pragātha; all to sky and earth in the place of (the hymn) to sky and earth; all (verses) of two Padas in the place of (the verse) of two Padas; all addressed to Bṛhaspati before the final verse. That is whatever of the Ṛcs is not set forth.

sanskrit_iast: saptatim anuṣṭubhaḥ saptatim paṅktayaś catvāriṃśat śatam bṛhatīnām |
meaning: सप्ततिम् अनुष्टुभः सप्ततिम् पङ्क्तयश् चत्वारिंशत् शतम् बृहतीनाम् |

sanskrit_iast: trayāṇām triṣṭup śatānām gāyatrī śatam uddhṛtya tāni trīṇi bṛhatī śatāni |
meaning: त्रयाणाम् त्रिष्टुप् शतानाम् गायत्री शतम् उद्धृत्य तानि त्रीणि बृहती शतानि |

sanskrit_iast: tac ca gāyatrī śatam jagatī śatam ca te dve bṛhatī śate |
meaning: तच् च गायत्री शतम् जगती शतम् च ते द्वे बृहती शते |

sanskrit_iast: pañcāśat triṣṭubhaḥ pañcāśad uṣṇihaḥ śatam bṛhatyaḥ sampadyante |
meaning: पञ्चाशत् त्रिष्टुभः पञ्चाशद् उष्णिहः शतम् बृहत्यः सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: atha yāḥ sapta pañcāśatam bṛhatyo atra eva tāḥ sampannātḥ |
meaning: अथ याः सप्त पञ्चाशतम् बृहत्यो अत्र एव ताः सम्पन्नात्ः |

sanskrit_iast: atha ye dvāpañcāśyau triṣṭubhau dvipadā ca tās tiro bṛhatyaḥ sampadyante |
meaning: अथ ये द्वापञ्चाश्यौ त्रिष्टुभौ द्विपदा च तास् तिरो बृहत्यः सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: tan nānāc chandasyānām sahasram sat sahasram bṛhatyaḥ sampadyante |
meaning: तन् नानाच् छन्दस्यानाम् सहस्रम् सत् सहस्रम् बृहत्यः सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: na sahasram atiśaṃsen na arvāk sahasrād ity eṣā ha eva sthitiḥ |
meaning: न सहस्रम् अतिशंसेन् न अर्वाक् सहस्राद् इत्य् एषा ह एव स्थितिः |

sanskrit_iast: pro tv eva āśvinasya vibhūtir iti diśyate |
meaning: प्रो त्व् एव आश्विनस्य विभूतिर् इति दिश्यते |

sanskrit_iast: atha yady āgneyam kratum purā kālāt samatīyāt |
meaning: अथ यद्य् आग्नेयम् क्रतुम् पुरा कालात् समतीयात् |

sanskrit_iast: āśvinam anu yat kiṃca dvidevatyam ṛkṣu tad anuvartayet |
meaning: आश्विनम् अनु यत् किंच द्विदेवत्यम् ऋक्षु तद् अनुवर्तयेत् |

sanskrit_iast: gāyatrīr gāyatre triṣṭubhas traiṣṭubhe jagatīr jāgate |
meaning: गायत्रीर् गायत्रे त्रिष्टुभस् त्रैष्टुभे जगतीर् जागते |

sanskrit_iast: sarvam dyāvā pṛthivīyam dyāvā pṛthivīyasya āyatane |
meaning: सर्वम् द्यावा पृथिवीयम् द्यावा पृथिवीयस्य आयतने |

sanskrit_iast: etad vai kiṃcid iva ṛcām na pradiśyate |
meaning: एतद् वै किंचिद् इव ऋचाम् न प्रदिश्यते |

text:
The Āśvina is like (a wagon) with wheels; the two Ālambanas are the wheels, the aimless verses the axle, (the verse ) ‘Hither your chariot, O Aśvins, with the speed of the falcon’ the seat; the four Agastya hymns the yokes. This is the chariot of the gods. With this chariot of the gods he attains in safety the world of heaven. (The Śastra) should include the Suparṇa; the Suparṇa is a bird; like it becoming a winged one, a bird, so he attains in safety the world of heaven. Twice he utters the call for the Āśvina, for the introduction and for the concluding verse; that is as when one, not being covered, makes a covering by an obstruction. Now comes the question of the conclusion. Whenever the sun creeps over on to the front (of the oblation holder), whenever the Hotṛ himself can discern it,
whenever its ruddiness comes on, whenever all its rays move out towards him, that is the time for the conclusion; for at this time he is freed from evil, severed from evil. He smites away evil, he is severed from evil, who concludes at this time. If there is rain, that is the form of him by which he supports offspring; this breath in the self is one with it; ‘It is not concealed from me’,

sanskrit_iast: ā vām ratho aśvinā śyenapatvā iti sa uddhiḥ |
meaning: आ वाम् रथो अश्विना श्येनपत्वा इति स उद्धिः |

sanskrit_iast: sa etena deva rathena svasti svargaṃl lokam samaśnute |
meaning: स एतेन देव रथेन स्वस्ति स्वर्गंल् लोकम् समश्नुते |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā pakṣi vayo bhūtvā evam tat svasti svargaṃl lokam samaśnute |
meaning: तद् यथा पक्षि वयो भूत्वा एवम् तत् स्वस्ति स्वर्गंल् लोकम् समश्नुते |

sanskrit_iast: dvir eva āśvināya āhvayete pratipade ca eva paridhānīyāyai ca |
meaning: द्विर् एव आश्विनाय आह्वयेते प्रतिपदे च एव परिधानीयायै च |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā pratighātena aniveṣṭyamāno dhāvayed evam tat |
meaning: तद् यथा प्रतिघातेन अनिवेष्ट्यमानो धावयेद् एवम् तत् |

sanskrit_iast: yad eva enam sarve raśmayaḥ pratyupyeran |
meaning: यद् एव एनम् सर्वे रश्मयः प्रत्युप्येरन् |

sanskrit_iast: etasmin ha vā eṣa kāle apahata pāpmā vivikta pāpmā bhavati |
meaning: एतस्मिन् ह वा एष काले अपहत पाप्मा विविक्त पाप्मा भवति |

sanskrit_iast: apahate pāpmānam vivicyate pāpmanā ya etasmin kāle paridadhāti |
meaning: अपहते पाप्मानम् विविच्यते पाप्मना य एतस्मिन् काले परिदधाति |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā asya tad rūpam yena prajā bibharti |
meaning: एतद् वा अस्य तद् रूपम् येन प्रजा बिभर्ति |

sanskrit_iast: idam ekam yad ayam prāṇo adhyātmam |
meaning: इदम् एकम् यद् अयम् प्राणो अध्यात्मम् |

sanskrit_iast: atirohito mad ity eva tam manyamānaḥ paridadhyāt |
meaning: अतिरोहितो मद् इत्य् एव तम् मन्यमानः परिदध्यात् |

text: so regarding it, he should conclude. He should offer a libation to the shining one, when the sun cannot be discerned, he who is unsuited; he becomes then revealed to them. With two (verses) should he sacrifice, for by reason of two it is called the Āśvina. Having recited the Gāyatrī without breathing in, he takes in breath at the half verse of the Virāj; the Virāj is prosperity and proper food; verily thus he finds support in the Virāj as prosperity and proper food. With the second half verse of the Virāj he says the vaṣaṭ call; verily thus he places the sacrificer in the world of heaven. ‘He should use the Virāj only as offering verse’, Kauṣītaki used to say; the Virāj has thirty-three syllables; the gods are thirty-three; the gods he makes to share the syllables. ‘O Aśvins, ye of keen insight, with Vāyu’, is, however, the rule, namely a Triṣṭubh to the Aśvins, containing (the words) ‘Kept over night’, for the Somas are kept over night. Moreover, the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus he places might and strength in the sacrificer. He says the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations. When the Sāman chanters have finished, he offers the two libations of the offering for the choosing (of priests) (thinking) ‘Speech and mind being delighted shall support the great Śastra.’

sanskrit_iast: anavānam gāyatrīm uktvā virājo ardharce avān iti |
meaning: अनवानम् गायत्रीम् उक्त्वा विराजो अर्धर्चे अवान् इति |

sanskrit_iast: śriyām tad virājy anna adye pratitiṣṭhati |
meaning: श्रियाम् तद् विराज्य् अन्न अद्ये प्रतितिष्ठति |

sanskrit_iast: svarga eva tal loke yajamānam dadhāti |
meaning: स्वर्ग एव तल् लोके यजमानम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: virājā eva yajed iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: विराजा एव यजेद् इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: aśvinā vāyunā yuvam sudakṣa iti tv eva sthitā āśvinī triṣṭup tiro ahnyavatī |
meaning: अश्विना वायुना युवम् सुदक्ष इति त्व् एव स्थिता आश्विनी त्रिष्टुप् तिरो अह्न्यवती |

sanskrit_iast: balam eva tad vīryam yajamāne dadhāti |
meaning: बलम् एव तद् वीर्यम् यजमाने दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: saṃsanneṣu chandogeṣu pravṛta homīye āhutī juhoti |
meaning: संसन्नेषु छन्दोगेषु प्रवृत होमीये आहुती जुहोति |

sanskrit_iast: mahat śastram vāk ca manaś ca prīte udyacchātam iti |
meaning: महत् शस्त्रम् वाक् च मनश् च प्रीते उद्यच्छातम् इति |

text:
They proceed with the offering to the yoker of bays; verily thus they delight the two bays; therein the gods with their horses are delighted. Having recited a Triṣṭubh as invitatory verse, he uses a Jagatī as offering verse; the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; the Jagatī is cattle; verily thus in might and strength at the end and in cattle he
finds support. The offering verse contains (the words) 'be drunk', for the third pressing is connected with 'be drunk'. He says the second vaṣaṭ for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations. He should take the most of the grains; the grains are cattle; verily thus he confers a multitude of cattle upon himself. In that they mutter the Ṛc, in that they offer the libation, verily thus they produce a benediction, for the healing of the sacrifice, and for the curing of the sacrificer. They cast them down on the ash border of the Āhavanīya; the Āhavanīya is the birthplace of cattle; verily thus he places them in a secure fold.

sanskrit_iast: atra devāḥ sa aśvāḥ prītā bhavanti |
meaning: अत्र देवाः स अश्वाः प्रीता भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: triṣṭubham hāri yojanasya puronuvākyām anūcya jagatyā yajati |
meaning: त्रिष्टुभम् हारि योजनस्य पुरोनुवाक्याम् अनूच्य जगत्या यजति |

sanskrit_iast: bala eva tad vīrye antataḥ paśuṣu ca pratitiṣṭhati |
meaning: बल एव तद् वीर्ये अन्ततः पशुषु च प्रतितिष्ठति |

sanskrit_iast: madvatī yājyā madvadd hi tṛtīya savanam |
meaning: मद्वती याज्या मद्वद्द् हि तृतीय सवनम् |

sanskrit_iast: bhūmānam eva tat paśūnām ātman dhatte |
meaning: भूमानम् एव तत् पशूनाम् आत्मन् धत्ते |

sanskrit_iast: atha yad ṛcam japanti svastyayanam eva tat kurvate |
meaning: अथ यद् ऋचम् जपन्ति स्वस्त्ययनम् एव तत् कुर्वते |

sanskrit_iast: sva eva enāṃs tad goṣṭhe anapakrame dadhati |
meaning: स्व एव एनांस् तद् गोष्ठे अनपक्रमे दधति |

text: Then they offer the Śākalas. Just as a snake is rid of its old skin, or the stem from reed grass, so are they set free from all evil.

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā ahir jīrṇāyai tvaco nirmucyeta |
meaning: तद् यथा अहिर् जीर्णायै त्वचो निर्मुच्येत |

sanskrit_iast: evam eva ete sarvasmāt pāpmanaḥ sampramucyante |
meaning: एवम् एव एते सर्वस्मात् पाप्मनः सम्प्रमुच्यन्ते |

text: Then turning to the left, they approach the Somas in the waters; they place them here within the altar, for that is the abode of the Soma; they distribute the branches of Darbha grass; when the waters and the plants come together, then the Soma is complete. With a verse to Viṣṇu they pour them down; Viṣṇu is the sacrifice; verily thus they establish them at the end in the sacrifice. Then they stroke the vital organs; verily thus they make whole whatever here has been ill-treated or injured of the vital organs, they cure it. They make enclosures for the food; verily thus the food of the gods they sever from the food of man.

sanskrit_iast: yadā vā āpaś ca auṣadhayaś ca saṃgacchante |
meaning: यदा वा आपश् च औषधयश् च संगच्छन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: yajña eva enāṃs tad antataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayanti |
meaning: यज्ञ एव एनांस् तद् अन्ततः प्रतिष्ठापयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tad yad eva atra prāṇānām krūrī kṛtam yad viliṣṭam tad eva etad āpyāyayanti tad bhiṣajyanti |
meaning: तद् यद् एव अत्र प्राणानाम् क्रूरी कृतम् यद् विलिष्टम् तद् एव एतद् आप्याययन्ति तद् भिषज्यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: mānuṣeṇa eva tad bhakṣeṇa daivam bhakṣam antar dadhate |
meaning: मानुषेण एव तद् भक्षेण दैवम् भक्षम् अन्तर् दधते |

text:
The final bath (is described). Him who yonder gives heat they seek by these pressings to obtain; the rising by the morning pressing, (the sun) in the middle (of his course) by the midday pressing, (the sun) as he sets by the third pressing. He, having entered the waters, becomes Varuṇa; therefore he offers to Varuṇa a cake on one potsherd; prosperity is solitary; Varuṇa is prosperity; verily thus he finds support at the end in prosperity. They depart between the pit and the mound, for that is
the proper path of the sacrifice, named Āpnāna. That is declared in a Ṛc, ‘Who here hath proclaimed the Āpnāna passage?’ Having approached the sacrifice by this passage, they obtained all desires. Verily thus also the sacrificer by this passage having approached the sacrifice obtains all desires.

sanskrit_iast: amum eva etat savanair īpsanti yo asau tapati |
meaning: अमुम् एव एतत् सवनैर् ईप्सन्ति यो असौ तपति |

sanskrit_iast: sa vā eṣo apaḥ praviśya varuṇo bhavati |
meaning: स वा एषो अपः प्रविश्य वरुणो भवति |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād vāruṇam eka kapālam puroḍāśam nirvapanti |
meaning: तस्माद् वारुणम् एक कपालम् पुरोडाशम् निर्वपन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tadd hi yajñasya tīrtham āpnānam nāma |
meaning: तद्द् हि यज्ञस्य तीर्थम् आप्नानम् नाम |

sanskrit_iast: āpnānam tīrtham kim iha pra vocad iti |
meaning: आप्नानम् तीर्थम् किम् इह प्र वोचद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: etena vai devās tīrthena yajñam prapadya sarvān kāmān āpuḥ |
meaning: एतेन वै देवास् तीर्थेन यज्ञम् प्रपद्य सर्वान् कामान् आपुः |

sanskrit_iast: tatho eva etad yajamāna etena eva tīrthena yajñam prapadyate |
meaning: तथो एव एतद् यजमान एतेन एव तीर्थेन यज्ञम् प्रपद्यते |

sanskrit_iast: te yasyām diśy āpo bhavanti tām diśam abhyāvṛtya caranti |
meaning: ते यस्याम् दिश्य् आपो भवन्ति ताम् दिशम् अभ्यावृत्य चरन्ति |
text: Turning to the region in which are the waters, they proceed (with the rite); it is the eastern quarter in which the deities are. He offers four fore-offerings, omitting that for the strew; that for the strew he omits, for the strew is not strewn here. The butter portions contain a reference to the slaying of Vṛtra, for the slaying of evil; moreover, thus he does not depart from the model of the full moon sacrifice. Some make them contain (the words) ‘in the waters’, but the rule is that they should refer to the slaying of Vṛtra. In that he sacrifices to Varuṇa in the waters, verily thus he delights him in his own abode. In that he sacrifices to Agni and Varuṇa, therein Agni becomes a sharer in all the oblations. He offers two after-offerings, omitting that for the strew; he leaves out that for the strew, (thinking) ‘The strew is offspring; let me not cast offspring into the waters.’ There are a hundred and one fore-offerings and after-offerings; man has a hundred (years of) life, has a hundred joints, has a hundred strengths, has a hundred powers; the hundred and first is the body. This is the way of the Aṅgirases; he sets out by this way, he obtains identity of world and union with the Aṅgirases. The six or eight vaṣaṭ calls are the way of the Ādityas; he sets out by this way, he obtains identity of world and union with the Ādityas.

sanskrit_iast: sā vai prācī dig yasyām devatāḥ |
meaning: सा वै प्राची दिग् यस्याम् देवताः |

sanskrit_iast: vārtraghnāv ājya bhāgau bhavataḥ pāpmana eva vadhāya |
meaning: वार्त्रघ्नाव् आज्य भागौ भवतः पाप्मन एव वधाय |

sanskrit_iast: atho ha asya paurṇamāsāt tantrād anitam bhavati |
meaning: अथो ह अस्य पौर्णमासात् तन्त्राद् अनितम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: sva eva enam tad āyatane prīṇāti |
meaning: स्व एव एनम् तद् आयतने प्रीणाति |

sanskrit_iast: atra agniḥ sarveṣu havihṣu bhāgī bhavati |
meaning: अत्र अग्निः सर्वेषु हविह्षु भागी भवति |

sanskrit_iast: na it prajām apsu pravṛṇajāni iti |
meaning: न इत् प्रजाम् अप्सु प्रवृणजानि इति |

sanskrit_iast: ta eka śatam prayāja anuyājā bhavanti |
meaning: त एक शतम् प्रयाज अनुयाजा भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: śata āyur vai puruṣaḥ śata vīryaḥ śata indriyaḥ |
meaning: शत आयुर् वै पुरुषः शत वीर्यः शत इन्द्रियः |

sanskrit_iast: upa ya eka śatatamaḥ sa ātmā |
meaning: उप य एक शततमः स आत्मा |

sanskrit_iast: sa etena ayanena pratipadya aṅgirasām salokatām sāyujyam āpnoti |
meaning: स एतेन अयनेन प्रतिपद्य अङ्गिरसाम् सलोकताम् सायुज्यम् आप्नोति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yāḥ ṣaḍ vā aṣṭau vā vaṣaṭ kṛtayaḥ |
meaning: अथ याः षड् वा अष्टौ वा वषट् कृतयः |

sanskrit_iast: sa etena ayanena pratipadya ādityānām salokatām sāyujyam āpnoti |
meaning: स एतेन अयनेन प्रतिपद्य आदित्यानाम् सलोकताम् सायुज्यम् आप्नोति |

text: The Anūbandhyā (is explained). The offering of the cow is the fourth pressing; therefore is it immovable, for it is the fourth of the pressings. It is offered to Mitra and Varuṇa, for (the victim) for Agni and Soma has been offered before; therefore is it for Mitra and Varuṇa, to secure the equipoise of the sacrifice. Moreover, in that he sacrifices to Varuṇa in the waters, therein is Mitra neglected; therefore is it for Mitra and Varuṇa, to secure Mitra also.

sanskrit_iast: caturtham eva etat savanam yad anūbandhyā |
meaning: चतुर्थम् एव एतत् सवनम् यद् अनूबन्ध्या |

sanskrit_iast: atha yadi paśur āvīto anupākṛto ṃriyeta |
text: If the victim has been brought up but before being prepared for sacrifice dies, he should cause it to be given to the priests; then they should offer another, of the same form and of the same deity. When the Āprīs have been said over it and the fire carried round it, they should lead it northwards and should dispose of it. In the manner of it they should take another. Having forced out their omenta separately and cooked them separately, they should offer them, cutting off portions separately, with one vaṣaṭ call. Having cooked separately the cakes for the victims, and having made portions separately, they should offer them with one vaṣaṭ call. Having cooked separately the oblations and having made portions separately, they should offer them with one vaṣaṭ call. So with the thirds of the intestines, so with the hind portions. ‘Even if, however, but one of the Āprīs has been said, with it should they proceed’ is the rule. The Āprīs are the breaths; verily thus he places the breaths in it. Now (they ask) ‘If (the victim) is eight-footed, how shall it be?’ Having cooked on the slaughtering fire from the skin of the embryo (a portion) shaped like the omentum and from chaff of the pounded grains an embryo itself, they should offer on the slaughterer’s fire to the vaṣaṭ calls of the other. The Rakṣases go to the sacrifice when such a thing occurs; them thereby he smites away; that is not smitten by Rakṣases. So now if that which is to be offered is an animal, but if it is a milk mess (it is because) the milk mess is Mitra and Varuṇa’s own oblation, for it is the rule that to Mitra and Varuṇa the milk mess is offered.

sanskrit_iast: atha anyam tad rūpam tad varṇam ālabheran |
meaning: अथ अन्यम् तद् रूपम् तद् वर्णम् आलभेरन् |

sanskrit_iast: tam āprītam paryagni kṛtam udañcam nayeyuḥ |
meaning: तम् आप्रीतम् पर्यग्नि कृतम् उदञ्चम् नयेयुः |

sanskrit_iast: tayor nānā vape utkhidya nānā śrapayitvā nānā vadāya samāne vaṣaṭ kāre juhuyuḥ |
meaning: तयोर् नाना वपे उत्खिद्य नाना श्रपयित्वा नाना वदाय समाने वषट् कारे जुहुयुः |

sanskrit_iast: tayor nānā eva paśu puroḍāśau śrapayitvā nānā vadāya samāne vaṣaṭ kāre juhuyuḥ |
meaning: तयोर् नाना एव पशु पुरोडाशौ श्रपयित्वा नाना वदाय समाने वषट् कारे जुहुयुः |

sanskrit_iast: tayor nānā eva haviṣī śrapayitvā nānā vadāya samāne vaṣaṭ kāre juyuhuḥ |
meaning: तयोर् नाना एव हविषी श्रपयित्वा नाना वदाय समाने वषट् कारे जुयुहुः |

sanskrit_iast: yadi tv apy ekayā eva āpriya āprītaḥ syāt |
meaning: यदि त्व् अप्य् एकया एव आप्रिय आप्रीतः स्यात् |

sanskrit_iast: tena eva pracureyur iti sā sthitiḥ |
meaning: तेन एव प्रचुरेयुर् इति सा स्थितिः |

sanskrit_iast: atha yady aṣṭāpadī syāt katham syād iti |
meaning: अथ यद्य् अष्टापदी स्यात् कथम् स्याद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: garbhasya tvaco vapā rūpam phālī karaṇān garbham iti śāmitre śrapayitvā itarasya vaṣaṭ kāreṣu śāmitra eva juhuyuḥ |
meaning: गर्भस्य त्वचो वपा रूपम् फाली करणान् गर्भम् इति शामित्रे श्रपयित्वा इतरस्य वषट् कारेषु शामित्र एव जुहुयुः |

sanskrit_iast: rakṣāṃsi ha vā etad yajñam gacchanti yad atra etādṛg bhavati |
meaning: रक्षांसि ह वा एतद् यज्ञम् गच्छन्ति यद् अत्र एतादृग् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: evam nu yadi paśur anūbandhyā bhavati |
meaning: एवम् नु यदि पशुर् अनूबन्ध्या भवति |

text: If the victim is a cow, (it is because) Mitra and Varuṇa are praised with the cow; therefore the victim is a cow. The offering verse for the omentum is ‘Ye two are clothed in garments of fatness’; ‘fatness’ is the symbol of the fat of the omentum. That of the cake is ‘What is most abundant, not to be pierced, O ye rich in dew’; ‘most abundant’, (he says), for the cake is abundant as it were. ‘Do ye stretch forth your arms for life for us’ is that of the oblation; ‘arms’ is the symbol of the members of the oblation.

sanskrit_iast: balam eva tad vīryam yajamāne dadhāti |
meaning: बलम् एव तद् वीर्यम् यजमाने दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: yuvam vastrāṇi pīvasā vasāthe iti vapāyai yājyā |
meaning: युवम् वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे इति वपायै याज्या |

sanskrit_iast: pīvasā it tad vapāyai medaso rūpam |
meaning: पीवसा इत् तद् वपायै मेदसो रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: yad baṃhiṣṭham na atividhe sudānū iti puroḍāśasya |
meaning: यद् बंहिष्ठम् न अतिविधे सुदानू इति पुरोडाशस्य |

sanskrit_iast: baṃhiṣṭham iti bahula iva hi puroḍāśaḥ |
meaning: बंहिष्ठम् इति बहुल इव हि पुरोडाशः |

sanskrit_iast: pra bāhavā sisṛtam jīvase na iti haviṣaḥ |
meaning: प्र बाहवा सिसृतम् जीवसे न इति हविषः |

sanskrit_iast: bāhava iti tadd haviṣo aṅgānām rūpam |
meaning: बाहव इति तद्द् हविषो अङ्गानाम् रूपम् |

text:
He concludes facing north, for north is the world of the living. Having concluded facing north, he offers a full libation with a verse to Viṣṇu; Viṣṇu is the sacrifice; verily thus he grasps the sacrifice. The
cake is offered on five potsherds, for the Paṅkti has five Padas; the sacrifice is fivefold; verily (it serves) to obtain the sacrifice. But, if it is offered on eight potsherds, verily this is the model of the full moon sacrifice; the full moon sacrifice is a support; verily (it serves) for support. In that the invitatory and offering verses are Padapaṅkti verses, this is obviously the symbol of the re-establishment (of the fires). So also are they interwoven. When this has been completed, the sacrificer offers the Agnihotra, for on the completion of the establishment of the fires the Agnihotra is offered; therefore, when this is completed, the sacrificer should offer the Agnihotra, (so they say).

sanskrit_iast: udann udavasāya vaiṣṇavyā ṛcā pūrṇa āhutim juhoti |
meaning: उदन्न् उदवसाय वैष्णव्या ऋचा पूर्ण आहुतिम् जुहोति |

sanskrit_iast: pāṅkto vai yajño yajñasya eva āptyai |
meaning: पाङ्क्तो वै यज्ञो यज्ञस्य एव आप्त्यै |

sanskrit_iast: yady u vā aṣṭā kapālaḥ paurṇamāsam eva tantram bhavati |
meaning: यद्य् उ वा अष्टा कपालः पौर्णमासम् एव तन्त्रम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: idam tv eva pratyakṣam punar ādheyasya rūpam yat pada paṅktayo yājyā puronuvākyāḥ |
meaning: इदम् त्व् एव प्रत्यक्षम् पुनर् आधेयस्य रूपम् यत् पद पङ्क्तयो याज्या पुरोनुवाक्याः |

sanskrit_iast: saṃsthite hy agny ādheye agnihotram hūyate |
meaning: संस्थिते ह्य् अग्न्य् आधेये अग्निहोत्रम् हूयते |

sanskrit_iast: tasmāt tasyām saṃsthitāyām yajamāno agnihotram juhuyād iti yajamāno agnihotram juhuyād iti |
meaning: तस्मात् तस्याम् संस्थितायाम् यजमानो अग्निहोत्रम् जुहुयाद् इति यजमानो अग्निहोत्रम् जुहुयाद् इति |

text: They being about to consecrate themselves gather together the fires; verily thus they place might and strength in one place in themselves. Then they perform the gathering together sacrifice; they offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni of the holy power, to Agni of the lordly power one on eleven potsherds, to Agni, supporter of the lordly power, one on twelve potsherds. Verily thus the sacrificers mount on the holy power and the lordly power; verily thus with them in safety they pass over the year. Of many who are about to pile (the fire) this is the gathering together (offering), connected with the bringing together of the firepan; for one who is about to consecrate himself it is the same.

sanskrit_iast: ekadhā eva tad balam vīryam yajamānā ātman dadhate |
meaning: एकधा एव तद् बलम् वीर्यम् यजमाना आत्मन् दधते |

sanskrit_iast: te agnaye brahmaṇvate aṣṭā kapālam puroḍāśam nirvapanti |
meaning: ते अग्नये ब्रह्मण्वते अष्टा कपालम् पुरोडाशम् निर्वपन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: brahma kṣatre eva tad yajamānāḥ samārohanti |
meaning: ब्रह्म क्षत्रे एव तद् यजमानाः समारोहन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tābhyām eva etat svasti saṃvatsaram taranti |
meaning: ताभ्याम् एव एतत् स्वस्ति संवत्सरम् तरन्ति |

text:
Then they sacrifice with a victim for Prajāpati, (thinking) ‘Instigated by Prajāpati, in safety let us attain this year.’ Some make the cake
for it for Vāyu (saying), ‘Vāyu is clearly the symbol of Prajāpati.’ Others again make it for Agni as desire; Agni as desire is lord of the gods; verily (it serves) to delight all the gods. Some make the cake for the victim for Vaiśvānara; Vaiśvānara is he yonder that gives heat; verily thus they delight him. They make ready beforehand the Soma pressings for the consecration. ‘They should consecrate themselves on one day after the new moon of Taiṣa or of Māgha,’ they say; both of these views are current, but that as to Taiṣa is the more current as it were. They obtain this thirteenth additional month; the year is as great as this thirteenth month; in it verily the whole year is obtained.

sanskrit_iast: prajāpati prasūtāḥ svasti imam saṃvatsaram samaśnavāmahā iti |
meaning: प्रजापति प्रसूताः स्वस्ति इमम् संवत्सरम् समश्नवामहा इति |

sanskrit_iast: etad vai prajāpateḥ pratyakṣam rūpam yad vāyuri iti |
meaning: एतद् वै प्रजापतेः प्रत्यक्षम् रूपम् यद् वायुरि इति |

sanskrit_iast: agnaya u ha eke kāmāya kurvanti |
meaning: अग्नय उ ह एके कामाय कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tasya ha eke vaiśvānarīyam paśu puroḍāśam kurvanti |
meaning: तस्य ह एके वैश्वानरीयम् पशु पुरोडाशम् कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tasya ha eke vaiśvānarīyam paśu puroḍāśam kurvanti |
meaning: तस्य ह एके वैश्वानरीयम् पशु पुरोडाशम् कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: asau vai vaiśvānaro yo asau tapati |
meaning: असौ वै वैश्वानरो यो असौ तपति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yā bahūnām samnivapanīya ukhā sambharaṇīyā sā ekasya dīkṣiṣyamāṇasya bhavati |
meaning: अथ या बहूनाम् सम्निवपनीय उखा सम्भरणीया सा एकस्य दीक्षिष्यमाणस्य भवति |

sanskrit_iast: te purastād eva dīkṣā prasavān kalpayante |
meaning: ते पुरस्ताद् एव दीक्षा प्रसवान् कल्पयन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: taiṣasya amāvāsyāyā eka aha upariṣṭād dīkṣeran |
meaning: तैषस्य अमावास्याया एक अह उपरिष्टाद् दीक्षेरन् |

sanskrit_iast: ta etam trayodaśam adhicaram māsam āpnuvanti |
meaning: त एतम् त्रयोदशम् अधिचरम् मासम् आप्नुवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: etāvān vai saṃvatsaro yad eṣa trayodaśo māsaḥ |
meaning: एतावान् वै संवत्सरो यद् एष त्रयोदशो मासः |
text:
On the new moon of Māgha he rests, being about to turn northwards; these also rest, being about to sacrifice with the introductory Atirātra; thus for the first time they obtain him; on him they lay hold with the Caturviñśa; that is why the laying hold rite has its name. He goes north for six months; him they follow with six-day periods in forward arrangement. Having gone north for six months he stands still, being about to turn southwards; these also rest, being about to sacrifice with the Viṣuvant day; thus for the second time they obtain him. He goes south for six months; him they follow with six-month periods in reverse order. Having gone south for six months he stands still, being about to turn north; these also rest, being about to sacrifice with the Mahāvrata day; thus for the third time they obtain him. In that they obtain him thrice, and the year is in three ways arranged, verily (it serves) to obtain the year. With regard to this this sacrificial verse is sung,
Ordaining the days and nights,
Like a cunning spider,
For six months south constantly,
For six north the sun goeth.
For six months he goes north, six south. They should not consecrate themselves at this time; the corn has not arrived, the days are short; shivering they come out from the final bath. Therefore they should not consecrate themselves at this time. They should consecrate themselves one day after the new moon of Caitra; the corn has come, the days are long, not shivering do they come out from the final bath. Therefore that is the rule.

sanskrit_iast: tad atra eva sarvaḥ saṃvatsara āpto bhavati |
meaning: तद् अत्र एव सर्वः संवत्सर आप्तो भवति |

sanskrit_iast: sa vai māghasya amāvāsyāyām upavasaty udann āvartsyan |

sanskrit_iast: sa ṣaṇ māsān udannitvā tiṣṭhate dakṣiṇā āvartsyan |

sanskrit_iast: upa ime vasanti vaiṣuvatīyena ahnā yakṣyamāṇāḥ |

sanskrit_iast: sa ṣaṇ māsān dakṣiṇetvā tiṣṭhata udann āvartsyan |
meaning: स षण् मासान् दक्षिणेत्वा तिष्ठत उदन्न् आवर्त्स्यन् |

sanskrit_iast: upa ime vasanti māhāvratīyena ahnā yakṣyamāṇāḥ |

sanskrit_iast: ṣaḍḍ hy eṣa māsān udann eti |

sanskrit_iast: atha etām agni cityāyām pañca haviṣam dīkṣaṇīyām iṣṭim eke tanvate |
meaning: अथ एताम् अग्नि चित्यायाम् पञ्च हविषम् दीक्षणीयाम् इष्टिम् एके तन्वते |
text: Then in the piling of the fire some offer this consecration sacrifice consisting of five oblations; the Paṅkti has five Padas; the sacrifice is fivefold; verily (it serves) to obtain the sacrifice. Then some offer this guest reception sacrifice, consisting of five oblations; the Paṅkti has five Padas; the sacrifice is fivefold; verily (it serves) to obtain the sacrifice. Then he recites these many fire (verses); for they carry forward many fires; they are four; all this (universe) is fourfold; verily (they serve) to obtain all this. (He recites) the first thrice and the last thrice; they make up eight; the Gāyatrī has eight syllables; Agni is connected with the Gāyatrī and has the Gāyatrī as metre; verily thus with their own metre they carry forward the fires. Then they pile for so much of the day as they wish. Then they celebrate it when piled with Sāmans. Then they say to the Hotṛ, ‘Mutter the Agni litany’; (the fire) when piled becomes Rudra, the unappeased one of the gods; him verily thus he appeases. He says the offering verse for Vaiśvānara distinctly, for he becomes distinct when they carry forward the fires.

sanskrit_iast: pāṅkto vai yajño yajñasya eva āptyai |

sanskrit_iast: atha etām ātithyām pañca haviṣam eva iṣṭim eke tanvate |
meaning: अथ एताम् आतिथ्याम् पञ्च हविषम् एव इष्टिम् एके तन्वते |

sanskrit_iast: svena eva tac chandasā agnīn praṇayanti |

sanskrit_iast: atha enam cinvanti yāvad aham kāmayante |

sanskrit_iast: atha hotāram āhur agny uktham anuśaṃsa iti |

sanskrit_iast: nirukto hy eṣa tadā bhavati yadā agnīn praṇayanti |

text: Thereafter is as the one-day rite; the moving forward of the oblation holders, the carrying forward of Agni and Soma, the victim for Agni and Soma. The explanation of this has been given. Following on the cake for the victim for Agni and Soma, they offer oblations for the divine instigators; these deities are the lords of the pressings; them herein they delight; they being delighted herein instigate the offerings; therefore are they instigators. They are eight; by them the gods attained all attainments (aṣṭīḥ); verily thus also the sacrificers by them attain all attainments. Here some offer the oblation of (the sacrifice) with all the Pṛṣṭhas, (thinking) ‘The fire piling is all; by all all let us obtain’; there are ten oblations; the Virāj consists of sets of ten; the Virāj is prosperity and proper food; (verily it serves) to obtain the Virāj as prosperity and proper food. Then they press (Soma) for as much of the day as they wish.

sanskrit_iast: havir dhānayoḥ pravartanam agnīṣomayoḥ praṇayanam agnīṣomīyaḥ paśus tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: हविर् धानयोः प्रवर्तनम् अग्नीषोमयोः प्रणयनम् अग्नीषोमीयः पशुस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha agnīṣomīyasya paśu puroḍāśam anvañci devasūbhyo havīṃṣi nirpavanti |
meaning: अथ अग्नीषोमीयस्य पशु पुरोडाशम् अन्वञ्चि देवसूभ्यो हवींषि निर्पवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: etā ha vai devatāḥ savānām īśate |
meaning: एता ह वै देवताः सवानाम् ईशते |

sanskrit_iast: etābhir vai devāḥ sarvā aṣṭīr āśnuvata |
meaning: एताभिर् वै देवाः सर्वा अष्टीर् आश्नुवत |

sanskrit_iast: tatho eva etad yajamānā etābhir eva sarvā aṣṭīr aśnuvate |
meaning: तथो एव एतद् यजमाना एताभिर् एव सर्वा अष्टीर् अश्नुवते |

sanskrit_iast: atra ha eke sarva pṛṣṭhāyai havīṃṣi nirvapanti |
meaning: अत्र ह एके सर्व पृष्ठायै हवींषि निर्वपन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atha anūbandhyasya vapāyām saṃsthitāyām tvāṣṭreṇa paśunā caranti |
meaning: अथ अनूबन्ध्यस्य वपायाम् संस्थितायाम् त्वाष्ट्रेण पशुना चरन्ति |
text:
When (the offering of) the omentum of the Anūbandhyā (cow)
has been completed, they proceed with the victim for Tvaṣṭṛ; that for Tvaṣṭṛ is a pouring of seed; in the hut of the wife they proceed; in wives is seed poured. Inaudibly they proceed; (the victim) for Tvaṣṭṛ is a pouring of seed; inaudibly is seed poured. After surrounding it with fire they let it go; they do not dispose of it, (thinking) ‘(The victim) for Tvaṣṭṛ is a pouring of seed; let us not dispose of seed poured before the time.’ They say ‘Seeing that he invites these two deities, Tvaṣṭṛ and the lord of the forest, in what place are these two sacrificed to by him?’ In the fore-offerings he sacrifices to these two deities; then are these two sacrificed to by him.

sanskrit_iast: na id retaḥ siktam purā kālāt saṃsthāpayāma iti |
meaning: न इद् रेतः सिक्तम् पुरा कालात् संस्थापयाम इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad ete devate āvāhayati tvaṣṭāram ca vanaspatim ca kva asya ete iṣṭe bhavata iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् एते देवते आवाहयति त्वष्टारम् च वनस्पतिम् च क्व अस्य एते इष्टे भवत इति |

sanskrit_iast: atra eva asya ete iṣṭe bhavata iti |
meaning: अत्र एव अस्य एते इष्टे भवत इति |

sanskrit_iast: atha anūbandhyasya paśu puroḍāśam anvañci devikābhyo havīṃṣi nirvapanti |
meaning: अथ अनूबन्ध्यस्य पशु पुरोडाशम् अन्वञ्चि देविकाभ्यो हवींषि निर्वपन्ति |
text: Following on the cake for the victim in the Anūbandhyā rite, they offer the oblations to the minor deities. The metres of him who offers the Soma sacrifice become exhausted; the minor deities are the metres; in that they offer oblations to the minor deities, thus (his metres) become unexhausted and fresh. The metres of him who offers the Soma sacrifice lose their sap; the minor deities are the metres; in that they offer oblations to the minor deities, verily (it serves) to confer sap on the metres. Now these are deities (devī) and Prajāpati is Ka; therefore are they minor deities (devikā). There are five oblations; the Paṅkti has five Padas; the sacrifice is fivefold; verily (it serves) to obtain the sacrifice. Here some offer oblations to the female deities, (thinking) ‘The fire piling is all; by all all let us obtain.’ There are ten oblations; the Virāj consists of sets of ten; the Virāj is prosperity and proper food; (verily it serves) to obtain the Virāj as prosperity and proper food. Here some perform the offerings to appease the quarters, (thinking) ‘The fire piling is all; by all all let us obtain.’ There are six oblations; the year has six seasons; verily (it serves) to obtain the year. When the concluding rite has been completed, he should sacrifice with a milk mess to Mitra and Varuṇa; the explanation of this has been given. ‘No piler of the fire should indulge in sexual union without having offered this sacrifice,’ (they say).

sanskrit_iast: yāta yāmāni ha vā etasya chandāṃsi bhavanti yaḥ somena yajate |
meaning: यात यामानि ह वा एतस्य छन्दांसि भवन्ति यः सोमेन यजते |

sanskrit_iast: tena ha asya ayāta yāmāni punar yāmāni bhavanti |
meaning: तेन ह अस्य अयात यामानि पुनर् यामानि भवन्ति |

meaning: अथो धिर रसानि ह वा एतस्य छन्दांसि भवन्ति यः सोमेन यजन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: pāṅkto vai yajño yajñasya eva āptyai |
meaning: पाङ्क्तो वै यज्ञो यज्ञस्य एव आप्त्यै |

sanskrit_iast: atra ha eke devībhyo havīṃṣi nirvapanti |
meaning: अत्र ह एके देवीभ्यो हवींषि निर्वपन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atra ha eke diśām aveṣṭīḥ kurvanti |
meaning: अत्र ह एके दिशाम् अवेष्टीः कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atha udavasānīyāyām saṃsthitāyām maitrāvaruṇyā payasyayā yajeta tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ उदवसानीयायाम् संस्थितायाम् मैत्रावरुण्या पयस्यया यजेत तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: na etayā aniṣṭvā agnicin maithunam cared iti |
meaning: न एतया अनिष्ट्वा अग्निचिन् मैथुनम् चरेद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: mukham vā etat saṃvatsarasya yac caturviṃśaḥ |
meaning: मुखम् वा एतत् संवत्सरस्य यच् चतुर्विंशः |
text:
The Caturviṅśa is the beginning of the year; therefore it is an Agniṣṭoma, for the Agniṣṭoma is the beginning of the sacrifices; verily thus at the beginning they delight the year. Some make it an Ukthya, for the equipoise of the sacrifice. It has the Caturviṅśa Stoma; the half months of the year are twenty-four; verily (it serves) to obtain the year. There are in it three hundred and sixty Stotriyās; three hundred and sixty are the days of the year; verily (they serve) to obtain the year.
The Pṛṣṭha (Stotra) in it is the Bṛhat (Sāman); this is the second of the days; the Bṛhat is the second of the Pṛṣṭhas; therefore is its Pṛṣṭha the Bṛhat. Again the Mahāvrata is fixed there where they approach the Caturviṅśa; the Bṛhat is in its place the Pṛṣṭha of the Mahāvrata; therefore (they say) ‘Let the Bṛhat be the Pṛṣṭha of this (day).’ It has the word ‘together’; the year is uttered around about. There are in its verses the following symbols. ‘The Hotṛ is born, the wise’ is the Ājya of eight verses in Gāyatrī metre; the Stoma is in Gāyatrī metre; that Śastra is perfect which accords with the Stoma. The Praüga is of Madhuchandas; it is perfect; in its model are other Praügas shaped, (thinking) ‘May I have accomplished a rite successful from the beginning.’ ‘Thee like a car for aid’ is the strophe of the Marutvatīya; ‘This drink, O bright one, is pressed’ is the antistrophe. This is the regular one-day form; the explanation of it has been given.

sanskrit_iast: tasya vai trīṇi ṣaṣṭi śatāni stotriyāṇām bhavanti |
meaning: तस्य वै त्रीणि षष्टि शतानि स्तोत्रियाणाम् भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: trīṇi vai ṣaṣṭi śatāni saṃvatsarasya ahnām |
meaning: त्रीणि वै षष्टि शतानि संवत्सरस्य अह्नाम् |

sanskrit_iast: dvitīyam vā etad ahnām dvitīyam bṛhat pṛṣṭhānām |
meaning: द्वितीयम् वा एतद् अह्नाम् द्वितीयम् बृहत् पृष्ठानाम् |

sanskrit_iast: avadhṛtam vā u tatra mahā vratam |
meaning: अवधृतम् वा उ तत्र महा व्रतम् |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhad u vā āyatanena mahā vratasya pṛṣṭham bhavati |
meaning: बृहद् उ वा आयतनेन महा व्रतस्य पृष्ठम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād bṛhad eva etasya ahnaḥ pṛṣṭham syād iti |
meaning: तस्माद् बृहद् एव एतस्य अह्नः पृष्ठम् स्याद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tasya saṃvat saṃvatsaram abhi paryuditāni chando rūpāṇi |
meaning: तस्य संवत् संवत्सरम् अभि पर्युदितानि छन्दो रूपाणि |

sanskrit_iast: hotā ajaniṣṭa cetana ity aṣṭarcam ājyam gāyatrī mātram |
meaning: होता अजनिष्ट चेतन इत्य् अष्टर्चम् आज्यम् गायत्री मात्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad vai śastram samṛddham yas stomena sampadyate |
meaning: तद् वै शस्त्रम् समृद्धम् यस् स्तोमेन सम्पद्यते |

sanskrit_iast: mādhuc chandasaḥ praugaḥ sa vai samṛddhaḥ |
meaning: माधुच् छन्दसः प्रौगः स वै समृद्धः |

sanskrit_iast: samṛddham me prathamataḥ karma kṛtam asad iti |
meaning: समृद्धम् मे प्रथमतः कर्म कृतम् असद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: ā tvā ratham yathā ūtaya iti marutvatīyasya pratipat |
meaning: आ त्वा रथम् यथा ऊतय इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपत् |

sanskrit_iast: idam vaso sutam andha ity anucaraḥ |
meaning: इदम् वसो सुतम् अन्ध इत्य् अनुचरः |

sanskrit_iast: eṣa eva nitya ekāha ātānas tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: एष एव नित्य एकाह आतानस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīḍā iti marutvatīyam |
meaning: कया शुभा सवयसः सनीडा इति मरुत्वतीयम् |
text:
‘With what array, of one age, of one home?’ is the Marutvatīya. The ninth (verse) is ‘Thou canst not be overthrown, O generous one, no one’; with it he concludes, having recited in front of it the later verses, for they are verses to the Maruts, and this is connected (with Indra) only. There is in this (Śastra) ‘The Maruts are joined together’ containing (the word) ‘together’; thus he refers to the year; this is the symbol of this day. ‘That was the highest in the worlds’ is the Niṣkevalya, of Bṛhaddiva; here the Hotṛ pours seed with the Bṛhaddiva, (thinking) ‘That he propagates yonder with the Mahāvrata day.’ After each year the pouring of seed is fruitful. In this there is ‘Together they sing to thee, brought forward at the carouses,’ containing (the word) ‘together’; thus he refers to the year; this is the symbol of this day. ‘That of Savitṛ we choose’ and ‘To-day for us, O god Savitṛ’ are the normal strophe and antistrophe of the Vaiśvadeva; the explanation of these two has been given. ‘That desirable greatness of Savitṛ, the god’ is the Savitṛ (hymn); it contains (the word) ‘together’ in ‘Wealth with offspring for us together
may he instigate’; thus he refers to the year; this is the symbol of this day. ‘They two, sky and earth, all weal producing’ is (the hymn) to sky and earth; it contains (the word) ‘together’ in ‘Force to be glorified may ye together instigate for us’; thus he refers to the year; this is the symbol of this day. ‘Why hath the best, why hath the youngest come to us?’ is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus; ‘Thus in the year to-day did ye discern’ (it contains); thus openly he refers to the year; this is the symbol of this day. ‘The charioteer of the sacrifice, the lord of the folk’ is the Vaiśvadeva hymn of Śaryāta; it contains (the word) ‘together’ in ‘Together have Indra, Mitra, and Varuṇa pondered’; thus he refers to the year; this is the symbol of this day. ‘To Vaiśvānara the praise, increasing holy order’ is (the hymn) to Vaiśvānara; it contains (the word) ‘together’ in ‘With skill, as (a carpenter’s) axe a car, he brings together’; thus he refers to the year; this is the symbol of this day. ‘To the strong host, majestic, pious’ is (the hymn) to the Maruts; it contains (the word) ‘together’ in ‘Together I adorn the words, powerful in the assemblies’; thus he refers to the year; this is the symbol of this day. ‘With the sacrifice make to increase the All-knower’ is (the hymn) for Jātavedas; it contains (the word) ‘together’ in ‘Together giving riches shine among us’; thus he refers to the year; this is the symbol of the day.
