These are the Āgnimāruta hymns; these are the hymns of this day. So the day is either an Agniṣṭoma or an Ukthya; ‘an Agniṣṭoma is it’ is the view of Pāiṅgya, ‘an Ukthya is it’ is the view of Kauṣītaki.

sanskrit_iast: tasya anuttamā te maghavan nakirnv iti navamī |
meaning: तस्य अनुत्तमा ते मघवन् नकिर्न्व् इति नवमी |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin vā asti samānyā marutaḥ sam mimikṣur iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् वा अस्ति समान्या मरुतः सम् मिमिक्षुर् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad id āsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭham iti bṛhaddivo niṣkevalyam |
meaning: तद् इद् आस भुवनेषु ज्येष्ठम् इति बृहद्दिवो निष्केवल्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhad divena atra hotā retaḥ siñcati |
meaning: बृहद् दिवेन अत्र होता रेतः सिञ्चति |

sanskrit_iast: tad ado mahā vratīyena ahnā prajanayati saṃvatsare |
meaning: तद् अदो महा व्रतीयेन अह्ना प्रजनयति संवत्सरे |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin vā asti sam te navanta prabhṛtā madeṣv iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् वा अस्ति सम् ते नवन्त प्रभृता मदेष्व् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tat savitur vṛṇīmahe adyā no deva savitar iti nityā eva vaiśvadevasya pratipac ca anucaraś ca tayor uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: तत् सवितुर् वृणीमहे अद्या नो देव सवितर् इति नित्या एव वैश्वदेवस्य प्रतिपच् च अनुचरश् च तयोर् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad devasya savitur vāryam mahad iti sāvitram |
meaning: तद् देवस्य सवितुर् वार्यम् महद् इति सावित्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin vā asti prajāvantam rayim asme saminvatv iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् वा अस्ति प्रजावन्तम् रयिम् अस्मे समिन्वत्व् इति |

sanskrit_iast: te hi dyāvā pṛthivī viśva śambhuvā iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam |
meaning: ते हि द्यावा पृथिवी विश्व शम्भुवा इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin vā asti panāyyam ojo asme saminvatam iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् वा अस्ति पनाय्यम् ओजो अस्मे समिन्वतम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kim yaviṣṭho na ājagann ity ārbham |
meaning: किम् उ श्रेष्ठः किम् यविष्ठो न आजगन्न् इत्य् आर्भम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin vā asti saṃvatsara idam adyā vyākhyata iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् वा अस्ति संवत्सर इदम् अद्या व्याख्यत इति |

sanskrit_iast: yajñasya vo rathyam viśpatim viśām iti śāryātam vaiśvadevam |
meaning: यज्ञस्य वो रथ्यम् विश्पतिम् विशाम् इति शार्यातम् वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin vā asti indro mitro varuṇaḥ sam cikitrira iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् वा अस्ति इन्द्रो मित्रो वरुणः सम् चिकित्रिर इति |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin vā asti dhiyā ratham na kuliśaḥ samṛṇvati iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् वा अस्ति धिया रथम् न कुलिशः समृण्वति इति |

sanskrit_iast: vṛṣṇe śardhāya sumakhāya vedhasa iti mārutam |
meaning: वृष्णे शर्धाय सुमखाय वेधस इति मारुतम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin vā asti giraḥ samañje vidatheṣv ābhuva iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् वा अस्ति गिरः समञ्जे विदथेष्व् आभुव इति |

sanskrit_iast: yajñena vardhata jāta vedasam iti jāta vedasīyam |
meaning: यज्ञेन वर्धत जात वेदसम् इति जात वेदसीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmin vā asti saṃdadasvān rayim asmāsu dīdihi iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् वा अस्ति संददस्वान् रयिम् अस्मासु दीदिहि इति |

sanskrit_iast: tadd ha etad ahar eke chandogāḥ sarva stomam kurvanti |
meaning: तद्द् ह एतद् अहर् एके छन्दोगाः सर्व स्तोमम् कुर्वन्ति |
text:
Some Sāman chanters make this day have all the Stomas, (saying) ‘By this day they obtained the six-day period, by the six-day period the year and the desires in the year; the whole year is the six-day period.’ If they do this he should make the Śastra composed of the six-day period. The Ājya should be the Ājya of the first day; the Praüga the Praüga of the second day; the Marutvatīya the Marutvatīya of the third day; the Niṣkevalya the Niṣkevalya of the fourth day; the Vaiśvadeva the Vaiśvadeva of the fifth day; the Āgnimāruta the Āgnimāruta of the sixth day. Then collecting all the verses of the Pṛṣṭha Stotras and making them into Pragāthas he should recite them after the Pragātha, to obtain the six-day period. Just as by this day the Sāman chanters obtain the six-day period
and by the six-day period the year and the desires in the year, so by this day the Hotṛ obtains the six-day period, and by the six-day period the year and the desires in the year. Indicating that he used to say, 'This is confusion.' 'Whatever Stoma the Sāman chanters resort to, that he should not regard; the Śastra which we have here already considered, from that he should not depart; the two hymns "With what array" and "That was" are Stoma subduing; verily he should not fall away from these two' (he used to say).

sanskrit_iast: ṣaḍ aho vā u sarvaḥ saṃvatsara iti vadantaḥ |
meaning: षड् अहो वा उ सर्वः संवत्सर इति वदन्तः |

sanskrit_iast: yat prathamasya ahna ājyam tad ājyam |
meaning: यत् प्रथमस्य अह्न आज्यम् तद् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: yac caturthasya ahno niṣkevalyam tan niṣkevalyam |
meaning: यच् चतुर्थस्य अह्नो निष्केवल्यम् तन् निष्केवल्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: yat pañcamasya ahno vaiśvadevam tad vaiśvadevam |
meaning: यत् पञ्चमस्य अह्नो वैश्वदेवम् तद् वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: yat ṣaṣṭhasya ahna āgnimārutam tad āgnimārutam |
meaning: यत् षष्ठस्य अह्न आग्निमारुतम् तद् आग्निमारुतम् |

sanskrit_iast: tatra pṛṣṭhya stotriyānt sarvānt samāhṛtya upariṣṭāt pragāthasya pragāthī kṛtya śaṃset ṣaḍ ahasya āptyai |
meaning: तत्र पृष्ठ्य स्तोत्रियान्त् सर्वान्त् समाहृत्य उपरिष्टात् प्रगाथस्य प्रगाथी कृत्य शंसेत् षड् अहस्य आप्त्यै |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā eva etena ahnā chandogāḥ ṣaḍ aham āpnuvanti ṣaḍ ahena saṃvatsaram |
meaning: तद् यथा एव एतेन अह्ना छन्दोगाः षड् अहम् आप्नुवन्ति षड् अहेन संवत्सरम् |

sanskrit_iast: evam eva etena ahnā hotā ṣaḍ aham āpnoti ṣaḍ ahena saṃvatsaram |
meaning: एवम् एव एतेन अह्ना होता षड् अहम् आप्नोति षड् अहेन संवत्सरम् |

sanskrit_iast: tadd ha sma etat pradiśya āha sā eṣā mugdhir eva iti |
meaning: तद्द् ह स्म एतत् प्रदिश्य आह सा एषा मुग्धिर् एव इति |

sanskrit_iast: yam kam ca chandogāḥ stomam upāpadyera |
meaning: यम् कम् च छन्दोगाः स्तोमम् उपापद्येर |

sanskrit_iast: ete vā u stoma sāhe sūkte yat kayāśubhīya tadidāsīye |
meaning: एते वा उ स्तोम साहे सूक्ते यत् कयाशुभीय तदिदासीये |

sanskrit_iast: tābhyām eva na niścyaveta iti na niścyaveta iti |
meaning: ताभ्याम् एव न निश्च्यवेत इति न निश्च्यवेत इति |

sanskrit_iast: deva cakram vā etat pariplavam yat saṃvatsaraḥ |
meaning: देव चक्रम् वा एतत् परिप्लवम् यत् संवत्सरः |
text: The year is a revolving wheel of the gods; that is immortality; in it is the there sixfold proper food, wild animals, domesticated animals, plants, trees, that which goes in the waters and that which swims. Mounted on this the gods move round all the worlds, the world of the gods, the world of the fathers, the world of the living, the world of Agni without water, the world of Vāyu, established in moral order, the world of Indra, unconquerable, the world of Varuṇa over the sky, the world of death the highest sky, the world of Brahman the welkin, the most real of worlds the vault. In that they perform the Abhiplava, verily thus the sacrificers mount on the year; in it they obtain this sixfold proper food, wild animals, domesticated animals, plants, trees, that which goes in the waters and that which swims. Twice they perform the Jyotis (Stoma); thereby they obtain a double portion of proper food, wild animals and domesticated animals. Twice they perform the Go; thereby they obtain a double portion of proper food, plants and trees. Twice they perform the Āyus; thereby they obtain a double portion of proper food, that which goes in the waters and that which swims.

sanskrit_iast: tasminn etat ṣaṭ tayam anna adyam |
meaning: तस्मिन्न् एतत् षट् तयम् अन्न अद्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: grāmyāś ca paśava āraṇyāś ca oṣadhayaś ca vanaspatayaś ca apsu caram ca pariplavam ca |
meaning: ग्राम्याश् च पशव आरण्याश् च ओषधयश् च वनस्पतयश् च अप्सु चरम् च परिप्लवम् च |

sanskrit_iast: tad devāḥ samāruhya sarvāṃl lokān anu pariplavante |
meaning: तद् देवाः समारुह्य सर्वांल् लोकान् अनु परिप्लवन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: deva lokam pitṛ lokam jīva lokam |
meaning: देव लोकम् पितृ लोकम् जीव लोकम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasminn etat ṣaṭtayam anna adyam āpnuvanti grāmyāṃś ca paśūn āraṇyāṃś ca oṣadhīś ca vanaspatīṃś ca apsu caram ca pariplavam ca |
meaning: तस्मिन्न् एतत् षट्तयम् अन्न अद्यम् आप्नुवन्ति ग्राम्यांश् च पशून् आरण्यांश् च ओषधीश् च वनस्पतींश् च अप्सु चरम् च परिप्लवम् च |

sanskrit_iast: tena dvayam anna adyam āpnuvanti grāmyāṃś ca paśūn āraṇyāṃś ca |
meaning: तेन द्वयम् अन्न अद्यम् आप्नुवन्ति ग्राम्यांश् च पशून् आरण्यांश् च |

sanskrit_iast: tena dvayam anna adyam āpnuvanty oṣadhīś ca vanaspatīṃś ca |
meaning: तेन द्वयम् अन्न अद्यम् आप्नुवन्त्य् ओषधीश् च वनस्पतींश् च |

sanskrit_iast: tena dvayam anna adyam āpnuvanty apsu caram ca pariplavam ca |
meaning: तेन द्वयम् अन्न अद्यम् आप्नुवन्त्य् अप्सु चरम् च परिप्लवम् च |

text:
They perform the Jyotis as the first day; it has the same symbols in its verses as the first day. ‘Forward to the god Agni’ is the Ājya, containing (the word) ‘forward’; what contains ‘forward’ is a symbol of the first day. The Praüga is by Madhuchandas; when the Rathantara Sāman was created, the Praüga by Madhuchandas was created after it; thus he makes the rite successful with its symbol; that rite is likely to cause success which is successful with its symbol. ‘Thee like a car for aid’ is the strophe of the Marutvatīya; ‘This drink, O bright one, is pressed’ is the antistrophe; this is the normal one-day form; the explanation of it has been given. ‘Indra maketh for the car a way forward’ is the Marutvatīya, containing (the word) ‘forward’; what contains forward is a symbol of the first day. ‘Come hither, standing on thy chariot seat’ is the Niṣkevalya, containing (the word) ‘hither’; what contains ‘hither’ is a symbol of the first day. ‘That of Savitṛ we choose’ and ‘To-day for us, O god Savitṛ’ are the normal strophe and antistrophe of the Vaiśvadeva; the explanation of these two has been given. ‘They yoke their minds, they also yoke their thoughts’ is (the hymn) to Savitṛ, containing (the word) ‘yoke’; what contains ‘yoke’ is a symbol of the first day. ‘Forward sky and earth, increasing holy order, with the sacrifices’ is (the hymn) to sky and earth, containing (the word) ‘forward’; what contains ‘forward’ is a symbol of the first day. ‘Here, here in mind is your relationship, O heroes’ is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus, containing (the word) ‘to’ in ‘Desiring they came to these with wealth’; that is the symbol of the Rathantara. ‘How, of what one of the gods, in this service?’ is (the hymn) to the All-gods, containing the word ‘hither’ in ‘Which one with aid will come hitherward?’; what contains ‘hither’ is a symbol of the first day. ‘To Vaiśvānara with broad radiance bards’ is (the hymn) to Vaiśvānara, containing (the word) ‘forward’; what contains ‘forward’ is a symbol of the first day. ‘Forward pressing, mighty and resounding’ is (the hymn) to the Maruts, containing (the word) ‘forward’; what contains ‘forward’ is the symbol of the first day. ‘The Hotṛ goeth forward to the sacrifice with the power of him’ is (the hymn) to Jātavedas, containing (the word) ‘forward’; what contains ‘forward’ is the symbol of
the first day. This world they move up to with the first day, Agni the god, the name the supreme essence of the deities; they confer speech upon themselves.

sanskrit_iast: tasya tāny eva chando rūpāṇi yāni prathamasya ahnaḥ |
meaning: तस्य तान्य् एव छन्दो रूपाणि यानि प्रथमस्य अह्नः |

sanskrit_iast: pra vo devāya agnaya ity ājyam pravat |
meaning: प्र वो देवाय अग्नय इत्य् आज्यम् प्रवत् |

sanskrit_iast: rathantaram vai sāma sṛjyamānam mādhuc chandasa praugo anvasṛjyata |
meaning: रथन्तरम् वै साम सृज्यमानम् माधुच् छन्दस प्रौगो अन्वसृज्यत |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā ārdhnukam karma yad rūpa samṛddham |
meaning: एतद् वा आर्ध्नुकम् कर्म यद् रूप समृद्धम् |

sanskrit_iast: indro rathāya pravatam kṛṇoti iti marutvatīyam pravat |
meaning: इन्द्रो रथाय प्रवतम् कृणोति इति मरुत्वतीयम् प्रवत् |

sanskrit_iast: ā yāhy arvān upavandhurā iṣṭā iti niṣkevalyam āvat |
meaning: आ याह्य् अर्वान् उपवन्धुरा इष्टा इति निष्केवल्यम् आवत् |

sanskrit_iast: yuñjate mana uta yuñjate dhiya iti sāvitram yuktavat |
meaning: युञ्जते मन उत युञ्जते धिय इति सावित्रम् युक्तवत् |

sanskrit_iast: pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī ṛtāvṛdhā iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam pravat |
meaning: प्र द्यावा यज्ञैः पृथिवी ऋतावृधा इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् प्रवत् |

sanskrit_iast: uśijo jagmur abhi tāni vedasā ity abhivat |
meaning: उशिजो जग्मुर् अभि तानि वेदसा इत्य् अभिवत् |

sanskrit_iast: kathā devānām katamasya yāmanī iti vaiśvadevam |
meaning: कथा देवानाम् कतमस्य यामनी इति वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: katama ūtī abhyā vavartati ity abhivat |
meaning: कतम ऊती अभ्या ववर्तति इत्य् अभिवत् |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānarāya pṛthu pājase vipa iti vaiśvānarīyam |
meaning: वैश्वानराय पृथु पाजसे विप इति वैश्वानरीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmint sumnāni yajamāna ā caka ity āvat |
meaning: तस्मिन्त् सुम्नानि यजमान आ चक इत्य् आवत् |

sanskrit_iast: pratyakṣasaḥ pratavaso virapśina iti mārutam pravat |
meaning: प्रत्यक्षसः प्रतवसो विरप्शिन इति मारुतम् प्रवत् |

sanskrit_iast: ehi pra hotā vratam asya māyayā iti jātavedasīyam pravat |
meaning: एहि प्र होता व्रतम् अस्य मायया इति जातवेदसीयम् प्रवत् |

text:
They perform the Go as the second day; the symbols in its verses are those of the second day. 'Thou hast a glory of rule' is the Ājya containing (the word) 'apart' in 'Thou, O active one (vicarṣaṇe), fame'; this is the symbol of this atmosphere; for this atmosphere is wide apart as it were. The Praüga is by Gṛtsamada; when the Bṛhat Sāman was created, the Praüga by Gṛtsamada was created after it; thus he makes the rite successful with its symbol; that rite is likely to cause success which is successful with its symbol. 'Lord of every man' is the strophe of the Marutvatīya, containing the word 'apart'; the explanation of this has been given. 'Indra alone is the drinker of Soma' is the antistrophe, containing (the word) 'apart' in 'Indra, drinker of the pressed juice, of all life'; the explanation of this has been given. 'Rise up, O Brahmaṇaspati' is addressed to Brahmaṇaspati, and contains (the word) 'up'; there is 'up' in 'Rise up'; the second day has 'up'. 'These thee of many a poet' is the Marutvatīya, containing (the word) 'up'; the explanation of this has been given. 'Thou art mingled with the pressed drink, O Indra' is the Niṣkevalya, containing (the word) 'up' in 'The Stoma, the prayer, the hymn being recited'; the explanation of this has been given. 'Every man of the god that leadeth' is the strophe of the Vaiśvadeva, containing (the word) 'apart'; the explanation of this has been given. 'The god of all, lord of the good' is the antistrophe, containing (the word) 'apart'; the explanation of this has been given. There are two strophes for the Vaiśvadevas, two antistrophes; the year has six seasons and is sixfold; sky and earth are two; these supports are two; this body has six members; day and night are two: these, expiration and inspiration, are two; thus they depart not from the completion of the year, nor from the perfection of the body, nor the perfection of the breaths. 'The god Savitṛ hath appeared, to be praised by us now' is (the hymn) to Savitṛ, containing (the word) 'up'; the explanation of this has been given. 'They two, sky and earth, all weal producing' is (the hymn) to sky and earth, containing (the word) 'apart'; the explanation of this has
been given. ‘My work hath been stretched, now is it stretched again’ is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus, containing the word ‘up’; the explanation of this has been given. ‘I hail the gods, of great fame, for security’ is (the hymn) to the All-gods, containing the word ‘up’; the explanation of this has been given. ‘The might of the swift, strong, ruddy one’ is (the hymn) to Vaiśvānara, containing (the word) ‘strong’; Indra is strong, the Triṣṭubh is strong; therefore it contains ‘strong’. ‘To the strong host, majestic, pious’ is (the hymn) to the Maruts; the explanation of this has been given. ‘By the sacrifice make to increase the All-knower’ is (the hymn) to Jātavedas containing ‘up’ in ‘Kindled, well fed, hero of heaven’; the explanation of this has been given. The world of the atmosphere with the second day they obtain, Indra the god, force the supreme essence of the deities; they confer breath upon themselves.

sanskrit_iast: tasya tāny eva chando rūpāṇi yāni dvitīyasya ahnaḥ |
meaning: तस्य तान्य् एव छन्दो रूपाणि यानि द्वितीयस्य अह्नः |

sanskrit_iast: tvam hi kṣaitavad yaśa ity ājyam |
meaning: त्वम् हि क्षैतवद् यश इत्य् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhad vai sāma sṛjyamānam gārtsamadaḥ praugo anvasṛjyata |
meaning: बृहद् वै साम सृज्यमानम् गार्त्समदः प्रौगो अन्वसृज्यत |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā ārdhnukam karma yad rūpa samṛddham |
meaning: एतद् वा आर्ध्नुकम् कर्म यद् रूप समृद्धम् |

sanskrit_iast: viśvānarasya vaspatim iti marutvatīyasya pratipad vivatī tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: विश्वानरस्य वस्पतिम् इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपद् विवती तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: indra it somapā eka ity anucaraḥ |
meaning: इन्द्र इत् सोमपा एक इत्य् अनुचरः |

sanskrit_iast: indraḥ sutapā viśva āyur iti vivāṃs tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: इन्द्रः सुतपा विश्व आयुर् इति विवांस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: imā u tvā purutamasya kāror iti udvat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: इमा उ त्वा पुरुतमस्य कारोर् इति उद्वत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: suta it tvam nimiśla indra soma iti niṣkevalyam |
meaning: सुत इत् त्वम् निमिश्ल इन्द्र सोम इति निष्केवल्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: stome brahmaṇi śasyamāna uktha ity udvat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: स्तोमे ब्रह्मणि शस्यमान उक्थ इत्य् उद्वत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: viśvo devasya netur iti vaiśvadevasya pratipad vivatī tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: विश्वो देवस्य नेतुर् इति वैश्वदेवस्य प्रतिपद् विवती तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: ā viśvadevam satpatim ity anucaro vivāṃs tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: आ विश्वदेवम् सत्पतिम् इत्य् अनुचरो विवांस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: anu dve dyāvā pṛthivī dve ime pratiṣṭhe |
meaning: अनु द्वे द्यावा पृथिवी द्वे इमे प्रतिष्ठे |

sanskrit_iast: anu tan na saṃvatsara sampado yanti |
meaning: अनु तन् न संवत्सर सम्पदो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: na ātma saṃskṛter na prāṇa saṃskṛteḥ |
meaning: न आत्म संस्कृतेर् न प्राण संस्कृतेः |

sanskrit_iast: abhūd devaḥ savitā vandyo nu na iti sāvitram udvat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अभूद् देवः सविता वन्द्यो नु न इति सावित्रम् उद्वत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: te hi dyāvā pṛthivī viśva śambhuvā iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam vivat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: ते हि द्यावा पृथिवी विश्व शम्भुवा इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् विवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: tatam me apas tad u tāyate punar ity ārbhavam udvat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: ततम् मे अपस् तद् उ तायते पुनर् इत्य् आर्भवम् उद्वत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: devān huve bṛhat śravasaḥ svastaya iti vaiśvadevam udvat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: देवान् हुवे बृहत् श्रवसः स्वस्तय इति वैश्वदेवम् उद्वत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: pṛkṣasya vṛṣṇo aruṣasya nū saha iti vaiśvānarīyam vṛṣaṇvat |
meaning: पृक्षस्य वृष्णो अरुषस्य नू सह इति वैश्वानरीयम् वृषण्वत् |

sanskrit_iast: vṛṣṇe śardhāya sumakhāya vedhasa iti mārutam vṛṣaṇvat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: वृष्णे शर्धाय सुमखाय वेधस इति मारुतम् वृषण्वत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: samidhānam suprayasam svarṇaram ity udvat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: समिधानम् सुप्रयसम् स्वर्णरम् इत्य् उद्वत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

text:
They perform the Āyus as the third day; the symbols in its verses are those of the third day. ‘Thou, O Agni, the Vasus here’ is the Ājya; self collected is that metre which accords with the symbol of the day; there is (the word) ‘thou’ in ‘O thou of the ruddy steeds, singer, bring hither the three and thirty’; that is the symbol of the third day. The Praüga is in Uṣṇih verses by Viśvamanas; when the Rathantara Sāman was created, the Praüga in Uṣṇih by Viśvamanas was created after it; thus he makes the rite successful with its symbol; that rite is likely to cause success which is successful with its symbol. ‘Him for great gain’ is the strophe of the Marutvatīya; at ‘him’ there is a repetition; the third day is the end; having gone to the end he repeats as it were, for hence whitherward should he go? ‘Three Soma draughts for Indra’ is the antistrophe. This is the symbol of the third day. ‘Let Brahmaṇaspati move forward’, containing (the word) ‘forward’, is addressed to Brahmaṇaspati; there is repetition in ‘Forward let the kindly goddess move’; the third day is the end; having gone to the end he repeats as it were; for hence whitherward should he go? There are three strophes of the Marutvatīyas, three antistrophes, three (Pragāthas) for Brahmaṇaspati;
these worlds are three; verily thus they obtain these worlds. ‘Stand on the bays being yoked to the car’ is (the hymn ) containing (the word) ‘stand’; it is the symbol of the end; the third day is the end; having gone to the end he stands as it were, for hence whitherward should he go. ‘I shall proclaim the manly deeds of Indra’ is the Niṣkevalya; it contains the symbol of ending in the reference to what has been; ‘He slew the dragon, he penetrated the waters’ is about what has been as it were. ‘Hitherwards the god Savitṛ with the golden’ is (the hymn) to Savitṛ; it contains (the word) ‘ghee’ in ‘With ghee both hands he imbueth, the sacrificer’; the ghee has many deities; the third pressing has many deities; therefore it contains (the word) ‘ghee’. ‘In ghee sky and earth enveloped’ is (the hymn) to sky and earth, containing (the word) ‘ghee’; the explanation of this has been given. ‘They have wrought the car well covered, skilled workers’ is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus; there is repetition in ‘They have wrought the two steeds, that bear Indra, strong in riches’; the third day is the end; having come to the end he repeats as it were, for hence whitherward should he go? ‘To us from all sides may favouring powers come’ is (the hymn) for the All-gods; there is repetition in ‘Unfailing guardians day by day’; the third day is the end; having gone to the end, he repeats as it were, for hence whitherward should he go? ‘To Vaiśvānara, the praise, increasing holy order’ is (the hymn) to Vaiśvānara; in ‘Like purified ghee to Agni we present’ it contains (the word) ‘ghee’; the explanation of this has been given. ‘The Rudras, with Indra, accordant’ is (the hymn) to the Maruts; it contains the words ‘from the sky’ in ‘Like springs of water from the sky for a thirsty man’; this is the symbol of yonder world. ‘Thee, O Agni, the righteous have kindled’ is (the hymn) to Jātavedas, beginning with the same word ‘Thee’ (in each verse); just as that with the same end, so that with the same beginning is a symbol of the end. They obtain yonder world with the third day, Āditya the god, the form the supreme essence of the deities; they confer sight upon themselves.

sanskrit_iast: tasya tāny eva chando rūpāṇi yāni tṛtīyasya ahnaḥ |
meaning: तस्य तान्य् एव छन्दो रूपाणि यानि तृतीयस्य अह्नः |

sanskrit_iast: tvam agne vasūṃr iha ity ājyam |
meaning: त्वम् अग्ने वसूंर् इह इत्य् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: svayam sambhṛtam vā etac chando yad ahno rūpeṇa sampadyate |
meaning: स्वयम् सम्भृतम् वा एतच् छन्दो यद् अह्नो रूपेण सम्पद्यते |

sanskrit_iast: tān rohid aśva girvaṇas trayas triṃśatam ā vaha iti |
meaning: तान् रोहिद् अश्व गिर्वणस् त्रयस् त्रिंशतम् आ वह इति |

sanskrit_iast: rathantaram vai sāma sṛjyamānam auṣṇiho vaiśvamanasaḥ praugo anvasṛjyata |
meaning: रथन्तरम् वै साम सृज्यमानम् औष्णिहो वैश्वमनसः प्रौगो अन्वसृज्यत |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā ārdhnukam karma yad rūpa samṛddham |
meaning: एतद् वा आर्ध्नुकम् कर्म यद् रूप समृद्धम् |

sanskrit_iast: taṃtam id rādhase maha iti marutvatīyasya pratipat |
meaning: तंतम् इद् राधसे मह इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपत् |

sanskrit_iast: traya iti tat tṛtīyasya ahno rūpam |
meaning: त्रय इति तत् तृतीयस्य अह्नो रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: pra devy etu sūnṛtā iti ninartiḥ |
meaning: प्र देव्य् एतु सूनृता इति निनर्तिः |

sanskrit_iast: tisro marutvatīyānām pratipadas trayo anucarās trayo brāhmaṇaspatyāḥ |
meaning: तिस्रो मरुत्वतीयानाम् प्रतिपदस् त्रयो अनुचरास् त्रयो ब्राह्मणस्पत्याः |

sanskrit_iast: tiṣṭhā harī ratha ā yujyamānā iti marutvatīyam |
meaning: तिष्ठा हरी रथ आ युज्यमाना इति मरुत्वतीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam iti niṣkevalyam |
meaning: इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्र वोचम् इति निष्केवल्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasya tad eva anta rūpam yad bhūta anuvādy ahann ahim anvapas tatarda iti |
meaning: तस्य तद् एव अन्त रूपम् यद् भूत अनुवाद्य् अहन्न् अहिम् अन्वपस् ततर्द इति |

sanskrit_iast: ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayā iti sāvitram |
meaning: उद् उ ष्य देवः सविता हिरण्यया इति सावित्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtena pāṇī abhi pruṣṇute makha iti ghṛtavat |
meaning: घृतेन पाणी अभि प्रुष्णुते मख इति घृतवत् |

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtena dyāvā pṛthivī abhīvṛte iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam ghṛtavat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: घृतेन द्यावा पृथिवी अभीवृते इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् घृतवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: takṣan ratham suvṛtam vidmanā apasa ity ārbhavam |
meaning: तक्षन् रथम् सुवृतम् विद्मना अपस इत्य् आर्भवम् |

sanskrit_iast: takṣan harī indra vāhā vṛṣaṇ vasū iti ninartiḥ |
meaning: तक्षन् हरी इन्द्र वाहा वृषण् वसू इति निनर्तिः |

sanskrit_iast: ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvata iti vaiśvadevam |
meaning: आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वत इति वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: aprāyuvo rakṣitāro dived iva iti ninartiḥ |
meaning: अप्रायुवो रक्षितारो दिवेद् इव इति निनर्तिः |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānarāya dhiṣaṇām ṛtā vṛdha iti vaiśvānarīyam |
meaning: वैश्वानराय धिषणाम् ऋता वृध इति वैश्वानरीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtam na pūtam agnaye janām asi iti ghṛtavat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: घृतम् न पूतम् अग्नये जनाम् असि इति घृतवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: ā rudrāsa indravantaḥ sajoṣasa iti mārutam |
meaning: आ रुद्रास इन्द्रवन्तः सजोषस इति मारुतम् |

sanskrit_iast: tṛṣṇaje na diva utsā udanyava iti |
meaning: तृष्णजे न दिव उत्सा उदन्यव इति |

sanskrit_iast: diva iti tad amuṣya lokasya rūpam |
meaning: दिव इति तद् अमुष्य लोकस्य रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: tvām agna ṛtāyavaḥ samīdhira iti jātavedasīyam |
meaning: त्वाम् अग्न ऋतायवः समीधिर इति जातवेदसीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: yathā vai sodarkam evam saprabhṛty anta rūpam |
meaning: यथा वै सोदर्कम् एवम् सप्रभृत्य् अन्त रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: rūpam adhibhūtam cakṣur ātman dadhate cakṣur ātman dadhate |
meaning: रूपम् अधिभूतम् चक्षुर् आत्मन् दधते चक्षुर् आत्मन् दधते |

sanskrit_iast: devā vai mṛtyum pāpmānam apajighāṃsamānā brahmaṇaḥ salokatām sāyujyam īpsanta etam abhiplavam ṣaḍaham apaśyan |
meaning: देवा वै मृत्युम् पाप्मानम् अपजिघांसमाना ब्रह्मणः सलोकताम् सायुज्यम् ईप्सन्त एतम् अभिप्लवम् षडहम् अपश्यन् |
text: The gods, desirous of smiting away death, the evil, and desiring identity of world and union with Brahman, saw this Abhiplava six-day (rite); by this Abhiplava they approach, and having smitten away death, the evil, obtained identity of world and union with Brahman; verily thus also the sacrificers approach by the Abhiplava, and having smitten away death, the evil, obtain identity of world and union with Brahman. Having approached with the first set of three days, they sacrificed on the fourth day with the Go, for going; they performed the Āyus as the fifth day, to secure full life; the Jyotis as the sixth day they put around behind again, to prevent evil following after.

sanskrit_iast: ta etena abhiplavena abhiplutya mṛtyum pāpmānam apahatya brahmaṇaḥ salokatām sāyujyam āpuḥ |
meaning: त एतेन अभिप्लवेन अभिप्लुत्य मृत्युम् पाप्मानम् अपहत्य ब्रह्मणः सलोकताम् सायुज्यम् आपुः |

sanskrit_iast: tatho eva etad yajamānā etena eva abhiplavena abhiplutya mṛtyum pāpmānam apahatya brahmaṇaḥ salokatām sāyujyam āpnuvanti |
meaning: तथो एव एतद् यजमाना एतेन एव अभिप्लवेन अभिप्लुत्य मृत्युम् पाप्मानम् अपहत्य ब्रह्मणः सलोकताम् सायुज्यम् आप्नुवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: ta etena pūrveṇa tryaheṇa abhiplutya gavā caturthe ahann ayatanta gamanāya eva |
meaning: त एतेन पूर्वेण त्र्यहेण अभिप्लुत्य गवा चतुर्थे अहन्न् अयतन्त गमनाय एव |

sanskrit_iast: āpyuḥ pañcamam ahar upāyant sarva āyutvāya |
meaning: आप्युः पञ्चमम् अहर् उपायन्त् सर्व आयुत्वाय |

sanskrit_iast: jyotiḥ ṣaṣṭham ahaḥ punaḥ parastāt paryāsyan mṛtyor eva pāpmano na anvavāyanāya |
meaning: ज्योतिः षष्ठम् अहः पुनः परस्तात् पर्यास्यन् मृत्योर् एव पाप्मनो न अन्ववायनाय |

text:
They perform the Go as the fourth day; the symbols in its verses are those of the fourth day. ‘The Hotṛ is born, the wise’ is the Ājya, containing (the word) ‘born’; that which contains (the word) ‘born’ is a symbol of the fourth day. The Praüga is by Medhātithi; as the Bṛhat Sāman was created, the Praüga by Medhātithi was created after it; thus he makes the rite successful with its symbol; that rite is likely to cause success which is successful with its symbol. ‘Thou hast been born dread, for impetuous strength’ is the Marutvatīya, containing (the word) ‘born’; that which contains ‘born’ is a symbol of the fourth day. ‘He hath been born dread for strength, possessed of will’ is the Niṣkevalya, containing (the word) ‘born’; that which contains (the word) ‘born’ is a symbol of the fourth day. ‘That desirable greatness of the god Savitṛ’ is (the hymn) to Savitṛ, containing (the word) ‘born’ in ‘Savitṛ hath made to be born the hymn of good will’; that which contains (the word) ‘born’ is a symbol of the fourth day. ‘They two, sky and earth, all weal producing’ is (the hymn) to sky and earth, containing (the word) ‘born’ in ‘Between the two presses of noble birth he goeth’; that which contains (the word) ‘born’ is a symbol of the
fourth day: ‘Born without steed, without reins, worthy of praise’ is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus, containing (the word) ‘born’; that which contains (the word) ‘born’ is a symbol of the fourth day. ‘Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman’ is (the hymn) to the All-gods, containing (the word) ‘born’ in ‘Having caused the sacrifice to be born they wipe their bodies’; that which contains (the word) ‘born’ is a symbol of the fourth day. ‘To Vaiśvānara with broad radiance bards’ is (the hymn) to Vaiśvānara, containing (the word) ‘hither’ in ‘In him the sacrificer looks hither for favour’; that which contains (the word) ‘hither’ is a symbol of the fourth day as an opening ceremony, for the fourth day is a repetition of the opening ceremony. In ‘Born thou didst fill the worlds, the two firmaments’, it contains (the word) ‘born’; that which contains (the word) ‘born’ is a symbol of the fourth day. ‘Those that shine forth, like women, the racers’ is (the hymn) to the Maruts, containing (the word) ‘born’; that which contains (the word) ‘born’ is a symbol of the fourth day. ‘He hath been born, guardian of men, wakeful’ is (the hymn) to Jātavedas, containing (the word) ‘born’; that which contains (the word) ‘born’ is a symbol of the fourth day. Food with the fourth day they obtain, the moon the god, the quarters the supreme essence of the deities; the ear they confer upon themselves.

sanskrit_iast: tasya tāny eva chando rūpāṇi yāni caturthasya ahnaḥ |
meaning: तस्य तान्य् एव छन्दो रूपाणि यानि चतुर्थस्य अह्नः |

sanskrit_iast: hotā ajaniṣṭa cetana ity ājyam jātavat |
meaning: होता अजनिष्ट चेतन इत्य् आज्यम् जातवत् |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhad vai sāma sṛjyamānam maidhātithaḥ praugo anvasṛjyata |
meaning: बृहद् वै साम सृज्यमानम् मैधातिथः प्रौगो अन्वसृज्यत |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā ārdhnikam karma yad rūpa samṛddham |
meaning: एतद् वा आर्ध्निकम् कर्म यद् रूप समृद्धम् |

sanskrit_iast: janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāya iti marutvatīyam jātavad |
meaning: जनिष्ठा उग्रः सहसे तुराय इति मरुत्वतीयम् जातवद् |

sanskrit_iast: ugro jajñe vīryāya svadhāvān iti niṣkevalyam jātavat |
meaning: उग्रो जज्ञे वीर्याय स्वधावान् इति निष्केवल्यम् जातवत् |

sanskrit_iast: tad devasya savitur vāryam mahad iti sāvitram |
meaning: तद् देवस्य सवितुर् वार्यम् महद् इति सावित्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: ajījanat savitā suṃram ukthyam iti jātavat |
meaning: अजीजनत् सविता सुंरम् उक्थ्यम् इति जातवत् |

sanskrit_iast: te hi dyāvā pṛthivī viśva śambhuvā iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam |
meaning: ते हि द्यावा पृथिवी विश्व शम्भुवा इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: anaśvo jāto anabhīśur ukthya ity ārbhavam jātavat |
meaning: अनश्वो जातो अनभीशुर् उक्थ्य इत्य् आर्भवम् जातवत् |

sanskrit_iast: agnir indro varuṇo mitro aryamā iti vaiśvadevam |
meaning: अग्निर् इन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा इति वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: yajñam janitvī tanvī ni māmṛjur iti jātavat |
meaning: यज्ञम् जनित्वी तन्वी नि मामृजुर् इति जातवत् |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānarāya pṛthu pājase vipa iti vaiśvānarīyam |
meaning: वैश्वानराय पृथु पाजसे विप इति वैश्वानरीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmint sumnāni yajamāna ā caka ity āvat |
meaning: तस्मिन्त् सुम्नानि यजमान आ चक इत्य् आवत् |

sanskrit_iast: āvad vai caturthasya ahnaḥ prāyaṇīya rūpam |
meaning: आवद् वै चतुर्थस्य अह्नः प्रायणीय रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: jāta āpṛṇo bhuvanāni rodasī iti jātavat |
meaning: जात आपृणो भुवनानि रोदसी इति जातवत् |

sanskrit_iast: pra ye śumbhante janayo na saptaya iti mārutam jātavat |
meaning: प्र ये शुम्भन्ते जनयो न सप्तय इति मारुतम् जातवत् |

sanskrit_iast: janasya gopā ajaniṣṭa jāgṛvir iti jātavedasīyam jātavat |
meaning: जनस्य गोपा अजनिष्ट जागृविर् इति जातवेदसीयम् जातवत् |

text:
They perform the Āyus as the fifth day; the symbols in its verses are those of the fifth day. ‘O Agni, bring the mightiest’ is the Ājya, containing (the word) ‘wealth’ in (the word) ‘wealth’ in ‘Forward for us with wealth, with abundance’; containing (the word) ‘wealth’ is a symbol of this (day); it also contains an addition; this is the symbol of the Paṅkti. The Praüga is one to be gathered together; when the Rathantara Sāman was created, the Praüga which is to be gathered together was created after it; thus he makes the rite successful with its symbol; that rite is likely to cause success, which is successful with its symbol. ‘Where is this hero, who hath seen Indra?’ is the Marutvatīya, containing (the word) ‘wealth’ in (the word) ‘wealth’ in ‘The bearer of the bolt seeking the pressed Soma with wealth’; containing (the word) ‘wealth’ is the symbol of this. ‘Come, let us approach Indra, seeking for cows’ is the Niṣkevalya, containing (the word) ‘cattle’ in ‘seeking for cows’; con-
taining (the word) ‘cattle’ is the symbol of this. ‘Hitherward the god Savitṛ with the golden’ is (the hymn) to Savitṛ, containing (the word) ‘ghee’ in ‘With ghee both hands he imbueth, the sacrificer’; in ‘ghee’ it contains (the word) ‘cattle’; containing (the word) ‘cattle’ is a symbol of this. ‘Rich in ghee, encompassing the worlds’ is (the hymn) to sky and earth, containing (the word) ‘ghee’; the explanation of this has been given. ‘My work hath been stretched; now is it stretched again’ is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus, containing (the word) ‘ghee’ in ‘As ghee with the ladle let us offer with knowledge’; the explanation of this has been given. ‘How, of what one of the gods, in this service?’ is (the hymn) to the All-gods, containing (the word) ‘cattle’ in ‘Winners of thousands’ in ‘Winners of thousands in the attainment of the offering, by themselves’; containing (the word) ‘cattle’ is the symbol of this. ‘The might of the swift, strong, ruddy one’ is (the hymn) to Vaiśvānara, containing (the word) ‘cattle’ in ‘the bulls’ in ‘The bulls seized them in the lap of the waters’; containing (the word) ‘cattle’ is the symbol of this. ‘Your spy hath called to you to accord favour’ is (the hymn) to the Maruts, containing (the word) ‘cattle’ in ‘as of kine’ in ‘As of kine the lofty horn for splendour’; containing (the word) ‘cattle’ is the symbol of this. ‘Wonderous is the growth of the tender young one’ is (the hymn) to Jātavedas, containing (the word) ‘strong’ in ‘To the most strong, the mighty, O thou of a good father’; this is a symbol of this day; it contains an addition. Cattle by the fifth day they obtain, Rudra the god, fame the supreme essence of the deities; they confer strength upon themselves.

sanskrit_iast: tasya tāny eva chando rūpāṇi yāni pañcamasya ahnaḥ |
meaning: तस्य तान्य् एव छन्दो रूपाणि यानि पञ्चमस्य अह्नः |

sanskrit_iast: agna ojiṣṭham ā bhara ity ājyam |
meaning: अग्न ओजिष्ठम् आ भर इत्य् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: pra no rāyā parīṇasā iti rāyā it rayimat |
meaning: प्र नो राया परीणसा इति राया इत् रयिमत् |

sanskrit_iast: rathantaram vai sāma sṛjyamānam saṃhāryaḥ praugo anvasṛjyata |
meaning: रथन्तरम् वै साम सृज्यमानम् संहार्यः प्रौगो अन्वसृज्यत |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā ārdhnukam karma yad rūpa samṛddham |
meaning: एतद् वा आर्ध्नुकम् कर्म यद् रूप समृद्धम् |

sanskrit_iast: kva sya vīraḥ ko apaśyad indram iti marutvatīyam |
meaning: क्व स्य वीरः को अपश्यद् इन्द्रम् इति मरुत्वतीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: yo rāyā vajrī suta somam icchann iti rayā iti rayimat |
meaning: यो राया वज्री सुत सोमम् इच्छन्न् इति रया इति रयिमत् |

sanskrit_iast: etāyām ā upa gavuaṃta indram iti niṣkevalyam |
meaning: एतायाम् आ उप गवुअंत इन्द्रम् इति निष्केवल्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayā iti sāvitram |
meaning: उद् उ ष्य देवः सविता हिरण्यया इति सावित्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtena pāṇī abhi pruṣṇute makha iti ghṛtena iti paśumat |
meaning: घृतेन पाणी अभि प्रुष्णुते मख इति घृतेन इति पशुमत् |

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtavatī bhuvanānām abhiśriyā iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam ghṛtavat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: घृतवती भुवनानाम् अभिश्रिया इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् घृतवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: tatam me apas tad u tāyate punar ity ārbhavam |
meaning: ततम् मे अपस् तद् उ तायते पुनर् इत्य् आर्भवम् |

sanskrit_iast: srucā iva ghṛtam juhavāma vidmanā iti ghṛtavat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: स्रुचा इव घृतम् जुहवाम विद्मना इति घृतवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: kathā devānām katamasya yāmanī iti vaiśvadevam |
meaning: कथा देवानाम् कतमस्य यामनी इति वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: sahasrasā medhasātāv iva tmanā iti sahasrasā iti paśumat |
meaning: सहस्रसा मेधसाताव् इव त्मना इति सहस्रसा इति पशुमत् |

sanskrit_iast: pṛkṣasya vṛṣṇo aruṣasya nū saha iti vaiśvānarīyam |
meaning: पृक्षस्य वृष्णो अरुषस्य नू सह इति वैश्वानरीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: apām upasthe mahiṣā agṛbhṇata iti mahiṣā iti paśumat |
meaning: अपाम् उपस्थे महिषा अगृभ्णत इति महिषा इति पशुमत् |

sanskrit_iast: pravaḥ spaḍakrant suvitāya dāvana iti mārutam |
meaning: प्रवः स्पडक्रन्त् सुविताय दावन इति मारुतम् |

sanskrit_iast: gavām iva śriyase śṛṅgam uttamam iti gavām iva iti paśumat |
meaning: गवाम् इव श्रियसे शृङ्गम् उत्तमम् इति गवाम् इव इति पशुमत् |

sanskrit_iast: citra it śiśos taruṇasya vakṣatha iti jātavedasīyam |
meaning: चित्र इत् शिशोस् तरुणस्य वक्षथ इति जातवेदसीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: vājintamāya sahyase supitryā iti vājinn iti paśumat |
meaning: वाजिन्तमाय सह्यसे सुपित्र्या इति वाजिन्न् इति पशुमत् |

text:
They perform the Jyotis as the sixth day; the symbols in its verses are those of the sixth day. ‘O friends, together the seemly’ is the Ājya; ‘O friends’ is the symbol of all; the sixth day has the symbol all; therefore in ‘O friends’ he refers to all. The Praüga is one to be gathered together; when the Bṛhat Sāman was created, the Praüga which is to be gathered together was created after it; thus he makes the rite successful with its symbol; that rite is likely to cause success which is successful with its symbol. ‘Great is Indra, manlike, spreading over mortals’ is the Marutvatīya; there is repetition in ‘He hath become broad, wide,
well made by the makers'; the sixth day is the end; having gone to the end, he repeats as it were, for hence whitherward should he go? 'He who is born the first, the wise' is the Niṣkevalya; it contains a symbol of ending in the reference to what has been; 'He who hath in secret depressed the hostile colour' is about what has been as it were. It has the same ending; that is a second symbol of the end. 'That desirable greatness of Savitṛ, the god' is (the hymn) to Savitṛ; there is 'of the sky' in 'Prajāpati, supporter of the sky, of the earth'; this is the symbol of yonder world. 'With ghee sky and earth enveloped' is (the hymn) to sky and earth, containing (the word) 'ghee'; ghee has all as its deity; the sixth day has all as its deity; therefore it contains (the word) 'ghee'. 'Why hath the best, why hath the youngest come to us?' is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus; there is repetition in 'the best, the youngest'; the sixth day is the end; having gone to the end, he repeats as it were, for hence whitherward should he go? 'These fires with Indra have awakened' is (the hymn) to the All-gods; in that it has the same ending it is a symbol of the end. 'To Vaiśvānara the praise, increasing holy order' is (the hymn) to Vaiśvānara; containing (the word) 'ghee' in 'Like pure ghee to Agni we accord'; the explanation of this has been given. 'Rich in showers, the Maruts of daring might' is (the hymn) to the Maruts; there is repetition in 'rich in showers'; the sixth day is the end, having gone to the end, he repeats as it were, for hence whitherward should he go? 'Thou, O Agni, with the days, the shining' is (the hymn) to Jātavedas; in 'Thou' it has the same beginning; just as that with the same end, so that with the same beginning is a symbol of the end. The waters by the sixth day they obtain, Prajāpati the god, brilliance the supreme essence of the deities; the immortal they confer on themselves.

sanskrit_iast: tasya tāny eva chando rūpāṇi yāni ṣaṣṭhasya ahnaḥ |
meaning: तस्य तान्य् एव छन्दो रूपाणि यानि षष्ठस्य अह्नः |

sanskrit_iast: sakhāyaḥ sam vaḥ samyañcam ity ājyam |
meaning: सखायः सम् वः सम्यञ्चम् इत्य् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmāt sakhāya iti sarvān eva abhivadati |
meaning: तस्मात् सखाय इति सर्वान् एव अभिवदति |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhad vai sāma sṛjyamānam saṃhāryaḥ praugo anvasṛjyata |
meaning: बृहद् वै साम सृज्यमानम् संहार्यः प्रौगो अन्वसृज्यत |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā ārdhnukam karma yad rūpa samṛddham |
meaning: एतद् वा आर्ध्नुकम् कर्म यद् रूप समृद्धम् |

sanskrit_iast: mahān indro nṛvadā carṣaṇiprā iti marutvatīyam |
meaning: महान् इन्द्रो नृवदा चर्षणिप्रा इति मरुत्वतीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: uruḥ pṛthuḥ sukṛtaḥ kartṛbhir bhūd iti ninartiḥ |
meaning: उरुः पृथुः सुकृतः कर्तृभिर् भूद् इति निनर्तिः |

sanskrit_iast: yo jāta eva prathamo manasvān iti niṣkevalyam |
meaning: यो जात एव प्रथमो मनस्वान् इति निष्केवल्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasya tad eva anta rūpam yad bhūta anuvādi yo dāsam varṇam adharam guhākari iti |
meaning: तस्य तद् एव अन्त रूपम् यद् भूत अनुवादि यो दासम् वर्णम् अधरम् गुहाकरि इति |

sanskrit_iast: sodarkam bhavati tad dvitīyam anta rūpam |
meaning: सोदर्कम् भवति तद् द्वितीयम् अन्त रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad devasya savitur vāryam mahad iti sāvitram |
meaning: तद् देवस्य सवितुर् वार्यम् महद् इति सावित्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: diva iti tad amuṣya lokasya rūpam |
meaning: दिव इति तद् अमुष्य लोकस्य रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtena dyāvā pṛthivī abhivṛte iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam ghṛtavat |
meaning: घृतेन द्यावा पृथिवी अभिवृते इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् घृतवत् |

sanskrit_iast: kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kim yaviṣṭho na ājagann ity ārbhavam |
meaning: किम् उ श्रेष्ठः किम् यविष्ठो न आजगन्न् इत्य् आर्भवम् |

sanskrit_iast: abudhram u tya indravanto agnaya iti vaiśvadevam |
meaning: अबुध्रम् उ त्य इन्द्रवन्तो अग्नय इति वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasya tad eva anta rūpam yat sodarkam |
meaning: तस्य तद् एव अन्त रूपम् यत् सोदर्कम् |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānarāya dhiṣaṇām ṛtā vṛdha iti vaiśvānarīyam |
meaning: वैश्वानराय धिषणाम् ऋता वृध इति वैश्वानरीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtam na pūtam agnaye janām asi iti ghṛtavat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: घृतम् न पूतम् अग्नये जनाम् असि इति घृतवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: dhārāvarā maruto dhṛṣṇv ojasa iti mārutam |
meaning: धारावरा मरुतो धृष्ण्व् ओजस इति मारुतम् |

sanskrit_iast: tvam agne dyubhis tvam āśuśukṣaṇir iti jātavedasīyam |
meaning: त्वम् अग्ने द्युभिस् त्वम् आशुशुक्षणिर् इति जातवेदसीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: yathā vai sodarkam evam saprahṛty anta rūpam |
meaning: यथा वै सोदर्कम् एवम् सप्रहृत्य् अन्त रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhuḥ kasmād vaiśvadevāny eva anvāyāty ante na eka devatyāi na dvi devatyāni iti |
meaning: तद् आहुः कस्माद् वैश्वदेवान्य् एव अन्वायात्य् अन्ते न एक देवत्याइ न द्वि देवत्यानि इति |
text:
They say 'Why are (the litanies) for the All-gods expanded, and not those for one deity or for two deities?' No exhaustion arises through that for one deity or that for two deities, but exhaustion does arise through that for the All-gods; therefore those for the All-gods only are expanded, to secure the might of these days, to prevent exhaustion of the Abhiplavas. They perform the Jyotis as the first day, with the symbol of the one day (rite), for the one day (rite) is the light of the other days; the Go as the
second day, for they go by it; the Āyus as the third day, for they move by it. The first and last days are Agniṣṭomas, in the middle are four Ukthyas; the Agniṣṭoma is the holy power; the Ukthyas are cattle; verily thus by the holy power having surrounded cattle on both sides they confer them upon themselves. Of these four Ukthyas there are a thousand verses in the Stotras; cattle are connected with a thousand; a thousandfold prosperity he obtains who knows thus. Hence they perform sets of four Abhiplavas, ending with a Pṛṣṭhya; the Abhiplavas are cattle; the Pṛṣṭhyas are prosperity; verily thus having encompassed prosperity on both sides with cattle they confer it upon themselves. From the Viśvajit they perform sets of four Abhiplavas beginning with a Pṛṣṭhya; the Abhiplavas are prosperity; the Pṛṣṭhyas are cattle; verily thus with prosperity having encompassed cattle on both sides they confer them upon themselves.

sanskrit_iast: na eka devatyena yāta yāmam bhavati |
meaning: न एक देवत्येन यात यामम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśva devena eva yāta yāmam bhavati |
meaning: वैश्व देवेन एव यात यामम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: ayam hy ekāha uttareṣām ahnām jyotiḥ |
meaning: अयम् ह्य् एकाह उत्तरेषाम् अह्नाम् ज्योतिः |

sanskrit_iast: brahmaṇā eva tat paśūn ubhayataḥ parigṛhya ātman dadhate |
meaning: ब्रह्मणा एव तत् पशून् उभयतः परिगृह्य आत्मन् दधते |

sanskrit_iast: teṣām vā eteṣām caturṇām ukthyānām sahasram stotriyāḥ |
meaning: तेषाम् वा एतेषाम् चतुर्णाम् उक्थ्यानाम् सहस्रम् स्तोत्रियाः |

sanskrit_iast: pra sāhasram poṣam āpnoti ya evam veda |
meaning: प्र साहस्रम् पोषम् आप्नोति य एवम् वेद |

sanskrit_iast: pṛṣṭhyā antān vā itaś caturaś caturo abhiplavān upayanti |
meaning: पृष्ठ्या अन्तान् वा इतश् चतुरश् चतुरो अभिप्लवान् उपयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: paśubhir eva tat śriyam ubhayataḥ parigṛhya ātman dadhate |
meaning: पशुभिर् एव तत् श्रियम् उभयतः परिगृह्य आत्मन् दधते |

sanskrit_iast: pṛṣṭhyā ārambhaṇān vā ūrdhvam viṣuvataś caturaś caturo abhiplavān upayanti |
meaning: पृष्ठ्या आरम्भणान् वा ऊर्ध्वम् विषुवतश् चतुरश् चतुरो अभिप्लवान् उपयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: śriyā eva tat paśūn ubhayataḥ parigṛhya ātman dadhate |
meaning: श्रिया एव तत् पशून् उभयतः परिगृह्य आत्मन् दधते |

text: The Abhiplava is a definitely arranged (sacrifice) with definite metres. The Nivids inserted in a sacrificial rite which has definite metres are all in Jagatī at the third pressing. So duly are the Nivids inserted; they being duly inserted place them duly in all worlds and in all desires. In that the Nivids are inserted all in Jagatī at the third pressing, thereby is there obtained whatever is desired in a third pressing all of Jagatī (verses). Again, in that day by day these Triṣṭubh verses from the model are recited, thereby is there obtained whatever is desired in a third pressing all of Triṣṭubh (verses). Again, in that day by day this Gāyatrī from the model, 'Maker of fair forms', is recited, thereby is there obtained whatever is desired in a third pressing all of Gāyatrī. In that this six-day (rite) repeatedly approaches (abhiplavate), therefore is it called Abhiplava, for by it the sacrificers approach the world of heaven.

sanskrit_iast: yo vai yajña kratuḥ klṛptac chandā bhavati |
meaning: यो वै यज्ञ क्रतुः क्लृप्तच् छन्दा भवति |

sanskrit_iast: sarva jāgatāni ha vai tasya nividdhānāni bhavanti tṛtīya savane |
meaning: सर्व जागतानि ह वै तस्य निविद्धानानि भवन्ति तृतीय सवने |

sanskrit_iast: tā enān yathā yatham dhīyamānāḥ sarveṣu ca lokeṣu sarveṣu ca kāmeṣu yathā yatham dadhati |
meaning: ता एनान् यथा यथम् धीयमानाः सर्वेषु च लोकेषु सर्वेषु च कामेषु यथा यथम् दधति |

sanskrit_iast: tad yat sarva jāgatāni tasya nividdhānāni bhavanti tṛtīya savane |
meaning: तद् यत् सर्व जागतानि तस्य निविद्धानानि भवन्ति तृतीय सवने |

sanskrit_iast: teno yaḥ sarva jāgate tṛtīya savane kāmaḥ sa upāptaḥ |
meaning: तेनो यः सर्व जागते तृतीय सवने कामः स उपाप्तः |

sanskrit_iast: yad v eva etās tantryās triṣṭubha uktha pratipado ahar ahaḥ śasyante |
meaning: यद् व् एव एतास् तन्त्र्यास् त्रिष्टुभ उक्थ प्रतिपदो अहर् अहः शस्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: teno yaḥ sarva traiṣṭubhe tṛtīya savane kāmaḥ sa upāptaḥ |
meaning: तेनो यः सर्व त्रैष्टुभे तृतीय सवने कामः स उपाप्तः |

sanskrit_iast: yad v eva eṣā tantryā gāyatry ahar ahaḥ surūpa kṛtnuḥ śasyate |
meaning: यद् व् एव एषा तन्त्र्या गायत्र्य् अहर् अहः सुरूप कृत्नुः शस्यते |

sanskrit_iast: teno yaḥ sarva gāyatre tṛtīya savane kāmaḥ sa upāptaḥ |
meaning: तेनो यः सर्व गायत्रे तृतीय सवने कामः स उपाप्तः |

sanskrit_iast: yad v eva eṣa ṣaḍ ahaḥ punaḥ punaḥ abhiplavate |
meaning: यद् व् एव एष षड् अहः पुनः पुनः अभिप्लवते |

sanskrit_iast: abhiplavante hy anena svargāya lokāya yajamānāḥ svargāya lokāya yajamānāḥ |
meaning: अभिप्लवन्ते ह्य् अनेन स्वर्गाय लोकाय यजमानाः स्वर्गाय लोकाय यजमानाः |

sanskrit_iast: prathamam ahar ayam eva loka āyatanena |
meaning: प्रथमम् अहर् अयम् एव लोक आयतनेन |
text:
The first day is this world in abode, Agni, the Gāyatrī, the Trivṛt Stoma, the Rathantara Sāman, the base by Tanva. It has the following symbols in its verses: the future tense with the god mentioned in the first Pada—that which is to be is the future tense—(the word) 'hither', (the
word) ‘forward’, (the word) ‘this’, (the word) ‘go’, (the word) ‘adorn’, (the word) ‘yoked’, (the word) ‘yoking’, (the word) ‘light’, (the word) ‘bright’. ‘Advancing forward up to the sacrifice’ is the Ājya, containing (the word) ‘forward’; that which contains ‘forward’ is a symbol of the first day; it is in Gāyatrī, for this set of three days has the Gāyatrī at the morning pressing. So in the transposed form. Taking out that, ‘Forward to the god, Agni’ is used in the conjunct form; the explanation of this has been given. The Praüga is by Madhuchandas; the explanation of this has been given. ‘Let Indra come hither to aid us’ is the Marutvatīya, containing (the word) ‘hither’; that which contains (the word) ‘hither’ is a symbol of the first day; there is a reference to the Maruts in it in ‘From the realm of light, with the Maruts, to aid us’. ‘Hither to us, Indra, hither to us from afar, from near’ is the Niṣkevalya, containing (the word) ‘hither’; that which contains ‘hither’ is a symbol of the first day. The Niṣkevalya and the Marutvatīya are contiguous (hymns) on the first day; by the contiguous (hymns) the gods flew up to the world of heaven together; therefore these two are recited first as being heavenly. In that the Niṣkevalya and the Marutvatīya are contiguous (hymns) on the first day, verily (they serve) to obtain the world of heaven. ‘They yoke their minds, they also yoke their thoughts’, ‘Forward sky and earth, increasing holy order, with the sacrifices’, and ‘Here, here in mind is your relationship, O heroes’; (the last) is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus; with it he restrains; on the first day are recited hymns containing (the word) ‘yoked’ as well as (the word) ‘forward’; in that he uses as (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus, ‘Here, here is your,’ it is a symbol of restraint, of preventing falling away. ‘Like a skilled steed, he hath yoked himself to the pole’ is (the hymn) to the All-gods, containing (the word) ‘yoked’; that which contains (the word) ‘yoked’ is a symbol of the first day. The last two (verses) of it he omits. (Now they ask) ‘Shall these two prescribed be recited in the Āgnimāruta?’ Kauṣītaki used to say ‘He should recite (them), to avoid breaking up the hymn; the Ṛc is not exhausted by the litany nor by the supplementary repetition; it is by the vaṣaṭ call alone that it becomes exhausted on one day.’ ‘To Vaiśvānara with broad radiance bards’ is (the hymn) to Vaiśvā-
nara, containing (the word) ‘forward’; that which contains (the word) ‘forward’ is a symbol of the first day. ‘Forward to the horde of the Maruts, self-radiant’ is (the hymn) to the Maruts, containing (the word) ‘forward’; that which contains (the word) ‘forward’ is a symbol of the first day. ‘Forward the strong, new, hymn to Agni’ is (the hymn) to Jātavedas, containing (the word) ‘forward’; that which contains (the word) ‘forward’ is a symbol of the first day. This world with the first day they obtain, the Gāyatrī metre, the Trivṛt Stoma, the Rathantara Sāman, the eastern quarter, the spring of seasons, the Vasus the gods, Agni, born of the gods, the overlord.

sanskrit_iast: agnir gāyatrī trivṛt stomo rathantaram sāma |
meaning: अग्निर् गायत्री त्रिवृत् स्तोमो रथन्तरम् साम |

sanskrit_iast: āvat pravad eṣavad arṣavad adyavad yuktavad yuñjānavaj jyotiṣmad iti |
meaning: आवत् प्रवद् एषवद् अर्षवद् अद्यवद् युक्तवद् युञ्जानवज् ज्योतिष्मद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: gāyatram gāyatra prātaḥ savano hy eṣa tryahaḥ |
meaning: गायत्रम् गायत्र प्रातः सवनो ह्य् एष त्र्यहः |

sanskrit_iast: uddhṛtya etat pra vo devāya agnaya iti samūḍhe tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: उद्धृत्य एतत् प्र वो देवाय अग्नय इति समूढे तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: ā yātv indro avasa upa na iti marutvatīyam āvat |
meaning: आ यात्व् इन्द्रो अवस उप न इति मरुत्वतीयम् आवत् |

sanskrit_iast: svarṇarād avase no marutvān iti sa eva asmin marun nyaṅgaḥ |
meaning: स्वर्णराद् अवसे नो मरुत्वान् इति स एव अस्मिन् मरुन् न्यङ्गः |

sanskrit_iast: ā na indro dūrād ā na āsād iti niṣkevalyam āvat |
meaning: आ न इन्द्रो दूराद् आ न आसाद् इति निष्केवल्यम् आवत् |

sanskrit_iast: sampātau niṣkevalya marutvatīye bhavataḥ prathame ahan |
meaning: सम्पातौ निष्केवल्य मरुत्वतीये भवतः प्रथमे अहन् |

sanskrit_iast: sampātair vai devāḥ svargaṃl lokam samapatan |
meaning: सम्पातैर् वै देवाः स्वर्गंल् लोकम् समपतन् |

sanskrit_iast: tad yat sampātau niṣkevalya marutvatīye bhavataḥ prathame ahan |
meaning: तद् यत् सम्पातौ निष्केवल्य मरुत्वतीये भवतः प्रथमे अहन् |

sanskrit_iast: yuñjate mana uta yujñate dhiyaḥ pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī ṛtāvṛdhā iha iha vo manasā bandhutā nara ity ārbhavam |
meaning: युञ्जते मन उत युज्ञते धियः प्र द्यावा यज्ञैः पृथिवी ऋतावृधा इह इह वो मनसा बन्धुता नर इत्य् आर्भवम् |

sanskrit_iast: yuktavanti ca vai pravanti ca prathame ahant sūktāni śasyante |
meaning: युक्तवन्ति च वै प्रवन्ति च प्रथमे अहन्त् सूक्तानि शस्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: tad yad iha iha va ity ārbhavam karoti |
meaning: तद् यद् इह इह व इत्य् आर्भवम् करोति |

sanskrit_iast: hayo na vidvān ayuji svayam dhuri iti vaiśvadevam yuktavat |
meaning: हयो न विद्वान् अयुजि स्वयम् धुरि इति वैश्वदेवम् युक्तवत् |

sanskrit_iast: kuvid ete avadhṛte āgnimārute śasyete iti |
meaning: कुविद् एते अवधृते आग्निमारुते शस्येते इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad u ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: तद् उ ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: na ha vā ṛk śastreṇa yāta yāmā bhavati |
meaning: न ह वा ऋक् शस्त्रेण यात यामा भवति |

sanskrit_iast: vaṣaṭ kāreṇa ha vai sā yāta yāmā bhavati samāne ahan |
meaning: वषट् कारेण ह वै सा यात यामा भवति समाने अहन् |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānarāya pṛthu pājase vipa iti vaiśvānarīyam |
meaning: वैश्वानराय पृथु पाजसे विप इति वैश्वानरीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasmint sumnāni yajamāna ā caka ity āvat |
meaning: तस्मिन्त् सुम्नानि यजमान आ चक इत्य् आवत् |

sanskrit_iast: pra śardhāya mārutāya sva bhānava iti mārutam pravat |
meaning: प्र शर्धाय मारुताय स्व भानव इति मारुतम् प्रवत् |

sanskrit_iast: pra tavyasīm navyasīm dhītim agnaya iti jātavedasīyam pravat |
meaning: प्र तव्यसीम् नव्यसीम् धीतिम् अग्नय इति जातवेदसीयम् प्रवत् |

sanskrit_iast: gāyatrīm chandas trivṛtam stomam rathantaram sāma |
meaning: गायत्रीम् छन्दस् त्रिवृतम् स्तोमम् रथन्तरम् साम |

sanskrit_iast: vasūn devān deva jātam agnim adhipatim |
meaning: वसून् देवान् देव जातम् अग्निम् अधिपतिम् |

text:
The second day is the world of the atmosphere in its abode, Indra, the Triṣṭubh, the Pañcadaśa Stoma, the Bṛhat Sāman, the basis by Tanva. It has the following symbols in its verses: the present tense with the god mentioned in the middle Pada—the present is what is before the eyes, but not tangible—(the word) ‘deities’, (the word) ‘thunderbolt’, (the word) ‘slaying Vṛtra’, (the word) ‘strong’, (the word) ‘apart’, (the words) ‘stand’, ‘him’, and ‘thou’. ‘Agni we choose as envoy’ is the Ājya, containing the word ‘apart’ in ‘The Hotṛ of all knowledge’; the explanation of this has been given. It is in Gāyatrī, for this set of three days has the Gāyatrī at the morning pressing. So in the transposed form. Taking out that, ‘For thou hast a glory of rule’ is used in the conjunct form; the explanation of this has been given. The Praüga is by Gṛtsamada; the explanation of this has been given. ‘O Indra, drink this Soma, O lord of the Soma’ is the Marutvatīya, containing (the word) ‘thunderbolt’ in ‘At the midday pressing, O thou with the thunderbolt in thy hand’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘Thy nearest, farthest, help’ is the Niṣkevalya, containing (the word) ‘slaying Vṛtra’ in ‘With these thou hast helped us in slaying Vṛtra’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘That desirable greatness of Savitṛ, the god’ is (the hymn) to Savitṛ, containing ‘Three times the atmosphere Savitṛ with his greatness’; this is openly the symbol of the atmosphere. ‘They two, sky and earth, all weal producing’ is (the hymn) to sky and earth, containing (the word) ‘apart’; the explanation of this has been given. ‘They have wrought the car well covered, skilled workers’ is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus, containing (the word) ‘strong’ in ‘They have wrought the two steeds, that bear Indra, strong in riches’; the explanation of this has been given. ‘The
charioteer of the sacrifice, the lord of the folk' is (the hymn) to the All-gods by Śaryāta, containing (the word) 'strong' in 'The strong banner, the holy one, hath attained the sky'; the explanation of this has been given. 'The might of the swift, strong, ruddy one' and 'To the strong host, majestic, pious' are (two hymns) containing (the word) 'strong'; the explanation of them has been given. 'The immortal, born of strength, doth penetrate' is (the hymn) to Jātavedas, containing (the word) 'apart' in 'What time he became a messenger of Vivasvant'; the explanation of this has been given. The last verse of it is 'Early and soon at the prayer may the bright one come'; verily thus he refers to the next day; 'Verily thus they keep taking hold of the next day' Kauṣītaki used to say. The world of the atmosphere with the second day they obtain, the Triṣṭubh metre, the Pañcadaśa Stoma, the Bṛhat Sāman, the southern quarter, the summer of the seasons, the Maruts the gods, Indra, born of the gods, the overlord.

sanskrit_iast: yad vai pratyakṣam āsprakṣaṃs tat kurvat |
meaning: यद् वै प्रत्यक्षम् आस्प्रक्षंस् तत् कुर्वत् |

sanskrit_iast: hatavad vajravad vṛtrahavad vṛṣaṇvad udvad vivat sthitam tanvām iti |
meaning: हतवद् वज्रवद् वृत्रहवद् वृषण्वद् उद्वद् विवत् स्थितम् तन्वाम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: hotāram viśvavedasam iti vivat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: होतारम् विश्ववेदसम् इति विवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: gāyatram gāyatra prātaḥ savano hy eṣa tryahaḥ |
meaning: गायत्रम् गायत्र प्रातः सवनो ह्य् एष त्र्यहः |

sanskrit_iast: uddhṛtya etat tvam hi kṣaitavad yaśa iti samūḍhe tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: उद्धृत्य एतत् त्वम् हि क्षैतवद् यश इति समूढे तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: yā ta ūtir avamā yā paramā iti niṣkevalyam |
meaning: या त ऊतिर् अवमा या परमा इति निष्केवल्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: tābhir ū ṣu vṛtrahatye avīr na iti vṛtrahavat |
meaning: ताभिर् ऊ षु वृत्रहत्ये अवीर् न इति वृत्रहवत् |

sanskrit_iast: viśvo devasya netur ā viśva devam satpatim iti pratipad anucarau tayor uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: विश्वो देवस्य नेतुर् आ विश्व देवम् सत्पतिम् इति प्रतिपद् अनुचरौ तयोर् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad devasya savitur vāryam mahad iti sāvitram |
meaning: तद् देवस्य सवितुर् वार्यम् महद् इति सावित्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: te hi dyāvā pṛthivī viśva śambhuvā iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam vivat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: ते हि द्यावा पृथिवी विश्व शम्भुवा इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् विवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: takṣan ratham suvṛtam vidmanā apasa ity ārbhavam |
meaning: तक्षन् रथम् सुवृतम् विद्मना अपस इत्य् आर्भवम् |

sanskrit_iast: takṣan harī indra vāhā vṛṣaṇvasū iti vṛṣaṇvat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: तक्षन् हरी इन्द्र वाहा वृषण्वसू इति वृषण्वत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: yajñasya vo rathyam viśpatim viśām iti śāryātam vaiśvadevam |
meaning: यज्ञस्य वो रथ्यम् विश्पतिम् विशाम् इति शार्यातम् वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: vṛṣā ketur yajato dyām aśāyata iti vṛṣaṇvat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: वृषा केतुर् यजतो द्याम् अशायत इति वृषण्वत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: pṛṣkasya vṛṣṇo vṛṣṇe śardhāya iti vṛṣaṇvatī tayor uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: पृष्कस्य वृष्णो वृष्णे शर्धाय इति वृषण्वती तयोर् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: nū cit sahotā amṛto ni tundata iti jātavedasīyam |
meaning: नू चित् सहोता अमृतो नि तुन्दत इति जातवेदसीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: hotā yad dūto abhavad vivasvata iti vivat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: होता यद् दूतो अभवद् विवस्वत इति विवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasya prātar makṣū dhiyāvasur jagamyād ity uttamā |
meaning: तस्य प्रातर् मक्षू धियावसुर् जगम्याद् इत्य् उत्तमा |

sanskrit_iast: param eva etad ahar abhyārabhya vasanti iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: परम् एव एतद् अहर् अभ्यारभ्य वसन्ति इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: triṣṭubham chandaḥ pañcadaśam stomam bṛhat sāma |
meaning: त्रिष्टुभम् छन्दः पञ्चदशम् स्तोमम् बृहत् साम |

sanskrit_iast: rudrān devān deva jātam indram adhipatim |
meaning: रुद्रान् देवान् देव जातम् इन्द्रम् अधिपतिम् |

sanskrit_iast: tṛtīyam ahar asāv eva loka āyatanena |
meaning: तृतीयम् अहर् असाव् एव लोक आयतनेन |
text: The third day is yonder world in its abode, Varuṇa, the Jagatī, the Saptadaśa Stoma, the Vairūpa Sāman, the basis by Tanva; it has the following symbols in its verses: the past tense with the mention of the god in the last Pada—the past is what refers to what has happened—(the word) 'horse', (the word) 'cow', (the word) 'chariot', (the word) 'go', (the word) 'stand', (the word) 'end', the same ending, the lack of definite mention (of the deity), the same beginning. 'Yoke thou those best fit to invoke the gods' is the Ājya. They say 'Seeing that the third day is the end, then why does the Ājya contain (the word) "yoke"?' 'By this day the gods went to the world of heaven; yoked thither they went; therefore (it contains "yoke")' should he reply. It contains (the word) 'chariot' in 'The steeds, O Agni, like a charioteer'; this is a symbol of this day. It is in Gāyatrī, for this set of three days has the Gāyatrī at the morning pressing. So in the transposed form. Taking out that, 'Thou, O Agni, the Vasus here' is used in the conjunct form. The explanation of this has been given. The Praüga is in Uṣṇih verses by Atri; the third day is connected with the Jagatī; in that the Praüga is in Uṣṇih verses by Atri for the third day, thus the Jagatī enjoys the third pressing.

sanskrit_iast: varuṇo jagatī saptadaśa stomo vairūpam sāma |
meaning: वरुणो जगती सप्तदश स्तोमो वैरूपम् साम |

sanskrit_iast: yad vai bhūta anuvādi tac cakṛvat |
meaning: यद् वै भूत अनुवादि तच् चकृवत् |

sanskrit_iast: aśvāvad gomad rathavad gatavat sthitavad antavat sodarkam aniruktam saprabhṛti iti |
meaning: अश्वावद् गोमद् रथवद् गतवत् स्थितवद् अन्तवत् सोदर्कम् अनिरुक्तम् सप्रभृति इति |

sanskrit_iast: yukṣvā hi deva hūtamān ity ājyam |
meaning: युक्ष्वा हि देव हूतमान् इत्य् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad antas tṛtīyam ahar atha kasmād yuktavad ājyam iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् अन्तस् तृतीयम् अहर् अथ कस्माद् युक्तवद् आज्यम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: etena vā ahnā devāḥ svargaṃl lokam āyan |
meaning: एतेन वा अह्ना देवाः स्वर्गंल् लोकम् आयन् |

sanskrit_iast: aśvān agne rathīri iva iti ratahvat |
meaning: अश्वान् अग्ने रथीरि इव इति रतह्वत् |

sanskrit_iast: gāyatram gāyatra prātaḥ savano hy eṣa tryahaḥ |
meaning: गायत्रम् गायत्र प्रातः सवनो ह्य् एष त्र्यहः |

sanskrit_iast: uddhṛtya etat tvam agne vasūṃr iha iti samūḍhe tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: उद्धृत्य एतत् त्वम् अग्ने वसूंर् इह इति समूढे तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad yad auṣṇiha ātreyas tṛtīyasya ahnaḥ praugaḥ |
meaning: तद् यद् औष्णिह आत्रेयस् तृतीयस्य अह्नः प्रौगः |

text:
'Three friendships hath man's worship' is the Marutvatīya; (the word) 'three' is a symbol of the third day. 'If a hundred skies, O Indra, were thine' is the strophe of the Vairūpa; there is repetition in 'and
a hundred earths also'; the third day is the end; having gone to the end, he repeats (as it were); for hence whitherward should he go? 'O Indra, as many as thou' is the antistrophe; there is repetition in 'Day by day would I obey the mighty'; the third day is the end; having gone to the end, he repeats as it were, for hence whitherward should he go? 'O Indra, threefold protection' is the Pragātha of the Sāman, containing in 'three-fold' (the word) 'three'; this is a symbol of the third day. 'I was the first lord of wealth' is (the hymn) to Indra; in 'I' and 'I' it has the same beginning; just as that which has the same ending, so that which has the same beginning is a symbol of the end. In the Triṣṭubh (hymn), 'He who is born the first, the wise,' he inserts a Nivid. That hymn is the body of Indra. 'Placing in it a Nivid, Gṛtsamada Bhārgava went to the dear abode of Indra' (they say). He goes to the dear abode of Indra, he conquers the other world, who places a Nivid in this hymn. It contains a symbol of ending in the reference to what has been; 'He who in secret hath depressed the hostile colour' is about what has been as it were. It has the same ending; this is a second symbol of the end.

sanskrit_iast: tri iti tat tṛtīyasya ahno rūpam |
meaning: त्रि इति तत् तृतीयस्य अह्नो रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: yad dvāya indra te śatam iti vairūpasya stotriyaḥ |
meaning: यद् द्वाय इन्द्र ते शतम् इति वैरूपस्य स्तोत्रियः |

sanskrit_iast: śatam bhūmīr uta syur iti ninartiḥ |
meaning: शतम् भूमीर् उत स्युर् इति निनर्तिः |

sanskrit_iast: indra tri dhātu śaraṇam iti trivān pragāthaḥ |
meaning: इन्द्र त्रि धातु शरणम् इति त्रिवान् प्रगाथः |

sanskrit_iast: tri dhātv iti tat tṛtīyasya ahno rūpam |
meaning: त्रि धात्व् इति तत् तृतीयस्य अह्नो रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: aham bhuvam vasunaḥ pūrvyas patir iti indra sūktam |
meaning: अहम् भुवम् वसुनः पूर्व्यस् पतिर् इति इन्द्र सूक्तम् |

sanskrit_iast: yathā vai sodarkam evam saprabhṛty anta rūpam jāgatam |
meaning: यथा वै सोदर्कम् एवम् सप्रभृत्य् अन्त रूपम् जागतम् |

sanskrit_iast: yo jāta eva prathamo manasvān ity etasmiṃs traiṣṭubhe nividam dadhāti |
meaning: यो जात एव प्रथमो मनस्वान् इत्य् एतस्मिंस् त्रैष्टुभे निविदम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: etasmin ha gṛtsamado bābhravo nividam dadhad indrasya priyam dhāma upajagāma |
meaning: एतस्मिन् ह गृत्समदो बाभ्रवो निविदम् दधद् इन्द्रस्य प्रियम् धाम उपजगाम |

sanskrit_iast: upa ha vā indrasya priyam dhāma gacchati jayati param lokam ya etasmint sūkte nividam dadhāti |
meaning: उप ह वा इन्द्रस्य प्रियम् धाम गच्छति जयति परम् लोकम् य एतस्मिन्त् सूक्ते निविदम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: tasya tad eva anta rūpam yad bhūta anuvādi yo dāsam varṇam adharam guhākari iti |
meaning: तस्य तद् एव अन्त रूपम् यद् भूत अनुवादि यो दासम् वर्णम् अधरम् गुहाकरि इति |

sanskrit_iast: sodarkam bhavati tad dvitīyam anta rūpam |
meaning: सोदर्कम् भवति तद् द्वितीयम् अन्त रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: abhi tvā deva savitar ity abhivān anucaraḥ |
meaning: अभि त्वा देव सवितर् इत्य् अभिवान् अनुचरः |
text:
'Towards thee, O god Savitṛ' is the antistrophe, containing the word 'towards'. They say 'In that the third day is the end, then why has the antistrophe (the word) "towards"?' 'By this day the gods went to the world of heaven; desiring towards it they went; therefore (it has "towards")' he should reply. 'Hitherward the god Savitṛ with the golden' and 'Rich in ghee, encompassing the worlds' are (two triplets ) containing (the word) 'ghee'; the explanation of these has been given. 'Born, without steed, without reins, worthy of praise' is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus; there is the word 'with three wheels' in 'The chariot of three wheels circleth round the atmosphere'; this is a symbol of the third day. 'Those who from afar would assume kinship' is (the hymn) to the All-gods; (it contains the word) 'from afar'; from afar is the end; the third day is the end; in the end he places the end. These hymns end in half-verses, some in Padas, some in half-Padas; this ends with a third of a Pada; this is a symbol of the third day. 'To Vaiśvānara the praise, increasing holy order' is (the
hymn) to Vaiśvānara, containing (the word) ‘ghee’ in ‘Like pure ghee to Agni we accord’; the explanation of this has been given. ‘Rich in showers, the Maruts, of daring might’ is (the hymn) to the Maruts; in ‘Rich in showers’ there is repetition; the third day is the end; having gone to the end, he repeats as it were, for hence whitherward should he go? ‘Thou O Agni, the first Aṅgiras, the Ṛṣi,’ is (the hymn) to Jātavedas; it has the same beginning in ‘thou’ and ‘thou’; just as that which has the same ending, so that which has the same beginning is a symbol of the end. Yonder world with the third day they obtain, the Jagatī metre, the Saptadaśa Stoma, the Vairūpa Sāman, the western quarter, the rains of the seasons, the Ādityas the gods, Varuṇa, born of the gods, the overlord.

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad antas tṛtīyam ahar atha kasmād abhivān anucara iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् अन्तस् तृतीयम् अहर् अथ कस्माद् अभिवान् अनुचर इति |

sanskrit_iast: etena vā ahnā devāḥ svargaṃl lokam āyan |
meaning: एतेन वा अह्ना देवाः स्वर्गंल् लोकम् आयन् |

sanskrit_iast: ud u ṣya devaḥ savitā hiraṇyayā ghṛtavatī bhuvanānām abhiśriyā iti ghṛtavatī tayor uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: उद् उ ष्य देवः सविता हिरण्यया घृतवती भुवनानाम् अभिश्रिया इति घृतवती तयोर् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: anaśvo jāto anabhīśur ukthya ity ārbhavam |
meaning: अनश्वो जातो अनभीशुर् उक्थ्य इत्य् आर्भवम् |

sanskrit_iast: rathas ticakraḥ pari vartate raja iti |
meaning: रथस् तिचक्रः परि वर्तते रज इति |

sanskrit_iast: tricakra iti tat tṛtīyasya ahno rūpam |
meaning: त्रिचक्र इति तत् तृतीयस्य अह्नो रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: parāvato ye didhiṣanta āpyam iti vaiśvadevam |
meaning: परावतो ये दिधिषन्त आप्यम् इति वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānarāya dhiṣaṇām ṛtā vṛdha iti vaiśvānarīyam |
meaning: वैश्वानराय धिषणाम् ऋता वृध इति वैश्वानरीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: ghṛtam na pūtam agranye janām asi iti ghṛtavat tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: घृतम् न पूतम् अग्रन्ये जनाम् असि इति घृतवत् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: dhārā varā maruto dhṛṣaṇv ojasa iti mārutam |
meaning: धारा वरा मरुतो धृषण्व् ओजस इति मारुतम् |

sanskrit_iast: tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣir iti jātavedasīyam |
meaning: त्वम् अग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा ऋषिर् इति जातवेदसीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: yathā vai sodarkam evam saprabhṛty anta rūpam |
meaning: यथा वै सोदर्कम् एवम् सप्रभृत्य् अन्त रूपम् |

sanskrit_iast: jagatīm chandaḥ saptadaśam stomam vairūpam sāma |
meaning: जगतीम् छन्दः सप्तदशम् स्तोमम् वैरूपम् साम |

text: The third day is the end; the gods having gone to the end desired the fourth day; therefore it contains (the word) ‘desire’; having sacrificed they found it; therefore it contains (the word) ‘yoke’. They say ‘Since the third day is the end, then why on the fourth day does he insert the sound o?’ The fourth day is the abode of speech; the Virāj is food; the sound o is food; verily thus he places food in the sacrifice and in the sacrificers. Moreover by the third day is speech obtained; verily thus on the fourth day he expands it; this is as when one expands heated metal; this (serves) to expand speech. It has the following symbols in its verses, (the word) ‘ruling’, (the word) ‘self-ruling’, (the word) ‘Virāj’, (the word) ‘born’, (the word) ‘aid’, (the word) ‘delight’, (the word) ‘around’, (the word) ‘towards’, (the word) ‘up to’. ‘With offerings for ourselves Agni’ is the Ājya by Vimada. By means of Vimada(’s hymn) the gods confused the Asuras; in that (the hymn of) Vimada is recited both in the middle and in the recitations of the Hotrakas, from each limb the sacrificers expel in confusion evil. It contains (the word) ‘born’ in ‘Agni brought to birth by Atharvan’; this is a symbol of this day.

sanskrit_iast: te devā antam gatvā caturtham ahar aicchan |
meaning: ते देवा अन्तम् गत्वा चतुर्थम् अहर् ऐच्छन् |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad antas tṛtīyam ahar atha kasmāc caturthe ahan nyūṅkhayati iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् अन्तस् तृतीयम् अहर् अथ कस्माच् चतुर्थे अहन् न्यूङ्खयति इति |

sanskrit_iast: vāca eva tad āyatanam virājo yac caturtham ahaḥ |
meaning: वाच एव तद् आयतनम् विराजो यच् चतुर्थम् अहः |

sanskrit_iast: tām eva etac caturthe ahan vibhāvayati |
meaning: ताम् एव एतच् चतुर्थे अहन् विभावयति |

sanskrit_iast: yathā ayas taptam vinayed evam tat |
meaning: यथा अयस् तप्तम् विनयेद् एवम् तत् |

sanskrit_iast: saṃrāḍvad virāḍvat svarāḍvaj jātavad ūtimad vītimat parivad abhivad upavad iti |
meaning: संराड्वद् विराड्वत् स्वराड्वज् जातवद् ऊतिमद् वीतिमत् परिवद् अभिवद् उपवद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: āgnim na sva vṛktibhir iti vaimadam ājyam |
meaning: आग्निम् न स्व वृक्तिभिर् इति वैमदम् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad yac caturthe ahan vimadaḥ śasyate madhyataś ca hotrāsu ca |
meaning: तद् यच् चतुर्थे अहन् विमदः शस्यते मध्यतश् च होत्रासु च |

sanskrit_iast: aṅgād aṅgād eva tad yajamānāḥ pāpmānam vimadanti |
meaning: अङ्गाद् अङ्गाद् एव तद् यजमानाः पाप्मानम् विमदन्ति |

text:
They make up ten Jagatī verses, for this set of three days has the Jagatī at the morning pressing. They are twenty Gāyatrīs, the Gāyatrī bears the morning pressing; thus he departs not from the symbol of the morning pressing. So in the transposed form. Taking out that, ‘Agni men with praise from the fire sticks’ is used in the conjunct form. The Ājya is in Virāj metre; the Pṛṣṭha is in Virāj; that is accordant.
The Ājya is by Vasiṣṭha; the Pṛṣṭha is by Vasiṣṭha; that is accordant. It contains (the word) 'born' in 'By the movements of the hands they have made the famed one to be born'; this is a symbol of this day. The Praüga is in Anuṣṭubh verses; the fourth day is connected with the Anuṣṭubh; verily thus he makes it to succeed with its own metre. With 'Thee with the sacrifices we invoke', which contains the word 'sacrifice', he begins the Marutvatīya; the sacrifice has to be taken up again on the fourth day; verily thus he takes up again the sacrifice. 'Hear our call, O Indra, harm us not' is the Marutvatīya. These Triṣṭubh verses have a Virāj tinge; they are employed here, for they are endowed with the symbol of the day. 'O Indra, with the Maruts here drink the Soma' is (a triplet) in normal Triṣṭubh and supports the pressing; these in normal Triṣṭubh that support the pressing do not depart from the midday (pressing). Indra is connected with the Triṣṭubh and Indra has his abode in the midday pressing; in that these in normal Triṣṭubh which support the pressing do not depart from the midday (pressing) even with transposed metres, (it is because he thinks) 'Indra is connected with the Triṣṭubh; let me not cause Indra to depart from his own abode.' 'When born the gods did adorn thee' contains (the word) 'born'; this is a symbol of this day. 'Him the cunning I invoke' is the Marutvatīya; it is in Gāyatrī, for this set of three days has the Gāyatrī at the midday pressing.

sanskrit_iast: jagat prātaḥ savano hy eṣa tryahaḥ |
meaning: जगत् प्रातः सवनो ह्य् एष त्र्यहः |

sanskrit_iast: tad u ha prātaḥ savana rūpān na apaiti |
meaning: तद् उ ह प्रातः सवन रूपान् न अपैति |

sanskrit_iast: uddhṛtya etad agnim naro dīdhitibhir araṇyor iti samūḍhe vairājam ājyam |
meaning: उद्धृत्य एतद् अग्निम् नरो दीधितिभिर् अरण्योर् इति समूढे वैराजम् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: hasta cyutī janayanta praśastam iti jātavat |
meaning: हस्त च्युती जनयन्त प्रशस्तम् इति जातवत् |

sanskrit_iast: tam tvā yajñebhir īmaha iti yajñavatyā marutvatīyam pratipadyate |
meaning: तम् त्वा यज्ञेभिर् ईमह इति यज्ञवत्या मरुत्वतीयम् प्रतिपद्यते |

sanskrit_iast: punar ārambhyo vai caturthe ahan yajñaḥ |
meaning: पुनर् आरम्भ्यो वै चतुर्थे अहन् यज्ञः |

sanskrit_iast: śrudhī havam indra mā riṣaṇya iti marutvatīyam |
meaning: श्रुधी हवम् इन्द्र मा रिषण्य इति मरुत्वतीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: tā vā etās triṣṭubho virāḍ varṇāḥ |
meaning: ता वा एतास् त्रिष्टुभो विराड् वर्णाः |

sanskrit_iast: indra marutva iha pāhi somam iti vijñāta traiṣṭubham savana dharaṇam |
meaning: इन्द्र मरुत्व इह पाहि सोमम् इति विज्ञात त्रैष्टुभम् सवन धरणम् |

sanskrit_iast: tāni vā etāni vijñāta traiṣṭubhāni savana dharaṇāny api vyūḍhac chandaso madhyaṃdinān na cyavante |
meaning: तानि वा एतानि विज्ञात त्रैष्टुभानि सवन धरणान्य् अपि व्यूढच् छन्दसो मध्यंदिनान् न च्यवन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: na id indram svād āyatanāc cyavayāma iti |
meaning: न इद् इन्द्रम् स्वाद् आयतनाच् च्यवयाम इति |

sanskrit_iast: jātam yat tvā pari devā abhūṣann iti jātavat |
meaning: जातम् यत् त्वा परि देवा अभूषन्न् इति जातवत् |

sanskrit_iast: imam nu māyinam huva iti marutvatīyam gāyatram |
meaning: इमम् नु मायिनम् हुव इति मरुत्वतीयम् गायत्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha ata iha nyūṅkhayed iha iti |
meaning: अथ अत इह न्यूङ्खयेद् इह इति |
text:
Then (they ask) 'Should he utter the sound o here or here?' The sound o is intended for the strophe and the antistrophe and for (the verses) commencing litanies. That he should not trouble about; the strophe is the body, the antistrophe offspring, the Virāj food, the sound o food; verily he places food in the body and in offspring. 'The sound o as connected with the Anuṣṭubh should he utter' some say; the fourth day is connected with the Anuṣṭubh; verily thus he makes it successful with its own metre. 'The sound o as connected with the Virāj should he utter' is the rule; the Virāj is food, the sound o food; verily thus he places food in the body and in offspring. At the middle Pada should he utter o; the first Pada is the body, the last offspring, the middle Pada the middle, in the middle of the body is food placed; it is as when one eats food, swallowing it piece by piece. 'Indra to the divine service' is the Pragātha of the Sāman, by which Indra is attained; by it the gods
attained all attainments; verily thus also the sacrificers by it attain all attainments. 'Where is Indra famed, in what to-day?' are the 'Where famed' verses; they are Virāj or Anuṣṭubh; they are employed here, for they are endowed with the symbol of the day. 'Of thee, the warrior, the bull, self-ruling' is in normal Triṣṭubh and supports the pressing; the explanation of this has been given; it contains in 'self-ruling' (the word) 'self-ruling'; containing 'self-ruling' is a symbol of this (day). 'Him of you, ever enduring' is the Niṣkevalya, containing (the word) 'hither' in 'In all speech outstretched hither'; that which contains (the word) 'hither' is a symbol of the fourth day as introductory, for the fourth day is a second introduction; it is in Gāyatrī, for this set of three days has the Gāyatrī at the midday pressing.

sanskrit_iast: stotriya anurūpayoś ca eva uktha mukhīyayoś ca nyūṅkhaḥ |
meaning: स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपयोश् च एव उक्थ मुखीययोश् च न्यूङ्खः |

sanskrit_iast: annam eva tad ātmani ca prajānām ca dadhāti |
meaning: अन्नम् एव तद् आत्मनि च प्रजानाम् च दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: ānuṣṭubham nyūṅkham nyūṅkhayed iti ha eka āhuḥ |
meaning: आनुष्टुभम् न्यूङ्खम् न्यूङ्खयेद् इति ह एक आहुः |

sanskrit_iast: vairājam nyūṅkham nyūṅkhayed iti sā sthitiḥ |
meaning: वैराजम् न्यूङ्खम् न्यूङ्खयेद् इति सा स्थितिः |

sanskrit_iast: annam eva tad yajñe ca yajamāneṣu ca dadhāti |
meaning: अन्नम् एव तद् यज्ञे च यजमानेषु च दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: ātmā vai pūrvam padam prajā uttamam |
meaning: आत्मा वै पूर्वम् पदम् प्रजा उत्तमम् |

sanskrit_iast: madhye vā idam ātmano annam dhīyate |
meaning: मध्ये वा इदम् आत्मनो अन्नम् धीयते |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā abhigrāsam annam adyād evam tat |
meaning: तद् यथा अभिग्रासम् अन्नम् अद्याद् एवम् तत् |

sanskrit_iast: indram id devatātaya ity aṣṭa indraḥ pragāthaḥ |
