sanskrit_iast: ubhābhyām eva te lokābhyām yajamānāḥ pāpmānam apaghnate |
meaning: उभाभ्याम् एव ते लोकाभ्याम् यजमानाः पाप्मानम् अपघ्नते |

sanskrit_iast: tān vai svara sāmāna ity ācakṣate |
meaning: तान् वै स्वर सामान इत्य् आचक्षते |

sanskrit_iast: etair ha vā atraya ādityam tamaso aspṛṇvata |
meaning: एतैर् ह वा अत्रय आदित्यम् तमसो अस्पृण्वत |

sanskrit_iast: yam vai sūryam svar bhānus tamasā avidhyad āsuraḥ |
meaning: यम् वै सूर्यम् स्वर् भानुस् तमसा अविध्यद् आसुरः |
text:
'The sun which Svarbhānu The Asura pierced with darkness, The Atris found it. None other could do so.'
By this the Svarasāmans are mentioned. The Marutvatīyas have (the word) 'who'; the Pragāthas of the Niṣkevalyas have (the word) 'who'. Prajāpati is 'Who'; the Svarasāmans are Prajāpati; they have Anuṣṭubh Nivids inserted. The Anuṣṭubh is the waters; the Svarasāmans are the waters, for all this (universe) is surrounded with the waters, for on both sides of yonder sun there are waters below and above. This is declared in a Ṛc,

sanskrit_iast: atrayas tam anvavindan na ahy anye aśaknuvann iti |
meaning: अत्रयस् तम् अन्वविन्दन् न अह्य् अन्ये अशक्नुवन्न् इति |

sanskrit_iast: svara sāmāno ha vā etena abhyuktāḥ |
meaning: स्वर सामानो ह वा एतेन अभ्युक्ताः |

sanskrit_iast: ubhayato hy amum ādityam āpo avastāc ca upariṣṭāc ca |
meaning: उभयतो ह्य् अमुम् आदित्यम् आपो अवस्ताच् च उपरिष्टाच् च |

sanskrit_iast: yā rocane parastāt sūryasya yāś ca avastād upatiṣṭhanta āpa iti |
meaning: या रोचने परस्तात् सूर्यस्य याश् च अवस्ताद् उपतिष्ठन्त आप इति |
text:
'The waters that stand above and below, In the realm of the sun.'
'O god, the mortal with sacrifice hither' is the Ājya of the first Svarasāman (day), containing the word 'hither' and connected with the Rathantara. 'Great strength in the beam' is (the Ājya ) of the second, (containing the word) 'great', and connected with the Bṛhat. 'O Agni, bring hither the most mighty' is (the Ājya) of the third, containing (the word) 'hither', and connected with the Rathantara. The Praüga of the first Svarasāman is by Madhuchandas, that of the second by Gṛtsamada, and that of the third in Uṣṇih verses by Atri; the explanation of these has been given. The strophe and antistrophe of the Marutvatīyas, the verses to Brahmaṇaspati, follow the model of the three-day (rite); the explanation of them has been given. 'Where is this hero who hath seen Indra'? is the Marutvatīya of the first Svarasāman, containing (the word) 'who' in 'where'. 'With what array, of one age, of one home?' is (the Marutvatīya ) of the second, containing (the word) 'who' in 'what'. 'Let him sing the Sāman springing forth as of a bird' is (the Marutvatīya ) of the third, containing (the word) 'who' in 'work (ka-rma)' in 'Those works most welcome to him'; Prajāpati is 'Who'; the Svarasāmans are Prajāpati. 'When thou wast born, O unequalled one'; on this strophe, which has a Bṛhatī as the third verse, some daily bring in the Svaras; if they do so, the strophe and antistrophe and the inserted verse are the same. 'What newest of praisers?' is the Pragātha containing (the word) 'who'; the explanation of this has been given.

sanskrit_iast: ā yajñair deva martya iti prathamasya svara sāmna ājyam āvad rāthantaram |
meaning: आ यज्ञैर् देव मर्त्य इति प्रथमस्य स्वर साम्न आज्यम् आवद् राथन्तरम् |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhad vayo hi bhānava iti dvitīyasya bṛhad bārhatam |
meaning: बृहद् वयो हि भानव इति द्वितीयस्य बृहद् बार्हतम् |

sanskrit_iast: agna ojiṣṭham ā bhara iti tṛtīyasya āvad rāthantaram |
meaning: अग्न ओजिष्ठम् आ भर इति तृतीयस्य आवद् राथन्तरम् |

sanskrit_iast: anvāyattā marutvatīyānām pratipad anucarā anvāyattā brāhmaṇaspatyās tryaha rūpeṇa |
meaning: अन्वायत्ता मरुत्वतीयानाम् प्रतिपद् अनुचरा अन्वायत्ता ब्राह्मणस्पत्यास् त्र्यह रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: kva sya vīraḥ ko apaśyad indram iti prathamasya svara sāmno marutvatīyam kva iti kadvat |
meaning: क्व स्य वीरः को अपश्यद् इन्द्रम् इति प्रथमस्य स्वर साम्नो मरुत्वतीयम् क्व इति कद्वत् |

sanskrit_iast: kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīḍā iti dvitīyasya kayā iti kadvat |
meaning: कया शुभा सवयसः सनीडा इति द्वितीयस्य कया इति कद्वत् |

sanskrit_iast: yaj jāyathā apūrvyā ity etasminn u ha eke bṛhatī tṛtīye stotriye anvaham svarāṇy anvāyātayanti |
meaning: यज् जायथा अपूर्व्या इत्य् एतस्मिन्न् उ ह एके बृहती तृतीये स्तोत्रिये अन्वहम् स्वराण्य् अन्वायातयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: etāv eva stotriyā anurūpāv eṣā dhāyyā |
meaning: एताव् एव स्तोत्रिया अनुरूपाव् एषा धाय्या |

sanskrit_iast: kan navyo atasīnām iti kadvān pragāthas tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: कन् नव्यो अतसीनाम् इति कद्वान् प्रगाथस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha rathantarasya yonis tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ रथन्तरस्य योनिस् तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |
text:
Then the basis of the Rathantara (is recited). 'Which thou, O Indra, dost support' is a couple of verses, to avoid isolation; (it is used, thinking) 'Let not that Bṛhatī have been recited by itself alone as it were'. 'O Indra, O generous one, to thee we have turned' is the normal Triṣṭubh (triad) which supports the pressing; the explanation of this has been given. 'That most effectual for aid (power) of them' is the
Niṣkevalya in Anuṣṭubhs, containing (the word) 'hither' in 'O Indra, do thou hither bear that power,' and connected with the Rathantara. 'What hath not been wrought by him?' is the Pragātha containing (the word) 'who'; the explanation of this has been given.

sanskrit_iast: yam indra dadhiṣe tvam iti dvṛco aneka pātitāyai |
meaning: यम् इन्द्र दधिषे त्वम् इति द्वृचो अनेक पातितायै |

sanskrit_iast: na id asau bṛhaty ekākinī iva śastā asad iti |
meaning: न इद् असौ बृहत्य् एकाकिनी इव शस्ता असद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: indra tubhyam in maghavann abhūma iti vijñāta traiṣṭubham savana dharaṇam tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: इन्द्र तुभ्यम् इन् मघवन्न् अभूम इति विज्ञात त्रैष्टुभम् सवन धरणम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: yas te sādhiṣṭho avasa ity ānuṣṭubham niṣkevalyam tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: यस् ते साधिष्ठो अवस इत्य् आनुष्टुभम् निष्केवल्यम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: indra kratuṣ ṭam ā bhara ity āvad rāthantaram |
meaning: इन्द्र क्रतुष् टम् आ भर इत्य् आवद् राथन्तरम् |

sanskrit_iast: kad ū nv asya akṛtam iti kadvān pragāthas tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: कद् ऊ न्व् अस्य अकृतम् इति कद्वान् प्रगाथस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha bṛhato yonis tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ बृहतो योनिस् तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |
text: Then the basis of the Bṛhat (is recited). 'They call thee, men, when (the juice) is pressed' is a couplet, to avoid isolation; (it is used, thinking) 'Let not that Bṛhatī have been recited by itself alone as it were.' 'O Adhvaryu, O hero, to the mighty the pressed (juices)' is the normal Triṣṭubh (triplet) which supports the pressing; the explanation of this has been given. 'The singers sing thee' is the Niṣkevalya in Anuṣṭubhs, containing (the word) 'up' in 'Up with a rod they have raised thee', and connected with the Bṛhat. 'These thee, O thou of much light' is the Pragātha, containing (the word) 'who (ka)' in kavarṇa in 'of pure hues (pāvakavarṇāḥ)'; the explanation of this has been given.

sanskrit_iast: svaranti tvā sute nara iti dvṛco aneka pātitāyai |
meaning: स्वरन्ति त्वा सुते नर इति द्वृचो अनेक पातितायै |

sanskrit_iast: na id asau bṛhaty ekākinī iva śastā asad iti |
meaning: न इद् असौ बृहत्य् एकाकिनी इव शस्ता असद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: adhvaryo vīra pra mahe sutānām iti vijñāta traiṣṭubham sanava dharaṇam tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अध्वर्यो वीर प्र महे सुतानाम् इति विज्ञात त्रैष्टुभम् सनव धरणम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇa ity ānuṣṭubham niṣkevalyam tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिण इत्य् आनुष्टुभम् निष्केवल्यम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: ud vaṃśam iva yemira ity udvad bārhatam |
meaning: उद् वंशम् इव येमिर इत्य् उद्वद् बार्हतम् |

sanskrit_iast: imā u tvā prūravaso iti pragāthaḥ pāvaka varṇāḥ kavarṇā iti kadvāṃs tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: इमा उ त्वा प्रूरवसो इति प्रगाथः पावक वर्णाः कवर्णा इति कद्वांस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha rathantarasya yonir atha bṛhatas tayor uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ रथन्तरस्य योनिर् अथ बृहतस् तयोर् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |
text:
Then the basis of the Rathantara (is recited), then that of the Bṛhat. 'Bounding as a wild elephant' is a couplet, to avoid isolation; (it is used, thinking) 'Let not that Bṛhatī have been recited by itself alone as it were'. 'This bowl with the drink for Indra' is the normal Triṣṭubh (triplet) which supports the pressing; the explanation of this has been given. 'Indra all have caused to grow' is the Niṣkevalya in Anuṣṭubhs, containing (the word) 'towards' in 'Towards thee we sing our praise'; this is a symbol of the Rathantara. They say 'He should not place the Nivid in the Anuṣṭubh (hymns), he confuses the arrangement of metres at the midday (performance).' Having recited the Anuṣṭubhs first for the obtaining of desire, he inserts a Nivid in the Triṣṭubh (hymns); thus in due order is the Nivid inserted; it being inserted in due order places them in due order in all the worlds and in all desires. 'Hither thy car with every boon, O dread one'; (he inserts a Nivid) in (this hymn), containing (the word) 'hither' and connected with the Rathantara on the first day. 'He hath drunk hence, most marvellous and up for us', (he inserts a Nivid) in (this hymn) containing (the word) 'up', and connected with the Bṛhat on the second (day). 'In thee from of old the songs have gone together, O Indra', (he inserts a Nivid) in (this hymn), containing (the word) 'go' and being a symbol of the end on the third (day). If the Pṛṣṭhas are the Svaras the Sāman
chanters use the Bṛhat and the Rathantara in the Pavamānas, but, if the Pṛṣṭhas are the Bṛhat and the Rathantara, then the Sāman chanters use the Svaras in the Pavamānas. ‘But the Pṛṣṭhas should be the Svaras only,’ Kauṣītaki used to say; ‘for they are the Svarasāmans; by the Pṛṣṭhas the gods have touched the world of heaven; the Pṛṣṭhas are the Svaras, for the touching of the world of heaven.’

sanskrit_iast: dānā mṛgo na vāraṇa iti dvṛco aneka pātitāyai |
meaning: दाना मृगो न वारण इति द्वृचो अनेक पातितायै |

sanskrit_iast: na id asau bṛhaty ekākinī iva śastā asad iti |
meaning: न इद् असौ बृहत्य् एकाकिनी इव शस्ता असद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: idam tyat pātram indra pānam iti vijñāta traiṣṭubham savana dharaṇam tasya uktam brahmaṇam |
meaning: इदम् त्यत् पात्रम् इन्द्र पानम् इति विज्ञात त्रैष्टुभम् सवन धरणम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्रह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: indram viśvā avīvṛdhann ity ānuṣṭubham niṣkevalyam tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: इन्द्रम् विश्वा अवीवृधन्न् इत्य् आनुष्टुभम् निष्केवल्यम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: tvām abhi pra ṇonuma ity abhivat |
meaning: त्वाम् अभि प्र णोनुम इत्य् अभिवत् |

sanskrit_iast: evam nu yadi svara pṛṣṭhā bhavanti |
meaning: एवम् नु यदि स्वर पृष्ठा भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: yadi vā svara yoniṣu bṛhad rathantare ūḍhe syātām |
meaning: यदि वा स्वर योनिषु बृहद् रथन्तरे ऊढे स्याताम् |

sanskrit_iast: yady u bṛhad rathantare pṛṣṭhe kuryuḥ |
meaning: यद्य् उ बृहद् रथन्तरे पृष्ठे कुर्युः |

sanskrit_iast: prajātā stotriyā anurūpā bārhata rāthantarāḥ prajñātā dhāyyā |
meaning: प्रजाता स्तोत्रिया अनुरूपा बार्हत राथन्तराः प्रज्ञाता धाय्या |

sanskrit_iast: sāmnoḥ pragāthau pūrvau śastvā kadvataḥ pragāthān śaṃsanti |
meaning: साम्नोः प्रगाथौ पूर्वौ शस्त्वा कद्वतः प्रगाथान् शंसन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: uddharati dvecāṃś ca savana dharaṇāni ca |
meaning: उद्धरति द्वेचांश् च सवन धरणानि च |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur na anuṣṭupsu nividam dadhyān mohayati klṛptac chandaso madhyaṃdinam iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् न अनुष्टुप्सु निविदम् दध्यान् मोहयति क्लृप्तच् छन्दसो मध्यंदिनम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: ānuṣṭubhāni pūrvāṇi śastvā kāmasya upāptyai traiṣṭubheṣu nividam dadhāti |
meaning: आनुष्टुभानि पूर्वाणि शस्त्वा कामस्य उपाप्त्यै त्रैष्टुभेषु निविदम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: arvāg ratham viśva vāram ta ugra iti prathame ahany āvati rāthantare |
meaning: अर्वाग् रथम् विश्व वारम् त उग्र इति प्रथमे अहन्य् आवति राथन्तरे |

sanskrit_iast: apādita ud u naś citratama iti dvitīya udvati bārhate |
meaning: अपादित उद् उ नश् चित्रतम इति द्वितीय उद्वति बार्हते |

sanskrit_iast: sam ca tve jagmur gira indra pūrvīr iti tṛtīye gatavay anta rūpe |
meaning: सम् च त्वे जग्मुर् गिर इन्द्र पूर्वीर् इति तृतीये गतवय् अन्त रूपे |

sanskrit_iast: sā enān yathā yatham dhīyamānā sarveṣu ca lokeṣu sarveṣu ca kāmeṣu yathā yatham dadhāti |
meaning: सा एनान् यथा यथम् धीयमाना सर्वेषु च लोकेषु सर्वेषु च कामेषु यथा यथम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhad rathantare eva tarhi sāmagāha pavamāneṣu kurvanti |
meaning: बृहद् रथन्तरे एव तर्हि सामगाह पवमानेषु कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: svarāṇi tv eva pṛṣṭhāni syur iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: स्वराणि त्व् एव पृष्ठानि स्युर् इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: pṛṣṭhair vai devāḥ svargam lokam asprakṣan |
meaning: पृष्ठैर् वै देवाः स्वर्गम् लोकम् अस्प्रक्षन् |

sanskrit_iast: pṛṣṭhyasya ṣaḍahasya samūḍhasya yāḥ pūrvasya tryahasya vaiśvadevānām pratipadas tāḥ pratipadaḥ |
meaning: पृष्ठ्यस्य षडहस्य समूढस्य याः पूर्वस्य त्र्यहस्य वैश्वदेवानाम् प्रतिपदस् ताः प्रतिपदः |
text: The strophes (used) are those of the Vaiśvadeva (litanies) of the first three days of the Pṛṣṭha Ṣaḍaha in conjunct form. The third pressings with the antistrophes are the third pressings of the second three days. The Vaiśvadeva (hymns) there are taken out and other crypto-Vaiśvadevas, without mention (of the deities), connected with Prajāpati, are inserted, ‘This drink to you, O swift to wrath,’ ‘Him of old, aforetime, at all times, now,’ and ‘What vessel here of those that are pious?’ in place of (the hymn) of Nābhānediṣṭha. There should, however, be used the open Vaiśvadevas, ‘Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman’ on the first day, containing (the word) ‘who’ in ‘Having established (s-ka-bhitvī) the sky’; ‘I hail the gods of great fame for security’ on the second, containing (the word) ‘who’ in ‘Light making (jyotiṣkṛtaḥ).’ ‘Dawn and night (uṣāsā naktā) the great ones, of fair form’ on the third (day), containing (the word) ‘who’ in ‘night’. Prajāpati is ‘Who’; the Svarasāmans are Prajāpati. They are made up as Agniṣṭomas or Ukthyas; ‘As Agniṣṭomas’ (is) Paiṅgya's view; they become possessed of splendour who perform Agniṣṭomas. ‘Let them be Ukthyas,’ Kauṣītaki used to say. The Ukthya is a successful form of sacrifice, for it has fifteen Stotras, fifteen Śastras; they make thirty Stotras and Śastras; it makes up the Virāj; the Virāj is prosperity and proper food; (it serves) for the winning of the Virāj as prosperity and proper food.

sanskrit_iast: yāny uttarasya tryahasya tṛtīya savanāni tāni tṛtīya savanāni sānucarāṇi |
meaning: यान्य् उत्तरस्य त्र्यहस्य तृतीय सवनानि तानि तृतीय सवनानि सानुचराणि |

sanskrit_iast: tad yāni tatra vaiśvadevāni tāny uddhṛtya anyāny anyāny aniruktāni prājāpatyāni parokṣa vaiśvadevāny avadhīyante |
meaning: तद् यानि तत्र वैश्वदेवानि तान्य् उद्धृत्य अन्यान्य् अन्यान्य् अनिरुक्तानि प्राजापत्यानि परोक्ष वैश्वदेवान्य् अवधीयन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: pra vaḥ pāntam raghu manyavo andhas tam pratnathā pūrvathā viśvathā īmathā kad itthā nṝnḥ pātram devayatām iti |
meaning: प्र वः पान्तम् रघु मन्यवो अन्धस् तम् प्रत्नथा पूर्वथा विश्वथा ईमथा कद् इत्था नॄन्ः पात्रम् देवयताम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad vai khalu pratyakṣa vaiśvadevāny eva avadhīyeran |
meaning: तद् वै खलु प्रत्यक्ष वैश्वदेवान्य् एव अवधीयेरन् |

sanskrit_iast: agnir indro varuṇo mitro aryamā iti prathame ahani dyām skabhitvī iti kadvat |
meaning: अग्निर् इन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा इति प्रथमे अहनि द्याम् स्कभित्वी इति कद्वत् |

sanskrit_iast: devān huve bṛhat śravasaḥ svastaya iti dvitīye jyotiṣ kṛta iti kadvat |
meaning: देवान् हुवे बृहत् श्रवसः स्वस्तय इति द्वितीये ज्योतिष् कृत इति कद्वत् |

sanskrit_iast: uṣāsā naktā bṛhatī supeśasā iti tṛtīye naktā iti kadvat |
meaning: उषासा नक्ता बृहती सुपेशसा इति तृतीये नक्ता इति कद्वत् |

sanskrit_iast: te agniṣṭomā vā ukthyā vā saṃtiṣṭhante |
meaning: ते अग्निष्टोमा वा उक्थ्या वा संतिष्ठन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: brahma varcasino bhavanti ye agniṣṭomān upayanti |
meaning: ब्रह्म वर्चसिनो भवन्ति ये अग्निष्टोमान् उपयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: ukthyāḥ syur iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: उक्थ्याः स्युर् इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: sa vai yajña kratuḥ samṛddho ya ukthyaḥ |
meaning: स वै यज्ञ क्रतुः समृद्धो य उक्थ्यः |

sanskrit_iast: śriyo virājo anna adyasya upāptyai śriyo virājo anna adyasya upāptyai |
meaning: श्रियो विराजो अन्न अद्यस्य उपाप्त्यै श्रियो विराजो अन्न अद्यस्य उपाप्त्यै |

text:
The waters practised fervour; after practising fervour they
conceived; thence was this sun born on the sixth month; therefore on the sixth month the performers of a session perform the Divākīrtya. It goes north for six months, then for six reversed; therefore the performers go for six months forward, then for six months reversed. Without it are hunger and repeated death; they conquer hunger and repeated death who perform the Viṣuvant day. It has these symbols in its verses: (the word) ‘sun’, (the word) ‘blaze’, (the word) ‘light’, (the word) ‘ornament’, (the word) ‘shine’, (the word) ‘delight’. ‘From the ocean the wave rich in sweetness hath arisen’ is the Ājya; for from the ocean, from the waters he comes out. It contains (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘Indra one, the sun one hath produced’; this is a symbol of this day. These (verses) recited together make up twenty-one Anuṣṭubhs; he who gives heat here is twenty-onefold; thus he makes it successful with its own symbol. The Praüga is in Triṣṭubh; this is the middle of the days; the Triṣṭubh is the middle of metres. Thus he makes it successful with its own metre.

sanskrit_iast: tata eṣa ādityo ajāyata ṣaṣṭhe māsi |
meaning: तत एष आदित्यो अजायत षष्ठे मासि |

sanskrit_iast: tasmāt satriṇaḥ ṣaṣṭhe māsidivā kīrtyam upayanti |
meaning: तस्मात् सत्रिणः षष्ठे मासिदिवा कीर्त्यम् उपयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: sa ṣaṇ māsān udann eti ṣaḍ āvṛttaḥ |
meaning: स षण् मासान् उदन्न् एति षड् आवृत्तः |

sanskrit_iast: tasmāt satriṇaḥ ṣaḍ eva ūrdhvān māso yanti ṣaḍ āvṛttān |
meaning: तस्मात् सत्रिणः षड् एव ऊर्ध्वान् मासो यन्ति षड् आवृत्तान् |

sanskrit_iast: antareṇa u ha vā etam aśanāyā ca punar mṛtyuś ca |
meaning: अन्तरेण उ ह वा एतम् अशनाया च पुनर् मृत्युश् च |

sanskrit_iast: apāśanāyām ca punar mṛtyum ca jayanti ye vaiṣuvatam ahar upayanti |
meaning: अपाशनायाम् च पुनर् मृत्युम् च जयन्ति ये वैषुवतम् अहर् उपयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: sūryavad bhānumaj jyotiṣmad rukmavad rucitavadd haryatavad iti |
meaning: सूर्यवद् भानुमज् ज्योतिष्मद् रुक्मवद् रुचितवद्द् हर्यतवद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: samudrād ūrmir madhumān udārad ity ājyam |
meaning: समुद्राद् ऊर्मिर् मधुमान् उदारद् इत्य् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: indra ekam sūryam ekam jajāna iti sūryavat |
meaning: इन्द्र एकम् सूर्यम् एकम् जजान इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: ekaviṃśo vā eṣa ya eṣa tapati |
meaning: एकविंशो वा एष य एष तपति |

sanskrit_iast: kuvid aṅga namasā ye vṛdhāsa iti vāyavyam |
meaning: कुविद् अङ्ग नमसा ये वृधास इति वायव्यम् |
text: ‘Were not they who were made great with homage?’ is (the triplet) to Vāyu, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘They made bright the dawn with the sun’; this is a symbol of this day. The succeeding triplet is addressed to Indra and Vāyu, ‘So far as the power of the body, so far as the might’, with the symbol (of the day) in ‘So far as men with the eye may discern’. ‘Up the eye of you two, O Varuṇa, fair of aspect’ is (the triplet) to Indra and Varuṇa, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘The sun goeth extending of the pious one’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘Hither, O Nāsatyas, with chariot rich in cattle’ is (the triplet) to the Aśvins; the third (verse) contains (the word) ‘blaze’ in ‘The god Savitṛ hath raised aloft the blaze’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘Come hither to us, O impetuous god, with might’ is (the triplet) to Indra, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘Heroes for life for the gaining of the sun’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘Let the prayer go forward from the abode of holy order’ is (the triplet) to the All-gods, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘The sun hath created the kine with his rays’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘May Sarasvatī for us rejoicing’ is (the triplet) to Sarasvatī, with the symbol in ‘O happy one, thou hast unbound the doors of holy order.’ This is the Praüga of Vasiṣṭha arranged in triads of Triṣṭubh verses, and containing (the word) ‘sun’. Vasiṣṭha is Prajāpati; verily in Prajāpati they succeed in all their desires.

sanskrit_iast: ata eva uttaram tṛcam aindravāyavam yāvat taras tanvo yāvad oja iti |
meaning: अत एव उत्तरम् तृचम् ऐन्द्रवायवम् यावत् तरस् तन्वो यावद् ओज इति |

sanskrit_iast: yāvan naraś cakṣasā dīdhyānā ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: यावन् नरश् चक्षसा दीध्याना इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: ud vām cakṣur varuṇa supratīkam iti maitrāvaruṇam |
meaning: उद् वाम् चक्षुर् वरुण सुप्रतीकम् इति मैत्रावरुणम् |

sanskrit_iast: devayor eti sūryas tatanvān iti sūryavat |
meaning: देवयोर् एति सूर्यस् ततन्वान् इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: ā gomatā nāsatyā rathena ity āśvinam |
meaning: आ गोमता नासत्या रथेन इत्य् आश्विनम् |

sanskrit_iast: tasya ūrdhvam bhānum savitā devo aśred iti tṛtīyā bhānumatī |
meaning: तस्य ऊर्ध्वम् भानुम् सविता देवो अश्रेद् इति तृतीया भानुमती |

sanskrit_iast: ā no deva śavasā yāhi śuṣminn ity aindram |
meaning: आ नो देव शवसा याहि शुष्मिन्न् इत्य् ऐन्द्रम् |

sanskrit_iast: tanūṣu śūrāḥ sūryasya sātāv iti sūryavat |
meaning: तनूषु शूराः सूर्यस्य साताव् इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: pra brahma etu sadanād ṛtasya iti vaiśvadevam |
meaning: प्र ब्रह्म एतु सदनाद् ऋतस्य इति वैश्वदेवम् |

sanskrit_iast: vi raśmibhiḥ sasṛje sūryo gā iti sūryavat |
meaning: वि रश्मिभिः ससृजे सूर्यो गा इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣoṇā iti sārasvatam |
meaning: उत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषोणा इति सारस्वतम् |

sanskrit_iast: dvāra āvṛtasya subhage vyāvar ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: द्वार आवृतस्य सुभगे व्यावर् इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: eṣa vā u vāsiṣṭhas tṛca klṛptas traiṣṭubhaḥ praugaḥ |
meaning: एष वा उ वासिष्ठस् तृच क्लृप्तस् त्रैष्टुभः प्रौगः |

sanskrit_iast: sa punas tatāv ayāta yāmā bhavati |
meaning: स पुनस् तताव् अयात यामा भवति |

sanskrit_iast: prajāpatāv eva tat sarvān kāmān ṛdhnuvanti |
meaning: प्रजापताव् एव तत् सर्वान् कामान् ऋध्नुवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur na traiṣṭubham prātaḥ savanam syān mohayati klṛptac chandaso yajña mukham iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् न त्रैष्टुभम् प्रातः सवनम् स्यान् मोहयति क्लृप्तच् छन्दसो यज्ञ मुखम् इति |
text: They say ‘The morning pressing should not be in Triṣṭubh; he disturbs the beginning of the sacrifice from its appointed metre; let it be the one-day (form) only’. The one-day (rite) is light; he who here gives heat is light; verily thus they cause light to prosper with light. ‘Forward to the god, to Agni’ and ‘Thou hast glory of rule’, these two are the Ājya. These (verses) recited together make up twenty-one Anuṣṭubhs; the explanation of these has been given. The Praüga is by Madhuchandas; the explanation of this has been given. ‘Thee like a car for aid’ is the strophe of the Marutvatīya; ‘This drink, O bright one, is pressed’ is the antistrophe; this is the normal one-day form; the explanation of this has been given. ‘With what array, of one age, of one home?’ is the Marutvatīya, with the symbol (of this day) in ‘brightness’ in ‘array’ (śubhā). ‘That ram that winneth the light I glorify’ is in Jagatī, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘Thou didst support the sun in the sky to see’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘Thou hast been born dread for impetuous strength,’ in this Triṣṭubh (hymn) he inserts a Nivid. (The hymn has) the symbol (of this day) in ‘Dispel the darkness, fill full our vision’. Two sets, Triṣṭubhs and Jagatīs, are recited, for the sun here gives heat, resting on the Triṣṭubh and the Jagatī; thus openly they obtain it.

sanskrit_iast: tasya pra vo devāya agnaye tvam hi kṣaitavad yaśa ity ete ubhe tad ājyam |
meaning: तस्य प्र वो देवाय अग्नये त्वम् हि क्षैतवद् यश इत्य् एते उभे तद् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: tā ekaviṃśatim anuṣṭubhas tāsām uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: ता एकविंशतिम् अनुष्टुभस् तासाम् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīḍā iti marutvatīyam |
meaning: कया शुभा सवयसः सनीडा इति मरुत्वतीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: tyam su meṣam mahayā svarvidam iti jāgatam adhārayo divyā sūrya dṛśa iti sūryavat |
meaning: त्यम् सु मेषम् महया स्वर्विदम् इति जागतम् अधारयो दिव्या सूर्य दृश इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāya ity etasmiṃs traiṣṭubhe nividam dadhāti |
meaning: जनिष्ठा उग्रः सहसे तुराय इत्य् एतस्मिंस् त्रैष्टुभे निविदम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: apa dhvāntam ūrṇuhi pūrdhi cakṣur ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: अप ध्वान्तम् ऊर्णुहि पूर्धि चक्षुर् इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: tā vā ubhayyas triṣṭub jagatyaḥ śasyante |
meaning: ता वा उभय्यस् त्रिष्टुब् जगत्यः शस्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: triṣṭub jagatyor ha vā eṣa āhita ādityaḥ pratiṣṭhitas tapati |
meaning: त्रिष्टुब् जगत्योर् ह वा एष आहित आदित्यः प्रतिष्ठितस् तपति |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhad etasya ahnaḥ pṛṣṭham syād iti ha eka āhuḥ |
meaning: बृहद् एतस्य अह्नः पृष्ठम् स्याद् इति ह एक आहुः |
text:
‘The Bṛhat should be the Pṛṣṭha of this day’ some hold, saying ‘He who here gives heat is connected with the Bṛhat; the Bṛhat gives heat; moreover, the Mahādivākīrtya is not a Pṛṣṭha, the Bṛhat and Rathantara are openly Pṛṣṭhas; therefore the Bṛhat alone should be the Pṛṣṭha of this day.’ If they should perform the Bṛhat on a Pragātha containing (the word) ‘sun’ and Pragāthas containing ‘sun’, (it is) with the symbol of this day. ‘Indra hath knowledge for the hearing of this’ is the beginning of the litany, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘He is the lively pathmaker for the sun’; this is the symbol of this day. ‘The Mahādivākīrtya alone should be the Pṛṣṭha of this day’ is the rule. The Mahādivākīrtya is openly a Sāman; thus with its own Sāman they make it success-
ful. Now some perform it on Triṣṭubh verses; he who here gives heat is connected with the Triṣṭubh; thus it with its own metre they make successful. ‘Let it be performed on Bṛhatī verses’ some say; he who here gives heat is connected with the Bṛhatī; thus with its own metre they make it successful. But the rule is ‘Let it be performed on Jagatī verses’; he who here gives heat is connected with the Jagatī; thus with its own metre they make it successful.

sanskrit_iast: bārhato vā eṣa ya eṣa tapati |
meaning: बार्हतो वा एष य एष तपति |

sanskrit_iast: atho apṛṣṭham vā etad yan mahā divā kīrtyam |
meaning: अथो अपृष्ठम् वा एतद् यन् महा दिवा कीर्त्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha ete eva pratyakṣe pṛṣṭhe yad bṛhad rathantare |
meaning: अथ एते एव प्रत्यक्षे पृष्ठे यद् बृहद् रथन्तरे |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād bṛhad eva etasya ahnaḥ pṛṣṭham syād iti |
meaning: तस्माद् बृहद् एव एतस्य अह्नः पृष्ठम् स्याद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: yady u sūryavati pragāthe bṛhat kuryuḥ |
meaning: यद्य् उ सूर्यवति प्रगाथे बृहत् कुर्युः |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād bṛhad eva etasya ahnaḥ pṛṣṭham syād iti |
meaning: तस्माद् बृहद् एव एतस्य अह्नः पृष्ठम् स्याद् इति |

sanskrit_iast: yady u sūryavati pragāthe bṛhat kuryuḥ |
meaning: यद्य् उ सूर्यवति प्रगाथे बृहत् कुर्युः |

sanskrit_iast: sūryavataś ca pragāthān etasya eva ahno rūpeṇa |
meaning: सूर्यवतश् च प्रगाथान् एतस्य एव अह्नो रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: indraḥ kila śrutyā asya veda ity uktha mukhīyā sa hi jiṣṇuḥ pathikṛt sūryāya iti sūryavatī |
meaning: इन्द्रः किल श्रुत्या अस्य वेद इत्य् उक्थ मुखीया स हि जिष्णुः पथिकृत् सूर्याय इति सूर्यवती |

sanskrit_iast: mahā divā kīrtyam eva etasya ahnaḥ pṛṣṭham syād iti sā sthitiḥ |
meaning: महा दिवा कीर्त्यम् एव एतस्य अह्नः पृष्ठम् स्याद् इति सा स्थितिः |

sanskrit_iast: asau vā etat pratyakṣam sāma yo asau tapati yan mahā divā kīrtyam |
meaning: असौ वा एतत् प्रत्यक्षम् साम यो असौ तपति यन् महा दिवा कीर्त्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: traiṣṭubho vā eṣa ya eṣa tapati |
meaning: त्रैष्टुभो वा एष य एष तपति |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhatīṣu syād ity u ha eka āhuḥ |
meaning: बृहतीषु स्याद् इत्य् उ ह एक आहुः |

sanskrit_iast: bārhato vā eṣa ya eṣa tapati |
meaning: बार्हतो वा एष य एष तपति |

sanskrit_iast: jagatīṣu syād iti tv eva sthitam |
meaning: जगतीषु स्याद् इति त्व् एव स्थितम् |

sanskrit_iast: jāgato vā eṣa ya eṣa tapati |
meaning: जागतो वा एष य एष तपति |

sanskrit_iast: vibhrāḍ bṛhat pibatu somyam madhv iti stotriyas tṛco viśva bhrāḍ bhrājo mahi sūryo dṛśa iti vivān bhrājiṣmānt sūryavān |
meaning: विभ्राड् बृहत् पिबतु सोम्यम् मध्व् इति स्तोत्रियस् तृचो विश्व भ्राड् भ्राजो महि सूर्यो दृश इति विवान् भ्राजिष्मान्त् सूर्यवान् |
text: ‘May the radiant one drink the great Soma-made mead’ is the strophe triplet, containing in ‘All radiant, brilliant, great, the sun to see’ (the words) ‘apart (vi)’, ‘radiance’, and ‘sun’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘The sun hath loosened apart his car in the middle of the sky’ is the antistrophe, containing (the words) ‘apart’ and ‘sun’; the common metre is Jagatī, but the rule is (the triplet) to Sūrya, ‘For all love thee, of one mind, one countenance’, with the symbol of the sun in ‘Long living may we see, O sun’. ‘Assuredly thou art great, O sun’ is the Pragātha of the Sāman, containing (the word) ‘sun’; this is a symbol of this day. Here he recites the bases of the Bṛhat and the Rathantara; ‘Indra hath knowledge for the hearing of this’ is the beginning of the litany, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘He is the lively pathmaker for the sun’; this is a symbol of this day, but the rule is (a verse ) to Sūrya, ‘Be favourable to us with thine eye, favourable to us with the day’, containing the symbol of the sun in ‘Give us, O sun, this wealth varied.’ ‘Who alone is to be invoked by mortals’ is (a hymn ) in Triṣṭubh, with the symbol ‘The divine atmosphere thou didst make to shine.’ So if they make the Mahādivākīrtya the Pṛṣṭha, but, if they perform the Bṛhat on its own basis, having recited the extension of the Bṛhat, he recites the basis of the Rathantara; ‘Indra hath knowledge for the hearing of this’ is the beginning of the litany, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘He is the lively pathmaker for the sun’; this is a symbol of this day.

sanskrit_iast: vi sūryo madhye amucad ratham diva ity anurūpo vivānt sūryavān |
meaning: वि सूर्यो मध्ये अमुचद् रथम् दिव इत्य् अनुरूपो विवान्त् सूर्यवान् |

sanskrit_iast: viśvahā tvā sumanasaḥ sucakṣasa iti tv eva sthitaḥ saruyaḥ sauryasya |
meaning: विश्वहा त्वा सुमनसः सुचक्षस इति त्व् एव स्थितः सरुयः सौर्यस्य |

sanskrit_iast: jyog jīvāḥ prati paśyema sūryā ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: ज्योग् जीवाः प्रति पश्येम सूर्या इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: baṇ mahān asi sūrya iti sūryavānt sāma pragāthaḥ |
meaning: बण् महान् असि सूर्य इति सूर्यवान्त् साम प्रगाथः |

sanskrit_iast: indraḥ kila śrutyā asya veda ity ukthya mukhīyā sa hi jiṣṇu pathikṛt sūryāya iti sūryavatī |
meaning: इन्द्रः किल श्रुत्या अस्य वेद इत्य् उक्थ्य मुखीया स हि जिष्णु पथिकृत् सूर्याय इति सूर्यवती |

sanskrit_iast: śam no bhava cakṣasā śam no ahnā iti tv eva sthitā saurī sauryasya |
meaning: शम् नो भव चक्षसा शम् नो अह्ना इति त्व् एव स्थिता सौरी सौर्यस्य |

sanskrit_iast: tat sūrya draviṇam dhehi citram ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: तत् सूर्य द्रविणम् धेहि चित्रम् इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: ya eka idd havyaś carṣaṇīnām iti traiṣṭubham |
meaning: य एक इद्द् हव्यश् चर्षणीनाम् इति त्रैष्टुभम् |

sanskrit_iast: divyāni dīpayo antarikṣā ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: दिव्यानि दीपयो अन्तरिक्षा इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: evam nu yadi mahā divā kīrtyam pṛṣṭham bhavati |
meaning: एवम् नु यदि महा दिवा कीर्त्यम् पृष्ठम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: yady u vai bṛhat sva yonau kuryuḥ |
meaning: यद्य् उ वै बृहत् स्व योनौ कुर्युः |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhata ātānam śastvā rathantarasya yonim śaṃsati |
meaning: बृहत आतानम् शस्त्वा रथन्तरस्य योनिम् शंसति |

sanskrit_iast: indraḥ kila śrutyā asya veda ity ukthya mukhīyā sa hi jiṣṇuḥ pathikṛt sūryāya iti sūryavatī |
meaning: इन्द्रः किल श्रुत्या अस्य वेद इत्य् उक्थ्य मुखीया स हि जिष्णुः पथिकृत् सूर्याय इति सूर्यवती |

sanskrit_iast: dyaur na ya indra abhi bhūma arya iti traiṣṭubham indraḥ kutsāya sūryasya sātāv iti sūryavat |
meaning: द्यौर् न य इन्द्र अभि भूम अर्य इति त्रैष्टुभम् इन्द्रः कुत्साय सूर्यस्य साताव् इति सूर्यवत् |
text:
‘As the sky surpasseth the earth, O Indra, that which our foes’ is (the hymn) in Triṣṭubh, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘Indra to Kutsa in the winning of the sun’; this is a symbol of this day. If they do not (perform it) on its own basis, ‘Turning as it were to the sun’ is the
strophe, containing (the word) 'sun'; this is a symbol of this day. 'If, O Indra, a hundred skies were thine' is the antistrophe, containing (the word) 'sun' in 'a thousand suns'; this is the symbol of this day. 'Who most active, ever slayeth' is the Pragātha of the Sāman, containing (the word) 'sun' in 'In bodies, in the waters, the sun'; this is a symbol of this day. Then he recites the bases of the Bṛhat and the Rathantara. 'Indra hath knowledge for the hearing of this' is the beginning of the litany; the explanation of this has been given. 'Who alone is to be invoked by mortals' is (the hymn) in Triṣṭubh; the explanation of this has been given. So now if they perform the Bṛhat on its own basis or on a different basis. If they perform without the two Sāmans, it is the same up to the beginning of the litany; he should take out the bases of the Bṛhat and the Rathantara. 'Praise him who hath might to overcome' is (the hymn) in Triṣṭubh, with the symbol in 'Increase with praises the bull of mortals.' The next is the same. 'The ram, much invoked, worthy of praise' is (the hymn) in Jagatī, containing (the word) 'sun' in 'Thou didst indeed mount the sun in heaven to see'; this is a symbol of this day. Both sets, Triṣṭubh and Jagatī, are recited; the sun here gives heat, resting established on the Triṣṭubh and the Jagatī; thus it openly they touch.

sanskrit_iast: śrāyanta iva sūryam iti sūryavānt stotriyaḥ |
meaning: श्रायन्त इव सूर्यम् इति सूर्यवान्त् स्तोत्रियः |

sanskrit_iast: yad dyāva indra te śatam ity anurūpaḥ sahasram sūryā iti sūryavān |
meaning: यद् द्याव इन्द्र ते शतम् इत्य् अनुरूपः सहस्रम् सूर्या इति सूर्यवान् |

sanskrit_iast: yaḥ satrāhā vicarṣaṇir iti sāma pragāthas tanūṣv apsu sūrya iti sūryavān |
meaning: यः सत्राहा विचर्षणिर् इति साम प्रगाथस् तनूष्व् अप्सु सूर्य इति सूर्यवान् |

sanskrit_iast: indraḥ kila śrutyā asya veda ity uktha mukhīyā tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: इन्द्रः किल श्रुत्या अस्य वेद इत्य् उक्थ मुखीया तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: ya eka idd havyaś carṣaṇīnām iti traiṣṭubham tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: य एक इद्द् हव्यश् चर्षणीनाम् इति त्रैष्टुभम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: evam nu yadi bṛhat sva yonau vā asva yonau vā kuryuḥ |
meaning: एवम् नु यदि बृहत् स्व योनौ वा अस्व योनौ वा कुर्युः |

sanskrit_iast: tam u ṣṭuhi yo abhibhūty ojā iti traiṣṭubham |
meaning: तम् उ ष्टुहि यो अभिभूत्य् ओजा इति त्रैष्टुभम् |

sanskrit_iast: gīrbhir vardha vṛṣabham carṣaṇīnām ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: गीर्भिर् वर्ध वृषभम् चर्षणीनाम् इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: abhi tyam meṣam puru hūtam ṛbmiyam iti jāgatam ād it sūryam divya ārohayo dṛśa iti sūryavat |
meaning: अभि त्यम् मेषम् पुरु हूतम् ऋब्मियम् इति जागतम् आद् इत् सूर्यम् दिव्य आरोहयो दृश इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: tā vā ubhayyas triṣṭup jagatyaḥ śasyante |
meaning: ता वा उभय्यस् त्रिष्टुप् जगत्यः शस्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: triṣṭub jagatyor ha vā eṣa āhita ādityaḥ pratiṣṭhitas tapati |
meaning: त्रिष्टुब् जगत्योर् ह वा एष आहित आदित्यः प्रतिष्ठितस् तपति |

sanskrit_iast: pra te mahe vidathe śaṃsiṣam harī iti |
meaning: प्र ते महे विदथे शंसिषम् हरी इति |
text:
'I shall proclaim at the great assembly thy two bays', having recited nine verses of this (hymn) and having uttered the call, he inserts a Nivid. It contains (the word) 'sun' in 'Reveal to the bright one, the sun'; this is a symbol of this day. He then recites four verses of the 'All-bay' hymn. 'May the true one come hither, the generous, he of the Soma lees' has twenty-one verses, with the symbol (of this day) in 'What time at the dawn they made to shine the great light.' These make up twenty-five. 'To the all conquering, the booty conquering, the light conquering' is six Jagatī verses, with the symbol (of this day) in 'To Indra the Soma, to him worthy of sacrifice the delightful.' These make up thirty-one. In these Jagatīs he performs the difficult mounting; he who here
gives heat is connected with the Jagatī, the difficult mounting is the sacrificers; verily thus the sacrificers mount him. By Padas he mounts first; thus they obtain this world; by half verses for the second time; thus they obtain the world of the atmosphere; by three Padas for the third time; thus they obtain yonder world; the entrance is by performance as one unit; then by three Padas, by half verses, by Padas (he descends); thus he rests in this world, on a support immovable. This difficult mounting verse being recited together makes up seven. These are thirty-eight in all. ‘For his full oblations’, (these) are six (verses) in Jagatī, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘Indra it waiteth on as the sun on the dawn’; this is a symbol of this day. These make up forty-four. ‘The bird anointed by the craft of the Asura’, (these) are three (verses), with the symbol (of this day) in ‘This radiant sun-like prayer’. These are forty-seven. With the concluding verse thrice repeated, ‘Lead us to a wide space, wise one’, with the symbol (of this day) in ‘The heaven, the light, freedom from danger’, they make up fifty. Those preceding are fifty-one; they make up a hundred and one verses; man has a hundred (years of life), a hundred forms, a hundred strengths, a hundred powers; the hundred and first verse over is the world of the sacrificer; thus here they make ready the sacrificers; thus here having made ready the sacrificers at the beginning, he propagates them with the Mahāvrata day. So the total as made up by Paiṅgya.

sanskrit_iast: tasya nava śastvā āhūya nividam dadhāti |
meaning: तस्य नव शस्त्वा आहूय निविदम् दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: āviṣ kṛdhi haraye sūryāya iti sūryavat |
meaning: आविष् कृधि हरये सूर्याय इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: ā satyo yātu maghavān ṛjīṣī ity ekaviṃśatiḥ |
meaning: आ सत्यो यातु मघवान् ऋजीषी इत्य् एकविंशतिः |

sanskrit_iast: mahi jyotī rurucur yadd ha vastor ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: महि ज्योती रुरुचुर् यद्द् ह वस्तोर् इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: viśvajite dhanajite svar jita iti ṣaḍ jagatyaḥ |
meaning: विश्वजिते धनजिते स्वर् जित इति षड् जगत्यः |

sanskrit_iast: indrāya somam yajatāya haryatam ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: इन्द्राय सोमम् यजताय हर्यतम् इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: jāgato vā eṣa ya eṣa tapati |
meaning: जागतो वा एष य एष तपति |

sanskrit_iast: sā eṣā dūrohaṇīyā saṃśastā sapta jagatyaḥ sampadyante |
meaning: सा एषा दूरोहणीया संशस्ता सप्त जगत्यः सम्पद्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: eṣa pra pūrvīr ava tasya caṃriṣa iti jāgatam ṣaḍṛcam indram siṣakty uṣasam na sūrya iti sūryavat |
meaning: एष प्र पूर्वीर् अव तस्य चंरिष इति जागतम् षडृचम् इन्द्रम् सिषक्त्य् उषसम् न सूर्य इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: pataṅgam aktam asurasya māyayā iti tisraḥ |
meaning: पतङ्गम् अक्तम् असुरस्य मायया इति तिस्रः |

sanskrit_iast: tām dyotamānām svaryam manoṣām ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: ताम् द्योतमानाम् स्वर्यम् मनोषाम् इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: urum no lokam anu neṣi vidvān iti triḥ śastayā paridhānīyayā |
meaning: उरुम् नो लोकम् अनु नेषि विद्वान् इति त्रिः शस्तया परिधानीयया |

sanskrit_iast: svarvaj jyotir abhayam svasti ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: स्वर्वज् ज्योतिर् अभयम् स्वस्ति इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: śata āyur vai puruṣaḥ śata parvā śata vīryaḥ śata indriyaḥ |
meaning: शत आयुर् वै पुरुषः शत पर्वा शत वीर्यः शत इन्द्रियः |

sanskrit_iast: upa yā eka śatatamī sa yajamāna lokaḥ |
meaning: उप या एक शततमी स यजमान लोकः |

sanskrit_iast: tad atra yajamānānt saṃskṛtya ādau mahā vratīyena ahnā prajanayanti iti paṅgī sampat |
meaning: तद् अत्र यजमानान्त् संस्कृत्य आदौ महा व्रतीयेन अह्ना प्रजनयन्ति इति पङ्गी सम्पत् |

text:
Then (the computation) of Kauṣītaki. It is the same up to the beginning of the litany. If one removes the Bṛhat and the Rathantara, the Ṛjujanitrīya (is used); eleven (verses) of it (are used, if the Bṛhat is performed) on its own basis, nine otherwise, with the symbol (of this day) in ‘Now allotting the forms, now the works one goeth.’ ‘O Indra, come hither with thy bays’, (these) are fifteen verses, with the symbol (of this day) in ‘With those of fair form do thou come to us’. Having recited eleven (verses) of (the hymn of) Baru or of the ‘All-bay’ hymn, (he recites) a Nivid in the middle of the hundred and one verses; having recited fifty-one he recites the two (remaining verses) of the Baru (hymn) or of the ‘All-bay’ (hymn). ‘May the true one come hither, the generous, he of the Soma lees’, (these) are twenty-one verses. These make up
twenty-three. ‘To the all-conquering’, (these) are six verses. These make up twenty-nine. The ‘difficult mounting’ verses are seven. These make up thirty-six. ‘Thou art alone the lord of wealth’ is a Triṣṭubh (hymn) of five verses, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘Thou didst destroy at the rising of the sun’; this is a symbol of this day. These make up forty-one. ‘This strong one, god speeded’, (these) are three (verses), with the symbol (of this day) in ‘As the sun with light, he hath stretched out the waters’. These make up forty-four. The bird (hymn) is three (verses); these make up forty-seven. ‘Lead us to wide space, wise one’, with this concluding verse thrice repeated, they make up fifty; the preceding are fifty-one. They make up a hundred and one verses; the explanation of these has been given.

sanskrit_iast: ṛtur janitrīyam trayodaśarcam uddhṛta bṛhad rathantare |
meaning: ऋतुर् जनित्रीयम् त्रयोदशर्चम् उद्धृत बृहद् रथन्तरे |

sanskrit_iast: tad rūpā minan tad apā eka īyata ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: तद् रूपा मिनन् तद् अपा एक ईयत इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: ā indra yāhi haribhir iti pañcadaśa |
meaning: आ इन्द्र याहि हरिभिर् इति पञ्चदश |

sanskrit_iast: sarūpair ā su no gahi ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: सरूपैर् आ सु नो गहि इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: madhya ekaśatasya eka pañcāśatam śastvā dve baror abhyudaiti |
meaning: मध्य एकशतस्य एक पञ्चाशतम् शस्त्वा द्वे बरोर् अभ्युदैति |

sanskrit_iast: ā satyo yātu maghavān ṛjīṣī ity ekaviṃśatis tās trayoviśaṃtiḥ |
meaning: आ सत्यो यातु मघवान् ऋजीषी इत्य् एकविंशतिस् तास् त्रयोविशंतिः |

sanskrit_iast: viśvajita iti ṣaṭ tā ekayāna triṃśat |
meaning: विश्वजित इति षट् ता एकयान त्रिंशत् |

sanskrit_iast: abhūr eko rayi pate rayīṇām iti traiṣṭubham pañcarcam daśa prapitve adha sūryasya iti sūryavat |
meaning: अभूर् एको रयि पते रयीणाम् इति त्रैष्टुभम् पञ्चर्चम् दश प्रपित्वे अध सूर्यस्य इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: tyam ū ṣu vājinam deva jūtam iti tārkṣyas tisraḥ |
meaning: त्यम् ऊ षु वाजिनम् देव जूतम् इति तार्क्ष्यस् तिस्रः |

sanskrit_iast: sūrya iva jyotiṣā apas tatāna ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: सूर्य इव ज्योतिषा अपस् ततान इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: urum no lokam anu neṣi vidvān iti triḥ śastayā paridhānīyayā tāḥ pañcāśat |
meaning: उरुम् नो लोकम् अनु नेषि विद्वान् इति त्रिः शस्तया परिधानीयया ताः पञ्चाशत् |

sanskrit_iast: tā ekaśatam ṛco bhavanti tāsām uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: ता एकशतम् ऋचो भवन्ति तासाम् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: yuñjate mana uta yuñjate dhiya iti sāvitram uta sūryasya raśmibhiḥ samucyasi iti sūryavat |
meaning: युञ्जते मन उत युञ्जते धिय इति सावित्रम् उत सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिः समुच्यसि इति सूर्यवत् |
text:
‘That of Savitṛ we choose’ and ‘To-day for us, O god Savitṛ’ are the normal strophe and antistrophe of the Vaiśvadeva; the explanation of these two has been given. ‘They yoke their minds, they also yoke their thoughts’ is (the hymn) to Savitṛ, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘Thou dost shine forth with the rays of the sun’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘They two, sky and earth, all weal producing’ is (the hymn) to sky and earth, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘The god, the bright sun, between the goddesses in accord with law’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘Why hath the best, the youngest come to us?’ is (the hymn) to the Ṛbhus with the symbol (of the day) in ‘He discerned’ in ‘What time he discerned the four beakers they had made.’ ‘I hail the gods of great fame, for security’ is (the hymn) for the All-gods, containing (the words) ‘sun’ and ‘light’ in ‘Those who obtained a share of the light of the sun’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘To Vaiśvānara, the praise, increasing holy order’ is (the hymn) for Vaiśvānara, containing (the words) ‘shining’, ‘radiance’, and ‘light’ in ‘Shining with radiance, with light in greatness’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘Forward the Maruts, devoted, with gleaming lances’ is (the hymn) to the Maruts, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘The shining rays of the sun’;
this is a symbol of this day. ‘To him who sitteth on the altar, with a dear abode, of fair radiance’ is (the hymn) to Jātavedas, with the symbol (of this day) in ‘The light, the car, of bright hue destroying the darkness.’ These are the hymns of the Āgnimāruta (Śastra). These are the hymns of this day. It is an Agniṣṭoma. The Agniṣṭoma is light; he who here gives heat is light; verily thus they make light successful with light; immortality they obtain who perform the Viṣuvant day.

sanskrit_iast: te hi dyāvā pṛthivī viśva śambhuvā iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam devo devī dharmaṇā sūryaḥ śucit iti sūryavat |
meaning: ते हि द्यावा पृथिवी विश्व शम्भुवा इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् देवो देवी धर्मणा सूर्यः शुचित् इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: kim u śreṣṭhaḥ kim yaviṣṭho na ājagann ity ārbhavam |
meaning: किम् उ श्रेष्ठः किम् यविष्ठो न आजगन्न् इत्य् आर्भवम् |

sanskrit_iast: yad āvākhyac camasān caturaḥ kṛtān ity avākhyad ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: यद् आवाख्यच् चमसान् चतुरः कृतान् इत्य् अवाख्यद् इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: devān huve bṛhat śravasaḥ svastaya iti vaiśvadevam ye sūryasya jyotiṣo bhāgam ānaśur iti sūryavaj jyotiṣmat |
meaning: देवान् हुवे बृहत् श्रवसः स्वस्तय इति वैश्वदेवम् ये सूर्यस्य ज्योतिषो भागम् आनशुर् इति सूर्यवज् ज्योतिष्मत् |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvānarāya dhiṣaṇām ṛtā vṛdha iti vaiśvānarīyam rurucānam bhānunā jyotiṣā mahām iti rucitavad bhānumaj jyotiṣmat |
meaning: वैश्वानराय धिषणाम् ऋता वृध इति वैश्वानरीयम् रुरुचानम् भानुना ज्योतिषा महाम् इति रुचितवद् भानुमज् ज्योतिष्मत् |

sanskrit_iast: prayajyavo maruto bhrājad ṛṣṭaya iti mārutam virokiṇaḥ sūryasya iva raśmaya iti sūryavat |
meaning: प्रयज्यवो मरुतो भ्राजद् ऋष्टय इति मारुतम् विरोकिणः सूर्यस्य इव रश्मय इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: vediṣade priya dhāmāya sudyuta iti jāta vedasīyam |
meaning: वेदिषदे प्रिय धामाय सुद्युत इति जात वेदसीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: jyotī ratham śukra varṇam tam ohanam ity etena rūpeṇa |
meaning: ज्योती रथम् शुक्र वर्णम् तम् ओहनम् इत्य् एतेन रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: te amṛtatvam āpnuvanti ye vaiṣuvatam ahar upayanti |
meaning: ते अमृतत्वम् आप्नुवन्ति ये वैषुवतम् अहर् उपयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: uprād ity asyās tam ayād etad ahaḥ saṃsthāpayiṣeyuḥ |
meaning: उप्राद् इत्य् अस्यास् तम् अयाद् एतद् अहः संस्थापयिषेयुः |
text: Before the setting of the sun should they seek to complete (the rite of) this day; the day has its morning litany, to be recited by day. They should seek to complete with this day including its morning litany and the offerings to the wives (with the gods) before the setting of the sun. ‘Agni, I deem father, Agni friend’, with this (verse) the Hotṛ begins the morning litany on this day, with the symbol of the ‘rich waters’ verse in ‘friend (āpim)’. It contains (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘In the sky the bright, worthy of sacrifice, of the sun’; this is a symbol of this day. As to this Kauṣītaki used to say, ‘The morning litany is Prajāpati, and is not connected with the darkness; verily in due order should he commence it; that is its prosperity; so in due order are offered the Upāṅśu and the Antaryāma (cups); that is their prosperity.’ The Āprī hymn is by Vasiṣṭha, containing (the word) ‘sun’ in ‘Overspread thyself with the rays of the sun’; this is a symbol of this day. ‘The Hotṛ for this day should be white, with red eyes’ some say; with this day they seek to obtain him who yonder gives heat; this is as if one should approach a superior with a gift. But the rule is ‘Just as it may happen to be’. With the Śastra alone should he seek to produce the symbol of this day. A victim to the sun should be offered (in addition) to the usual victim for the pressing. It is offered inaudibly; if a man should utter aloud (the recitation) for it, then if one were to say of him, ‘He will become afflicted with skin disease, a leper’ it would be so. Four victims only are offered inaudibly; that to the sun, that to Savitṛ, that to Prajāpati, and that whose divinity is speech; the others are offered aloud. Then they perform three Svarasāman (days) reversed; the explanation of these has been given.

sanskrit_iast: saprātar anuvākam etad ahar divā kīrtyam bhavati |
meaning: सप्रातर् अनुवाकम् एतद् अहर् दिवा कीर्त्यम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: saprātar anuvākena sapatnī samyājena etena ahnā purād ity asyās tam ayāt samīpseyuḥ |
meaning: सप्रातर् अनुवाकेन सपत्नी सम्याजेन एतेन अह्ना पुराद् इत्य् अस्यास् तम् अयात् समीप्सेयुः |

sanskrit_iast: agnim manye pitaram agnim āpim ity etayā hotā tad ahaḥ prātar anuvākam pratipadyate |
meaning: अग्निम् मन्ये पितरम् अग्निम् आपिम् इत्य् एतया होता तद् अहः प्रातर् अनुवाकम् प्रतिपद्यते |

sanskrit_iast: divi śukram yajatam sūryasya iti sūryavatī |
meaning: दिवि शुक्रम् यजतम् सूर्यस्य इति सूर्यवती |

sanskrit_iast: tad u ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: तद् उ ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: na tamasa etam yathā yatham eva tam upākuryuḥ |
meaning: न तमस एतम् यथा यथम् एव तम् उपाकुर्युः |

sanskrit_iast: tathā yathā yatham upāṃśv antaryāmau hūyete |
meaning: तथा यथा यथम् उपांश्व् अन्तर्यामौ हूयेते |

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣṭham āprī sūktam sam raśmibhis tatanaḥ sūryasya iti sūryavat |
meaning: वसिष्ठम् आप्री सूक्तम् सम् रश्मिभिस् ततनः सूर्यस्य इति सूर्यवत् |

sanskrit_iast: śukra etasya ahnaḥ piṅga akṣo hotā syād iti ha eka āhuḥ |
meaning: शुक्र एतस्य अह्नः पिङ्ग अक्षो होता स्याद् इति ह एक आहुः |

sanskrit_iast: amum vā etena ahnā īpsanti yo asau tapati |
meaning: अमुम् वा एतेन अह्ना ईप्सन्ति यो असौ तपति |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā śreyāṃsam āharann upeyād evam tat |
meaning: तद् यथा श्रेयांसम् आहरन्न् उपेयाद् एवम् तत् |

sanskrit_iast: yathā upapādam iti tv eva sthitam |
meaning: यथा उपपादम् इति त्व् एव स्थितम् |

sanskrit_iast: śastreṇa eva etasya ahno rūpam sampādyiṣeyuḥ |
meaning: शस्त्रेण एव एतस्य अह्नो रूपम् सम्पाद्यिषेयुः |

sanskrit_iast: duścarmā kilāsī bhaviṣyati iti tathā ha syāt |
meaning: दुश्चर्मा किलासी भविष्यति इति तथा ह स्यात् |

sanskrit_iast: te vā ete catvāra eva paśava upāṃśu bhavanti |
meaning: ते वा एते चत्वार एव पशव उपांशु भवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: sauryaḥ sāvitraḥ prājāpatyo vāg devatya iti |
meaning: सौर्यः सावित्रः प्राजापत्यो वाग् देवत्य इति |

sanskrit_iast: atha trīnt svara sāmna āvṛttān upayanti teṣām uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ त्रीन्त् स्वर साम्न आवृत्तान् उपयन्ति तेषाम् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: trayodaśam adhicaram māsam āpnuvanti yad viśvajitam upayanti |
meaning: त्रयोदशम् अधिचरम् मासम् आप्नुवन्ति यद् विश्वजितम् उपयन्ति |
text: They obtain this thirteenth month in that they perform the Viśvajit; the thirteenth month is as great as the year; here verily the whole year is made up. Of it they say 'The six-day (rite) is the one-day (rite)', for whatever is done each day in the six-day (rite) that is done on the one-day (rite), the Viśvajit. Much and varied is done on the Viśvajit, in that all the Pṛṣṭhas, and all the various Stomas are together put in it. Its Pṛṣṭha is openly the Vairāja, the Rathantara at the midday Pavamāna, the Bṛhat at the third Pavamāna is performed, the Śākvara as the Maitrāvaruṇa's, the Vairūpa as the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin's, the Raivata as the Achāvāka's. They obtain this thirteenth supernumerary month, for that is thirteenth, as they perform the Pṛṣṭhas; 'Agni men with praise from the fire sticks' is the Ājya of this (day) in Virāj verses; the explanation of this has been given. The Praüga is by Madhuchandas; the explanation of this has been given. 'Thee like a car for aid' is the strophe of the Marutvatīya; 'This drink, O bright one, is pressed' is the antistrophe. This is the normal one-day form; the explanation of it has been given. 'With what array, of one age, of one home? is the Marutvatīya; the 'What array' hymn contains the word 'who'; the Viśvajit as Prajāpati is 'Who'. The strophe and antistrophe of the Vairāja are the strophe and antistrophe; in them he inserts a repeated o just as yonder in the fourth day (rite); for as it is in Virāj it is not the place to omit the repetition of o; then there is the inserted verse, then the Pragātha in which Indra is attained; then he recites the bases of the Bṛhat and the Rathantara. 'That was the best in the worlds' is the Niṣkevalya; the sacrifice is the best in the worlds; the Viśvajit as Prajāpati is the sacrifice. Then, if the third pressing of the sixth day is the third pressing, (it is because) the sixth day is connected with Prajāpati, the Viśvajit is Prajāpati. The strophe is from the one-day (rite); the Viśvajit is a one-day (rite); the one-day (rite) is a support; verily (it serves) for support. The antistrophe contains the word 'towards'; the explanation of this has been given.

sanskrit_iast: etāvān vai saṃvatsaro yad eṣa trayodaśo māsaḥ |
meaning: एतावान् वै संवत्सरो यद् एष त्रयोदशो मासः |

sanskrit_iast: tad atra eva sarvaḥ saṃvatsara āpto bhavati |
meaning: तद् अत्र एव सर्वः संवत्सर आप्तो भवति |

sanskrit_iast: tad vā idam bahu viśva rūpam viśvajiti kriyate |
meaning: तद् वा इदम् बहु विश्व रूपम् विश्वजिति क्रियते |

sanskrit_iast: yat sarvāṇi pṣṭhāni sarve stomā ucca avacāḥ samavadhīyante |
meaning: यत् सर्वाणि प्ष्ठानि सर्वे स्तोमा उच्च अवचाः समवधीयन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: vairājam eva asya pratyakṣam pṛṣṭham bhavati |
meaning: वैराजम् एव अस्य प्रत्यक्षम् पृष्ठम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: ta etam trayodaśam adhicaram māsam āpnuvanti |
meaning: त एतम् त्रयोदशम् अधिचरम् मासम् आप्नुवन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tasya agnim naro dīdhitibhir araṇyor iti vairājam ājyam |
meaning: तस्य अग्निम् नरो दीधितिभिर् अरण्योर् इति वैराजम् आज्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: mādhuc chandasaḥ praugas tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: माधुच् छन्दसः प्रौगस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīḍā iti marutvatīyam |
meaning: कया शुभा सवयसः सनीडा इति मरुत्वतीयम् |

sanskrit_iast: yāv eva amū vairājasya stotriya anurūpau ta stotriya anurūpau |
meaning: याव् एव अमू वैराजस्य स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ त स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ |

sanskrit_iast: tayos tathā eva nyūṅkhayati yathā adaś caturthe ahan |
meaning: तयोस् तथा एव न्यूङ्खयति यथा अदश् चतुर्थे अहन् |

sanskrit_iast: na hi vairājam tat sthānam anyūṅkhanāya |
meaning: न हि वैराजम् तत् स्थानम् अन्यूङ्खनाय |

sanskrit_iast: tad id āsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭham iti niṣkevalyam |
meaning: तद् इद् आस भुवनेषु ज्येष्ठम् इति निष्केवल्यम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha yat ṣaṣṭhasya ahnas tṛtīya savanam tat tṛtīya savanam |
meaning: अथ यत् षष्ठस्य अह्नस् तृतीय सवनम् तत् तृतीय सवनम् |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur atha kasmād viśvajiti sarva pṛṣṭha ekāhe tṛtīya savane śilpāni śasyante kasmād agniṣṭome madhyaṃdina iti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् अथ कस्माद् विश्वजिति सर्व पृष्ठ एकाहे तृतीय सवने शिल्पानि शस्यन्ते कस्माद् अग्निष्टोमे मध्यंदिन इति |
text:
They say 'Why in the Viśvajit with all the Stomas as a one-
day rite are the Śilpas recited at the third pressing? Why (in it) as an Agniṣṭoma at the midday pressing?' The Śilpas are the lower breaths; the sacrifice is man; the morning pressing is the upper breaths; the midday is the body; the third pressing the lower; these are the Śilpas; therefore the Śilpas are performed at the third pressing, for this is their abode. Then why are the Śilpas recited at the midday pressing in the Viśvajit as an Agniṣṭoma in a year-long sacrificial session? The Pṛṣṭhas are the body; the Śilpas are the breaths; the breaths are not known without the body, nor without the breaths the body; assuredly the two are not severable. Therefore are the Śilpas recited at the midday pressing in the Viśvajit as an Agniṣṭoma, (for they think) 'Let me not separate the body from the breaths.' Moreover, the Viśvajit is Prajāpati; as Prajāpati the Viśvajit is all; therefore all the Pṛṣṭhas are performed, all the Śilpas; the Viśvajit as Prajāpati is all; with all he obtains all he who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: ye vā ime avāñcaḥ prāṇās tāni śilpāni |
meaning: ये वा इमे अवाञ्चः प्राणास् तानि शिल्पानि |

sanskrit_iast: tasya ya ūrdhvā prāṇās tat prātaḥ savanam |
meaning: तस्य य ऊर्ध्वा प्राणास् तत् प्रातः सवनम् |

sanskrit_iast: ye avāñcas tat tṛtīya savanam tāi śilpāni |
meaning: ये अवाञ्चस् तत् तृतीय सवनम् ताइ शिल्पानि |

sanskrit_iast: atha yad agniṣṭome satriye sāṃvatsarike viśvajiti sarva pṛṣṭhe madhyaṃdine śilpāni śasyante |
meaning: अथ यद् अग्निष्टोमे सत्रिये सांवत्सरिके विश्वजिति सर्व पृष्ठे मध्यंदिने शिल्पानि शस्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: na vā antareṇa ātmānam prāṇāḥ khyāyante |
meaning: न वा अन्तरेण आत्मानम् प्राणाः ख्यायन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād agniṣṭoma eva api madhyaṃdine śilpāni śasyante |
meaning: तस्माद् अग्निष्टोम एव अपि मध्यंदिने शिल्पानि शस्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: na it prāṇebhya ātmānam apādadhāni iti |
meaning: न इत् प्राणेभ्य आत्मानम् अपादधानि इति |

sanskrit_iast: tat sarveṇa sarvam āpnoti ya evam veda |
meaning: तत् सर्वेण सर्वम् आप्नोति य एवम् वेद |

sanskrit_iast: tatra agni mārute raudrīm śastvā hotā evayā marutam paṅkti śaṃsam śaṃsati |
meaning: तत्र अग्नि मारुते रौद्रीम् शस्त्वा होता एवया मरुतम् पङ्क्ति शंसम् शंसति |
text: In the Āgnimāruta (Śastra) the Hotṛ having recited the Rudra verse, recites the Evayāmarut hymn in Paṅkti form; the sacrifice is fivefold; verily (it serves) to obtain the sacrifice. 'Let me not,' (he thinks), 'obstract the Śilpa of the Achāvāka.' Moreover Rudra is the oldest and best of the gods, the Atichandas of metres, the Viśvajit of one-day rites. Thus he makes it successful with its own symbol. At three verses of it should he repeat o; if he desire to repeat o he should do it at all. The repetition of o is food; the breaths are food; the Śilpas are the breaths; verily thus he places the breath in the breaths. Moreover by the Viśvajit Prajāpati propagated all offspring, and conquered all. Thus is it the Viśvajit. Now is he born who sacrifices with the Viśvajit; therefore does he repeat o. Stumbling as it were does he move as he seeks to walk for the first time. Thus him from the immortal metre he propagates to immortality. They obtain immortality who perform the Viśvajit.

sanskrit_iast: pāṅkto vai yajño yajñasya eva avāptyai |
meaning: पाङ्क्तो वै यज्ञो यज्ञस्य एव अवाप्त्यै |

sanskrit_iast: na id acchāvākasya śilpam antarayāma iti |
meaning: न इद् अच्छावाकस्य शिल्पम् अन्तरयाम इति |

sanskrit_iast: atho rudro vai jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca devānām |
meaning: अथो रुद्रो वै ज्येष्ठश् च श्रेष्ठश् च देवानाम् |

sanskrit_iast: atho viśvajitā vai prajāpatiḥ sarvāḥ prajā ajanayat sarva udajayat |
meaning: अथो विश्वजिता वै प्रजापतिः सर्वाः प्रजा अजनयत् सर्व उदजयत् |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā eṣa jāyate viśvajitā yo yajate |
meaning: एतद् वा एष जायते विश्वजिता यो यजते |

sanskrit_iast: nyūṅkhamānaka iva vai prathamam cicarṣaṃś carati |
meaning: न्यूङ्खमानक इव वै प्रथमम् चिचर्षंश् चरति |

sanskrit_iast: tad enam amṛtāt chandaso amṛtatvāya prajanayanti |
meaning: तद् एनम् अमृतात् छन्दसो अमृतत्वाय प्रजनयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: te amṛtatvam āpnuvanti ye viśvajitam upayanti |
meaning: ते अमृतत्वम् आप्नुवन्ति ये विश्वजितम् उपयन्ति |

text:
The Viśvajit of the year-long session is composed as an Agniṣṭoma with all the Stomas and all the Pṛṣṭhas; the Agniṣṭoma is a support; verily (it serves) for support. If the Viśvajit is a one-day (rite), or the middle day of a night session, it should be an Atirātra. The Atirātra is the complete Viśvajit; half of the Viśvajit is performed by day, half by night. The (Viśvajit), which is performed apart from a case
when all one's property is given or a session, is one which brings all ruin. It is a loss of all if a man gives all without a Viśvajit. If there is a Viśvajit (he should give) all; if (he gives) all, it (should be) a Viśvajit. 'If a man does not give all, saying "Let me give all," he prepares for himself a pitfall, he comes to ruin,' he used to say. 'Or a thousand makes this up,' Kauṣītaki used to say, 'The thousand is all; the Viśvajit is all; by all may I obtain all,' (so thinking he gives a thousand).

sanskrit_iast: ekāha u ced viśvajid rātri satrasya vā viṣuvān atirātra eva syāt |
meaning: एकाह उ चेद् विश्वजिद् रात्रि सत्रस्य वा विषुवान् अतिरात्र एव स्यात् |

sanskrit_iast: sarva parājid u ha eva sa yo anyatra sarva vedasād vā satrād vā kriyate |
meaning: सर्व पराजिद् उ ह एव स यो अन्यत्र सर्व वेदसाद् वा सत्राद् वा क्रियते |

sanskrit_iast: yo ha vai na sarvam dadāmi iti bruvan |
meaning: यो ह वै न सर्वम् ददामि इति ब्रुवन् |

sanskrit_iast: kartapatyam eva taj jīyate pra vā mīyate iti ha sma āha |
meaning: कर्तपत्यम् एव तज् जीयते प्र वा मीयते इति ह स्म आह |

sanskrit_iast: sahasram vā enam avarundha iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: सहस्रम् वा एनम् अवरुन्ध इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: tat sarveṇa sarvam āpnoti ya evam veda |
meaning: तत् सर्वेण सर्वम् आप्नोति य एवम् वेद |

text: He should put round a calfskin; bare as it were becomes the body of him who gives all. (He puts round thinking) 'Cattle desire a calf; let cattle again desire me.' He should dwell in an Udumbara wood; the Udumbara is strength and proper food; (verily it serves) to obtain strength and proper food. He should dwell with a Naiṣāda; the Naiṣāda is the minimum of proper food; (verily it serves) to obtain the minimum of proper food. He should dwell with a Vaiśya; the Vaiśya prospers; (verily it serves) to obtain the proper food which is with a Vaiśya. He should dwell with a Kṣatriya; the Kṣatriya is the maximum of proper food; (verily it serves) to obtain the maximum of proper food. He should dwell with a Brahman of the same family, to obtain the proper food which is with a Brahman of the same family. For a year should he wander, lying on the ground, accepting only uncultivated (fruits), not asking for food, clothed in what is given. With that he clothes himself. 'Having done this for twelve nights he may devote himself to another desire,' Kauṣītaki used to say, 'the year has twelve months, this is an image of the year.' The Ājya (Śastras) of the Hotrakas are addressed to Prajāpati, as having no deity mentioned. The strophes of this day (of these priests) are 'Do ye two aid us to terrestrial,' 'They yoke the tawny ruddy one,' and 'Them they ever praise' or 'Praise him who with his light.' The strophes of the sixth day they should make the antistrophes; the sixth day is connected with Prajāpati; the other five are Prajāpati as the Viśvajit the litanies they conclude with the ending sets of verses; the ending verses are a support; verily (they serve) for support.

sanskrit_iast: riricāna iva vā etasya ātmā bhavati yaḥ sarvam dadāti |
meaning: रिरिचान इव वा एतस्य आत्मा भवति यः सर्वम् ददाति |

sanskrit_iast: etad vā avara ardhyam anna adyam nan naiṣādaḥ |
meaning: एतद् वा अवर अर्ध्यम् अन्न अद्यम् नन् नैषादः |

sanskrit_iast: yad vaiśye anna adyam tasya upāptyai |
meaning: यद् वैश्ये अन्न अद्यम् तस्य उपाप्त्यै |

sanskrit_iast: etad vai para ardhyam anna adyam yat kṣatriyaḥ |
meaning: एतद् वै पर अर्ध्यम् अन्न अद्यम् यत् क्षत्रियः |

sanskrit_iast: yat samāne gotre anna adyam tasya upāptyai |
meaning: यत् समाने गोत्रे अन्न अद्यम् तस्य उपाप्त्यै |

sanskrit_iast: saṃvatsaram cared adhaḥ saṃveśya phāla kṛṣṭāśya pratigṛhṇan na annam yācann idam tat tad anuvasānaḥ |
meaning: संवत्सरम् चरेद् अधः संवेश्य फाल कृष्टाश्य प्रतिगृह्णन् न अन्नम् याचन्न् इदम् तत् तद् अनुवसानः |

sanskrit_iast: dvādaśa rātram caritvā atha anyasyai bubhūṣāyai syād iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
meaning: द्वादश रात्रम् चरित्वा अथ अन्यस्यै बुभूषायै स्याद् इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |

sanskrit_iast: tasya tā naḥ śaktam pārthivasya yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam tā hi śaśvanta īḍate tam īḍiṣva yo arciṣā iti vā stotriyāḥ |
meaning: तस्य ता नः शक्तम् पार्थिवस्य युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नम् अरुषम् ता हि शश्वन्त ईडते तम् ईडिष्व यो अर्चिषा इति वा स्तोत्रियाः |

sanskrit_iast: ye ṣaṣṭhasya ahnaḥ stotriyās te viśvajito anurūpāḥ |
meaning: ये षष्ठस्य अह्नः स्तोत्रियास् ते विश्वजितो अनुरूपाः |

text: The first month has thirty-two (days), the last thirty-two; the Anuṣṭubh has thirty-two syllables; the Anuṣṭubh is speech; thus with speech they advance, in speech they conclude. There are two months of twenty-eight days on both sides of the Viṣuvant (day); the Uṣṇih has twenty-eight syllables; the neck is connected with the Uṣṇih. Now the Viṣuvant is the head of the sacrifice; verily thus having produced a neck they fit the head upon it. They say 'Of which of the two sets of days is it (the head), of the previous or the subsequent?' 'Neither of the previous nor of the subsequent,' they say. Of both sets of days is it (the head); both sets of days are its. They say 'How many sets of six days are in the year?' There are sixty six-day sets; thus the course of the year by six-day sets is unbroken. Those who yoke thus the days of the year, they attain those desires which are in the year. Those who yoke them otherwise than that, they attain not those desires which are in the year. Now some perform the months in the forward order only, and the days in the forward order, (saying) 'We are mounting the year in the forward direction in both ways.' 'The months alone should be reversed, not the days,' some (hold), saying 'The months are reversed in that this Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha comes round again from the back.' Others say 'The Trivṛt and the Trayastriñca Stomas are characterized by being at a great distance; it is as if from a mountain peak one should fall into a pit; that is a cleaving of the Stomas, therefore the days alone should be reversed, and not the months, to prevent cleaving of the Stomas.'

sanskrit_iast: atha etat śiro yajñasya yad viṣuvān |
meaning: अथ एतत् शिरो यज्ञस्य यद् विषुवान् |

sanskrit_iast: grīvā eva tat kalpayitvā tāsu śiraḥ pratidadhati |
meaning: ग्रीवा एव तत् कल्पयित्वा तासु शिरः प्रतिदधति |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhuḥ katareṣām eṣo ahnām avareṣām pareṣām iti |
meaning: तद् आहुः कतरेषाम् एषो अह्नाम् अवरेषाम् परेषाम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: na avareṣām na pareṣām ity āhuḥ |
meaning: न अवरेषाम् न परेषाम् इत्य् आहुः |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhuḥ kati ṣaḍahāḥ saṃvatsara iti |
meaning: तद् आहुः कति षडहाः संवत्सर इति |

sanskrit_iast: tad ya evam saṃvatsarasya ahāni yuñjanti |
meaning: तद् य एवम् संवत्सरस्य अहानि युञ्जन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: ta etānt sarvān kāmān ṛdhnuvanti ye saṃvatsare |
meaning: त एतान्त् सर्वान् कामान् ऋध्नुवन्ति ये संवत्सरे |

sanskrit_iast: atha ye ato anyathā saṃvatsarasya ahāni yuñjanti |
meaning: अथ ये अतो अन्यथा संवत्सरस्य अहानि युञ्जन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: na te tānt sarvān kāmān ṛdhnuvanti ye saṃvatsare |
meaning: न ते तान्त् सर्वान् कामान् ऋध्नुवन्ति ये संवत्सरे |

sanskrit_iast: atha ha eka ūrdhvān eva māsān upayanty ūrdhvāny ahāni |
meaning: अथ ह एक ऊर्ध्वान् एव मासान् उपयन्त्य् ऊर्ध्वान्य् अहानि |

sanskrit_iast: ūrdhvam vā u vayam saṃvatsaram rohāma iti vadantaḥ |
meaning: ऊर्ध्वम् वा उ वयम् संवत्सरम् रोहाम इति वदन्तः |

sanskrit_iast: māsā eva āvarteran na ahāni ity eke |
meaning: मासा एव आवर्तेरन् न अहानि इत्य् एके |

sanskrit_iast: ya eva eṣa pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ punaḥ parastāt paryeti tena māsā āvṛttā iti vadantaḥ |
meaning: य एव एष पृष्ठ्यः षडहः पुनः परस्तात् पर्येति तेन मासा आवृत्ता इति वदन्तः |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur vidūra rūpam vā etad yat trivṛc ca trayas triṃśaś ca stomau |
meaning: तद् आहुर् विदूर रूपम् वा एतद् यत् त्रिवृच् च त्रयस् त्रिंशश् च स्तोमौ |

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā giri śikharāt kartam abhi praskanded evam tat stoma kṛntatram |
meaning: तद् यथा गिरि शिखरात् कर्तम् अभि प्रस्कन्देद् एवम् तत् स्तोम कृन्तत्रम् |

text:
Then (follows) the discussion of the Go and Āyus. They should
perform the Go and Āyus as inverted; the Go and Āyus are day and night; day and night are inverted towards each other; moreover the Go and Āyus are sky and earth; sky and earth are inverted towards each other; moreover the Go and Āyus are expiration and inspiration; expiration and inspiration, being inverted, find support in each other. Some perform them in the forward order, saying 'The Go and Āyus should be performed in the forward direction; the Abhiplava Stomas are reversed, and the Pṛṣṭhya Stomas in the ten-night (period).' They say 'The Go and Āyus are the second and the third day.'

sanskrit_iast: atho dyāvā pṛthivī vai go āyuṣī |
meaning: अथो द्यावा पृथिवी वै गो आयुषी |

sanskrit_iast: vihṛte vā ime dyāvā pṛthivī anyonyasmin |
meaning: विहृते वा इमे द्यावा पृथिवी अन्योन्यस्मिन् |

sanskrit_iast: atho prāṇa apānau vai go āyuṣī |
meaning: अथो प्राण अपानौ वै गो आयुषी |

sanskrit_iast: vihṛtau vā imau prāṇa apānāv anyonyasmin pratitiṣṭhataḥ |
meaning: विहृतौ वा इमौ प्राण अपानाव् अन्योन्यस्मिन् प्रतितिष्ठतः |

sanskrit_iast: te ha eka ūrdhve upayanty ūrdhve upetavye go āyuṣī iti |
meaning: ते ह एक ऊर्ध्वे उपयन्त्य् ऊर्ध्वे उपेतव्ये गो आयुषी इति |

sanskrit_iast: anvābhiplavikāḥ stomā āvartatnte daśarātram anupṛṣṭhyas stomā iti vadantaḥ |
meaning: अन्वाभिप्लविकाः स्तोमा आवर्तत्न्ते दशरात्रम् अनुपृष्ठ्यस् स्तोमा इति वदन्तः |

sanskrit_iast: tad yad eva idam dvitīyam ahar yac ca tṛtīyam ete vā u go āyuṣī |
meaning: तद् यद् एव इदम् द्वितीयम् अहर् यच् च तृतीयम् एते वा उ गो आयुषी |

sanskrit_iast: atha kaścit śastre vā anuvacane vā pramatta upahanyād vicikitsā vā syād upahatam abuddham atikrāntam manyamāno manasā vṛtta antam īkṣamāṇo vinivṛtya upahatam anupahatam kṛtvā ānantaryāt prayogaḥ syād vṛtta antād iti mīmāṃsante |
meaning: अथ कश्चित् शस्त्रे वा अनुवचने वा प्रमत्त उपहन्याद् विचिकित्सा वा स्याद् उपहतम् अबुद्धम् अतिक्रान्तम् मन्यमानो मनसा वृत्त अन्तम् ईक्षमाणो विनिवृत्य उपहतम् अनुपहतम् कृत्वा आनन्तर्यात् प्रयोगः स्याद् वृत्त अन्ताद् इति मीमांसन्ते |
text: Now they discuss (this question), 'Supposing some one in carelessness makes a blunder in a Śastra or a recitation or if there is doubt, should one, thinking that the error has passed unnoticed, mentally considering the (place of) occurrence, having gone back and remedied the error, proceed immediately from the (place of) occurrence (of the error)?' Now Paiṅgya used to say 'Superfluous would be a Mantra repeated twice when not prescribed; therefore he should not proceed immediately.' So used Paiṅgya to say. Now Kauṣītaki used to say 'These rites in which the number of Mantras employed is limited have limited fruits. Those in which an unlimited number of Mantras is employed have unlimited fruits; the unlimited is mind; mind is Prajāpati, Prajāpati is the sacrifice; the sacrifice rejoices in the sacrifice itself as mind in mind; therefore should he proceed immediately.' So used Kauṣītaki to say. 'By the limited he conquers the limited, the unlimited by the unlimited; (it serves) for the winning of the unlimited; in that there is no flaw', so used Kauṣītaki to say. He should not offer a libation. So the sacrificer obtains the worlds of heaven, all desires, all attainments, and all immortality, and acquires the pre-eminence, rule, and overlordship of all creatures, for whom it is done thus.

sanskrit_iast: atha ha sma āha paiṅgyo na ānantaryāt prayogaḥ syād atirikto vā eṣa mantraḥ syād yo avacanād dvir ucyate |
meaning: अथ ह स्म आह पैङ्ग्यो न आनन्तर्यात् प्रयोगः स्याद् अतिरिक्तो वा एष मन्त्रः स्याद् यो अवचनाद् द्विर् उच्यते |

sanskrit_iast: tasmān na āntaryāt prayogaḥ syād iti ha sma āha paiṅgyaḥ |
meaning: तस्मान् न आन्तर्यात् प्रयोगः स्याद् इति ह स्म आह पैङ्ग्यः |

sanskrit_iast: atha ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ parimita phalāni vā etāni karmāṇi yeṣu parimito mantra gaṇaḥ prayujyate |
meaning: अथ ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः परिमित फलानि वा एतानि कर्माणि येषु परिमितो मन्त्र गणः प्रयुज्यते |

sanskrit_iast: atha aparimita phalāni yeṣu aparimito mantra gaṇaḥ prayujyate |
meaning: अथ अपरिमित फलानि येषु अपरिमितो मन्त्र गणः प्रयुज्यते |

sanskrit_iast: mano vā etad yad aparimitam prajāpatir vai mano yajña u vai prajāpatiḥ svayam vai tad yajño yajñasya juṣate yan mano manasas tasmād ānantaryāt prayogaḥ syād iti ha sma āha kauṣītakir |
meaning: मनो वा एतद् यद् अपरिमितम् प्रजापतिर् वै मनो यज्ञ उ वै प्रजापतिः स्वयम् वै तद् यज्ञो यज्ञस्य जुषते यन् मनो मनसस् तस्माद् आनन्तर्यात् प्रयोगः स्याद् इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिर् |

sanskrit_iast: mitam ha vai mitena jayaty amitam amitena aparimitasya avaruddhyā anulbaṇam etad iti ha sma āha kauṣītakir |
meaning: मितम् ह वै मितेन जयत्य् अमितम् अमितेन अपरिमितस्य अवरुद्ध्या अनुल्बणम् एतद् इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिर् |

sanskrit_iast: na āhutim juhuyāt tathā ha yajamānaḥ svargāṃl lokānt sarvān kāmān sarvā aṣṭīḥ sarvam ca amṛtatvam āpnoti sarveṣām ca bhūtānām śraiṣṭhyam svārājyam ādhipatyam paryeti yasya evam kriyate |
meaning: न आहुतिम् जुहुयात् तथा ह यजमानः स्वर्गांल् लोकान्त् सर्वान् कामान् सर्वा अष्टीः सर्वम् च अमृतत्वम् आप्नोति सर्वेषाम् च भूतानाम् श्रैष्ठ्यम् स्वाराज्यम् आधिपत्यम् पर्येति यस्य एवम् क्रियते |

sanskrit_iast: atha yady ūrdhvam paridhānāt praṇava vaṣaṭ kārayor vā ūrdhvam yājyā puronuvākyayor budhyeta atikrāntam ulbaṇam etasyām velāyām bhavati iti ha sma āha prāgahiḥ |
meaning: अथ यद्य् ऊर्ध्वम् परिधानात् प्रणव वषट् कारयोर् वा ऊर्ध्वम् याज्या पुरोनुवाक्ययोर् बुध्येत अतिक्रान्तम् उल्बणम् एतस्याम् वेलायाम् भवति इति ह स्म आह प्रागहिः |
text:
'Now if after the conclusion or after the Praṇava or vaṣaṭ call of the invitatory and offering verses, (an error) is perceived, by that time the flaw has been passed over', Prāgahi used to say. 'Therefore the priest in
the Sadas should not call attention to a flaw passed over at this time', Paiṅgya used to say; 'he knocks into a pillar or falls into a pit or is put into one or perishes', he used to say. 'If the priest in the Sadas should call attention to a flaw passed over, there must not be repetition of what has been done,' Āruṇi used to say; 'There is loss of a secondary element,' said Śvetaketu. 'Therefore the priest in the Sadas should not call attention to a flaw passed over,' Paiṅgya used to say. 'It is a tribulation to the sacrifice if the priest in the Sadas calls attention to a flaw passed over'. 'Therefore the priest in the Sadas should not call attention to a flaw passed over,' Paiṅgya used to say.

sanskrit_iast: tasmān na etasyām velāyām atikrāntam ulbaṇam sadasyo bodhayeta iti ha sma āha paiṅgyaḥ |
meaning: तस्मान् न एतस्याम् वेलायाम् अतिक्रान्तम् उल्बणम् सदस्यो बोधयेत इति ह स्म आह पैङ्ग्यः |

sanskrit_iast: sthāṇum vā ṛcchati garte vā patati dhīyate vā pra vā mīyata iti ha sma āha yady atikrāntam ulbaṇam sadasyo bodhayeta |
meaning: स्थाणुम् वा ऋच्छति गर्ते वा पतति धीयते वा प्र वा मीयत इति ह स्म आह यद्य् अतिक्रान्तम् उल्बणम् सदस्यो बोधयेत |

sanskrit_iast: kṛtasya anāvṛttir iti ha sma āha āruṇir guṇa lopa iti śvetaketus tasmān na atikrāntam ulbaṇam sadasyo bodhayeta iti ha sma āha paiṅgyaḥ |
meaning: कृतस्य अनावृत्तिर् इति ह स्म आह आरुणिर् गुण लोप इति श्वेतकेतुस् तस्मान् न अतिक्रान्तम् उल्बणम् सदस्यो बोधयेत इति ह स्म आह पैङ्ग्यः |

sanskrit_iast: aṃho vā etad yajñasya yady atikrāntam ulbaṇam sadasyo bodhayeta iti tasmān na atikrāntam ulbaṇam sadasyo bodhayeta iti ha sma āha paiṅgyaḥ |
meaning: अंहो वा एतद् यज्ञस्य यद्य् अतिक्रान्तम् उल्बणम् सदस्यो बोधयेत इति तस्मान् न अतिक्रान्तम् उल्बणम् सदस्यो बोधयेत इति ह स्म आह पैङ्ग्यः |

sanskrit_iast: atha ha sma āha daivodāsiḥ pratardano naimiṣīyāṇām satram upagamya upāsyad ya vicikitsām papraccha yady atikrāntam ulbaṇam sadasyo bodhayeta ṛtvijām vā anyatamo budhyeta katham vo anulbaṇam syāt iti |
meaning: अथ ह स्म आह दैवोदासिः प्रतर्दनो नैमिषीयाणाम् सत्रम् उपगम्य उपास्यद् य विचिकित्साम् पप्रच्छ यद्य् अतिक्रान्तम् उल्बणम् सदस्यो बोधयेत ऋत्विजाम् वा अन्यतमो बुध्येत कथम् वो अनुल्बणम् स्यात् इति |
text: Further he used to say this. Daivodāsi Pratardana having gone to a sacrificial season of the Naimiṣīyas and having glided up asked a question on this point of doubt, 'If the priest in the Sadas should call attention to a flaw passed over or any one of the priests should note it, how would you remove the flaw?' They were silent; Alikayu Vācaspata was their Brahman priest; he said 'I know that not; but will ask Jātūkarṇya, the aged teacher of those formerly.' Him he asked, 'If the performer himself should note a flaw passed over or another should call attention to it, how is that flaw to be made flawless? By repetition of the Mantra or by an oblation?' 'The Mantra should be recited again', Jātūkarṇya said. Him Alikayu again asked, 'Should one recite in full the Śastra or recitation or Nigada or offering verse or whatever else it be?' 'So much as is erroneous only need be repeated, a verse, or half verse, or quarter verse, or word, or letter,' Jātūkarṇya replied. But Kauṣītaki used to say, 'He should not repeat the Mantra, nor offer a libation; there is no flaw', for, whatever flaw the Hotṛs make in the sacrifice through inattention, all that Agni as divine Hotṛ makes flawless. This is declared in a Ṛc,

'If that in poverty of mind, with feeble intellect,
Men think not of the sacrifice, Then Agni the Hotṛ skilled in the offering, well knowing, Most skilled to offer, to the gods shall offer in due season.’ In that also, when the sacrifice is completed, he says ‘The All-knower hath offered the sacrifice,’ he says ‘The All-knower hath offered this sacrifice.’ In that he says ‘Having sat down before us,’ he says ‘Agni, as divine Hotṛ, having sat down before the human Hotṛ sacrifices.’ Verily with the second half verse or the first verse he utters a benediction.

text: On the sixth day the gods obtained the Stomas and the months; having obtained these Stomas they compressed these same Stomas in couples, being the Stomas of the Pṛṣṭhya, for whence could they have obtained another Stoma? The Trivṛt and the Pañcadaśa Stomas becoming the Caturviṅśa Stoma support the seventh day; the Saptadaśa and the Triṇava Stomas, becoming the Catuṣcatvāriṅśa Stoma, support the eighth day; the Ekaviṅśa and the Trayastriṅśa Stomas, becoming the Aṣṭācatvāriṅśa Stoma, support the ninth day. Of them the first is measured by the Gāyatrī, the second by the Triṣṭubh, the third by the Jagatī; in that they are measured by the metres, therefore are they Chandomas. The six Stotriyā verses which are over the Aṣṭācatvāriṅśa Stoma, these they call the seasons; the seasons are six; by these the tenth day is performed.
