meaning: स्तोत्रियान् शस्त्वा श्वः स्तोत्रियान् अनुरूपम् कुर्वते |

sanskrit_iast: ahar eva tad ahno anurūpam kurvate |
meaning: अहर् एव तद् अह्नो अनुरूपम् कुर्वते |

sanskrit_iast: tad āhuḥ kasmāt stutam anuśasyate kasmāt stomam atiśaṃsanti iti |
meaning: तद् आहुः कस्मात् स्तुतम् अनुशस्यते कस्मात् स्तोमम् अतिशंसन्ति इति |

sanskrit_iast: na vai tat stutam bhavati yan na anuśasyate |
meaning: न वै तत् स्तुतम् भवति यन् न अनुशस्यते |

sanskrit_iast: na sa stomo devān gacchati yam na atiśaṃsanti |
meaning: न स स्तोमो देवान् गच्छति यम् न अतिशंसन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tasmāt stutam anuśasyate tasmāt stomam atiśaṃsanti iti |
meaning: तस्मात् स्तुतम् अनुशस्यते तस्मात् स्तोमम् अतिशंसन्ति इति |

sanskrit_iast: atha yatra ha tat sarva carau devā yajñam atanvata |
meaning: अथ यत्र ह तत् सर्व चरौ देवा यज्ञम् अतन्वत |
text:
When the gods at Sarvacaru performed the sacrifice, Arbuda Kādraveya came up to them at the midday (pressing) and said to them, 'One Hotṛ's office is not being performed for you, that of the Grāvastut; let me perform it for you, do ye invite me.' They said 'So be it'; they invited him; he saw these appropriate (verses) of the Grāvastut, namely, 'Let them call forth; let us call forth,' when they call forth, for they call forth indeed; then when (they say) 'mightily mightily' (the verse containing 'mightily' is used), 'They speak out mightily with the strong exhilarating (drink)'; 'Set free the thought of him that hath pressed' (is the verse) when they set free. They are fourteen; the fingers are ten, the pressing stones are four; they make up this (number). They are Jagatī verses; the stones are connected with the Jagatī. In that he concludes
with a Triṣṭubh, thereby at the midday (pressing) is the Triṣṭubh secured. He praises, standing; the stones stand as it were. He praised wearing a turban, and with eyes tied up; therefore now also wearing a turban (the priest) praises the stones. Moreover they say ‘The eye came’; it was a serpent; thus did poison come to the priests; he used these (verses) connected with (Soma) the purifying, and repelling poison, in praise; in that he uses these (verses) connected with (Soma) the purifying and repelling poison, verily (it serves) for the healing of the sacrifice and the curing of the sacrificers.’

sanskrit_iast: tān ha arbudaḥ kādraveyo madhyaṃdina upodāsṛpyā uvāca |
meaning: तान् ह अर्बुदः काद्रवेयो मध्यंदिन उपोदासृप्या उवाच |

sanskrit_iast: ekā vai va iyam hotrā na kriyate grāva stotriyā |
meaning: एका वै व इयम् होत्रा न क्रियते ग्राव स्तोत्रिया |

sanskrit_iast: tām vo aham karavāṇy upa mā hvayadhvam iti |
meaning: ताम् वो अहम् करवाण्य् उप मा ह्वयध्वम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: sa etā grāva stotriyā abhirūpā apaśyat |
meaning: स एता ग्राव स्तोत्रिया अभिरूपा अपश्यत् |

sanskrit_iast: pra ete vadantu pra vayam vadāma iti pravadatsu |
meaning: प्र एते वदन्तु प्र वयम् वदाम इति प्रवदत्सु |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhad vadanti madireṇa mandinā iti tatra |
meaning: बृहद् वदन्ति मदिरेण मन्दिना इति तत्र |

sanskrit_iast: sa vā uṣṇīṣy apinaddha akṣo abhituṣṭāva |
meaning: स वा उष्णीष्य् अपिनद्ध अक्षो अभितुष्टाव |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād v apy etarhy uṣṇīṣy eva grāvṇo abhiṣṭauti |
meaning: तस्माद् व् अप्य् एतर्ह्य् उष्णीष्य् एव ग्राव्णो अभिष्टौति |

sanskrit_iast: cakṣur hā ha sa sarpa āsa |
meaning: चक्षुर् हा ह स सर्प आस |

sanskrit_iast: sa etāḥ pāvamānīr viṣa apamadanīr abhituṣṭāva |
meaning: स एताः पावमानीर् विष अपमदनीर् अभितुष्टाव |

sanskrit_iast: tad yat pāvamānīr viṣa apamadanīr abhiṣṭauti |
meaning: तद् यत् पावमानीर् विष अपमदनीर् अभिष्टौति |

sanskrit_iast: atha stute pavamāne dadhi gharmeṇa caranti tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ स्तुते पवमाने दधि घर्मेण चरन्ति तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |
text: When the Pavamāna has been sung, they proceed with the pot of milk, for this is the time for it; moreover (it serves) to secure the sap of the pressing. Then they proceed with the sacrifice of five oblations; the explanation of this has been given. (Verses) by Vasiṣṭha he repeats for (the goblets) being filled at the midday (pressing); Vasiṣṭha it was who proclaimed the Soma to Indra at the midday. They contain (the words) ‘hither’ and ‘bay steeds’, with the symbols of the invitatory verses. They are Triṣṭubh verses to Indra, for the midday pressing is connected with Indra and the Triṣṭubh. Ten he recites; ten goblets do they fill here. Then the Hotrakas sacrifice together; the explanation of this has been given. Triṣṭubh verses to Indra they use as offering verses for the Prasthitas at the midday (pressing), for the midday pressing is connected with Indra and the Triṣṭubh. They say the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations. Then comes the sacrificial food, then the goblet of the Hotṛ; the explanation of this has been given; when the Dakṣiṇā offerings have been made, the sacrificial fees are taken; the explanation of these has been given. He recites (a verse) by Viśvāmitra as the invitatory verse for the cup for the Maruts; the explanation of this has been given.

sanskrit_iast: atha haviṣ paṅktyā caranti tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ हविष् पङ्क्त्या चरन्ति तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣṭho ha madhyaṃdina indrāya somam provāca |
meaning: वसिष्ठो ह मध्यंदिन इन्द्राय सोमम् प्रोवाच |

sanskrit_iast: tā vā āvatyo harivatyo bhavanti puronuvākyā rūpeṇa |
meaning: ता वा आवत्यो हरिवत्यो भवन्ति पुरोनुवाक्या रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: atha hotrāḥ samyajanti tāsām uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ होत्राः सम्यजन्ति तासाम् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha iḍā atha hotṛ camasas tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ इडा अथ होतृ चमसस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: huteṣu dākṣiṇeṣu dakṣiṇā nīyante tāsām uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: हुतेषु दाक्षिणेषु दक्षिणा नीयन्ते तासाम् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvāmitrīm marutvatīya grahasya puronuvākyām anvāha tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: वैश्वामित्रीम् मरुत्वतीय ग्रहस्य पुरोनुवाक्याम् अन्वाह तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

text:
The Pṛṣṭha for the Maitrāvaruṇa is the Vāmadevya; the Vāmadevya is healing and medicine; verily thus are healing and medicine produced in the sacrifice. That of the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin is the Naudhasa; that has a finale; the finale is a support; verily (it serves) for support. That of the Achāvāka is the Kāleya; that they perform as the Aiḍa on Bṛhatī verses; the sacrificial food is cattle; the Bṛhatī is cattle; cattle are connected with the Bṛhatī; verily (it serves) to obtain cattle. They recite
the Pragāthas of the Sāman; thus they depart not from the Hotṛ's rule. The beginnings of the litanies of the Maitrāvaruṇa and Achāvāka are of five verses, the conclusions are of eleven verses; verily thus they make the two ends alike. The Maitrāvaruṇa recites (verses) by Viśvāmitra and Vāmadeva, for his conclusion is by Vāmadeva. The Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin recites (verses) by Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha, for his conclusion is by Vasiṣṭha. The Achāvāka recites (verses) by Bharadvāja and Viśvāmitra, for his conclusion is by Viśvāmitra. They recite (verses) by four Ṛṣis; up to four (degrees) are pairing, union, propagation; (they serve) for generation. The beginnings of the litanies of the Maitrāvaruṇa and Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin are by Viśvāmitra, and so is the conclusion of the Achāvāka; Viśvāmitra is speech; verily thus with speech on all sides they extend the sacrifice. This is the explanation of the introductory and concluding rites and of the one day form.

sanskrit_iast: śāntir eva eṣā bheṣajam yajñe kriyate |
meaning: शान्तिर् एव एषा भेषजम् यज्ञे क्रियते |

sanskrit_iast: tathā eṣām hotur nyāyād anitam bhavati |
meaning: तथा एषाम् होतुर् न्यायाद् अनितम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: pañcarce maitrāvaruṇasya ca acchāvākasya ca uktha mukhe bhavataḥ |
meaning: पञ्चर्चे मैत्रावरुणस्य च अच्छावाकस्य च उक्थ मुखे भवतः |

sanskrit_iast: viśvāmitrasya ca vāmadevasya ca maitrāvaruṇaḥ śaṃsati |
meaning: विश्वामित्रस्य च वामदेवस्य च मैत्रावरुणः शंसति |

sanskrit_iast: ā caturam vai dvandvam mithunam prajananam prajātyai |
meaning: आ चतुरम् वै द्वन्द्वम् मिथुनम् प्रजननम् प्रजात्यै |

sanskrit_iast: vaiśvāmitre maitrāvaruṇasya ca brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaś ca uktha mukhe bhavataḥ |
meaning: वैश्वामित्रे मैत्रावरुणस्य च ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनश् च उक्थ मुखे भवतः |

sanskrit_iast: vācā eva tat sarvato yajñam tanvata ity etad brāhmaṇam |
meaning: वाचा एव तत् सर्वतो यज्ञम् तन्वत इत्य् एतद् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: vāmadevyam maitrāvaruṇasya ahar ahaḥ pṛṣṭham bhavati |
meaning: वामदेव्यम् मैत्रावरुणस्य अहर् अहः पृष्ठम् भवति |
text: Day by day the Pṛṣṭha for the Maitrāvaruṇa is the Vāmadevya; the Vāmadevya is healing and medicine; verily thus are healing and medicine day by day produced in the sacrifice. Then day by day they recite these Pragāthas containing (the word) 'who'; Prajāpati is Who; verily thus day by day they continue finding support in Prajāpati. Moreover they continue employing the varied hymns, the Ahīnas (by name), unappeased; verily they continue to appease them day by day with the Pragāthas containing (the word) 'who'. Then these regular Triṣṭubh verses are recited day by day as the strophes of the litanies; the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus day by day they continue finding support in might and strength. '(Drive) all our enemies away, O Indra,' the Maitrāvaruṇa (recites) this verse by Sukīrti, containing (the word) 'drive away', for the driving away of the evil. By the same Ṛṣis as are the two hymns are the two beginnings of the litanies of the other two. 'Those yoked with prayer I yoke with prayer' and 'Lead us to a wide space, wise one' are the beginnings of the litanies, containing (the words) 'prayer' and 'wide'; verily thus day by day they continue finding support in the prayer and in the wide goer.

sanskrit_iast: śāntir eva eṣā bheṣajam ahar ahar yajñe kriyate |
meaning: शान्तिर् एव एषा भेषजम् अहर् अहर् यज्ञे क्रियते |

sanskrit_iast: atha etān kadvataḥ pragāthān ahar ahaḥ śaṃsanti |
meaning: अथ एतान् कद्वतः प्रगाथान् अहर् अहः शंसन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: prajāpatāv eva tad ahar ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: प्रजापताव् एव तद् अहर् अहः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atho aśāntāni vā ete ahīna sūktāny anyāny anyāny upayuñjānā yanti |
meaning: अथो अशान्तानि वा एते अहीन सूक्तान्य् अन्यान्य् अन्यान्य् उपयुञ्जाना यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tāny eva etaiḥ kadvadbhiḥ pragāthair ahar ahaḥ śamayanto yanti |
meaning: तान्य् एव एतैः कद्वद्भिः प्रगाथैर् अहर् अहः शमयन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atha etās tantryās triṣṭubha uktha pratipado ahar ahaḥ śasyante |
meaning: अथ एतास् तन्त्र्यास् त्रिष्टुभ उक्थ प्रतिपदो अहर् अहः शस्यन्ते |

sanskrit_iast: bala eva tad vīrye ahar ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: बल एव तद् वीर्ये अहर् अहः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: apa praca indra viśvān amitrān iti saukīrtim maitrāvaruṇo apanuttavatīm pāpmana eva apanuttyai |
meaning: अप प्रच इन्द्र विश्वान् अमित्रान् इति सौकीर्तिम् मैत्रावरुणो अपनुत्तवतीम् पाप्मन एव अपनुत्त्यै |

sanskrit_iast: yad ārṣeye sūkte tad ārṣeye uktha mukhīye itarayoḥ |
meaning: यद् आर्षेये सूक्ते तद् आर्षेये उक्थ मुखीये इतरयोः |

sanskrit_iast: brahmaṇā te brahma yujā yunajmy urum no lokam anu neṣi vidvān iti brahmavaty uruvatyau |
meaning: ब्रह्मणा ते ब्रह्म युजा युनज्म्य् उरुम् नो लोकम् अनु नेषि विद्वान् इति ब्रह्मवत्य् उरुवत्यौ |

sanskrit_iast: brahmaṇi ca eva tad uru gāye ca ahar ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: ब्रह्मणि च एव तद् उरु गाये च अहर् अहः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atha etān śilpāni madhyame tryahe śasyante |
meaning: अथ एतान् शिल्पानि मध्यमे त्र्यहे शस्यन्ते |
text:
Then the Śilpas are recited in the middle three days, for the
middle (set of) three days contains the Śilpas. Virāj verses and verses by Vimada (are used) on the first day, for the fourth day is connected with the Virāj. Paṅkti and great Paṅkti verses (are used) on the fifth day, for the fifth day is connected with the Paṅkti. Atichandas verses (are used) on the sixth day, for the sixth day is connected with the Atichandas. Moreover that which is performed without the Bṛhatī is not a Pṛṣṭha; the Pṛṣṭhas here fall away from the Bṛhatī; verily thus day by day they continue finding support in the Śilpas. Moreover the middle (set of) three days is the atmosphere; the atmosphere is without base or support; verily thus day by day they continue finding support in the Śilpas. They are triplets; the Śilpa is threefold, dancing, music, and singing. Verily thus day by day they continue finding support in them. 'Praise nought else' and 'Let us not fear, let us not be troubled' is the Pṛṣṭha for the Maitrāvaruṇa on the tenth day by Medhātithi, for his Pṛṣṭha is not performed on Bṛhatī verses before the tenth day; prosperity is solitary; the Bṛhatī is prosperity; verily thus at the end he finds support in prosperity. Having recited (verses) of two Padas, they recite (the hymn) of the one day (rite); the one day (rite) is a support; the tenth day is a support; (the verses) of two Padas are the metre in which support can be found; verily (they serve) for support.

sanskrit_iast: śilpavān hy eṣa madhyamas tryaho bhavati |
meaning: शिल्पवान् ह्य् एष मध्यमस् त्र्यहो भवति |

sanskrit_iast: virājaś ca vaimadyaś ca caturthe ahan |
meaning: विराजश् च वैमद्यश् च चतुर्थे अहन् |

sanskrit_iast: paṅktayaś ca mahā paṅktayaś ca pañcame ahan |
meaning: पङ्क्तयश् च महा पङ्क्तयश् च पञ्चमे अहन् |

sanskrit_iast: atho apṛṣṭham vā u tad yad anyatra bṛhatyai kriyate |
meaning: अथो अपृष्ठम् वा उ तद् यद् अन्यत्र बृहत्यै क्रियते |

sanskrit_iast: cyavanta u vā atra bṛhatyai pṛṣṭhāni |
meaning: च्यवन्त उ वा अत्र बृहत्यै पृष्ठानि |

sanskrit_iast: śilpeṣv eva tad ahar ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: शिल्पेष्व् एव तद् अहर् अहः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atho antarikṣam vā eṣa madhyamas tryahaḥ |
meaning: अथो अन्तरिक्षम् वा एष मध्यमस् त्र्यहः |

sanskrit_iast: śilpeṣv eva tad ahar ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: शिल्पेष्व् एव तद् अहर् अहः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: trivṛd vai śilpam nṛttam gītam vāditam iti |
meaning: त्रिवृद् वै शिल्पम् नृत्तम् गीतम् वादितम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: teṣv eva tad ahar ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: तेष्व् एव तद् अहर् अहः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: mā cid anyad vi śaṃsata mā bhema mā śramiṣma iti maithātham maitrāvaruṇasya daśame ahan bṛhatīṣu pṛṣṭham bhavati |
meaning: मा चिद् अन्यद् वि शंसत मा भेम मा श्रमिष्म इति मैथाथम् मैत्रावरुणस्य दशमे अहन् बृहतीषु पृष्ठम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: na hi tasya prāg daśamād ahno bṛhatīṣu pṛṣṭham bhavati |
meaning: न हि तस्य प्राग् दशमाद् अह्नो बृहतीषु पृष्ठम् भवति |

sanskrit_iast: śriyām eva tad antataḥ pratitiṣṭhante yanti |
meaning: श्रियाम् एव तद् अन्ततः प्रतितिष्ठन्ते यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: pratiṣṭhā vā ekāhaḥ pratiṣṭhā daśamam ahaḥ |
meaning: प्रतिष्ठा वा एकाहः प्रतिष्ठा दशमम् अहः |

sanskrit_iast: pratiṣṭhānīyam vai chando dvipadāḥ pratiṣṭhityā eva |
meaning: प्रतिष्ठानीयम् वै छन्दो द्विपदाः प्रतिष्ठित्या एव |

text: The Naudhasa is (the Pṛṣṭha) for the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin; the explanation of this has been given. In Gāyatrī verses they give the lead for the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin on the sixth day with the symbol of the Raivata, of the day, to secure the form of the Ahīnas, for the continuity of the Ahīnas, (thinking) 'Undiminished (ahīnān) we secure all desires,' for here is nothing taken away. 'Prayers they have offered up through seeking glory' is the conclusion day by day; the 'Prayers up' hymn is the seasons; verily thus day by day they continue finding support in the seasons. They are six (verses); the seasons are six; verily thus day by day they continue finding support in the seasons.

sanskrit_iast: paṅktiṣu brāhmaṇācchaṃsine ca acchāvākāya ca praṇayanti pañcame ahan |
meaning: पङ्क्तिषु ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिने च अच्छावाकाय च प्रणयन्ति पञ्चमे अहन् |

sanskrit_iast: ud u brahmāṇy airata śravasya ity ahar ahaḥ paryāsaḥ |
meaning: उद् उ ब्रह्माण्य् ऐरत श्रवस्य इत्य् अहर् अहः पर्यासः |

sanskrit_iast: ṛtuṣv eva tad ahar ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: ऋतुष्व् एव तद् अहर् अहः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: ṛtuṣv eva tad ahar ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: ऋतुष्व् एव तद् अहर् अहः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

text:
The Kāleya is (the Pṛṣṭha) for the Achāvāka; the explanation of this has been given. In (verses) of six Padas they give the lead to the Achāvāka on the sixth day, with the symbol of the sixth day. 'Having with thought, like a carpenter, a hymn' is the conclusion day by day; the
'carpenter like' hymn is Prajāpati; verily thus they continue day by day finding support in Prajāpati. That (hymn) has no (deity) mentioned; Prajāpati is he (whose name is) not mentioned; verily thus they continue day by day finding support in Prajāpati. There is one (verse) alone with (the deity) expressed; Prajāpati is one alone; verily thus they continue day by day finding support in Prajāpati. Of them the following are unchanged, the Maitrāvaruṇa's Pṛṣṭha, and the conclusions of the other two; verily thus they continue day by day finding support in them.

sanskrit_iast: abhi taṣṭā iva dīdhayā manīṣām ity ahar ahaḥ paryāsaḥ |
meaning: अभि तष्टा इव दीधया मनीषाम् इत्य् अहर् अहः पर्यासः |

sanskrit_iast: prajāpatāv eva tad ahar ahaḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: प्रजापताव् एव तद् अहर् अहः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: sā vā atra ekā eva niruktā |
meaning: सा वा अत्र एका एव निरुक्ता |

text: It is of ten verses; these breaths are ten; verily thus he places these breaths in the sacrifice and in the sacrificers; the midday (performances) of the Hotrakas consist of two hymns, to counterpoise the Hotṛ's two litanies. Moreover, the Hotṛ is the year, the Hotrakas the seasons; in that the seasons being united in couples are called summer, the rains, and winter, therefore the midday (performances) of the Hotrakas consist of two hymns. Moreover, the Hotṛ is the body, the Hotrakas the limbs; in that the limbs are twofold, therefore the midday (performances) of the Hotrakas consist of two hymns. Having recited at the morning pressings the over recitation of the Stomas, they recite the Ahīna hymns at the midday (pressings) on the Caturviñśa, Abhijit, Viṣuvant, Viśvajit and Mahāvrata days, for these days are not deficient. Having recited the Ahīna hymns (on these days) those of the one day (rite) they recite. These days are turned away and not returning; in that having recited the Ahīna hymns, they recite those of the one day (rite), and the one day (rite) is a support, verily (they serve) for support. Five hymns each time the Maitrāvaruṇa recites in all the Chandomas; the Chandomas are cattle; cattle are fivefold; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. Four each the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin and the Achāvāka; the Chandomas are cattle; cattle are fourfold and also four-footed; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. The Śastras have five calls; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fivefold; verily (they serve) to win cattle. The offering verses of the litanies are from the one day (rite); the one day (rite) is a support; verily (they serve) for support. They say the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇān eva tad yajñeṣu ca yajamāneṣu ca dadhāti |
meaning: प्राणान् एव तद् यज्ञेषु च यजमानेषु च दधाति |

sanskrit_iast: tad yad dvandvam samastā ṛtava ākhyāyante grīṣmo varṣā hemanta iti |
meaning: तद् यद् द्वन्द्वम् समस्ता ऋतव आख्यायन्ते ग्रीष्मो वर्षा हेमन्त इति |

sanskrit_iast: stoma atiśaṃsam prātaḥ savaneṣu śastvā ahīna sūktāni madhyaṃdineṣu śaṃsanti caturviṃśe abhijit viṣuvati bṛhat pṛṣṭhe viśvajiti mahāvratīye ahan |
meaning: स्तोम अतिशंसम् प्रातः सवनेषु शस्त्वा अहीन सूक्तानि मध्यंदिनेषु शंसन्ति चतुर्विंशे अभिजित् विषुवति बृहत् पृष्ठे विश्वजिति महाव्रतीये अहन् |

sanskrit_iast: tad yad ahīna sūktāni madhyaṃdineṣu śaṃsanti |
meaning: तद् यद् अहीन सूक्तानि मध्यंदिनेषु शंसन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: catvāri catvāri sūktāni brāhmaṇācchaṃsī ca acchāvākaś ca śaṃsataḥ sarveṣu chandomeṣu |
meaning: चत्वारि चत्वारि सूक्तानि ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी च अच्छावाकश् च शंसतः सर्वेषु छन्दोमेषु |

sanskrit_iast: triṣṭubham āditya grahasya puronuvākyām anvāha tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: त्रिष्टुभम् आदित्य ग्रहस्य पुरोनुवाक्याम् अन्वाह तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |
text: The morning pressing is the Vasus', the midday pressing the Rudras', the third pressing the Ādityas'. In that he begins the third pressing with the Āditya cup, verily thus he begins with its own deity. Moreover, the third pressing is a pressing which has the sap sucked out; the Āditya cup is a cup rich in sap; verily thereby he makes the third pressing rich in sap. He recites a Triṣṭubh as invitatory verse for the Āditya cup; the explanation of this has been given. Then, when the Pavamāna has been sung, they proceed with the animal victim, for this is the time for it; moreover (it serves) to confer sap on the pressing. Then they proceed with the sacrifice of five oblations; the explanation of this has been given. He recites (verses) by Vāmadeva at the third pressing for (the goblets) being filled, for Vāmadeva it was who proclaimed the Soma to Indra at the third pressing. They contain (the words) 'hither' and 'bay steed', with the symbol of the invitatory verses; they are Triṣṭubhs addressed to Indra and the Ṛbhus; verily thus he makes Indra a half-sharer in the pressing. Nine he recites; ten goblets do they fill here, but the concluding is as the introductory rite. The Hotrakas sacrifice together; the explanation of this has been given. The offering verses are Jagatī verses, containing (the words) 'draught', 'be drunk', and 'drunk', for the third pressing is connected with the Jagatī; they contain (the word) 'be drunk', for the third pressing contains (the word) 'be drunk'. They say a second vaṣaṭ for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations. Then comes the sacrificial food, then the Hotṛ's goblet; the explanation of this has been given. Then they offer the cakes (for the Pitṛs) at the third pressing; the explanation of these has been given. Then they proceed with the cup for Savitṛ; the explanation of this has been given. He recites one Triṣṭubh as invitatory verse for the cup for Savitṛ; the explanation of this has been given. Again in that between the two litanies the Agnīdh says the offering verses for the cup for the wives, thereby the two reach the Hotṛ.

sanskrit_iast: atha stute pavamāne paśunā caranti tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ स्तुते पवमाने पशुना चरन्ति तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha haviṣ paṅktyā caranti tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ हविष् पङ्क्त्या चरन्ति तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: vāmadevo ha tṛtīya sanava indrāya somam provāca |
meaning: वामदेवो ह तृतीय सनव इन्द्राय सोमम् प्रोवाच |

sanskrit_iast: tā vā āvatyo harivatyo bhavanti puronuvākyā rūpeṇa |
meaning: ता वा आवत्यो हरिवत्यो भवन्ति पुरोनुवाक्या रूपेण |

sanskrit_iast: indram eva tad ardha bhājam savanasya karoti |
meaning: इन्द्रम् एव तद् अर्ध भाजम् सवनस्य करोति |

sanskrit_iast: atha hotrāḥ samyajanti tāsām uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ होत्राः सम्यजन्ति तासाम् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha iḍā atha hotṛ camasas tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: अथ इडा अथ होतृ चमसस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: aupāsanāṃs tṛtīya savana upāsyanti teṣām uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: औपासनांस् तृतीय सवन उपास्यन्ति तेषाम् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: triṣṭubham sāvitra grahasya puronuvākyām anvāha tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: त्रिष्टुभम् सावित्र ग्रहस्य पुरोनुवाक्याम् अन्वाह तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha yad uktha antareṇa agnīn patnīvatasya yajati |
meaning: अथ यद् उक्थ अन्तरेण अग्नीन् पत्नीवतस्य यजति |

sanskrit_iast: aindrāgnāny ukthya ukthāni bhavant teṣām uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: ऐन्द्राग्नान्य् उक्थ्य उक्थानि भवन्त् तेषाम् उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |
text: The litanies of the Ukthya are addressed to Indra and Agni; the explanation of these has been given. These to Indra in Jagatī they recite day by day; the Jagatī is cattle; cattle are connected with the Jagatī; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. 'These should be unchanged' some state, saying 'These are the supporters of the pressing.' But the rule is 'They should be varied,' for one day, then another, they approach. (Recitations) to Varuṇa, to Bṛhaspati, and to Viṣṇu they recite; their metre is the Jagatī; Indra's the Triṣṭubh; in that the metres are inverted, it is to secure the characteristic of the deities. (Recitations ) to Indra and Varuṇa, to Indra and Bṛhaspati, to Indra and Viṣṇu they recite; verily with these they accompany the cups, for so are the cups drawn.

sanskrit_iast: atha etāny aindrāṇi jāgatāni sūktāni śaṃsanti |
meaning: अथ एतान्य् ऐन्द्राणि जागतानि सूक्तानि शंसन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: tāny acyutāni syur iti ha eka āhuḥ savana dharaṇāni iti vadantaḥ |
meaning: तान्य् अच्युतानि स्युर् इति ह एक आहुः सवन धरणानि इति वदन्तः |

sanskrit_iast: anyāny anyāni iti tv eva sthitam |
meaning: अन्यान्य् अन्यानि इति त्व् एव स्थितम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha vāruṇam bārhaspatyam vaiṣṇavam iti śaṃsanti |
meaning: अथ वारुणम् बार्हस्पत्यम् वैष्णवम् इति शंसन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: jagatī vā eteṣām chandas triṣṭub indrasya |
meaning: जगती वा एतेषाम् छन्दस् त्रिष्टुब् इन्द्रस्य |

sanskrit_iast: aindrāvaruṇam aindrā bārhaspatyam aindrāvaiṣṇavam iti śaṃsanti |
meaning: ऐन्द्रावरुणम् ऐन्द्रा बार्हस्पत्यम् ऐन्द्रावैष्णवम् इति शंसन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: carṣaṇī dhṛtam maghavānam ukthyam iti maitrāvaruṇas tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: चर्षणी धृतम् मघवानम् उक्थ्यम् इति मैत्रावरुणस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |
text: 'Holder of the people, the generous, worthy of praise' the Maitrāvaruṇa (says); the explanation of this has been given. The conclusion is by Vasiṣṭha day by day; Vasiṣṭha saw the third pressing for the Maitrāvaruṇa's function; therefore day by day the conclusion is by Vasiṣṭha. In Kakubh verses they give the lead to the Maitrāvaruṇa on the third day; thereby he falls into the power of the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin. On the fourth day they give the lead to each in his own metre; verily thus each in his own metre they continue finding support. In Gāyatrī verses they give the lead to the Maitrāvaruṇa, in Uṣṇih verses to the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin, in Anuṣṭubh verses to the Achāvāka, to secure a progressive increase. So their metres increase with four syllables each. In Paṅkti verses they give the lead to the Maitrāvaruṇa on the fifth day, for the fifth day is connected with the Paṅkti; in (verses) of two Padas they give the lead on the sixth day, for the sixth day is connected with (verses) of two Padas. Moreover they perform the Sāmans, Gūrda, Bhadra, Udvaṅcaputra; moreover the Śilpas are accompanied by (verses) of two feet; therefore here the Śilpas are recited, (thinking) 'Let us not depart from the Śilpas.'

sanskrit_iast: vasiṣṭho ha etan maitrāvaruṇīyāyai tṛtīya savanam dadarśa |
meaning: वसिष्ठो ह एतन् मैत्रावरुणीयायै तृतीय सवनम् ददर्श |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād vāsiṣṭho ahar ahaḥ paryāso bhavati |
meaning: तस्माद् वासिष्ठो अहर् अहः पर्यासो भवति |

sanskrit_iast: atha caturthe ahant sve sve chandasi praṇayanti |
meaning: अथ चतुर्थे अहन्त् स्वे स्वे छन्दसि प्रणयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: sve sva eva tac chandasi pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
meaning: स्वे स्व एव तच् छन्दसि प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: gāyatrīṣu maitrāvaruṇāya praṇayanty uṣṇikṣu brāhmaṇācchaṃsine anuṣṭupsv acchāvākāya uttara uttaritāyai |
meaning: गायत्रीषु मैत्रावरुणाय प्रणयन्त्य् उष्णिक्षु ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिने अनुष्टुप्स्व् अच्छावाकाय उत्तर उत्तरितायै |

sanskrit_iast: tathā eṣām caturbhiś caturbhir akṣaraiś chandāṃsy abhyudyanti |
meaning: तथा एषाम् चतुर्भिश् चतुर्भिर् अक्षरैश् छन्दांस्य् अभ्युद्यन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atho gūrdam bhadram udvaṃśa putram iti sāmāni kurvanti |
meaning: अथो गूर्दम् भद्रम् उद्वंश पुत्रम् इति सामानि कुर्वन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: atho dvipadā sahacarāṇi vai śilpāni bhavanti |
meaning: अथो द्विपदा सहचराणि वै शिल्पानि भवन्ति |

text:
With the Nābhānediṣṭha the Hotṛ sprinkles seed; it he hands to the Maitrāvaruṇa; it he develops with the Vālakhilyās; these Vālakhilyās he recites as divided; by Padas the first two hymns he divides; verily thus
by joints he gathers him together; by half verses the second two; man consists of two portions; verily thus he unites them; verse by verse the third two hymns; verily thus he gathers him whole; he should invert in the Nārāśaṁsa; therefore foetuses are born inverted.

In the Tārkṣya he mounts the difficult mounting; Tārkṣya is Vāyu; Vāyu is breath verily thus he places breath in him; him he hands over to the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin. Him he receives in the womb of the Sukīrti (hymn ); for him born he recites in Paṅkti form with repetition of o the Vṛṣākapi (hymn); the repetition of o is food; verily thus born he finds support in proper food. Then he recites the Kuntāpa according to the metres, for the obtaining of all desires; viz. the Nārāśaṅsīs, the Raibhīs, the Kāravyās, the Indragāthās, the Bhūtechads, the Parikṣit verses, and the prattle of Etaśa. Etaśa, the sage, saw the life of the sacrifice. He said to his sons 'My boys, I have seen the life of the sacrifice; that I shall prattle forth; think me not mad.' They said 'Be it so.' Then he prattled it forth; his eldest son, creeping up, stopped his mouth, (saying) 'Our father has become mad.' To him he said 'Be gone; fie on thee, O fool; I make thine offspring the worst; hadst thou not, O fool, stopped my mouth, I had made the cow of a hundred (years of) life, and man of a thousand.' Therefore the descendants of Etaśa being the Ājāneyas are the worst of the Bhṛgus, for they are under curse by a father, their own deity, their own Prajāpati.

sanskrit_iast: tam sa sukīrtinā yoninā pragigṛhṇāti jātam |
meaning: तम् स सुकीर्तिना योनिना प्रगिगृह्णाति जातम् |

sanskrit_iast: atha etam vṛṣākapim paṅkti śaṃsam śaṃsati |
meaning: अथ एतम् वृषाकपिम् पङ्क्ति शंसम् शंसति |

sanskrit_iast: jāta eva asmiṃs tad anna adyam pratidadhāti |
meaning: जात एव अस्मिंस् तद् अन्न अद्यम् प्रतिदधाति |

sanskrit_iast: atha etat kuntāpam yathā chandasam śaṃsati |
meaning: अथ एतत् कुन्तापम् यथा छन्दसम् शंसति |

sanskrit_iast: nārāśaṃsī raibhīḥ kāravyā indra gāthā bhūtecchadaḥ pārikṣitīr etaśa pralāpam iti |
meaning: नाराशंसी रैभीः कारव्या इन्द्र गाथा भूतेच्छदः पारिक्षितीर् एतश प्रलापम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: etaśo ha vai munir yajñasya āyur dadarśa |
meaning: एतशो ह वै मुनिर् यज्ञस्य आयुर् ददर्श |

sanskrit_iast: putrakā yajñasya āyur adarśam tad abhilapṣyāmi |
meaning: पुत्रका यज्ञस्य आयुर् अदर्शम् तद् अभिलप्ष्यामि |

sanskrit_iast: tasya ha jyeṣṭhaḥ putro abhisṛpya mukham apijagrāha |
meaning: तस्य ह ज्येष्ठः पुत्रो अभिसृप्य मुखम् अपिजग्राह |

sanskrit_iast: yad vai me jālma mukham na apy agrahīṣyaḥ |
meaning: यद् वै मे जाल्म मुखम् न अप्य् अग्रहीष्यः |

sanskrit_iast: śata āyuṣam gām akariṣyam sahasra āyuṣam puruṣam iti |
meaning: शत आयुषम् गाम् अकरिष्यम् सहस्र आयुषम् पुरुषम् इति |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād aitaśāyanā ājāneyāḥ santo bhṛgūṇām pāpiṣṭhāḥ pitrā abhiśaptāḥ svayā devatayā svena prajāpatinā |
meaning: तस्माद् ऐतशायना आजानेयाः सन्तो भृगूणाम् पापिष्ठाः पित्रा अभिशप्ताः स्वया देवतया स्वेन प्रजापतिना |

text:
(The verses) of the Ādityas and Aṅgirases he recites next. The Ādityas and the Aṅgirases were at variance, 'We shall go first to the world
of heaven' (said) the Āditya; 'we' the Aṅgirases. The Aṅgirases sent to the Ādityas (saying) 'Ours is the pressing day to-morrow; do ye cause us to sacrifice.' Agni was their envoy; the Ādityas said 'Ours is the pressing day to-day; and thou art the Hotṛ for us here, Bṛhaspati the Brahman, Ayāsya the Udgātṛ, Ghora Āṅgirasa the Ādhvaryu.' Them they rejected; him they desired to please with these (verses); thus they repeat these (verses). They brought a white horse as sacrificial fee, that one which here gives heat; therefore the Ādityas went to heaven; he goes to heaven who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: ādityāś ca ha vā aṅgirasaś ca aspardhanta |
meaning: आदित्याश् च ह वा अङ्गिरसश् च अस्पर्धन्त |

sanskrit_iast: vayam pūrve svargam lokam eṣyāma ity ādityāḥ |
meaning: वयम् पूर्वे स्वर्गम् लोकम् एष्याम इत्य् आदित्याः |

sanskrit_iast: śvaḥ sutyā no yājayata na iti |
meaning: श्वः सुत्या नो याजयत न इति |

sanskrit_iast: teṣām nas tvam eva hotā asi |
meaning: तेषाम् नस् त्वम् एव होता असि |

sanskrit_iast: bṛhaspatir brahmāya asya udgātā ghora āṅgiraso adhvaryur iti |
meaning: बृहस्पतिर् ब्रह्माय अस्य उद्गाता घोर आङ्गिरसो अध्वर्युर् इति |

sanskrit_iast: te aśvam śvetam dakṣiṇām niṇyur etam eva ya eṣa tapati |
meaning: ते अश्वम् श्वेतम् दक्षिणाम् निण्युर् एतम् एव य एष तपति |

sanskrit_iast: tata u ha ādityāḥ svar īyuḥ |
meaning: तत उ ह आदित्याः स्वर् ईयुः |

text: He recites the orderings of the quarters; the quarters are in order for him. He recites the man-ordering (verses); men are in order for him. He says the riddles, the Pratīrādhas, the Ativādā, the Āhanasyās, all forms of speech. Therefore a man speaks all forms of speech, but other animals one only. They are eight; by them the gods attained all attainments; so verily also the sacrificers by them attain all attainments. 'The Kapṛth, O men, the Kapṛth extend,' and 'What time forward ye came' are two (verses ); thus they become perfect. They make up ten; the Virāj consists of sets of ten; the Virāj is prosperity and proper food; verily (they serve) to obtain the Virāj as prosperity and proper food.

sanskrit_iast: pravalhikāḥ pratīrādhān ativādām āhanasyāḥ sarvā vāco vadati |
meaning: प्रवल्हिकाः प्रतीराधान् अतिवादाम् आहनस्याः सर्वा वाचो वदति |

sanskrit_iast: etābhir vai devāḥ sarvā aṣṭīr āśnuvata |
meaning: एताभिर् वै देवाः सर्वा अष्टीर् आश्नुवत |

sanskrit_iast: tatho eva etad yajamānā etābhir eva sarvā aṣṭīr aśnuvate |
meaning: तथो एव एतद् यजमाना एताभिर् एव सर्वा अष्टीर् अश्नुवते |

sanskrit_iast: kapṛnnaraḥ kapṛtham uddadhātana yadd ha prācīr ajagantā iti dve eka pātinyau |
meaning: कपृन्नरः कपृथम् उद्दधातन यद्द् ह प्राचीर् अजगन्ता इति द्वे एक पातिन्यौ |

text:
He recites the Dadhikrā (verse ); the Dadhikrā (verse) is speech; verily thus he places speech in him; he recites (the verses) to Soma the purifying; (the verses) to Soma the purifying are a filter; verily thus he purifies him. Him he hands over to the Achāvāka; him he with the
Evayāmarut (hymn ) makes to move when born; he repeats o; stumbling as it were one moves when first desirous to walk; verily thus from the immortal metre he propagates him for immortality; they obtain immortality who perform the sixth day (rite). Having recited the strophe and antistrophe, he recites the Vālakhilyās; the strophe and antistrophe are the body, the Vālakhilyās the breaths; these breaths are not separated (from the body). They say ‘Why are they (called) Vālakhilyās?’ That which is not in contact in two fields, they call Khila; these breaths are a hair (vāla) in breadth and are not separated; therefore are they Vālakhilyās.

sanskrit_iast: nyūṅkha mānaka iva vai prathamam cicarṣaṃś carati |
meaning: न्यूङ्ख मानक इव वै प्रथमम् चिचर्षंश् चरति |

sanskrit_iast: tad enam amṛtāc chandaso amṛtatvāya prajanayanti |
meaning: तद् एनम् अमृताच् छन्दसो अमृतत्वाय प्रजनयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: te amṛtatvam āpnuvanti ya ṣaṣṭham ahar upayanti |
meaning: ते अमृतत्वम् आप्नुवन्ति य षष्ठम् अहर् उपयन्ति |

sanskrit_iast: anantarhitā u ha iem ātmanaḥ prāṇāḥ |
meaning: अनन्तर्हिता उ ह इएम् आत्मनः प्राणाः |

sanskrit_iast: vāla mātrā u hi ime prāṇā asambhinnāḥ |
meaning: वाल मात्रा उ हि इमे प्राणा असम्भिन्नाः |

sanskrit_iast: tārkṣye dūrohaṇam rohati iti tad uktam |
meaning: तार्क्ष्ये दूरोहणम् रोहति इति तद् उक्तम् |
text: ‘In the Tārkṣya he mounts the difficult mounting,’ it has been said. In Gāyatrī verses they give the lead for the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin on the second day, thereby he falls into the power of the Maitrāvaruṇa. ‘Forward to the most generous, the great, born of great wealth’ is a six verse (hymn ), twice as great as that of the Maitrāvaruṇa. The conclusion day by day is by Kṛṣṇa; Kṛṣṇa Āṅgirasa saw this third pressing for the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin’s office; therefore day by day the conclusion is by Kṛṣṇa. In Anuṣṭubhs they give the lead for the Achāvāka on the third day; thereby he falls into the power of the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin. The ‘season mother’ (hymn ) has thirteen verses; it is twice as great as that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin and there is one verse over. The conclusion day by day is by Bharadvāja; Bharadvāja saw this third pressing for the Achāvāka’s office; therefore day by day the conclusion is by Bharadvāja. The Achāvāka alternates the two Viṣṇu (hymns ), the conclusions the other two. The Maitrāvaruṇa and the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin have two conclusions; the Achāvāka has one conclusion. In that the Achāvāka has an unchanging conclusion, the Achāvāka is a support; verily (it serves) for support.

sanskrit_iast: pra maṃhiṣṭhāya bṛhate bṛhad raya iti jāgatam ṣaḍṛcam tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: प्र मंहिष्ठाय बृहते बृहद् रय इति जागतम् षडृचम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: kṛṣṇo ha etad āṅgiraso brāhmaṇācchaṃsīyāyai tṛtīya savanam dadarśa |
meaning: कृष्णो ह एतद् आङ्गिरसो ब्राह्मणाच्छंसीयायै तृतीय सवनम् ददर्श |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād kārṣṇo ahar ahaḥ paryāso bhavati |
meaning: तस्माद् कार्ष्णो अहर् अहः पर्यासो भवति |

sanskrit_iast: ṛtur janitrīyam trayodaśarcam tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
meaning: ऋतुर् जनित्रीयम् त्रयोदशर्चम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

sanskrit_iast: dvis tāvad yāvad brāhmaṇācchaṃsina ekā ca upa |
meaning: द्विस् तावद् यावद् ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन एका च उप |

sanskrit_iast: bharadvājo ha etad acchāvākīyāyai tṛtīya savanam dadarśa |
meaning: भरद्वाजो ह एतद् अच्छावाकीयायै तृतीय सवनम् ददर्श |

sanskrit_iast: tasmād bhāradvājo ahar ahaḥ paryāso bhavati |
meaning: तस्माद् भारद्वाजो अहर् अहः पर्यासो भवति |

text:
Thirty-six (verses) the Maitrāvaruṇa recites at the Caturviṅśa, forty the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin, and forty-four the Achāvāka. These are a hundred and twenty. A hundred and twenty are the days of the season; thus he obtains the season, with the season the year and the desires that are in the year. Five hymns the Maitrāvaruṇa recites on all the Chandoma days; the Chandomas are cattle; cattle are fivefold; verily (they
serve) to obtain cattle. Four hymns the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin recites in the first Chandoma; the Chandomas are cattle; cattle are fourfold, and also fourfooted; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. Five hymns the Achāvāka recites in the first Chandoma; the Chandomas are cattle; cattle are fivefold; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. Six (they recite) in the second and third; the year has six seasons; verily (they serve) to obtain the year. The Śastras have four calls; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fourfold, and also fourfooted; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. On the sixth day that of the Maitrāvaruṇa has five calls; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fivefold; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. The offering verses of the litanies are from the one day (rite); the one day (rite) is a support; verily (they serve) for support. They say the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations.

sanskrit_iast: pañca pañca sūktāni tṛtīya savane maitrāvaruṇaḥ śaṃsati sarveṣu chandomeṣu |
meaning: पञ्च पञ्च सूक्तानि तृतीय सवने मैत्रावरुणः शंसति सर्वेषु छन्दोमेषु |

sanskrit_iast: catvāri sūktāni brāhmaṇācchaṃsī śaṃsati prathame chandome |
meaning: चत्वारि सूक्तानि ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी शंसति प्रथमे छन्दोमे |

sanskrit_iast: pañca sūktāny acchāvākaḥ śaṃsati prathame chandome |
meaning: पञ्च सूक्तान्य् अच्छावाकः शंसति प्रथमे छन्दोमे |

sanskrit_iast: ṣaṣṭha eva ahan maitrāvaruṇasya pañca āhāvam bhavati |
meaning: षष्ठ एव अहन् मैत्रावरुणस्य पञ्च आहावम् भवति |

text:
Five metres they recite at night, Anuṣṭubh, Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Triṣṭubh and Jagatī; these are the metres of night. The night has five calls, and so the additional litany of the Vājapeya. ‘The night goes beyond the Uktha; verily thus from metre to metre they call’ Kauṣītaki used to say, to prevent sameness. In that he uses a Triṣṭubh containing the word ‘over the night’ as invitatory verse for the Aśvin litany cup, (it is because) the Praiṣa contains (the word) ‘over the night’, for the Somas are left over the night. Moreover, the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus might and strength he places in the sacrificer. The additional litanies of the Āptoryāma have four calls; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fourfold, and also fourfooted; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. They use as concluding verses (verses) to the lord of the field, (thinking) ‘The field is this earth; in it undepressed shall we find support at the end’; verily thus in it undepressed do they find support at the end. In that the offering verses are Triṣṭubhs containing (the word) ‘over the night’, (it is) because the Somas are left over the night. Moreover, the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus might and strength he places in the sacrificer. They say the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations. They then proceed with (the cup) for the yoker of the bays; the
explanation of this has been given. He recites a Triṣṭubh as invitatory verse for (the cup) for the yoker of the bays; the explanation of this has been given. In that he recites an invitatory verse for the Atipraiṣa, (it is because) without strength is the Praiṣa which has no invitatory verse. Moreover there are invitatory verses in the case of (the cups) for two deities, and in the case of all the Prasthitas; therefore he recites an invitatory verse for it. ‘In that he recites an Atipraiṣa, verily thus he refers to the next day, verily thus they keep taking hold of the next day’ Kauṣītaki used to say.

sanskrit_iast: anuṣṭubham gāyatrīm uṣṇiham triṣṭubham jagatīm iti |

sanskrit_iast: chandase chandasa eva tad āhvayanta iti ha sma āha kauṣītakir ajāmitāyai |

sanskrit_iast: atha yat tiro ahnyavatīm triṣṭubham āśvina iktha grahasya puronuvākyām anvāha |
meaning: अथ यत् तिरो अह्न्यवतीम् त्रिष्टुभम् आश्विन इक्थ ग्रहस्य पुरोनुवाक्याम् अन्वाह |
